entries: Your people have always been blessed with luck, and you've learned to lend it to your companions. You just wish, and it happens! You gain the following benefits:

items: When an ally you can see within 30 feet of you rolls a natural 1 on a d20 for an attack roll, saving throw, or skill check, you can use your reaction to let the ally reroll. They must use the second roll. When you use this reaction, you cannot use your Lucky racial feat until the end of your next turn.

name: Bounty Hunter
entries: When there's a price on someone's head, you make it your business to collect. You gain the following benefits:

items: You perfectly remember the name and face of every person you've ever met.

You can use your action to mark a creature you can see within 120 feet of you for 1 hour. You have advantage on any Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check you make to find the marked creature. Additionally, as long as the creature is marked, you can discern whether or not the creature has passed through a location. You can have only one creature marked at a time.
Whenever you reduce a target to 0 hit points with any attack you make or spell that you cast, you can choose to knock the creature out instead of killing it.

name: Bounty Hunter
entries: When there's a price on someone's head, you aim to collect. You gain the following benefits:

items: You perfectly remember the name and face of every person you've ever met.

You can use your action to mark a creature you can see within 120 feet of you for 1 hour. You have advantage on any Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks you make to find the marked creature. Additionally, as long as the creature is marked, you can discern whether or not the creature has passed through a location. You can have only one creature marked at a time.
Whenever you reduce a creature to 0 hit points with any attack you make or spell that you cast, you can choose to knock the creature out instead of killing it.

name: Bow Expert
entries: Your relentless practice with a bow grants you the following benefits while using one:

entries.name: Ranging Shots
entries: When you miss a ranged weapon attack with a bow, your next ranged weapon attack roll with a bow has advantage.

entries.name: Overwatch
entries: As a bonus action, you can ready a shot until the start of your next turn. If a creature moves 5 feet or more while within 30 feet of you while you have a shot readied, you can use your reaction to make a ranged weapon attack against that creature with a -5 penalty to the attack roll.

name: Bow Mastery
entries: Bows are used by many, but you have trained to make the most of these elegant weapons. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to damage rolls you make with shortbows and longbows.
When you use the Attack action with a shortbow on your turn, you can make one ranged weapon attack as a bonus action.
You can use Strength instead of Dexterity for the attack and damage rolls you make with longbows.

name: Brave at a Pinch
entries: One of the Wise once said that you have to put a Hobbit in a tight place before you find out what is in them. You prefer to avoid finding yourself in one, but you are also sure you would be able to take good care of yourself in the circumstances.

items: Whenever a hostile creature or harmful effect imposes a condition on you, you suffer one or more levels of {@condition exhaustion}, or you drop to half or less of your maximum hit points, you gain inspiration.

name: Bravo's Apprentice

prerequisite.other: Fighting Style feature, and no Dance Flares known

entries: You have studied the art of dance and developed martial techniques to convey this artistry. As a result, you learn one {@filter dance flare|optionalfeatures|feature type=DF|source=TPDanc} option of your choice from the dancer class. If the flare has a prerequisite of any kind, you can't choose it.

Whenever you reach a level that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can replace this feat's {@filter dance flare|optionalfeatures|feature type=DF|source=TPDanc} with another one from the dancer class that you don't have.

name: Brawling Initiate
entries: Your experience in brawls has helped you develop a particular style of fighting. As a result, you learn one Fighting Style option of your choice from the pugilist class. If you already have a style, the one you choose must be different.
Whenever you reach a level that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can replace this feat's scrap style with another one from the pugilist class that you don't have.

name: Brawny
entries: You become stronger, gaining the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Athletics} skill. If you are already proficient in the skill, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.
You count as if you were one size larger for the purpose of determining your carrying capacity.

name: Brawny (Revised)
entries: You have studied the craft of herbalism, mastering the art of gathering and cultivating alchemical reagents, along with a few other tricks of the trade.

items: You gain proficiency in the Athletics skill. If you are already proficient in the skill, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.
You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity, inventory slots, and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

name: Brazen Courage
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Staunch Will
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against the {@condition Frightened} condition. Also, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to end the {@condition Frightened} condition on yourself a number of times per day equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Breaching Containment - Controlled Exposure
entries: As an action on your turn, you may release the pressure latches on your Xexel to enter your uncontained state. When you enter your uncontained state weather through Extensive damage or Controlled Exposure, your Xexel falls empty in your space, along with any worn or carried items or equipment, and you gain the following traits:

entries.name: Lighter than Air
entries: While in your gaseous, uncontianed state, you gain a fly speed of 60 ft, and can hover in mid-air.

entries.name: Highly Flammable
entries: The vapours and gasses that make up your body are incredibly flammable. You are vulnerable to fire damage, and if dealt fire damage, you must succeed on a DC 15 constitution saving throw or continue to take 1d6 fire damage each round. You may repeat this saving throw at the beginning of each of your turns to end the effect.

entries.name: Insubstantial
entries: The shifting gasses that make up your body flow out of the way of most physical attacks, and can exert little to no force on their own. You have immunity to non-magical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, but are incapable of physically interacting with objects and creatures, and cannot wear armor or carry equipment through normal means.

entries.name: Vaporous Form
entries: Effects such as strong winds which would disperse gas or vapour are hazardous to you in this state. You cannot willingly enter zones or areas created by such effects, and forced movement caused by such effects is doubled for you. When you are subject to such an effect, you must succeed on a DC 15 constitution saving throw take 1d6 force damage.

entries.name: Poisonous Cloud
entries: Your cloudlike body forms a roughly spherical cloud 5ft in diameter, and is made up of luminous gasses and vapours that are poisonous to most creatures. You may occupy the same space as other creatures, and the space within your cloud is considered lightly obscured. Creatures who enter or start their turn within your space must succeed on a DC 17 constitution save or take poison damage equal to your level. Returning to an unruptured Xexel requires an action to complete. However, once ruptured, a Xexel enters emergency repair mode, and cannot be re-entered until after completing a long rest. This emergency repair only restores the Xexel to 1 hit point, and the suit must be repaired normally beyond that point.

name: Breaching Containment - Extensive Damage
entries: If your Xexel takes extensive damage, it can lose it's ability to properly contain your gaseous body, forcing you out of it's protection. When damage would reduce your Xexel hit points to 0 or fewer, your suit ruptures, and you enter an uncontained state.

name: Breaker
entries: You master the breaking of any creature within your grasp. You gain the following benefits:

items: {@b Ability Score Increase.} Increase your Strength or Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
{@b Punishing Blows.} You have advantage on attack rolls against a creature you are {@condition grappled|PHB|grappling}.
Gain the {@b Merciless Break} special attack (below)

entries.name: Merciless Break
entries: {@italic Active Ability (Attack)}
When you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks to inflict a debilitating injury on a creature you are {@condition grappled|PHB|grappling}.

The creature takes {@damage 2d6} + your Strength modifier bludgeoning damage and suffers an injury for 1 minute. The number of d6 increases by one when your proficiency bonus increases (with the total number of d6 equaling your proficiency bonus). While suffering from this injury, the creature subtracts 1d6 from attack rolls and ability checks, and must pass a DC 10 Constitution saving throw to successfully cast a spell.

The target creature makes a Constitution saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect of the injury on a success. A creature can spend their action treating their injury to automatically pass the saving throw.
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

name: Breaker
entries: Your attacks which deal bludgeoning damage deal double damage to objects and structures.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Breaker
entries: Your attacks which deal bludgeoning damage deal double damage to objects and structures.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

items: When the Scoridra makes a breath weapon attack, all three sibling heads exhume fire at once. On a successful breath weapon attack, may spend a reaction to add an extra 3d6 fire damage to the roll. You may use Breath As One again after a long rest.

name: Breath of the Bay*
entries: Ryujin has blessed the blood of your forefathers with the greatest power his beasts and guardians possess: Dragonfire, a flame far stronger and hotter than anything the mortals can hope to achieve. You gain the Following Benefits:

items: You learn to speak, read, and write Draconic if you cannot already.

Once per day you can use the breath weapon Dragonfire. You breath a bright green cone of fire up to 30 ft. All creatures caught in the cone must make a Dexterity Saving Throw against your Charisma modifier or take 3d6 fire damage (which will pierce resistances), or half as much on a successful save. The target will also remain burned, taking 1d4 fire damage at the beginning of each pf their turns. The target can make CON saves at the end of their turn to try and put out the flame, with a DC based o your CHA modifier, or continue to burn.

name: Breath Versatility
entries: You can alter your breath. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Constitution or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

When you use your {@classFeature Dragon's Breath|Demi-Dragon|TheDemiDragon|1|TheDemiDragon|Dragon's Breath} or Breath Weapon, you can freely choose between using a line breath or a cone breath. If you choose a line, you can increase the width of your breath from 5 feet to 10 feet.

name: Breath Weapon
entries: You can use your action to exhale destructive energy. Your draconic ancestry determines the size, shape, and damage type of the exhalation.

When you use your breath weapon, each creature in the area of the exhalation must make a saving throw, the type of which is determined by your draconic ancestry. The DC for this saving throw equals 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus. A creature takes {@dice 2d6} damage on a failed save, and half as much damage on a successful one. The damage increases to {@dice 3d6} at 6th level, {@dice 4d6} at 11th level, and {@dice 5d6} at 16th level.
After you use your breath weapon, you can't use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

entries.caption: Draconic Ancestry
rows: Fang ({@b Officially do not have a Breath Weapon})

name: Bree-Pony
entries: Bree-ponies are very similar to their owners, the Bree-folk—they don't seem to have anything special compared to their peers in other parts of Middle-earth, and yet some of them display uncommon courage and exceptional memory. You have acquired an unusually brave and intelligent beast that follows you everywhere.

items: Your pony uses your proficiency bonus rather than its own, and adds your proficiency bonus to each of its ability scores, AC, and to any ability check or saving throw that it makes.
Your pony has a number of Hit Dice equal to your character level instead of its normal Hit Dice (minimum 2).

Your pony obeys your commands. In combat, it takes its turn on your initiative and acts and moves as you direct it (no action required by you), or on its own if you are absent or {@condition incapacitated}. It cannot make {@action opportunity attack||opportunity attacks}, and its only action options are {@action Dash}, {@action Disengage}, and {@action Dodge}, unless you spend an action on your turn to command it to take another action. If your pony dies, you can acquire a new one during the next Yule Fellowship Phase.

name: Brew Master
entries: You are skilled in the art of producing beer and other alcoholic beverages. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with {@item brewer's supplies|phb}. If you are already proficient with them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.
You can purify twice as much water during a short or long rest.
You can customize your alcoholic beverages in such a way that they impose advantage or disadvantage (your choice) on saving throws against their effects.
As part of a long rest, you can distill a beverage to yield a container of pure alcohol, which can be used for medicinal purposes or as fuel for a fire.

name: Brew Master
entries: You have studied the craft of brewing intensely, and have learned to craft fine artisanal brews. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with brewer's supplies. If you are already proficient with them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.
You have advantage on saving throws vs. the effects of alcohol and can accurately identify any alcoholic beverage by taste, provided you have tasted it at least once before.
You can drink a specialty brew as an action, instead of the usual 1 minute required.

name: Brew Master
entries: You are an expert with {@item Brewer's Supplies|phb}.
You can purify twice as much water during a short or long rest.
You can customize your alcoholic beverages in such a way that they impose advantage or disadvantage (your choice) on saving throws against their effects.
As part of a long rest, you can distill a beverage to yield a container of pure alcohol, which can be used for medicinal purposes or as fuel for a fire.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Brewer
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Tool Proficiency
entries: You gain proficiency in {@item brewer's supplies|XPHB}.

entries.name: Discount
entries: You get a 50% discount when purchasing food and beverages.

entries.name: Quick Brewing
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can brew an invigorating mead, provided you have {@item Brewer's Supplies|XPHB} available. A creature can use a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to drink the mead, granting it {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. The mead's potency lasts until you start a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items: Whenever you roll a 1 on an Intelligence ability check or Intelligence saving throw, you can reroll the die. You must use the new result, even if it is a 1.

When you gain this feat, choose one of the following skills: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill Investigation}, {@skill History}, {@skill Nature} or {@skill Religion}. If you aren't proficient with it, you gain proficiency with the chosen skill, if you are proficient with it you double your proficiency bonus for any skill check you make with it instead. You may spend 1 hour studying as part of a long rest, if you do you may swap the chosen skill for another of the ones listed when you finish said long rest.

name: Broken Spells
entries: In ancient times, the Dwarves made mighty spells. You have been taught fragments of old enchantments that retain some power to this day.

items: Choose any combination of three skills or tools you are proficient with. Whenever you make an ability check that uses one of the chosen proficiencies, you can obtain a magical success. You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Brothers in Arms
entries: {@b {@i IMPORTANT: This feature requires {@color two (or more) separate characters|ff0000} having it to function!}}

items: When adjacent to one of your brothers you gain +2 to your weapon attacks, and you can split any bludgeoning, piercing or slashing (magical or not) damage that you take between you and your brother.
If you're flanking a creature with one of your brothers, you gain +4 to your weapon attacks.

foundryEffects.name: Brothers in Arms Adjacent Attack Bonus
Brothers in Arms Flanking Attack Bonus

name: BrotHers of the Mine
entries: Your time spent using pickaxes and war picks allows you to use them to aid your allies. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You gain proficiency with the {@item cartographer's tools|PHB}. The damage die of a war pick you wield is now 1d8 (1d12).

When you take the Attack action while using a pickaxe, a war pick, or a similar tool, you can forgo one of your attacks and instead pull a creature within 5 feet of you off balance; the next attack roll an ally makes against this target before the start of your next turn has advantage. If the target is wielding a shield, you temporarily pull it aside, granting all allies a +2 bonus to attack rolls against the target until the start of your next turn.

name: Brutal
entries: As a reaction when you reduce an enemy to 0 hit points, you can attempt to frighten nearby creatures. When you do so, each creature of your choice within 10 feet of that enemy must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your {@skill Intimidation} bonus) or be {@condition frightened} by you until the end of your next turn. Once you use this ability, you cannot do so again until you complete a short or long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Brutal
entries: As a reaction when you reduce an enemy to 0 hit points, you can attempt to frighten nearby creatures. When you do so, each creature of your choice within 10 feet of that enemy must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your {@skill Intimidation} bonus) or be {@condition frightened} by you until the end of your next turn. Once you use this ability, you cannot do so again until you complete a short or long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Brutal Attacker
entries: You master a reckless approach that maximizes your offensive capabilities.

items: You can wield a two-handed weapon in one hand, as long as your other hand is empty or wielding a one handed weapon.
When you reduce a creature to 0 hit points, your next attack roll before the end of your next turn gains advantage.

name: Brutal Casting
entries: You have practiced techniques that help you to empower your attacks with certain spells, gaining the following benefits:

items: When you score a critical hit with a spell attack, you can roll one of the spell's damage dice one additional time and add it to the extra damage of the critical hit.
When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that requires you to make a spell attack, your spell attack scores a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

You learn one cantrip that requires an attack roll. Choose the cantrip from the bard, cleric, druid, sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list. Your spellcasting ability for this cantrip depends on the spell list you chose from: Charisma for bard, sorcerer, or warlock; Wisdom for cleric or druid; or Intelligence for wizard.

name: Brutal Critical
entries: You can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a melee attack. You can select this feat a second time after 13th level, and a third time at 17th level.

entries.name: Heavy Duelist
entries: You can wield a Melee weapon with {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} in one hand.

entries.name: Versatile Dual Wielder
entries: While wielding a Melee weapon with {@itemProperty V|XPHB|Versatile} in one hand, the weapon has the {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light} property for you.

name: Brutal Grip
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Heavy Duelist
entries: You can wield a Melee weapon with {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} in one hand.

entries.name: Versatile Dual Wielder
entries: While wielding a Melee weapon with {@itemProperty V|XPHB|Versatile} in one hand, the weapon has the {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light} property for you.

name: Brutal Grip
entries: When there's a price on someone's head, you aim to collect. You gain the following benefits:

items: When wielding a {@filter versatile weapon|items|category=basic|property=Versatile} in one hand, you may use the two-handed damage die.
You can wield a two-handed melee weapon in one hand, treating it as a one-handed weapon. You have disadvantage on attack rolls made when wielding a two-handed weapon this way.

name: Brutal Strength
entries: Even amongst Man-Ogres you are considered to be strong and capable of impressive feats of brutish power. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your unarmed strikes can deal bludgeoning damage equal to {@damage 1d6} + your Strength modifier on a hit.
You count as one size larger when grappling and your speed is not halved when moving a {@condition grappled} creature if it is a smaller size than you.

When you hit with an attack using Strength, you can roll one of the attack's damage dice an additional time and add it as extra damage of the attack's damage type. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

entries.name: Brutal Weaponry
entries: You can wield a weapon that has the {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} property in one hand, provided your other hand isn't also wielding a weapon that has the {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} property or holding a {@item Shield|XPHB}.

entries.name: Killing Streak
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn and attack with a weapon that has the {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} property, you can make one extra attack as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light} weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative or you have the {@feat Two-Weapon Fighting|XPHB} feat.

name: Brutalizer
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Brutal Weaponry
entries: You can wield a weapon with the {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} property in one hand, as long as your other hand is empty or wielding a one-handed weapon.

entries.name: Killing Streak
entries: When you reduce a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, your next attack roll before the end of your next turn has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

name: Brute
entries: Your attacks leave your enemies devastated and cowering in fear. You gain the following benefits:

items: {@b Ability Score Increase.} Increase your Strength or Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
{@b Brutal Effort.} When you roll damage for a melee weapon attack, you can reroll the weapon's damage dice and use either total.
Gain the {@b Brutal Threat} special attack (below)

entries.name: Brutal Threat
entries: {@italic Active Ability (Attack)}

When you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks to issue a dire threat backed by your killing intent at a creature that can see or hear you within 60 feet. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw.

On failure, they become {@condition frightened} for 1 minute. If it fails by 5 or more, it becomes frozen in terror, suffering the {@condition paralyzed} condition while it is frightened. A frightened creature can repeat its saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on success (if it fails by less than 5 it can end the paralyze effect, but cannot become paralyzed after the initial save).

If you kill a target while it is frightened in this way, you can repeat this action as a reaction targeting another creature within 30 feet that can see or hear you bypassing the usual usage restriction of the feature.
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

name: Brute
entries: Your faith grants you a deep wisdom and serenity, you feel a special connection to your faith, in particular the moonlight. You gain the following benefits:

items: When you roll damage for a melee weapon attack, you can reroll the weapon's damage dice and use either total.

entries.name: Brutal Takedown
entries: As a reaction to reducing a creature to 0 hit points, you can perform a brutal display that forces all hostile creatures of the same creature type within 60 feet that can see or hear you to make a Wisdom saving throw, or become frightened of you until the start of your next turn.
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

name: Brute
entries: You are adept at raw feats of strength and destruction. You gain the following benefits:

items: When {@action shove|PHB|shoving} a creature, you can push the target an additional 5 feet away.
You deal double damage to objects and structures.
You have advantage on Strength ({@skill Athletics}) checks to break nonmagical inanimate objects (such as doors or crates) and can do so as a bonus action.

entries: {@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Brute
entries: You are adept at raw feats of strength and destruction. You gain the following benefits:

items: When {@action shove|PHB|shoving} a creature, you can push the target an additional 5 feet away.
You deal double damage to objects and structures.
You have advantage on Strength ({@skill Athletics}) checks to break nonmagical inanimate objects (such as doors or crates) and can do so as a bonus action.

entries: {@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Buccaneer
entries: You have mastered the art of dueling with gun and sword, you gain the following benefits:

items: When you use the {@action attack} action with a one-handed melee weapon, you can spend a bonus action to fire a firearm you wield in your other hand. You can use this bonus action to attack with a one handed melee weapon if you use your {@action attack} action with a firearm.
While wielding a firearm and a one-handed melee weapon, you gain a +1 bonus to your AC.
You do not need a free hand to load ammunition when wielding a weapon in both hands.

name: Budding Chief
entries: You have the makings of a great chief, and your allies revere your strength and leadership. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Deception}, {@skill Intimidation}, or {@skill Persuasion}.

As a bonus action, you can allow a creature who can see or hear you to maneuver itself into a more advantageous position. That creature can use its reaction to move up to half its movement speed without provoking opportunity attacks. The creature can't maneuver itself using this feat again until it finishes a short or long rest.

name: Budding Chief
entries: You have the makings of a great chief, and your allies revere your strength and leadership. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Deception}, {@skill Intimidation}, or {@skill Persuasion}.

As a bonus action, you can allow a creature who can see or hear you to maneuver itself into a more advantageous position. That creature can use its reaction to move up to half its movement speed without provoking opportunity attacks. The creature can't maneuver itself using this feat again until it finishes a short or long rest.

name: Bugbear's Rest
entries: Your ability to nap and rest is unrivaled. None would challenge your sleeping prowess. You gain the following benefits:

items: If you sleep for 10 or more hours as part of a long rest, you regain all of your Hit Dice, regardless of how many you have expended.

If you have taken at least one short or long rest within the last 8 hours, you have advantage on Constitution saving throws made to avoid gaining a level of Exhaustion, and magic can't put you to sleep.

name: Bugbear's Rest
entries: Your ability to nap and rest is unrivaled. None would challenge your sleeping prowess. You gain the following benefits:

items: If you sleep for 10 or more hours as part of a long rest, you regain all of your Hit Dice, regardless of how many you have expended.

If you have taken at least one short or long rest within the last 8 hours, you have advantage on Constitution saving throws made to avoid gaining a level of {@condition Exhaustion}, and magic can't put you to sleep.

name: Built to Stand
entries: When you're wearing heavy armor, you have advantage on contested checks and saving throws against effects which would knock you prone or push you. In addition, your speed is not reduced by wearing armor with a Strength requirement greater than your Strength score.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Built to Stand
entries: When you're wearing heavy armor, you have advantage on contested checks and saving throws against effects which would knock you prone or push you. In addition, your speed is not reduced by wearing armor with a Strength requirement greater than your Strength score.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Bulletstorm
entries: You love raining lead on your foes, flushing them from cover, and making them suffer, gaining the following benefits:

items: When you hit a creature with a firearm with the automatic property, you can push a Large or smaller creature 5 feet away from you. A creature pushed in this manner cannot benefit from half cover or three-quarters cover until the end of their next turn.
Firearms with the automatic property which require an action to reload can instead be reloaded with a bonus action.
Attacks made using the automatic property can be fired up to the normal range of the firearm and do not grant melee attacks advantage against you.

name: Bully

prerequisite.other: Proficiency with at least one firearm

entries: You are adept at using firearms in close quarters, gaining the following benefits:

items: Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls.

Once per turn, when you hit a creature within 10 feet of you with a ranged {@action attack} using a firearm, you can force the target to make a Strength saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier). On a failed save, you push the target 5 feet away from you and knock it {@condition prone}.

name: Bully

otherSummary.entry: Powerful Build feature

entries: You're content with picking on someone your own size, but little guys are just more convenient. You gain the following benefits:

items: You are proficient with improvised attacks you make with corpses and creatures.

You can use a Medium or Small creature you are grappling as both a {@item shield|PHB} and as an improvised weapon with the thrown property and a range of 20 feet. Attacks made with a creature this way deal {@dice 1d8} + your Strength modifier bludgeoning damage on a hit. If the creature you are using as a weapon  isn't a corpse, it takes this damage as well.
When you are hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to cause a creature you are grappling to take the damage instead. You can't use this reaction if the creature is a corpse.

name: Bulwark
entries: The defensive uses of your shield can be extended to your allies as well. You gain the following benefits while you are wielding a {@item shield|phb}:

items: Each ally within 5 feet of you that doesn't have this feat gains half cover while you aren't {@condition incapacitated} or {@condition prone}.
When a creature enters the area within 5 feet of you, or is in that area when they attack an ally of yours that isn't wielding a shield, you can use your reaction to shove them with your shield.

name: Bumbling Fool
entries: You have a peculiar way of fumbling through life that somehow always works out in your favor, succeeding in situations through what others might view as accidental luck. When you fail an ability check and roll a number on the die equal to half your level (rounded up) or lower, you can choose to replace the die roll with a 15 instead. You can use this ability three times, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Burglar
entries: You pride yourself on your quickness and your close study of certain clandestine activities. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with {@item thieves' tools|phb}. If you are already proficient with them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.

As part of a short rest, you can use scavenged or acquired materials to build a temporary set of {@item thieves' tools|phb} for when you lack access to a permanent one. This temporary set ceases to function after 1 hour.

name: Burglar
entries: You are an expert with {@item Thieves' Tools|phb}.

As part of a short rest, you can use scavenged or acquired materials to build a temporary set of thieves' tools for when you lack access to a permanent one. This temporary set ceases to function after 1 hour.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Buried in the Veil
entries: Once per long rest you may 'bury' an object of no more than one cubic foot in size as an action.It passes beyond the material plane. You may 'retrieve' it at any time as an action. You may bury a number of objects in total equal to your Charisma modifier.

items: Whenever you roll a 1 on a Strength ability check or Strength saving throw, you can reroll the die. You must use the new result, even if it is a 1.
You can attempt to {@action shove} or {@action grapple} creatures up to two sizes larger than you, instead of just one.
The Heavy property for weapons doesn't give you disadvantage on attack rolls.

name: Burning Blade
entries: You further master the destructive fire magic of your people. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Strength, Dexterity or Charisma score by 1, up to a maximum of 20.

You learn the {@spell flame blade} spell, and can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast the spell in this way when you finish a long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spell.
When making a melee spell attack with the {@spell flame blade} you can use Strength or Dexterity modifiers for the attack roll.
When you roll fire damage for a spell you cast, you can reroll any roll of 1 on the fire damage dice, but you must use the new roll, even if it is another 1.

name: Burning Soul
entries: You harbor within your soul an ember of the flame of life akin to the power of a phoenix. You gain the following benefits:

items: {@b Ability Score Bonus.} Increase your Strength, Constitution or Charisma ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
{@b Resilient Life.} You gain advantage on death saving throws. If you have Explosive Rejuvenation available when you would fail your 3rd death saving throw, it automatically activates instead.
You gain the {@b Explosive Rejuvenation} special bonus action (below).

entries.name: Explosive Rejuvenation
entries: {@italic Active Ability (Bonus Action, Supernatural)}

As a bonus action, you can unleash the power of the ember within your soul, exploding with fire. You regain {@dice 2d4} hit points, and all creatures within 10 feet of you must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 2d4} fire damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.
The fire damage and hit points regard increase by {@dice 1d4} each time your proficiency increases (remaining equal to your proficiency bonus).
Once you use this ability, you cannot use it again until you complete a long rest.

name: Cabal Broker
entries: You have passed the legal and ritualistic exams necessary to become a bonded soul broker for the Cabal. As a result, you gain the following benefits:

items: Due to your dealings with your infernal bosses, you gain resistance to fire damage. If you already have resistance to fire damage, you gain resistance to cold damage as well.
You have advantage on any ability check you make to negotiate the terms of a deal or write a binding contract in your favor.
A creature that breaks a contract with you or negotiated by you gains 1 level of {@condition exhaustion}. This level of {@condition exhaustion} can't be removed by any means for 7 days.

name: Call of the Void*

choose.entry: Increase the chosen ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

entries: You have risen from the ashes, from the bones and the blood, to be born anew. Let your power seep into the world. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain the {@spell Toll the Dead|yastah} cantrip, and the ability to cast {@spell Inflict Wounds|yastah}, {@spell Vampiric Touch|yastah} (at Character level 5 or higher), and {@spell Contagion|yastah} (at character level 9 or higher) once per day

name: Call of the Wild*
entries: Nature is within you, for you are a part of it. You have learned that with time and effort, you can channel your natural ancestry. You gain the Following Benefits:

items: You can ritually cast {@spell Speak with Animals|yastah} in order to communicate with your animal friends.

Once per day, you can summon an animal companion to accompany you. It must be a beast, and must be CR 1 or below. These beasts have their own turns in initiative (though may not have their own roll depending on the will of the DM) and their stats to do not escalate with your level.

name: Calligrapher
entries: Through hard work and perseverance, you have become an expert in the art of calligraphy. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with {@item calligrapher's supplies|phb}. If you are already proficient with them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.

You can permanently commit a person's handwriting to memory if you spend at least 8 hours studying it. In the future, you can identify another instance of this handwriting if you examine it for 1 minute. You also recognize forged versions of this handwriting, but discerning whether or not it is a forgery requires further study as normal.

name: Calligrapher
entries: You are an expert with {@item Calligrapher's Supplies|phb}.
The amount of time it takes you to write something nonmagical is halved.

You can permanently commit a person's handwriting to memory if you spend at least 8 hours studying it. In the future, you can identify another instance of this handwriting if you examine it for 1 minute. You also recognize forged versions of this handwriting, but discerning whether or not it is a forgery requires further study as normal.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Calming and Charming
entries: Your Best Friend racial talent now allows you to cast {@spell Calm Emotions} instead of {@spell Charm Person}; you add Charm Person to your list of Bard Spells Known.

name: Camouflage
entries: If you are outdoors or in a natural environment, you can spend 10 minutes to create a camouflage for the local natural area you're in (1 minute if you have a disguise kit). Being in a camouflage grants you advantage on all stealth checks, when Hiding in the chosen terrain.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Camouflage
entries: If you are outdoors or in a natural environment, you can spend 10 minutes to create a camouflage for the local natural area you're in (1 minute if you have a disguise kit). Being in a camouflage grants you advantage on all {@skill stealth} checks, when Hiding in the chosen terrain.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Canden and Moon's Master Cut

prerequisite.other: You must have beaten a master at Master Canden and Moon's Sword School

entries: Having trained with the masters of the first sword school of Obojima, you've picked up a handful of useful skills. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your walking speed increases by 5 feet.

Immediately after rolling initiative, you can use your reaction before the first turn of combat to draw a weapon and move up to half your speed (rounded up). If you end this movement within reach of another creature, you can use the weapon to make one melee attack against that creature.

When you are hit by an attack, you can use a reaction to assume a defensive stance, allowing you to fend off incoming strikes. Until the start of your next turn, you have a +5 bonus to AC, including against the triggering attack. Once you assume this stance, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

name: Cannoneer
entries: Your familiarity with {@object ballista|DMG|ballistas}, {@object cannon|DMG|cannons}, and other heavy mounted weaponry grants you the following benefits:

items: You can load, aim, or fire a {@object ballista} or {@object cannon} as a bonus action on your turn.
When a {@object ballista} or {@object cannon} you loaded deals damage, you can reroll the weapon's damage dice and use either total.
When a {@object ballista} or {@object cannon} that you aimed is fired, you can add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll.
When you fire a {@object ballista} or {@object cannon}, attacking at long range doesn't impose disadvantage on the ranged weapon attack roll.
If you spend 1 minute repairing a {@object ballista} or {@object cannon}, it regains hit points equal to {@dice 1d6} + your level.

name: Cannoneer
entries: Your familiarity with {@object ballista|DMG|ballistas}, {@object cannon|DMG|cannons}, and other heavy mounted weaponry grants you the following benefits:

items: You can load, aim, or fire a {@object ballista} or {@object cannon} as a bonus action on your turn.
When a {@object ballista} or {@object cannon} you loaded deals damage, you can reroll the weapon's damage dice and use either total.
When a {@object ballista} or {@object cannon} that you aimed is fired, you can add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll.
When you fire a {@object ballista} or {@object cannon}, attacking at long range doesn't impose disadvantage on the ranged weapon attack roll.
If you spend 1 minute repairing a {@object ballista} or {@object cannon}, it regains hit points equal to {@dice 1d6} + your level.

name: Cannoneer
entries: You have spent significant time operating siege equipment, earning you the following benefits:

items: You add your proficiency bonus to attack and damage rolls using siege weapons.
If a siege weapon would require an action to aim, you can use a bonus action instead.
During a short rest, provided you have access to {@item carpenter's tools|phb} or similar equipment, you can restore {@dice 1d10} hit points to a siege weapon.

name: Cannoneer
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Cannon Proficiency
entries: You gain proficiency with {@item Cannon|SGEHPP|Cannons}, and you can reload a {@item Cannon|SGEHPP} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} instead of an action. You can take this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} only if you haven't moved during your turn, and after you take the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is 0 until the end of your turn. Starting at character level 11, this doesn't reduce your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, and when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can replace one of your attacks with reloading the {@item Cannon|SGEHPP}. When you reach character level 20, you can ignore the {@itemProperty SGEHPP:Art|SGEHPP|Artillery} property of {@item Cannon|SGEHPP|Cannons}.

entries.name: Siege
entries: Your attacks with {@item Cannon|SGEHPP|Cannons} deal double damage to objects and structures.

entries.name: Strong Back
entries: The weight of {@item Cannon|SGEHPP|Cannons} and {@item Cannonball|SGEHPP|Cannonballs} count as half for you.

name: Cannoneer
entries: The best defense is a good offense, and the best offense is a cannon; which you're an expert at:

items: You gain proficiency with cannons.

You can reload cannons as a bonus action instead of an action. You can use this bonus action only if you haven't moved during your turn, and after you use the bonus action, your speed is 0 until the end of your turn. Starting at 11th level, this doesn't hinder your movement, and you can use one of your attacks to reload instead. Starting at 20th level, you can ignore the {@itemProperty SGttEH:Art|SGttEH|artillery} property of cannons.
You know how to expertly handle cannons and their ammunition; the weight of cannons and cannonballs count as half for you.
Your attacks with cannons deal double damage against objects and structures.

name: Cannoneer
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Cannon Proficiency
entries: You gain proficiency with Cannons, and you can reload a Cannon as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} instead of an action. You can take this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} only if you haven't moved during your turn, and after you take the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is 0 until the end of your turn. Starting at character level 11, this doesn't reduce your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, and when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can replace one of your attacks with reloading the Cannon. When you reach character level 20, you can ignore the Artillery property of Cannons.

entries.name: Siege
entries: Your attacks with Cannons deal double damage to objects and structures.

entries.name: Strong Back
entries: The weight of Cannons and Cannonballs count as half for you.

name: Cantrip Combatant

prerequisite.other: A class feature that allows you to attack more than once when you take the Attack action on your turn, and the ability to cast at least one cantrip

entries: You have mastered the art of combining weapon strikes and spellcasting, granting you the following benefits:

items: When you use an action to cast a cantrip that requires you to make an unarmed strike or melee attack with a weapon you're holding as part of casting the spell, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action on that turn.

name: Cantrip Combinor

prerequisite.other: The ability to cast at least two cantrips

entries: When you cast a cantrip you know with a casting time of 1 action that does not deal damage, you can combine it with a different cantrip you know with a casting time of 1 action that does not deal damage, potentially creating a unique combination of effects.
A suggested list of combinations and their outcomes is given below, but the player is encouraged to think creatively about other possibilities as well:

entries.name: Hand of Grace
entries: {@spell mage hand} + {@spell guidance} or {@spell resistance} or {@spell spare the dying}. You can use your mage hand to touch another creature to cast guidance, resistance, or spare the dying.

entries.name: Battle Preparations
entries: {@spell blade ward} + {@spell true strike}. The duration of these cantrips is increased by 1 round when cast together.

entries.name: Magic Show
entries: {@spell prestidigitation} + {@spell thaumaturgy} or {@spell druidcraft}. You can produce multiple instantaneous effects from these cantrips at once, out to a range of 30 feet.

entries.name: Glowing Speaker
entries: {@spell dancing lights} + {@spell minor illusion}. You can create a humanoid figure made of light and speak through it.

entries.name: Elemental Pairing
entries: Any combination of {@spell control flames|XGE}, {@spell gust|XGE}, {@spell mold earth|XGE}, and {@spell shape water|XGE}. You can form a variety of shapes and sensory effects using two elements simultaneously.

entries.name: Secret Admirer
entries: {@spell friends} + {@spell message}. As long as you remain out of sight of the creature you communicate with through message, that creature will not know that you cast friends on it.

name: Cantrip Specialist
entries: Well practiced in fundamental spellcasting, you learn two Warmage tricks from among the following: {@optfeature Blasting Cantrip|VSS}, {@optfeature Corrosive Cantrip|VSS}, {@optfeature Draining Cantrip|VSS}, {@optfeature Explosive Cantrip|VSS}, {@optfeature Icy Cantrip|VSS}, {@optfeature Severe Cantrip|VSS}, {@optfeature Silent Cantrip|VSS}, and {@optfeature Static Cantrip|VSS}. Your cantrips count as warmage cantrips for the purposes of these tricks, and your character level counts as your warmage level, where applicable.

name: Captivating
entries: If you are able to interact with a creature that can understand you continuously for 10 or more minutes, whether through language or bodily cues, you can choose to have it make a Wisdom saving throw against a DC of 8 + your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus. On a failure, the target is {@condition charmed} by you for an amount of minutes equal to your Charisma modifier, ending if a hostile action is taken againt it or one of its allies. When the effect ends, the target has no hint that you {@condition charmed} it. Whether it succeeds or fails, it cannot be affected by this feature again until you finish a long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Captivating
entries: If you are able to interact with a creature that can understand you continuously for 10 or more minutes, whether through language or bodily cues, you can choose to have it make a Wisdom saving throw against a DC of 8 + your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus. On a failure, the target is {@condition charmed} by you for an amount of minutes equal to your Charisma modifier, ending if a hostile action is taken against it or one of its allies. When the effect ends, the target has no hint that you {@condition charmed} it. Whether it succeeds or fails, it cannot be affected by this feature again until you finish a long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Careful Attack
entries: You have become adept at studying and anticipating how your enemies respond to your attacks. You gain the following benefits:

items: As a bonus action, you can make an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check contested by the Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check of a creature you can see within 60 feet of you. On a success, you gain advantage on the next attack roll you make against that creature before the end of your next turn.

name: Careful Crafter

otherSummary.entry: Proficiency in a skill or tool

entries: You've trained in crafting items using a skill or tool that you're proficient with, and your creations are known for being well made and reliable. You gain the following benefits:

items: You make all ability checks for crafting with advantage.
Anyone assisting you in crafting an item gains advantage on their ability checks for crafting.
If you fail to successfully craft the item, the amount of time it took to complete the process is halved.

name: Careful Crafter

otherSummary.entry: Proficiency in a skill or tool

entries: You've trained in crafting items using a skill or tool that you're proficient with, and your creations are known for being well made and reliable. You gain the following benefits:

items: You make all ability checks for crafting with advantage.
Anyone assisting you in crafting an item gains advantage on their ability checks for crafting.
If you fail to successfully craft the item, the amount of time it took to complete the process is halved.

name: Careful Crafter

otherSummary.entry: Proficiency in a skill or tool

entries: You've trained in crafting items using a skill or tool that you're proficient with, and your creations are known for being well made and reliable. You gain the following benefits:

items: You make all ability checks for crafting with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.
Anyone assisting you in crafting an item gains {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on their ability checks for crafting.
If you fail to successfully craft the item, the amount of time it took to complete the process is halved.

name: Careful Dragon Mask

prerequisite.other: The ability to invoke a dragon mask

entries: You've mastered the ability to cast spells while wearing your dragon mask. With this feat, you no longer have disadvantage on attack rolls with spells and cantrips, and the targets of your spells don't have advantage on saving throws, while you're under the effect of your dragon mask.

name: Careless Assailant
entries: On your turn, before your first attack, you can roll a d8. Until the start of your next turn, you suffer a -2 penalty to your AC and you can apply the number rolled as extra damage on a number of melee attacks equal to your proficiency bonus. Unarmed strikes get half of the bonus damage rounded down.

name: Carpenter
entries: You are an expert with {@item Carpenter's Tools|phb}.
You can temporarily fortify a door or window using your action. The DC needed to open it increases by 5, but the fortification falls apart after 1 minute.

With 1 minute of work and raw materials, you can create a wooden barrier no more than 10 feet in any dimension. The barrier has AC 10 and HP 25, is immune to poison and psychic damage, and is vulnerable to fire damage. The barrier collapses 8 hours after being assembled.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Cartographer
entries: You have studied in the methods and techniques of mapmaking. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You gain proficiency with cartographer's and navigator's tools. If you are already proficient with them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.
You can easily and accurately understand maps, even those written in a language you can't read.
Even when you are drawing a map while traveling, you remain alert to danger.

Maps that you draw can be easily understood by any creature that shares a language with you, and a creature possessing such a map cannot become lost within the area the map displays if it can understand it. You must have cartographer's tools to use this benefit.
You cannot become lost except by magical means, and always know which way is north. You must have navigator's tools to use this benefit.

name: Cartographer
entries: You are an expert with {@item Cartographer's Tools|phb}.
Copying an existing map takes you half as much time.
While drawing a map, you can simultaneously draw a second copy of it without spending any extra time.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Cartomancer
entries: You gain the following benefit and the first two available Tiers of the Cartomancer Feat:
{@b The Tiers of the Cartomancer Feat:}

name: Carver
entries: You have studied woodcarving and from that learned the art of making intricate spellcasting foci. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with woodcarver's tools. If you are already proficient with them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.

If you spend 1 minute examining a wooden carving such as a piece of furniture or an idol, figurine or statue, you can accurately estimate its value and, at the discretion of the DM, you gain one further piece of information about it: its age, cultural origins, or some other snippet of potentially useful information.

Over the course of a short or long rest, you can polish and shine a single focus or holy symbol made of wood or bone and choose one of the following effects. Until your next short or long rest, whenever someone casts a spell for which these effects are applicable and using this focus, the chosen effect is applied to the spell (whether it triggers or not). Once a number of spells equal to your proficiency modifier have been modified this way, the focus loses the benefits of this feature until it is again shined and polished by someone with this feat.
You may reroll a single damage or healing die.
Add a +1 bonus to the spellcaster's first concentration check for this spell.

name: Castiron Stomach
entries: Your unnatural biological fortitude allows you to eat anything. You can gain sustenance from any organic or inorganic material that you eat, and things you ingest cannot deal poison damage to you, poison you, or affect you with a disease or curse.
Your Constitution score also increases by 1.

name: Cat's Caress

otherSummary.entry: Proficiency with {@item claw|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting}

entries: Manipulating your bladed digits with preternatural delicacy, you can switch from exsanguinating slash to soft caress with a deft flick.

items: After you take the Attack action using a {@item claw|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting} in one hand, you can use a bonus action to make up to two melee attacks with a different claw that you're holding in the other hand. You don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack(s), unless that modifier is negative, or you have the two-weapon Fighting Style.
You have advantage to hit a target you are grappling with an attack using a {@item claw|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting}.
You can equip or unequip either a single or a pair of claws using either a bonus action or action.

name: Catch and Fetch
entries: You are skilled at snatching things from the air and retrieving them. You can use your reaction to reduce the damage from a ranged weapon attack by {@dice 1d10} + your Dexterity modifier. If you reduce the damage to 0 in this way, you catch the weapon.

name: Cattle Dog
entries: You are a natural at herding your quarry. When you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, you may move that creature up to 10 feet in any direction before it resolves the rest of its movement.

name: Caustic Adaptation
entries: Long have your ancestors hunted and been hunted in the depths. Natural selection has given your blood an unpalatable, acidic quality.
You gain the following benefits:

items: When a creature hits you with a melee attack, it must make a Constitution saving throw with a DC equal to 10 + your proficiency bonus. On a failed save, the foul odor of your blood distracts it, and it has disadvantage on attack rolls made against you until the end of its next turn.

When you are reduced to 0 hit points by a melee attack, your blood splatters across the attacking creature, which must make a Dexterity saving throw with a DC equal to 10 + your proficiency bonus, taking {@damage 5d4} acid damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success.

name: Celestial Arts*
entries: You have tapped into the power of your celestial heritage and gained greater magical abilities. When you reach 5th level, the {@spell lesser restoration|yastah} and {@spell warding bond|yastah} spells are added to your Celestial Legacy trait, and you can cast each spell once per day. Once you cast either spell, you must finish a long rest before you can cast it again.

name: Celestial Legacy
entries: Your divine blood has granted you great power and awareness. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can cast the {@spell detect evil and good} spell at will, without expending a spell slot. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell.
You can use your Radiant Soul or Radiant Consumption trait as a bonus action instead of an action.

name: Celestial Legacy
entries: Your divine blood has granted you great power and awareness. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can cast the {@spell detect evil and good} spell at will, without expending a spell slot. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell.
You can use your Radiant Soul or Radiant Consumption trait as a bonus action instead of an action, and you regain the use of that ability whenever you finish a short or long rest.

name: Celestial Magic
entries: Your connection to your celestial essence is so strong you can tap into its power, you gain the following benefits:

items: You learn the {@spell command} spell and can cast it once per long rest, without expending a spell slot.

As a {@race Aasimar (Protector)|VGM|Protector} or {@race Aasimar (Scourge)|VGM|Scourge Aasimar} you also learn to cast {@spell Aid} and {@spell Remove Curse}, or as a {@race Aasimar (Fallen)|VGM|Fallen Aasimar} you also learn {@spell Blindness/Deafness} and {@spell Bestow Curse}, each of which you can cast once without expending a spell slot or needing material components.
You regain the ability to cast the these spells in this way when you finish a long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for all three spells.

name: Celestial Resilience
entries: Your connection with the celestial light that has infused the bright elves is stronger and more pure than that of the common folk, making you hearty like an angel. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have resistance to poison and necrotic damage.
You have advantage on saving throws against poison and disease.

You learn the {@spell Lesser Restoration} spell and one {@filter 1st-level spell|spells|level=1|school=A;T} of your choice. The 1st level spell must be from the abjuration or transmutation school of magic. You can cast each of these spells without expending a spell slot. Once you cast either of these spells in this way, you can't cast that spell in this way again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast these spells using spell slots you have of the appropriate level. The spells' spellcasting ability is the ability increased by this feat.

name: Centurion Training
entries: You have received the leadership training that other members of your race covet. You are always prepared, able to respond quickly and lead confidently. You gain the following benefits:

items: You may add half your proficiency bonus to your initiative rolls (rounded down).
You gain proficiency with medium armor and shields.
When you use your Saving Face trait, you do not expend a use of it unless your roll succeeds.

name: Centurion Training
entries: You have received the leadership training that other members of your race covet. You are always prepared, able to respond quickly and lead confidently. You gain the following benefits:

items: You may add half your proficiency bonus to your initiative rolls (rounded down).
You gain proficiency with medium armor and shields.
When you use your Saving Face trait, you do not expend a use of it unless your roll succeeds.

name: Centurion's Blessing*
entries: The Centurion knows that you can't really count on anyone else to fix you, you need to take care of yourself and grants you the knowledge to do it slightly better. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can now add your proficiency bonus to all self applied heals . (Spare Parts, Repair Kit, Hairline Fracture, Tempered Glass, Prime Sentience, {@spell Fabricate|yastah} if you cast it on yourself).

name: Chain Specialist
entries: You have studied extensively with the spiked chain and are able to fight with it and display more skill and finesse than most would believe. You gain the following benefits:

items: You may use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier for attack and damage rolls you make with a spiked chain.
You do not have disadvantage when you use a spiked chain to attack a target within 5 feet of you.

When you take the Attack action and attack with a only a spiked chain, you can use a bonus action to make a melee attack with it against an opponent within 5 feet of you. This attack deals normal damage, including your ability modifier.

When you draw a spiked chain, you can do so in such a way that the weapon's reach property is negated, wrapping the chain around your arms and shoulders so you can only strike targets up to 5 feet away from you. If you do, you gain a +1 bonus to AC while wielding a spiked chain in this way. Switching a spiked chain to or from this position while it is already drawn requires a bonus action.

name: Chameleon
entries: You have honed your natural shapeshifting powers. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can use your Shapeshifter trait as a bonus action.
As an action, you can blend into your surroundings becoming {@condition invisible}. This invisibility lasts until you move, make an attack, cast a spell, or deal damage to a creature.
When damage would reduce you to 0 hp or lower, make a {@skill Religion} check. You gain that many temporary hit points before reducing your hp lower than 1.
All your attacks deal +3 radiant damage.
Saving throws against your spells that deal radiant damage have a -5 penalty.
At the start of your long rest, you may pose a question to your deity. During your rest, omens show as answers, or a cryptic dream.

name: Change of Heart
entries: You have learned to use your words and body language to appear unthreatening. Creatures that you have fooled by a successful Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check within the last minute have disadvantage on initiative rolls to join combat against you.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Change of Heart
entries: You have learned to use your words and body language to appear unthreatening. Creatures that you have fooled by a successful Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check within the last minute have disadvantage on initiative rolls to join combat against you.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Changeling Metamorphosis
entries: Your ability to shapechange is more than skin deep. Increase your Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20. In addition, when you use your Shapechanging trait, you can choose one of the following benefits, which lasts until you use your Shapechanging trait again. Some of these benefits require specific physical features, such as gills or claws, that can be seen by observers.

entries.name: Aquatic Adaptation
entries: You adapt your body to an aquatic environment, sprouting gills and growing webbing between your fingers. You can breathe underwater and gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You adapt your eyes and gain {@sense darkvision} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Natural Weapons
entries: You grow claws, fangs, spines, horns, or a different natural weapon of your choice.Your unarmed strikes deal {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, as appropriate to the natural weapon you chose, and you are proficient with your unarmed strikes.

name: Changeling Metamorphosis
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Hardened Skin
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}.

entries.name: Metamorphosis
entries: When you use your Shape-Shifter trait, you may choose one of the following options. You gain the benefits of the chosen option until you use your Shape-Shifter trait again.

entries.name: Aquatic Adaptation
entries: You sprout gills and grow webs between your fingers. You can breathe underwater and gain a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@spell Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Natural Weapons
entries: You grow claws (Slashing), fangs (Piercing), horns (Piercing), or hooves (Bludgeoning). When you use your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} to deal damage with that new growth, it deals {@damage 1d6} damage of the type in parentheses instead of dealing the normal damage for your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, and you can choose to use your Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls rather than using Strength.

name: Changeling Mindreading
entries: You have honed your social intuition into palpable psionic talent, tapping into your race's latent telepathic abilities. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain an internal reserve of psionic energy represented by psi points. Your psi point maximum is 2, or your existing psi point maximum from another source (such as levels in a class with the Psionics feature) increases by 2. All expended psi points are restored when you finish a long rest. Your psi limit is 2, unless another effect increases it.

As an action, you can expend 2 psi points to magically read the surface thoughts of one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. While the target is in range, you can continue reading its thoughts, for as long as you concentrate (as if concentrating on a spell). While reading the target's mind, you have advantage on Wisdom (Insight) and Charisma (Deception, Intimidation, and Persuasion) checks against the target.

name: Chaos Magic
entries: Your magic is chaotic and unstable. Whenever you cast a 1st level or higher spell and consume a spell slot to do so, you may roll {@dice 1d6} on the chaos burst table. You may consume a 1st level or higher spell slot to choose which burst is activated instead of using the roll's result.
The effects of the chaotic burst happen immediately after you finish casting the spell.

entries.caption: Chaotic Burst Table
rows: {@bold Harmful Burst} You take 1 necrotic damage.

{@bold Harmless Burst} One of the following effects lasts until the end of your next turn (your choice): your eyes glow, or you are surrounded by a gentle wind or strange whispers can be heard around you..
{@bold Disappearing Burst} You teleport to an unoccupied space within 10 feet of you..
{@bold Thundering Burst} Each creature within 5 feet of you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or take {@dice 1d6} thunder damage and be pushed back 5 feet..
{@bold Restorative Burst} You gain {@dice 1d4} temporary hitpoints.
{@bold Protective Burst} You add 2 to your AC until the end of your next turn.

name: Charger
entries: You master the reckless rush of smashing into the enemy line. You gain the following benefits:

items: {@b Ability Score Increase.} Increase your Strength or Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
{@b Heavy Momentum.} If you move at least 20 feet in a direction before making your first melee weapon attack roll on your turn, the attack deals an additional {@damage 1d8} damage.
Gain the {@b Wild Charge} special attack (below).

entries.name: Wild Charge
entries: {@italic Active Ability (Attack)}

When you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with making a charge. You or a mount you are controlling can move up to 30 feet in a straight line, flinging your enemies out of your path.

This movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity. Large or smaller creatures in your path must make a Strength saving throw, or be knocked out of your way and prone. If a creature has no where they can move, they are knocked {@condition prone} but not moved, and you pass over them. A creature takes {@damage 2d6} + your Strength modifier bludgeoning damage on a failed save. The number of d6 increases by one when your proficiency bonus increases (with the total number of d6 equaling your proficiency bonus). Your charge ends early if a creature passes their save. Creatures with a CR equal to less than half of your character level automatically fail their save.
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

name: Charger
entries: You master the reckless rush of smashing into the enemy line.

items: After moving at least 20 feet in a direction, your next melee weapon attack deals an additional 1d8 damage. This damage increases by 1d8 for each additional 20 feet moved, up to your proficiency bonus.

entries.name: Wild Charge
entries: As an action, you or a mount your are controlling can move up to 30 feet in a straight line, flinging your enemies out of your path. Large or smaller creatures in your path must make a Strength saving throw, or be knocked out of your way and prone. If a creature has no where they can move, they are knocked prone but not moved, and you pass over them. A creature takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage on a failed save. Your charge ends early if a creature passes their save. Creatures with a CR equal to less than half of your character level automatically fail their save. At the end of the charge, you can make a single weapon attack as a bonus action.
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

name: Charger
entries: When you use your action to {@action Dash}, you can use a bonus action to make one melee weapon attack or to {@action shove} a creature.

If you move at least 10 feet in a straight line immediately before taking this bonus action, you either gain a +5 bonus to the attack's damage roll (if you chose to make a melee attack and hit) or push the target up to 10 feet away from you (if you chose to shove and you succeed).
{@homebrew You also gain the benefits of this feat if your mount satisfies its conditions (i.e. it takes the Dash action, and then it possibly moves up to 10 feet in a straight line).}

name: Charger
entries: When you use your action to {@action Dash}, you can use a bonus action to make one melee weapon attack or to {@action shove} a creature. If you move at least 15 feet in a straight line immediately before taking this bonus action, you either gain a +5 bonus to the attack's damage roll (if you chose to make a melee attack and hit) or push the target up to 15 feet away from you (if you chose to shove and you succeed, including the 5 feet from Brute).
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Charger
entries: When you use your action to {@action Dash}, you can use a bonus action to make one melee weapon attack or to {@action shove} a creature. If you move at least 15 feet in a straight line immediately before taking this bonus action, you either gain a +5 bonus to the attack's damage roll (if you chose to make a melee attack and hit) or push the target up to 15 feet away from you (if you chose to shove and you succeed, including the 5 feet from Brute).
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Charger
entries: You gain the following benefit and the first two available Tiers of the Charger Feat:
{@b The Tiers of the Charger Feat:}

name: Charger
entries: When you use your action to {@action Dash}, you can use a bonus action to make one melee weapon attack or to {@action shove} a creature.

If you move at least 10 feet in a straight line immediately before taking this bonus action, you either gain a +5 bonus to the attack's damage roll (if you chose to make a melee attack and hit) or push the target up to 10 feet away from you (if you chose to shove and you succeed).

name: Charm Twister
entries: You know hedge remedies and hexes passed down through Old Ways teachings, and you can impart them into small wicker charms you weave. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Old Blessing
entries: You can cast the {@spell Bless|XPHB} spell once using this benefit, targeting only creatures carrying a wicker charm you've woven, and you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have. Your spellcasting ability for casting the spell in this way is Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma (choose the ability when you select this feat).

entries.name: Twisted Hex
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can weave spite into a wicker charm you touch. Choose an ability. When another creature is carrying the charm, or while this charm is within an area that the creature considers home, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on ability checks and attack rolls using the chosen ability. When the creature fails one of these rolls, it can make a Charisma saving throw, destroying the charm on a success (DC = 8 plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and the ability modifier you chose for Old Blessing). You can only have one Twisted Hex charm at a time. If you make a new one, the previous one loses its magic.

name: Charming Presence*
entries: You've always been a dashing individual, superb in physical attributes. Those eyes. Mmf. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on Persuasion checks against members of the opposite sex.
You gain Surprise Attack benefits when attacking a member of the opposite sex before an initiative is rolled.

name: Cheat
entries: You can use your magic to boost your physical prowess.

You can temporarily raise one of your character's physical stats ( {@i Strength, Dexterity} or {@i Constitution}) to the same level as your spell casting stat for any {@i skill check, saving throw or attack}.
You can only use this feat a number of times equal to your spell casting bonus per long rest.
There are no physical changes to your character while this feat is active.

The stat change only lasts as long as the {@i action} it is used for is required, but cannot be sustained for very long: The effect will dissipate after a number of rounds equal to the natural stat's {@i modifier} no matter how long the action should take to complete.
Any buffs to stats are still applied - your current spell casting stat acts as the natural physical stat and any external buffs to the physical stat are then applied on top.
Any game mechanics to work out distance, capacity, endurance, accuracy, etc. are based on this new stat.

name: Chef
