entries: Whenever you gain a new level, you can replace one of the spells you chose for this feat with a different spell of the same level from the Warlock spell list.

name: Cultured
entries: You learn two languages of your choice.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Cultured
entries: You learn two languages of your choice.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Cunning Crafter
entries: You've become adept at tinkering and using devices in devious ways, granting you the following benefits:

items: You can use your action to perform object interactions and use magic items while frightened by your Scurry Away trait.

You gain proficiency with one type of artisan's tools of your choice, and you can use that type of tool as a spellcasting focus for any spell you cast that uses Intelligence as its spellcasting ability.

name: Curious
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Learn
entries: Whenever you make an ability check using a skill you are not proficient in, you can become proficient in that skill until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Once you use this benefit, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Observe
entries: Immediately after you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you can choose one creature you can see in the same combat. You learn any of the creature's Resistances and Vulnerabilities.

name: Cut Down the Nithingr
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Coward's Bane
entries: You have a +2 bonus to damage rolls you make against creatures with the {@condition Frightened} condition.

entries.name: Frightful Visage
entries: When you use a spell or effect that causes the {@condition Frightened} condition, the duration is doubled.

name: Cyberfiend
entries: Your birth was corrupted by the Foulest Abyss of mechademons, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Cyber Claw
entries: Your fingers bear retractable metal claws. You can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}. When you deal damage with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can deal Necrotic damage equal to {@dice 1d6} plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier instead of the strike's normal damage.

entries.name: Translocator
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can activate glowing circuits underneath your skin to magically teleport 15 feet to a location you can see.

You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Cybernetic Addict
entries: You prefer artificial body parts and enhancements over the old junk you were born with, gaining the following benefits:

items: You can attune to one additional cyberware, provided that it is tier 2 or lower.
You can have one additional augment installed.
You can select this feat multiple times.

name: Cypher Master
entries: You have learned a little something about cyphers, and have gained some additional facility with their use. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can bear one additional cypher beyond the standard {@book cypher limit|AotA|0|cypher limit} of three, and thus carry a total of four cyphers before risking a roll on the {@table Cypher Danger Table|AotA}.

When you use a cypher, you can try to use it in such a fashion that it doesn't burn out, though doing so is dangerous. When you use a cypher in this fashion, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a roll of 10 or higher, you succeed and the cypher remains available to be used again. Otherwise you fail, and the cypher burns out as normal. In addition to burning out, it detonates and deals half lightning and half force damage to you (no save to avoid the damage) according to the cypher's rarity: common 9 ({@dice 2d8}); uncommon 18 ({@dice 4d8}); rare 27 ({@dice 6d8}); very rare 36 ({@dice 8d8}).

name: Dagger Expert
entries: You wield daggers with perfection and poise, able to use them fluidly in any situation.

entries.name: Dagger Tricks
entries: You can draw or stow any number of daggers during your turn. You have advantage on any ability check to conceal your daggers.

entries.name: Improved Critical
entries: Your attacks with daggers score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

entries.name: Swift Stabbing
entries: When you use two-weapon fighting using a dagger in both hands, you can take both attacks as part of the {@action Attack} action on your turn (without expending your bonus action). You can only make this attack once per turn.

items: Your throwing range for daggers increases to 30/90 feet.
Any hit you score with a dagger against a creature that is surprised is a critical hit.
You gain advantage on any Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) checks to conceal a dagger on your person.

name: Dagger Master
entries: Daggers you wield deal {@dice 1d6} instead of {@dice 1d4} piercing damage and you can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a dagger.
Additionally, you can draw a dagger as part of the attack you make with one, and the range at which you can throw daggers increases to 30/90 feet.

Finally, you have advantage on Dexterity ({@skill sleight of hand}) and Dexterity ({@skill stealth}) checks made to conceal a dagger on your person or stash one elsewhere, and may attempt to do so as a bonus action.

name: Damage Specialist
entries: Choose a damage type from the following list: acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, poison, radiant, or thunder. Spells you cast ignore resistance to damage of the chosen type. You can select this talent multiple times. Each time you do so, you must choose a different damage type.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Damage Specialist
entries: Choose a damage type from the following list: acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, poison, radiant, or thunder. Spells you cast ignore resistance to damage of the chosen type. You can select this talent multiple times. Each time you do so, you must choose a different damage type.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Danger Sense
entries: You gain an uncanny sense of when things nearby aren't as they should be, giving you an edge when you prepare for the oncoming danger. Choose a saving throw. You have advantage on the chosen saving throw against effects that you can see, such as traps and spells. To gain this benefit, you can't be blinded, deafened, or incapacitated. You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do so, you must choose a different saving throw.

name: Dao Heritage
entries: You manifest more of the magical power of your dao heritage. You gain the following benefits:

items: You learn the {@spell detect magic} spell and can cast it at will, without expending a spell slot.
You gain natural armor. While you aren't wearing armor, you can calculate your AC as 13 + your Dexterity modifier. You can use a {@item shield} and still gain this benefit.

name: Dark Bark
entries: Your {@spell Eldritch Blast} is accompanied by an unearthly and disturbing howl from the hounds of the netherworld. Once per turn a creature that takes damage from your Eldritch Blast must make a Wisdom save versus your Spell DC or become Frightened of you until the end of their next turn.

name: Dark for Dark Business
entries: Your kind is not troubled by mere darkness in itself, as most members of other cultures are. On the contrary, you have grown to like the dark better than the light, finding yourself at ease in its cold embrace.

items: Dim light doesn't impose disadvantage on your Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks relying on sight.

When you are in dim light, in darkness, or underground, and you make an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw, you can do so with advantage. You can use this virtue a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Dark of the Deep
entries: You awaken to latent instincts you have from the cold, dark depths of the ocean, unlocking the hidden powers within you and enabling you to conjure inky clouds of mist and darkness. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have resistance to cold damage

You learn {@spell fog cloud} and {@spell darkness}, each of which you can cast once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast those two spells in this way when you finish a long rest. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for both spells. When you cast one of these spells in this way, you can't be perceived by blindsight while you are in the area.

name: Dark Reaping
entries: Additionally, when a creature within 30 feet of you is reduced to 0 hit points and dies, you can feed upon the power of their death to gain your choice of one of the following benefits:
You gain temporary hit points equal to your total character level + your Constitution modifier, which last for up to one minute
The first attack you hit with on your next turn deals additional necrotic damage equal to your total character level + your choice of either your Strength or Charisma modifier.
You have advantage on all saving throws until the start of your next turn.
Once you use this ability, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

name: Darklurker
entries: Your emergence strikes fear into the hearts of your targets, granting you the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in your choice of Stealth or Intimidation.

When you become visible on your turn, such as emerging from a {@spell fog cloud}, ending the invisible condition, or taking the Hide action, the first creature you damage before the end of your turn is frightened of you until your next turn ends.
Creatures that are frightened of you have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks against you.

entries.name: Frightened of Invisible Creatures?
entries: The Darklurker feat encourages characters who enjoy inflicting fear to pass in and out of line of sight. DMs and players have three options to adjudicate this playstyle's interaction with the {@condition frightened} condition, which states "the [frightened] creature can't willingly move closer to the source of its fear.
The first: if the frightened creature does not know where the source of its fear is, no movement willingly moves it toward the source of its fear, as it approaches unknowingly.
The second: the frightened creature cannot willingly move closer to the last place it knows the source of its fear was.
The third: the frightened creature has no idea where the source of its fear is. As it could be anywhere, the frightened creature cannot move at all.

Discuss your choice with the group and its ramifications when any member, including the DM, plans to use the feat or the associated playstyle in any way. Abi-Dalzim's Abhorrent Adventurers recommends the second option.

name: Dart Master
entries: You can draw a dart as part of the attack you make with one, and the range at which you can throw darts increases to 30/90 feet.
Finally, as a bonus action, you may aim with a dart, giving yourself advantage on the next attack you make with it this turn.

name: Daywalker
entries: The sun's light doesn't harm you as badly as it does other Kindred. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Dhampir's Boon
entries: When you take damage from sunlight, reduce the damage taken by 2.

entries.name: Endure Radiance
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend 1 Blood Point to remove your {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Radiant damage for 1 minute.

entries.name: Wake with Evening's Freshness
entries: When you start a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can make a DC 12 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, you count as having at least 1 Blood Point for that {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Daze
entries: When you score a critical hit, the target can't take reactions until the end of your next turn.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Daze
entries: When you score a critical hit, the target can't take reactions until the end of your next turn.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: DD&D: Artifactor
entries: You are one of DD&D's renowned Artifactors, tasked with acquiring valuable magic items, be it through shrewd negotiation or daring expedition. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Additional Attunement
entries: You can attune to up to four magic items at once rather than three.

entries.name: Eye for Quality
entries: You can cast {@spell Identify|XPHB} without a spell slot or components. When you cast {@spell Identify|XPHB}, you also appraise the target item, learning its market value in Credits.

entries.name: Faction Feats
entries: Veteran adventurers are likely to make enemies across the 'Verse, but if they're lucky, they might forge some alliances too. The greatest of these alliances are likely to be with factions, which provide work, services, and connections to spacers everywhere. Factions in Dark Matter are detailed in Chapter 1: The 'Verse.

Of course, such allies don't come free. Factions generally also require work and commitment from their members, which might come in the form of small tasks, important favors for higher ranking members, or even regular obligations for the organization. For their efforts, adventurers gain specific and useful skills from their factions, as represented by Faction feats.

entries.name: Gaining a Faction Feat
entries: The GM can award you a Faction feat for joining a faction or completing a quest for one. If allegiance to a faction is important to your backstory, the GM can also replace the feat granted by your background with an appropriate Faction feat.

name: Deadly Archery
entries: Elves possess a natural talent for hitting the mark when using their bows. You have honed this talent almost to perfection, and your arrows find their target with uncanny precision.

items: As a bonus action, you can give yourself advantage on your next ranged weapon attack roll on the current turn. You can use this bonus action only if you haven't moved during this turn, and after you use the bonus action, your speed is 0 until the end of the current turn.

name: Deadshot
entries: When you score a critical hit with a ranged weapon attack, the missile lodges itself in the target and causes a serious wound, which continues to bleed until staunched. The target takes {@dice 1d4} necrotic damage at the end of each of its turns until it or another creature uses an action and succeeds on a DC 10 {@skill Medicine} check to remove the projectile.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Deadshot
entries: When you score a critical hit with a ranged weapon attack, the missile lodges itself in the target and causes a serious wound, which continues to bleed until staunched. The target takes {@dice 1d4} necrotic damage at the end of each of its turns until it or another creature uses an action and succeeds on a DC 10 {@skill Medicine} check to remove the projectile.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Deaos' Trance*
entries: You've searched your dream-state for the gifts Deaos left upon your people and found within yourself the ability to enforce your dream-state upon others. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain the ability (At character level 9 or higher) to cast {@spell Chloroform|yastah} once per day without expending a Spell Slot.

Once per day while wearing a face that is not your perfect persona, you can create a dreamy aura around you that convinces people you are the person you claim to be without needing to roll deception or performance checks and lasts for 10 minutes. This ability will not effect anyone that saw you change your form, and due to the concentration it takes to keep the aura active, it cannot be used while you are in combat. If combat begins while you are using the Trance, it will immediately end. If your Trance ends while you are tricking someone, they must make the regular DC to see through your illusion or continue to be convinced by it until you give them a reason to doubt you.

name: Death Chirp
entries: Increase your Constitution score by 1, up to a maximum of 20.

You can use an action to emit a high pitched sound in a 15-foot radius around you. Each creature in that area must make a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus). On a failed save, the creature takes {@dice 1d8} thunder damage, loses concentration on a spell it is currently concentrating on and is deafened until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, the creature only takes half as much damage, is not deafened, and doesn't immediately lose concentration on a spell it is currently concentrating on. This damage increases by {@dice 1d8} when you reach 5th level ({@dice 2d8}), 11th level ({@dice 3d8}), and 17th level ({@dice 4d10}).
You can use your Death Chirp a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Death Defier
entries: When the hand of death reaches for your soul, you have found a way to reject its call. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Cling to Life
entries: You add your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1) to {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB|Death Saving Throws}.

entries.name: Enduring Vitality
entries: If an effect would kill you outright without {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB|Death Saving Throws} or would reduce you directly to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} without dealing damage, you are instead reduced to a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your level. You can't use this benefit again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Deathbound
entries: You have seen death many times, up close and personal, and sometimes at your own hand. These experiences have affected you deeply, teaching you about life and death. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: One Last Breath
entries: If you have two {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB} failures, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB|Death Saving Throws} until you are no longer at 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Recuperation
entries: When you spend a {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die} during a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} to recover {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can roll the {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die} twice and use the higher roll.

items: You gain proficiency in the Deception skill. if you already have it you gain Expertice in it.
You gain proficiency in the Disguise Kit. Other creatures have disadvantage on Perception checks to see through your disguises.

name: Decommissioner
entries: Charged with recalling defective constructs, hunting renegade androids, and quarantining the N-Virus, decommissioners are experts in slaying machines. You gain the following benefits:

items: By spending 1 minute observing or conversing with a creature, you can discern if that creature is a disguised construct, such as an android. If the creature is a construct or living construct, you can tell if the  construct is malfunctioning and if the construct is infected with the N-Virus (even if the virus is dormant).
When a construct or living construct within 5 feet of you makes an attack, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature.

When you hit a construct with a melee weapon attack, you can cripple its joints. Until the end of its next turn, its speed is reduced by 10 feet, to a minimum of 0, and it can't take the {@action Dash} action.
You can add your proficiency bonus to any saving throw you make against an effect caused by a piece of magical technology, such as a concussion grenade or a volcanic.

name: Dedicated Combatant
entries: Your fervent commitment to combat training puts your advanced weapon mastery on par with the most dedicated of specialists. You can calculate your martial level* using your full level in any class that is considered a half-martial, and half your levels in any class that is considered a non-martial.

entries.name: Advanced Weapon Mastery
entries: {@variantrule See Advanced Weapon Masteries|RyokoGuideToYokaiRealms|Advanced Weapon Mastery}

name: Deep Diver
entries: You've spent more than a natural amount of time underwater, and your lungs have grown to hold more air. In addition, you've become more adept at handling your movements while swimming.

items: The amount of time you can hold your breath is tripled.
You gain a swimming speed equal to half of your base movement speed.

name: Deep Diver
entries: You've spent more than a natural amount of time underwater, and your lungs have grown to hold more air. In addition, you've become more adept at handling your movements while swimming.

items: The amount of time you can hold your breath is tripled.
You gain a swimming speed equal to half of your base movement speed.

name: Deep Sense
entries: Your people have a natural knack for finding and appraising highly-valued items, typically ones that are magical in nature. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have a +5 bonus to your passive Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) score.

You learn to cast the {@spell detect magic} and {@spell identify} spells, but only as rituals. You can also cast these spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

name: Deep Sense
entries: Your people have a natural knack for finding and appraising highly-valued items, typically ones that are magical in nature. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have a +5 bonus to your passive Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) score.

You learn to cast the {@spell detect magic} and {@spell identify} spells, but only as rituals. You can also cast these spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

name: Deepest Lore
entries: When performing a skill check other than {@skill History}, the character can roll a {@skill History} check to recall a tangentially related detail regarding the activity. This might relate to an item used, a location the check takes place in, or a character involved. The DC for this check is 13 and can be rolled a number of times per day equal to the character's proficiency modifier. On a success, you can grant a friendly creature who can see and hear you a bonus to their next roll on a skill check of the same type equal to your Intelligence modifier. This bonus disappears if not used after an hour.

items: Decrease one random ability score by 3 and another one by 1. If it would decrease it to 0 or lower, randomize again until a higher one is picked.
You always pass your first two death saving throws.

name: Defender
entries: You learn to protect your allies from the tides of battle, you gain the following benefits:

items: When an ally you can see within 5 feet of you is the target of a creature's attack roll, you can use your reaction to leap in between your ally and the enemy as long as you are not prone, grappled, or restrained You move up to 5 feet into your ally's space, and your ally must have an unoccupied space within 5 feet of them that they take during the move. Your ally's movement does not provoke opportunity attacks. This makes you the new target of the triggering attack roll.

name: Defense
entries: You have +1 ac while you are wearing medium or composite armor.

name: Defensive Duelist (Alternate)
entries: When a creature you can see hits you with a melee attack while you are wielding a finesse or light melee weapon you are proficient with, you can use your reaction to add your Dexterity modifier to your Armor Class against that attack.
When you use this reaction and the attack misses, you can make a single melee weapon attack against your attacker as part of the same reaction.

activation.condition: When a creature you can see hits you with a melee attack while you are wielding a finesse or light melee weapon you are proficient with

name: Defensive Duelist
entries: When you are wielding a finesse weapon with which you are proficient in one hand and another creature hits you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to add your Dexterity modifier to your AC against that attack, potentially causing the attack to miss you.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Defensive Duelist
entries: When you are wielding a finesse weapon with which you are proficient and another creature hits you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to add your proficiency bonus to your AC for that attack, potentially causing the attack to miss you.

name: Defensive Weapon Master
entries: While you are wielding a shield or one or more defensive weapons, you gain the following benefits:

items: You can use a bonus action to protect a creature within 5 feet of you. Until the start of your next turn, any attack roll made against that creature has disadvantage if you can see the attacker. This benefit ends early if you are incapacitated (as explained in Appendix A of the Player's Handbook) or your speed drops to 0.

When you take the Dodge action on your turn, you can spend one Hit Die to steel yourself. Roll the die, add your Constitution modifier, and gain a number of temporary hit points equal to the total (minimum 1).

name: Defensive Weapon Master
entries: While you are wielding a shield or one or more defensive weapons, you gain the following benefits:

items: You can use a bonus action to protect a creature within 5 feet of you. Until the start of your next turn, any attack roll made against that creature has disadvantage if you can see the attacker. This benefit ends early if you are {@condition incapacitated} or your speed drops to 0.

When you take the {@action Dodge} action on your turn, you can spend one Hit Die to steel yourself. Roll the die, add your Constitution modifier, and gain a number of temporary hit points equal to the total (minimum 1).

name: Defiance
entries: Many realms have risen and fallen in the Lone-lands of Eriador since the Elder Days. Only ruins remain to mark their boundaries. Yet, the Bree-men have endured, revealing an unexpected reserve of strength and vigour in the face of adversity.

items: As a bonus action, you can spend one Hit Die to heal yourself.

name: Demolitionist
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Grenade
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can make one {@item Concussion Grenade|DarkMatter24}, {@item Flashbang|DarkMatter24}, or {@item Freeze Bomb|DarkMatter24}. This item lasts until you finish another {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, at which point it harmlessly falls apart.

entries.name: Improved Ordinance
entries: Your {@item Bomb|DarkMatter24|Bombs}, {@item Bottled Lightning|DarkMatter24}, {@item Concussion Grenade|DarkMatter24|Concussion Grenades}, {@item Flashbang|DarkMatter24|Flashbangs}, and {@item Freeze Bomb|DarkMatter24|Freeze Bombs} use the following DC if it is higher: 8 plus the modifier of the ability increased by this feat and your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Quick Grenade
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a {@item Concussion Grenade|DarkMatter24}, {@item Flashbang|DarkMatter24}, or {@item Freeze Bomb|DarkMatter24}.

items.name: Toss
items.entry: When you take the attack action you can spend one of its attacks to use a consumable that would normally take an action to use. If you do, you cannot do so again until the start of your next turn. You can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and regain all uses after a long rest.

items.name: Fuse
items.entry: As an action you can attach a consumable to a surface. Choose a number of rounds up to a minute, concluding at the end of your turn. It must be a consumable that takes an action to use. When someone steps on the 5ft square of surface it's attached to or the fuse's duration has passed, the item is used. The effect is centered on the space adjacent to the surface it was attached to.

items.name: At the ready
items.entry: You can draw or stow a consumable that takes an action to use when you would normally draw or stow a weapon.

name: Demolitions Expert
entries: You are a master with blast weapons and explosive equipment, gaining the following benefits:

items: When you miss an attack with a firearm with the blast property, you can use your reaction to detonate your ammunition in a space adjacent to the target, as if you had hit a target in that space with the attack.

You ignore the reload property on firearms with the blast property which require a bonus action to reload. Firearms with the blast property which require an action to reload can instead be reloaded with a bonus action.

You add half your proficiency bonus (rounded down) to damage rolls and the DC for saving throws caused by your explosives. When you use an antimagic grenade, you can add half your proficiency bonus to the d20 roll to end spells. You can throw explosives at twice the normal range.

name: Deprogramming
entries: You have advantage against effects and spells that magically compel you to take a certain course of action, such as {@spell suggestion} or {@spell confusion}, or that would alter or erase your memories, such as {@spell modify memory}. Additionally, if you spend 10 minutes or more speaking with a creature which is influenced by such a spell or effect, that creature can attempt to repeat its saving throw against that spell or effect. Once it has done so, it can't do so again until it completes a long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Deprogramming
entries: You have advantage against effects and spells that magically compel you to take a certain course of action, such as {@spell suggestion} or {@spell confusion}, or that would alter or erase your memories, such as {@spell modify memory}. Additionally, if you spend 10 minutes or more speaking with a creature which is influenced by such a spell or effect, that creature can attempt to repeat its saving throw against that spell or effect. Once it has done so, it can't do so again until it completes a long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Depth Module
entries: An advanced depth module has been integrated into your aqua suit, which grants you additional benefits while you're wearing your aqua suit:

items: You gain proficiency with the {@item net|PHB}, {@item trident|PHB}, and {@item spear|PHB}.
Your swimming speed increases to 60 feet.
A sonar system is incorporated into your suit. You gain {@sense blindsight} with a range of 5 feet, which extends to 20 feet while you are underwater.

name: Dermal Armour
entries: You have spent so long in your armour that you feel uncomfortable without it. It's a second skin.

entries.name: Attunement
entries: You need to spend a day adjusting straps, moving and feeling the weight of any new armour you wear to get the benefits of this feat.

entries.name: Sleep Standing Up
entries: While armour is never 'comfortable' to wear, you have mastered the art of getting a full night's rest while fully armoured. You will start to smell and any social interactions are at a -1 for every long rest your character spends in their armour. (Re-set with a bath/wash)

entries.name: Suit up
entries: You know the optimal way to get into and out of your armour; you can half the time it would take anyone else.

entries.name: Felt padding
entries: You can apply special padding on any armour (other than chainmail or ringmail) that enables you to negate any detrimental effects your armour has on stealth.
This takes the same length of time to prepare and apply as it does to don your armour.

This only lasts for 1 hour before it works loose and needs to be re-applied. Combat, dashing, athletics or acrobatics shifts the position of these pads and negates this effect. The skill is in the positioning of the materials rather than the materials themselves, however each application uses materials worth 1/100th of the base cost of the armour. (Non-magic version.)

name: Descendant of the Damned
entries: Wandering the sands of your ancestors and viewing the deaths of many, your Scion blood sings the songs of those beyond. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Strength, Dexterity or Wisdom score by 1, up to a maximum of 20.
Your unarmed strikes made with your natural weapons count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.
When you roll piercing damage for an attack made with your natural weapons, you can add halve your proficiency bonus (rounded up) to the damage dealt.
You gain resistance to necrotic damage.

When you have no spell slots left, you can attempt to cast a spell. Choose the level of spell slot (maximum 5th level) as normal, then roll a {@dice d100} and consult the following table. X is the spell slot level of the spell.

name: Desperate Courage
entries: You have lived all your life on the edge of the Wild, but the worst news that has come to Bree in your time concerned only brigands or packs of hungry wolves. You don't know yet what the likes of you can do against the Shadow in the East, but you are sure you will stand against it, no matter the cost.

items: Whenever you gain Shadow points, you also gain inspiration.

name: Destroyer
entries: You bring ruin to the battlefield, cleaving through hordes. You gain the following benefits:

items: {@b Ability Score Increase.} Increase your Strength or Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

{@b Cleaving Blows.} When you reduce a creature to 0 hit points with an attack, you can apply any overflow damage (damage dealt by the attack over what was required to bring the target to zero) to another creature within 5 feet of the target, if the attack roll would also hit that target.
Gain the {@b Whirlwind Slash} special attack (below).

entries.name: Whirlwind Slash
entries: {@italic Active Ability (Attack)}

When you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with spinning your weapon in a massive arc with great force. All creatures of your choice within 5 feet of you must make a Dexterity saving throw. On failure, they take {@damage 2d6} + your Strength modifier damage, or half as much on a successful save. The number of d6 increases by one when your proficiency bonus increases (with the total number of d6 equaling your proficiency bonus).
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

name: Desviar Objetos
entries: O personagem pode desviar flechas, virotes de besta, lanças ou outras armas de disparo ou arremesso.

{@b Beneficio:} É necessário que o personagem tenha pelo menos uma mão livre (sem estar segurando nada) para usar esse talento. Uma vez por rodada, quando o personagem normalmente seria atingido por uma arma de ataque à distância, ele será capaz de desviá-la sem sofrer qualquer dano. Ele precisa estar ciente do ataque e não pode estar surpreso. Desviar um objeto não é considerado uma ação. É impossível defletir as armas de ataque à distância incomuns (como as rochas arremessadas pelos gigantes ou os ataques gerados por magias, como a flecha ácida de Melf).

name: Devious
entries: Your cunning and agility give you an edge in combat. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with {@item thieves' tools|PHB} and one skill of your choice. If you are already proficient with {@item thieves' tools|PHB}, your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make with it.

You learn thieves' cant, a secret language that is described in the rogue's {@classFeature Thieves' Cant|Rogue|PHB|1} feature. If you already know thieves' cant, you learn to speak, read, and write two other languages of your choice.
If you have successfully hidden from a creature, your weapon attacks deal an additional {@dice 1d6} damage to it.

name: Devious Adversary
entries: You've practised scurrying in and out of combat and dispatching foes in underhanded ways, granting you the following benefits:

items: When you use your Scurry Away trait on a creature within 5 feet of you, you may choose to make a bite attack with disadvantage against that creature as part of the same action before you move.

When a creature you have been {@condition frightened} of by your Scurry Away feature since the start of your last turn misses an attack against you, any fear you have of that creature ends. You may then use your reaction to move up to half your speed towards it. If this movement brings you within 5 feet of the creature, or you were already within 5 feet of it, you may make a bite attack against it with advantage as part of your reaction.

name: Devious Training
entries: You have studied dastardly techniques to perform Devious Exploits. You gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Devious Exploits Known
entries: You learn two {@filter 1st-degree Devious Exploits|optionalfeatures|feature type=ll:1de} from the {@loader Alternate Rogue|class/LaserLlama; Alternate Rogue.json}. If they require a saving throw, the DC equals 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice).

entries.name: Retraining Exploits
entries: Whenever you gain a level, you can replace one of the Devious Exploits you learned through this Feat with another 1st-degree Devious Exploit of your choice.

entries.name: Exploit Dice
entries: You gain two {@dice d4} Exploit Dice to fuel these Exploits, which are expended when you use them. You regain expended Exploit Dice when you finish a short or long rest.
If you already have Exploit Dice when you gain this Feat, you instead gain a single Exploit Die equal to your others.

name: Devoted to the Pack
entries: When you use your Channel Divinity feature, in addition to your chosen effect, one friendly creature you nominate within 30 feet is encouraged for one minute, becoming immune to fear and resistant to necrotic damage.

name: Devour Treasure
entries: You forge a connection between yourself and a treasure chest on the Ethereal Plane, allowing you to gorge on treasure and send it there, or recall the treasure back yourself. You can spend 1 minute to devour up to 12 cubic feet of nonliving material (3 feet by 2 feet by 2 feet) and send it to the deepest reaches of the Ethereal Plane. The material remains on the Ethereal Plane until you use an {@variantrule Action|XPHB} to recall the material, whereupon it instantly appears in a special cavity you have created inside your own body.
After 60 days, there is a cumulative {@chance 5} chance per day that the material is irrevocably lost in a random location somewhere deep on the Ethereal Plane

name: Dexterous Fighting
entries: You can use dexterity for strength based weapons. Add 1 to your weapon's base damage when you make an attack in this way.

items: Taking the {@action Dash} action grants you half your current speed as extra movement.
Difficult terrain doesn't slow you down.
You can move through hostile creatures, and creatures have disadvantage on opportunity attacks made against you.
You also gain advantage on the next Dexterity saving throw you make before the start of your next turn.

name: Dhakaani Flail Master
entries: The ancient goblins of the Dhakaani Empire invented all manner of chain weapons, including the flail, dire flail, and mighty flail. You have spent countless hours studying their techniques with these weapons. You gain the following benefits when wielding any type of flail:

items: You gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls you make with the weapon.

As a bonus action on your turn, you can prepare yourself to extend your weapon to sweep over targets' shields. Until the end of this turn, your attack rolls with the weapon gain a +2 bonus against any target using a shield.
When you hit with an opportunity attack using the weapon, the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier) or be knocked prone.

name: Diehard
entries: You are difficult to wear down and kill. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on saving throws against effects that cause you to suffer a level of {@condition exhaustion}.
You have advantage on death saving throws.

name: Digger
entries: You just have to dig! You have advantage on ability checks for digging. In combat, if you are in an environment which can be dug into by your paws, you may take an action to go prone and gain half cover.

name: Dilettante
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you gain proficiency in a weapon, skill, or tool of your choice, or you temporarily learn a cantrip from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat's cantrip (choose when you select this feat). You retain this proficiency or cantrip until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Dilettante
entries: With a few minutes of preparation, a bit of improvisation, and some talent, you can appear proficient in just about anything. When you finish a long rest, you can spend 10 minutes practicing with a {@filter simple|items|source=phb|category=basic|type=simple weapon} or {@filter martial|items|source=phb|category=basic|type=martial weapon} weapon, skill, or {@filter tool|items|source=phb|type=tools}, or in the use of a {@filter cantrip|spells|level=0|class=Wizard} from the wizard spell list. You gain proficiency with that weapon, skill, or tool, or you learn that cantrip and can cast it using Intelligence as your spellcasting ability until you finish a long rest.

name: Dimension Digger
entries: You can dig and scramble through the weave of reality. Once per long rest, whenever you expend one or more sorcery points, you may cast the {@spell Misty Step} spell.

name: Diminutive

otherSummary.entry: You can only take this feat during character creation; Medium size

entries: You were born much smaller than others of your race, or simply never grew to full stature. You are Small instead of Medium. Additionally, suffer no penalty for squeezing into a space that is only large enough for a Tiny creature.

name: Diplomat
entries: You master the arts of diplomacy, gaining the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Persuasion} skill. If you are already proficient in the skill, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.

If you spend 1 minute talking to someone who can understand what you say, you can make a Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check contested by the creature's Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check. If you or your companions are fighting the creature, your check automatically fails. If your check succeeds, the target is {@condition charmed} by you as long as it remains within 60 feet of you and for 1 minute thereafter. This condition ends early if you or your companions do anything harmful to the target or its allies.

items.name: Concealed Weapon
items.entry: Attacking with a light weapon does not reveal you from hiding.

items.name: Bleed
items.entry: Once when you hit with a light weapon you can make the target bleed. If you do, they take damage equal to your proficiency bonus at the end of each of their turns until they use their action to stop it. You regain this ability after a short rest.

items.name: Repeatable
items.entry: You can take this feat more than once.

name: Dirty Tricks
entries: When you take this feat, choose two tricks. When you fulfill the criteria for {@feat Sneak Attack|Adventurer}, you can apply one of these tricks. You can only apply one trick to a single attack, unless otherwise stated. Some of your tricks require your target to make a saving throw to resist the trick's effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows:

If you have the {@feat Spellsneak|Adventurer} feat, you can also use these tricks on melee or ranged spell attacks. You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do so, must choose two different tricks.

entries.name: Duck Away
entries: You can forgo 1 Sneak Attack dice on a melee weapon attack. The target has disadvantage on opportunity attacks made against you until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Purloin
entries: You can forgo 1 Sneak Attack dice on a melee attack to make a Sleight of Hand check against the target's armor class. On a success, you steal one object from them if it isn't being worn or held, or is secured by thin string, straps, or chain.

entries.name: Fake Out
entries: You can forgo half of your Sneak Attack dice, rounded down, on a melee or ranged weapon attack. Your next attack on this turn can benefit from your Sneak Attack, dealing damage equal to number of dice forgone.

entries.name: Heel Cutter
entries: You can forgo 1 Sneak Attack dice on a melee or ranged weapon attack. The target's movement speed decreases by 5 feet until the start of your next turn. You can apply this trick to the same attack multiple times.

entries.name: Wing Clip
entries: You can forgo 1 Sneak Attack dice on a ranged weapon attack against a target with a fly speed granted by natural wings. The target must make a Strength saving throw or plummet 10 feet. You can apply this trick to the same attack multiple times.

entries.name: Blindside
entries: You can forgo 5 of your Sneak Attack dice on a melee or ranged weapon attack. The target must make a Constitution saving throw or become {@condition blinded}. At the end of each of its turns, the target can make a Constitution saving throw. On a success, the effect ends.

entries.name: Daze
entries: You can forgo 5 of your Sneak Attack dice on a melee or ranged weapon attack. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be {@condition stunned} until the end of your next turn.

name: Disappear
entries: You can utilize a foe's momentary distraction to disappear. When a creature within 30 feet of you moves away from you, makes an attack or casts a spell at a creature other than you, or takes damage from a source other than you, you can use your reaction to attempt to {@skill Hide}. If you succeed in hiding from it, you can immediately move up to 30 feet without revealing yourself to it. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you complete a short or long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Disappear
entries: You can utilize a foe's momentary distraction to disappear. When a creature within 30 feet of you moves away from you, makes an attack or casts a spell at a creature other than you, or takes damage from a source other than you, you can use your reaction to attempt to {@action Hide}. If you succeed in hiding from it, you can immediately move up to 30 feet without revealing yourself to it. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you complete a short or long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Discipline Acquisition (Animalism)
entries: You learn the basic concepts of a vampiric Discipline from another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.
You gain proficiency in the {@skill Animal Handling|XPHB} and {@skill Nature|XPHB} skills. If you already have proficiency in that skill, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it.

name: Discipline Acquisition (Auspex)
entries: You learn the basic concepts of a vampiric Discipline from another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.
You gain proficiency in the {@skill Investigation|XPHB} and {@skill Perception|XPHB} skills. If you already have proficiency in that skill, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it.

name: Discipline Acquisition (Celerity)
entries: You learn the basic concepts of a vampiric Discipline from another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.
You gain an extra {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, which you can use with any of your existing {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions}.

name: Discipline Acquisition (Dominate)
entries: You learn the basic concepts of a vampiric Discipline from another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.
You gain proficiency in the {@skill Deception|XPHB} and {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} skills. If you already have proficiency in that skill, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it.

name: Discipline Acquisition (Fortitude)
entries: You learn the basic concepts of a vampiric Discipline from another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.
{@variantrule Damage|XPHB} dealt to you except Fire and Radiant is reduced by an amount equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

name: Discipline Acquisition (Obfuscate)
entries: You learn the basic concepts of a vampiric Discipline from another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.
You gain proficiency in the {@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB} and {@skill Stealth|XPHB} skills. If you already have proficiency in that skill, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it.

name: Discipline Acquisition (Oblivion)
entries: You learn the basic concepts of a vampiric Discipline from another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.
You can see normally in {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} and {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}—both magical and nonmagical—within 90 feet of yourself.

name: Discipline Acquisition (Potence)
entries: You learn the basic concepts of a vampiric Discipline from another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.

When you hit a creature with a Melee weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} as part of the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can deal extra damage to the target equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

name: Discipline Acquisition (Presence)
entries: You learn the basic concepts of a vampiric Discipline from another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.
You gain proficiency in the {@skill Performance|XPHB} and {@skill Persuasion|XPHB} skills. If you already have proficiency in that skill, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it.

name: Discipline Acquisition (Protean)
entries: You learn the basic concepts of a vampiric Discipline from another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.
You can deal an extra {@damage 1d6} Slashing damage to a target you hit with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

name: Disguise Item
entries: You can use your talents at shaping yourself into objects in order to disguise another item, surrounding it with bits of yourself to create an illusory guise. As an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, you can touch one nonmagical item that isn't being worn or carried and is no larger than a 10-foot cube.
You surround the object with a magical illusion that lasts for 1 hour.

The illusion must be roughly the same {@variantrule Size|XPHB} and shape as the original object, but otherwise the details of the illusion are up to you. You can make the object look decrepit, appearing broken and shoddy. You can make it look perfect, appearing as though it's brand new and highly polished or well maintained. You can also make other similar disguises, as determined by the GM.
The illusion fails to hold up to physical inspection. For example, if you use this ability to make a chipped sword appear new, anyone running their thumb along the blade would feel the imperfections.

Otherwise, a creature can attempt to see through the illusion by using an {@variantrule Action|XPHB} to make an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check against a DC equal to 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Charisma modifier.
Once you have used this ability, you must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can do so again

name: Disguised Spellcaster
entries: In many public places, spellcasters simply aren't welcome. However, you've refined an ingenious disguise that conceals your magic within ordinary objects. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

When you cast a cantrip that requires a spell attack roll, you can disguise its casting (including its spell components) and effects as if it were a melee weapon attack. To do this, you must be holding a melee weapon and must target a creature within 5 feet of you. You don't have disadvantage on this spell attack roll for a hostile creature being within 5 feet of you. The effects of the spell are completely invisible, appearing as if you instead delivered a mighty blow with the weapon.

name: Disrupting Hostility
entries: If a hostile creature is within 10 feet of you, it has disadvantage on skill checks that rely on Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma and its ranged attack rolls.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Disrupting Hostility
entries: If a hostile creature is within 10 feet of you, it has disadvantage on skill checks that rely on Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma and its ranged attack rolls.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Disruptive Element
entries: A number of times per day equal to the character's proficiency bonus, the character can, when making an attack roll, gain advantage on all  attack rolls until the beginning of the character's next turn. All allied creatures within 20ft of the character will have disadvantage on all attack rolls until the beginning of the character's next turn.

name: Disruptive Timing
entries: When you damage a creature that is concentrating on a spell, that creature has disadvantage on the saving throw it makes to maintain its concentration.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Disruptive Timing
entries: When you damage a creature that is concentrating on a spell, that creature has disadvantage on the saving throw it makes to maintain its concentration.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Distinct Natures
entries: When using the alternate form racial ability, you assume the wolf's hit points and Hit Dice. When you revert to your elven form, you return to the number of hit points you had before you transformed. You automatically revert to your elven form if your wolf form drops to 0 hit points, and any excess damage carries over to your elven form.

name: Dive
entries: When you or a creature makes a {@skill Stealth} check, you can use your reaction to move up to 5 feet (towards the creature, if applicable) and fall {@condition prone}. If you do so, that creature can choose to do so as well. Any creatures that fall {@condition prone} in this way can reroll their checks.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Dive
entries: When you or a creature makes a {@skill Stealth} check, you can use your reaction to move up to 5 feet (towards the creature, if applicable) and fall {@condition prone}. If you do so, that creature can choose to do so as well. Any creatures that fall {@condition prone} in this way can reroll their checks.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Dive Bomb
entries: When you take the Dash action on your turn and move at least 20 feet, you can make one melee attack as a bonus action.

items: For a number of turns equal to your proficiency bonus, you can concentrate on two spells instead of one. After the duration, the one that was first cast, expires.
While concentrating on two spells, the DC for saving throws to maintain concentration is 10 + the sum of spell slot levels used in the two spells, or half the damage taken, whichever is higher.

name: Divine Attack
entries: If you are a sorcerer with the Divine Soul sorcerous origin, and provided you have your DM's permission, then you can exchange your Empowered Healing feature with the Divine Attack feature.
When you use your action to cast one of your cantrips, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action. You gain proficiency with one weapon of your choice.

name: Divine Awareness*
entries: The blood of the Archangels runs through you, and like them, nothing in the way of words gets by you. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in Insight. If you are already proficient, your proficiency becomes expertise.
You gain a +5 to your passive Insight.

name: Divine Diet
entries: You have choosen to take up a sanctified protocol in your eating.  The nature of the stricture around such is something your DM and you will work out - Are you a vegan? Do you have to eat only things you've hunted? Do you have to eat the heart & drink the blood of your enemies?

items: Undead (Good) or Celestials (evil) that claw, bite or grapple you take either (1d4) radiant or necrotic damage.
You need only eat one meal a day.
Resistance to either Radiant or Necrotic damage.
Choose one:
Cleric: Gain one additional channel divinity.
Druid: Gain 6 temp HP when in wildshape.
Monk: Add 1 to you Ki pool
Mystic: Add +1 point to you Psi Pool
Paladin: additioanl 1st level spell slot - can only be used for smite.
Sorcerer:Add +1 point to you metamagic Sorcery Points.
Wizard: You may use Arcane Recovery an additional time.
unlisted?: Gain an additional non combat cantrip.
If you fail to keep the diet, you gain 2 levels of exhaustion which cannot be removed until you've spent 3 months in a cleanse, without adventuring - cost is 5gp per day.

name: Divine Favour
entries: You gain the first two available Tiers of the Divine Favour Feat:
{@b The Tiers of the Divine Favour Feat:}

name: Divine Shield

prerequisite.other: Level 9 or higher, Divine Smite class feature

entries: When a target other than you that is within 5 feet of you takes damage, you can expend your reaction and a spell slot to reduce that damage equal to {@dice 2d8} for a 1st-level spell slot, plus {@dice ld8} for each spell level higher than 1st, to a maximum of {@dice 6d8}.

name: Djinn Heritage
entries: You manifest more of the magical power of your djinn heritage. You gain the following benefits:

items: You learn the {@spell detect magic} spell and can cast it at will, without expending a spell slot.
You have resistance to lightning and thunder damage.

name: Dogfighter
entries: Your dogfighting instincts guide you in the heat of combat, and grant you the following benefits.

entries.name: Barrel Roll
entries: When your ship is hit by an attack that reduces it to 0 {@variantrule Mega Hit Points|DarkMatter24} while you are the {@variantrule Pilot|DarkMatter24}, you can perform a Barrel Roll as a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to cause that attack to miss. You can only take this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} in a Fighter. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Precision Strike
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls when you take the Targeted Strike action.

entries.name: Ship Feats
entries: Life on a starship is arduous, and those without proper training can find themselves completely unprepared to face the challenges posed by deep space. Even a simple run-in with a spaceshark or a pack of var'zuul grubs can spell disaster for the uninitiated. Ship feats each correspond to a Crew Role aboard a starship and represent training and expertise in that role. Ship roles are detailed in the Ships chapter.

entries.name: Gaining a Ship Feat
entries: The GM can grant you a Ship feat to solidify your chosen role aboard the ship or to award you for excellence in a particular role.

name: Dogged Casting
entries: You are a determined mind when it comes to spell casting. You have advantage on any concentration checks to retain concentration spells that you are required to make.

name: Dogged Persistence
entries: You possess boundless energy and determination. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to gain resistance to all of the triggering damage. After you use this ability, you can't use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

name: Doppel-Blooded
entries: When you use your Flexible Form ability to transform into a creature, you also fully assume the target's appearance, as per the disguise self spell, instead of only vaguely copying its shape. This is not a magical effect, and can't be ended with dispel magic or similar spells. You can only maintain a target's appearance for 10 minutes, after which you revert to a vague copy of the target's form.

name: Doppelganger Telepathy
entries: Whatever the truth of the connection between your race and the monstrous doppelgangers, you have honed a similar talent as them for invading the minds of others. You gain the following benefits:

items: You learn the {@spell detect thoughts} spell and can innately cast it once without expending a spell slot. When cast as an innate spell, it requires no components for you to cast. You regain the ability to innately cast {@spell detect thoughts} when you finish a short or long rest. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is Charisma.

name: Double Artes

prerequisite.other: The Extra Attack feature, The ability to use at least two artes

entries: You gain the following benefits:

items: You can use two {@filter artes|spells|school=AR|subschool=!Grand} during your turn instead of one, but you cannot use the same arte twice and they need to be used on different attacks. The second arte does not scale, it is always casted as if you were level 1.

name: Double Throw
entries: You have developed special techniques to throw several weapons at once, granting you the following benefits:

items: Once on each of your turns when you make a ranged weapon attack using a weapon that has both the Light and Thrown properties, and you don't have disadvantage on the attack roll, you can choose to throw two weapons with a single flick of the wrist. If you do, make a separate attack roll with disadvantage for each weapon. If you had advantage on the original attack, you don't suffer disadvantage on the two attacks made using this feat. These attacks can be against different targets.

name: Dour-Handed
entries: Your blows have become more forceful and your aim steadier, allowing you to do greater harm.

items: You gain a +1 bonus to weapon damage rolls using Strength.

name: Downcaster
entries: Thanks to study or deep introspection, you have achieved a firm grasp on spellcasting fundamentals, granting you the following benefits:

items: If you learn spells, you learn 4 {@filter spells of your choice of 3rd level or lower|spells|level=1;2;3} from your class's spell list, which don't count against your total number of spells known. These spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

You can use your action to divide a spell slot of 5th level or lower into two or more lower-level spell slots whose combined level is equal to or less than the original slot's level. Any spell slot you create with this feat vanishes when you recover spell slots after a short or long rest.

name: Draconblood Decorum
entries: You're able to better utilize your sense of smell, giving you improved impressions of other creatures. Using this information, you know exactly how to manipulate both your allies and your enemies. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) checks against creatures you can smell within 15 feet of you.

You learn the {@spell friends} or {@spell vicious mockery} cantrip. If you choose {@spell friends}, you do not require a material component to cast it. Your spellcasting ability for the chosen spell is the ability increased by this feat.

name: Draconic Elite
entries: Whether as a blessing granted to you at birth, or some dormant part of your heritage, you have dragons blood within you. You gain the following benefits.

items: You learn one {@filter cantrip from the Sorcerer spell list|spells|source=|level=0|class=sorcerer}, Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this cantrip.
Choose one damage type: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison, you have resistance to the chosen damage type.

name: Draconic Fury
entries: You have learned to channel your draconic energy into a damaging breath weapon, granting you the following benefits:

items: When you select this feat, choose one damage type from among acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison, and thunder. When you use your Heartening Breath trait, you can choose to expel a 30-foot cone of destructive energy instead. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus), taking {@damage 1d12} damage of the type you chose on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. This damage increases by 1d12 when you reach 5th level ({@damage 2d12}), 11th level ({@damage 3d12}), and 17th level ({@damage 4d12}).

name: Draconic Heritage
entries: You are blessed by Bahamut or Tiamat, granting you another fragment of what makes a true dragon. You can take this feat up to three times.

items: The damage of your Breath Weapon trait increases by {@dice 1d6}.

When you take this feat you gain a trait of one of the other dragonborn subraces which you didn't choose. You can take this feat up to three times, but each time you must choose a dragonborn subrace whose trait you don't have yet. You gain the following trait based on your choice:

rows: You gain the Draconic Fear trait.
You gain the Tail Lash trait.
You gain the Hardened Scales trait.

entries.name: Playing as a Half Dragon with wings
entries: Some half dragons are blessed by the dragon gods and may choose the Draconic Heritage feat from the dragonborn as their feat once, to gain the Wings trait of the Wayfarer subrace. This grants them draconic wings.
{@b NOTE:} This is a powerful feat when given to a half dragon, so you can only take this feat once and with your DM's permission, and you must choose the Wings trait of the Wayfarer subrace.

name: Draconic Heritage (Half Dragon)
entries: You are a half dragon blessed by Bahamut, Tiamat, or another dragon god, granting you draconic wings.

items: Increase your Strength, Constitution, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
The damage of your Breath Weapon racial trait increases by 1d6.
You gain the Wings trait of the dragonborn (page 7).

name: Draconic Heritage
entries: You are blessed by Bahamut, Tiamat, or another dragon god, granting you another fragment of what makes a true dragon.
You can take this feat up to three times.

items: Increase your Strength, Constitution, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
The damage of your Breath Weapon racial trait increases by 1d6.
When you take this feat you gain a trait of one of the other dragonborn subraces of your choice, but you must choose a dragonborn subrace whose trait you don't have yet.

entries: You gain the following trait based on your choice:

entries.caption: Draconic Heritage Traits
rows: You gain the Draconic Fear trait
You gain the Tail Lash trait.
You gain the Hardened Scales trait.

name: Draconic Rune Casting
entries: You have unlocked the basic tenants of {@variantrule draconic rune casting|ToH} (see the Magic and Spells chapter). You gain the following benefits:

items: You learn two draconic runes of your choice. These runes can't be master runes.

You learn the master runes up to the highest level of spell you can currently cast. As you grow in power and increase in level, you automatically learn the master runes for each spell level you can cast.

You can inscribe draconic runes you know on objects and empower those runes with your magic when you finish a {@quickref resting|phb|2|0|long rest}. You can have a number of empowered runes at one time equal to 1 + your proficiency bonus. You can use empowered runes to replicate spells, as described in the Magic and Spells chapter.
You can magically mark an inscribed rune to use as a spellcasting focus for your spells.

name: Dragon Breath Art
entries: You master the art of gathering elemental power within yourself to unleash in blasts akin to a dragon's breath. You gain the following benefits:

items: {@b Ability Score Bonus.} Increase your Constitution, or Charisma ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
{@b Familiarity.} You gain advantage on saving throws against the breath weapons of dragons.

entries.name: Dragon Breath
entries: {@italic Active Ability (Attack, Supernatural)}

As an attack as part of the attack action, you can unleash a cone of elemental devastation. Creatures in a 15 foot cone or 5 by 30 foot line (your choice) must make a Dexterity (for acid, fire or lightning) or Constitution (for cold or poison) saving throw. On failure, they take {@damage 3d6} acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison damage (select when you take this feat), or half as much on a successful one. The number of d6 increases when your proficiency bonus increases (to {@damage 4d6} at 5th level, {@damage 5d6} at 9th level, {@damage 6d6} at 13th level, and {@damage 7d6} at 17th level).
If you are transformed by the Dragon Aspect of the Dragon Form feat, the area of effect is doubled (to a 30 foot cone or 60 foot line).
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

name: Dragon Discharge
entries: You have gained higher control of your elemental core. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your are able to control your breath in short bursts, which you can use as a ranged natural weapon. This weapon has a range of 30 feet, uses your Constitution or Charisma modifier (your choice) for it's attack and damage rolls, and deals {@dice 2d6} damage, the damage type determined by your ancestry.
You can use your Charisma modifier instead of Constitution when calculating the DC for your Breath Weapon racial trait.

name: Dragon Form
entries: You have been blessed by Bahamut or Tiamat, granting you a lesser dragon form of your Draconic Ancestry's chosen dragon.

While all half dragons aspire to assume their rightful true dragon form, only those with enough experience may be blessed with a lesser dragon form. This form varies in appearance, but it always looks similar to the half dragon's draconic ancestry. Sometimes it has wings like a wyvern, giving it four limbs instead of the true dragon's six, including wings. Other times, the dragon form looks like that of a smaller-scale dragon of their ancestor's type.

Regardless, the form drains those who use it, and as such, they are only able to stay in it for a limited time. Afterwards, these half dragons require rest in order to regain access to this form. Despite its power and majesty, the dragon form pales in comparison to the ascension to dragonhood. And this gift only makes them strive harder to achieve their true and ultimate form.

items: You gain {@sense blindsight} out to a range of 10 feet.

You can use your bonus action to change into a large sized form of your ancestral dragon. Your transformation lasts for 1 minute or until you end it as a bonus action. You can regain this form after finishing a long rest. Your weapons merge with you, and the magical bonuses of your equipped melee weapons are transferred to your bite attack. If you are able to attack with your claws, wings, or tail then you can continue to do so. This form doesn't hinder class abilities or spellcasting, nor the use of spell components. In addition, for each minute that you haven't entered combat while in this form, you can extend its duration by 1 minute, up to 10 minutes total.

entries: This dragon form grants you the following benefits:

items: You gain a flying speed of 30 feet.

You gain a bite attack, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with them, you deal piercing damage equal to {@dice 1d8} ({@dice 2d6} if you were wielding a two-handed weapon) + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice). Your bite counts as a finesse weapon. If you originally had a bite attack using higher damage dice then you can use that one instead.
You gain the effects of the Enlarge option of the {@spell enlarge/reduce} spell.

Your breath weapon immediately recharges after you change into your dragon form. Whenever you use your breath weapon during your Dragon Form, you can empower it with one of the three empower options of the Improved Breath Weapon feat without expending an empower point. The rules of the feat remain the same.

Once per turn, you can deal bonus damage (of your chosen damage type) equal to half your level to a single target you've damaged that turn. This only applies to those you've damaged with your bite attack, breath weapon, or spells.

You gain temporary hit points equal to twice your level. Your AC and other defensive boons remain the same (your scaled body parts can be used as your shield). However, your AC cannot be lower than 15 + your Dexterity or Strength modifier (your choice).
If you ascend to dragonhood, then True Dragon Form replaces this Dragon Form. In which case, you can choose a new feat immediately instead of this one.

name: Dragon Form
entries: You have learned to invoke the powers of a dragon. You gain the following features:

items: {@b Ability Score Bonus.} Increase your Strength, Constitution, or Charisma ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
{@b Mystic Language.} You learn draconic. If you already know draconic, you learn one additional language of your choice.
You gain the {@b Dragon Aspect} special transformation ability (below).

entries.name: Dragon Aspect
entries: {@italic Active Ability (Bonus Action, Supernatural)}
As a bonus action, you can physical transform your body, choose number up to your Proficiency bonus of the following draconic features:

items: {@b Fangs.} Gain dragon-like fangs, gaining a natural weapon that deals {@damage 1d8} piercing damage.
{@b Claws.} Transform one or both hands into dragon-like claws, gaining natural weapons that deal {@damage 1d6} slashing damage and have the Light property.

{@b Scales.} Gain dragon-like scales. When you aren't wearing armor, your base AC is 13 + Dexterity modifier. You can use your natural armor to determine your AC if the armor you wear would leave you with a lower AC. A shield's benefits apply as normal while you use your natural armor. You gain resistance to acid, cold, fire, lightning or poison damage (selected when you take the feat).
{@b Wings (Requires 9th level).} If you are not wearing armor, dragon-like wings sprout from your back. Until the transformation ends, you have a 30 foot flying speed.
{@b Eyes.} You gain a {@sense darkvision} of 60 feet. If you already have a darkvision, you gain a {@sense blindsight} of 15 feet.

{@b Elemental Damage.} A weapon you are holding or natural weapon of your choice is wreathed in elemental power, changing its damage type to that element. The first time you hit a creature with that weapon on your turn, you deal damage an additional {@damage 1d4} damage of that elemental type.

entries: The transformation lasts 1 minute or until you end it early as a bonus action. If they don't otherwise have a bonus to attack and damage rolls, natural weapons granted by this transformation gain a bonus to attack and damage rolls equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down). Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

name: Dragon Form
entries: As you strive to ascend to dragonhood, you have gained a lesser dragon form of your Draconic Ancestry's dragon.

While all half dragons aspire to assume their rightful true dragon form, only those truly dedicated to this goal will be blessed with a lesser dragon form. This form varies in appearance, but it always looks similar to the half dragon's draconic ancestry. Sometimes it has wings like a wyvern, with four limbs instead of the true dragon's six, including wings. Other times, the dragon form looks like a smaller or more humanoid version of their dragon ancestor.

Regardless, the form drains those who use it, and as such, they are only able to stay in this form for a limited time. Afterwards, these half dragons require rest in order to regain access to this form. Despite its power and majesty, the dragon form pales in comparison to the ascension to dragonhood, and this gift only makes them strive harder to achieve their true and ultimate form.

items: You gain blindsight out to a range of 10 feet.

As a bonus action, you can change into a draconic form based on your ancestral dragon. You can stay transformed for up to 10 minutes, with each use reducing the duration by a minimum of 1 minute. You can transform back early as a bonus action. Each round spent transformed in combat reduces the duration by 1 minute. You can regain the full duration of this form after finishing a long rest. Your weapons merge with you, and the magical bonuses of your equipped melee weapons are transferred to your bite attack. If you are able to attack with your claws, wings, or tail then you can continue to do so. This form doesn't hinder class abilities or spellcasting, nor the use of spell components.

entries: {@b This transformation grants you the following benefits:}

items: You gain a flying speed of 30 feet

You gain a bite attack, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with them, you deal piercing damage equal to 1d8 (2d6 if you were wielding a two-handed weapon) + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice). Your bite counts as a finesse weapon. If you originally had a bite attack that uses higher damage dice, then you can use those damage dice instead.
You gain the effects of the Enlarge option from the {@spell enlarge/reduce|PHB} spell.

Your Breath Weapon trait immediately recharges after you change into your Dragon Form. When you use your breath weapon during your Dragon Form, you can empower it with one of the three empower options of the {@feat Improved Breath Weapon|LEGDRAG} feat without expending an empower point. The rules of the feat remain the same.

Once per turn, you can deal bonus damage (of your chosen dragon's damage type) equal to your level to a single target you have damaged that turn. This only applies to those you've damaged with your bite attack, breath weapon, or spells.

You gain temporary hit points equal to twice your level. Your AC and other defensive boons remain the same (your scaled body parts can be used as your shield). However, your AC cannot be lower than 15 + your Dexterity modifier.

entries: If you ascend to dragonhood, then your True Dragon Form replaces this Dragon Form. In which case, you must immediately choose a new feat instead of this one.

name: Dragon Guillotine Dervish
