If you roll a misfire on an attack with a firearm, you can use your reaction to roll a {@dice d20}. If the number rolled is higher than the weapon's misfire score, the firearm does not misfire. You cannot use this feature of this feat again until you complete a short or long rest.
When you use the {@action Attack} action and attack with a one-handed weapon, you can use a bonus action to attack with a loaded firearm with the {@itemProperty L||light} property you are holding.

name: Firearms Expert
entries: Thanks to substantial practice with firearms, you gain the following benefits:

items: You ignore the loading quality of {@filter firearms|items|type=firearm} with which you are proficient.
Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls.

When you use the {@action Attack} action and attack with a {@filter one-handed weapon|items|type=Melee Weapon|property=!Two-handed}, you can use a bonus action to attack with a loaded {@item pistol} you are holding.

name: Firearms Expert
entries: Thanks to substantial practice with firearms, you gain the following benefits:

items: You ignore the loading quality of {@filter firearms|items|type=firearm} with which you are proficient.
Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls.

When you use the {@action Attack} action and attack with a {@filter one-handed weapon|items|type=Melee Weapon|property=!Two-handed}, you can use a bonus action to attack with a loaded {@item pistol} you are holding.

name: Firearms Expert
entries: Having practiced extensively with firearms of various sorts, you gain the following benefits:

items: You are proficient with all firearms and with tinker's tools.
Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls with any firearm.
Double the number of ammunition pieces you can normally load into a single firearm with each action or bonus action, up to the weapon's capacity.

name: Firearms Master
entries: You have practiced extensively with one or more firearms, and mastered the use of smokepowder in these weapons, gaining the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with the {@item pistol} and {@item musket}.

name: Firearms Master
entries: You have practiced extensively with one or more firearms, and mastered the use of smokepowder in these weapons, gaining the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with the {@item pistol} and {@item musket}.

name: Firebrand
entries: Born, imbued with, or later marked by the powers of Elemental Fire, these near-humans have an affinity for fire magic. Their heritage makes them dangerous adversaries in combat, as does the volatile nature of their innate powers. Firebrands are human in shape, but have deep red skin and flames behind their eyes. You have the following racial traits:

entries.name: Fire Resistance
entries: You have resistance to fire damage.

entries.name: Flame Magic
entries: You know the {@spell produce flame} cantrip. Starting at 3rd level, you can cast the {@spell burning hands} spell with this trait. Starting at 5th level, you can also cast the {@spell flaming sphere} spell with this trait, without requiring a material component. Once you cast {@spell burning hands} or flaming sphere with this trait, you can't cast that spell with it again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast either of those spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells when you cast them with this trait (choose when you select this race).

name: Firm Contractor
entries: As a licensed Contractor, you know that while the pen is mightier than the sword, the dagger is stronger still. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with one of the following skills of your choice: Data, {@skill Deception}, {@skill Intimidation}, or {@skill Stealth}.
On the first round of combat, you have advantage on melee weapon attacks you make against any creature in combat that is surprised.

name: First Strike
entries: You excel at leading ambushes and acting first in a fight. You have advantage on initiative rolls and gain a 10 ft bonus to movement speed on your first turn. If you take the Attack action on that turn, you can make one additional weapon attack as part of that action. If that attack hits, the target takes an extra 1d8 damage of the weapon's damage type.

name: Fisher
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Survivalist
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Survival} skill.

entries.name: Boat Familiarity
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule d20 Test|XPHB|d20 Tests} made to operate water vehicles.

entries.name: Fishing Prowess
entries: When you are exploring and have access to a body of water, you can spend 1 hour to fish and obtain enough food for up to 6 people for 1 day.

name: Five Finger Discount*
entries: You've always been a slippery little Goblin. It's just what your people do, right? You gain the following benefits:

items: You become proficient in Sleight of Hand. If you are already proficient, you gain expertise.
You have advantage on Dexterity (sleight of hand) checks to pickpocket others.

name: Fjord Jumper
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Cliff Leaping
entries: Your jumping distance (whether {@variantrule High Jump|XPHB|High} or {@variantrule Long Jump|XPHB|Long}) increases by 10 feet. You also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any attack roll, Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check, or Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check you make after jumping at least 10 feet high or 20 feet long.

entries.name: Safe Diving
entries: If you fall into a liquid, such as water, and you spend your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and succeed on a {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check, you take no damage from the fall. You also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on that check.

name: Flail Expert
entries: Your mastery with a flail allows you to use the challenging weapon with deadly skill. You gain the following benefits while wielding a flail:

entries.name: Dangerous Swings
entries: When you miss a melee weapon attack made with a flail, you can make a new attack roll against another creature you of your choice within the weapon's range. You cannot attack the same creature twice this way.

entries.name: Wind Up
entries: As a bonus action, you can whirl the flail building momentum. The next attack you make with it before the end of your turns an additional {@damage 1d8} damage on hit.

name: Flames of Phlegethos*
entries: You learn to call upon hellfire to serve your commands. You gain the following benefits:

items: When you roll a spell that casts fire damage, you can reroll any damage roll that comes out as a 1, but you must use the second roll even if it is another 1.

Whenever you cast a spell that causes fire damage, you can cause flames to wreathe you until the end of your next turn. These flames do not harm you or your possessions. You will shed bright light out to 30 ft and sim light for an additional 30 ft. While the flames are present, any creature within 5ft of you that hits you with a melee attack takes 1d4 fire damage.

name: Flamewoken
entries: Living in the Scorched Grove or other areas touched by elemental fire can sometimes cause strange abilities to manifest among their inhabitants. Known as "flamewoken" by the Tenders, these gifted few have the ability to communicate with fire-aspected creatures and have power over flames. Tenders guide the flamewoken in honing their talents in service of nature and many flamewoken choose to join the order. However, those outside the order usually keep their abilities hidden, as such powers are often seen as a curse. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can speak, read, and write {@language Primordial||Ignan}.
You learn the {@spell produce flame} cantrip. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

As a bonus action, you can strengthen the power of your flames. The next time you deal fire damage to one or more creatures before the end of your next turn, you can deal an additional {@damage 2d10} fire damage to one of those creatures. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

You can whisper magical words in {@language Primordial||Ignan} toward any nonmagical flames you can see within 30 feet of you that could fit within a 5-foot cube. As a bonus action, you can cause these flames to either grow by 5 feet in a single direction, provided there is fuel of some sort present in the new location, or you can extinguish the flames present in this space.

name: Flaming Fury
entries: By infusing your soul with energy from the Plane of Fire, flames flow through your blood and can ignite when enough of it is spilled.

entries.name: Catch These Hands on Fire
entries: While you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, your melee weapon attacks deal an extra {@damage 1d4} Fire damage on a hit. While you have only 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}, the Fire damage increases to {@damage 1d8}.

entries.name: Blaze of Glory
entries: Your inner flame keeps your body moving even at the point of collapse. If damage would reduce you to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 5 plus the damage taken. On a success, you're reduced to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead. Once you've succeeded on this saving throw, you can't use this benefit again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Flash Recall
entries: You've developed the ability to instantly recall an unprepared spell in moments of sudden necessity. As an action, you can instantly prepare a spell from your available class spell list (or spellbook, if you prepare spells from one) that you did not have prepared. This spell choice must be of a level for which you have spell slots. You then lose preparation of a different spell of your choice of equal or higher spell level.
If you are multiclassed, you can only Flash Recall spells from a class that prepares spells. Once you use this ability, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

name: Flash Recall
entries: You've developed the ability to instantly recall an unprepared spell in moments of sudden necessity.

As a bonus action, you prepare a spell of 1st level or higher from your spellbook (if you're a {@class wizard}) or from your class spell list (if you're not a {@class wizard}). This spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots, and it replaces another spell of an equal or higher level that you had previously prepared.
Once you use this feat to recall a spell, you can't do so again until you complete a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|short or long rest}.

entries.name: Rules Tip: Prepared Spells
entries: The Flash Recall feat requires you to be a spellcaster who prepares spells. This includes classes such as {@class cleric||clerics}, {@class druid||druids}, and {@class paladin||paladins}, who prepare spells each day from their class list, and {@class wizard||wizards}, who prepare spells from a spellbook. Classes such as {@class bard||bards} and {@class sorcerer||sorcerers}, who inherently know their spells rather than preparing them, can't benefit from this feat.

items: Damage you take that is less than two times your Constitution modifier, cannot disrupt your concentration

name: Fledgling Mark of Death
entries: You've developed a dragonmark. The mark has appeared unusually late in life, and you don't have the training or experience most heirs receive after the Test of Siberys. Your dragonmark provides the following benefits:

items: You learn the {@spell spare the dying} cantrip. Charisma is your spell casting ability for this spell.
When you make a Charisma ability check to interact with the dead or undead, you can roll one Intuition die, a {@dice d4}, and add the number rolled to the ability check

name: Fledgling Mark of Detection
entries: You possess the least form of the Dragonmark of Detection. This provides the following features:

items: When you make an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) or Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check, you can roll one Intuition die, a {@dice d4}, and add the number rolled to the ability check.
You can cast the {@spell detect magic} spell, but only as a ritual. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

name: Fledgling Mark of Finding
entries: You possess the least form of the Dragonmark of Finding. This provides the following features:

items: Your mark sharpens your senses and helps you find your prey. When you make a {@skill Perception} or {@skill Survival} ability check, you can roll one Intuition die, a {@dice d4}, and add the number rolled to the ability check.
You can cast locate animals or plants, but only as a ritual. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

name: Fledgling Mark of Handling
entries: You possess the least form of the Dragonmark of Handling. This provides the following features:

items: When you make a Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) or Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) check, you can roll one Intuition die, a {@dice d4}, and add the number rolled to the ability check.
When you cast a spell that affects only beasts, it also affects monstrosities with an Intelligence score of 3 or lower.

name: Fledgling Mark of Healing
entries: You possess the least form of the Dragonmark of Healing. This provides the following features:

items: As an action, you can use your mark to spend one of your Hit Dice to stabilize a dying creature you touch.
When you make a Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) check, you can roll one Intuition die, a {@dice d4}, and add the number rolled to the ability check.

name: Fledgling Mark of Hospitality
entries: You possess the least form of the Dragonmark of Hospitality. This provides the following features:

items: You learn the {@spell prestidigitation} cantrip.

When you make a Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check or an ability check involving {@item brewer's supplies|PHB} or {@item cook's utensils|PHB}, you can roll one Intuition die, a {@dice d4}, and add the number rolled to the ability check.

name: Fledgling Mark of Making
entries: You possess the least form of the Dragonmark of Making. This provides the following features:

items: You learn the {@spell mending} cantrip.
When you make an ability check with {@item artisan's tools|PHB}, you can roll one Intuition die, a {@dice d4}, and add the number rolled to the ability check.

name: Fledgling Mark of Passage
entries: You possess the least form of the Dragonmark of Passage. This provides the following features:

items: When you use the {@action Dash} action, difficult terrain doesn't cost you extra movement on that turn.

When you make a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check or any ability check to operate or maintain a land vehicle, you can roll one Intuition die, a {@dice d4}, and add the number rolled to the ability check.

name: Fledgling Mark of Scribing
entries: You possess the least form of the Dragonmark of Scribing. This provides the following features:

items: You learn the {@spell message} cantrip. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

You are proficient with {@item calligrapher's supplies|PHB} and {@item forgery kit|PHB|forgery kits}. When you make an ability check using either one of these tools, you can roll one Intuition die, a {@dice d4}, and add the number rolled to the ability check.

name: Fledgling Mark of Sentinel
entries: You possess the least form of the Dragonmark of Sentinel. This provides the following features:

items: You can cast the {@spell shield} spell. Once you cast it, you must finish a long rest before you can cast it again using this feat.
When you roll for Initiative or make a Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check to notice a threat, you can roll one Intuition die, a {@dice d4}, and add it to the ability check.

name: Fledgling Mark of Shadow
entries: You possess the least form of the Dragonmark of Shadow. This provides the following features:

items: You learn the {@spell minor illusion} cantrip. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell.
When you make a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) or Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check, you can roll one Intuition die, a {@dice d4}, and add the number rolled to the ability check.

name: Fledgling Mark of Storm
entries: You possess the least form of the Dragonmark of Storm. This provides the following features:

items: You learn the {@spell gust|XGE} cantrip. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

When you make a Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check or any ability check involving operating or maintaining a {@filter water or air vehicle|vehicles|terrain=sea;air}, you can roll one Intuition die, a {@dice d4}, and add the number rolled to the ability check.

name: Fledgling Mark of Warding
entries: You possess the least form of the Dragonmark of Warding. This provides the following features:

items: You learn the {@spell alarm} spell and can cast it as a ritual with this feat. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

When you make a {@skill History}, {@skill Investigation}, or {@item Thieves' Tools|PHB} check involving lock and trap mechanisms, you can roll one Intuition die, a {@dice d4}, and add the number rolled to the ability check.

entries: When hurt you've trained yourself to get out of danger quickly. While below one-quarter of your hit-point maximum (rounded down), you gain the following benefits:

items: Your speed increases by 20 feet
You can take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action as a bonus action

name: Fletcher
entries: You have studied woodcarving and learned the art of fletching, allowing you to use your talents to improve arrows or bolts. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with woodcarver's tools. If you are already proficient with them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.

As an action, you can look at an arrow, bolt, or other projectile, as well as the markings on the ground and area to determine the direction the projectile came from, the rough distance it traveled, and the speed it impacted.

Over the course of any short or long rest, you can temporarily improve a number of arrows, bolts or darts equal to your proficiency modifier. To use this benefit, you must have woodcarver's tools with you and the arrows, bolts, or darts must be within reach. Until your next short or long rest, these missiles gain one of the following effects of your choice:
+1 to attack rolls vs. targets wearing medium or heavy armor, or targets with natural armor.
+1 damage to unarmored targets or those wearing light armor, or targets with natural armor.

name: Flex Caster
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Upcast
entries: When you cast a spell, such as {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB}, that can be cast with a higher-level spell slot, you can expend an additional spell slot to increase the spell's effective level by 1.

entries.name: Downcast
entries: When you cast a spell using a higher-level spell slot, you choose to recycle the excess magical energy instead of improving the spell. The spell is cast at its base level and you regain an expended level 1 spell slot.

name: Flex Caster
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Upcast
entries: When you cast a spell, such as {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB}, that can be cast with a higher-level spell slot for more powerful effects, you can expend any additional spell slot to increase the spell's effective level by 1, to a maximum of level 9.

entries.name: Downcast
entries: When you cast a spell using a higher-level spell slot, you choose to recycle the excess magical energy instead of improving the spell. The spell is cast at its base level and you regain an expended level 1 spell slot.

entries.name: Upcast
entries: When you cast a spell, such as {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB}, that can be cast with a higher-level spell slot for more powerful effects, you can expend any additional spell slot to increase the spell's effective level by 1, to a maximum of level 9.

entries.name: Downcast
entries: When you cast a spell using a higher-level spell slot, you choose to recycle the excess magical energy instead of improving the spell. The spell is cast at its base level and you regain an expended level 1 spell slot.

name: Flexible Fighting

otherSummary.entry: When Gaining the Level 2 Jaegar "Fighting Style" Feature

entries: When you attack with a weapon you are wielding in one hand, you can make an extra attack as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} with a different weapon you are wielding in one hand, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. You can't benefit from this feature if you've used the {@itemMastery Nick|XPHB} Weapon Mastery this turn.
While wielding two weapons, you gain +1 to the damage rolls of both weapons.

name: Flexible Reach
entries: You have trained your body to produce lengthy pseudopods, extending your reach drastically. You can reach out to 10 feet. When you cast a spell that has a range of Touch, your range extends to that distance. Additionally, any melee weapon you use gains the Reach property if it didn't already have it.

name: Floriographer

prerequisite.other: Proficiency in one of the following skills: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, or {@skill Nature}

entries: You have studied the secret language of Floriography. You gain the following benefits:

items: You learn Floriography, the language of flowers. Similar to Druidic and Thieves' Cant, Floriography is a secret language often used to communicate subtle ideas, symbolic meaning, and even basic messages. Floriography is conveyed through the combinations of colors, styles, and even types of flowers in bouquets, floral arrangements, and floral illustrations, often with a gift-giving component.

Your fluency with the subtle messages in floral displays gives you a keen eye for discerning subtle or hidden messages elsewhere. You have advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) and Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) checks to notice and discern hidden messages of a visual nature, such as the runes of a magic trap or the subtle hand signals passing between two individuals.

name: Flower Power*
entries: You have an innate wonderment of the world around you, but these people need to be more careful with fire! You gain the following benefits:

items: You become proficient in the Nature skill. If you are already proficient, you gain Expertise.
When you use your Charcoal or Pleasant Aroma ability, you become resistant to the fire damage of the triggering attack instead of vulnerable.

name: Fluid Structure
entries: Your body is much more elastic, capable of taking less damage when it's needed the most. You can use your reaction when you take bludgeoning damage to gain resistance to bludgeoning damage until the start of your next turn.

name: Flurry
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Quick Strike
entries: Once on each of your turns when you make an attack roll with a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} and have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the roll, you can forgo {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on that attack roll. After resolving that attack, you can then make another attack with the same weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} against a different creature. The new target must be within 5 feet of the first target and within the weapon's reach.

name: Flying Figure
entries: If the creature you are transformed into has a flying speed, you gain that speed. If it has a flying speed that's higher than your movement speed, you only gain that speed equal to your movement speed. To use this speed, you can't be wearing medium or heavy armor.

Additionally, using your Shapechanger trait, you can turn into an aaracokra, harpy or winged tiefling. At DM's discretion, you can transform into other forms of flying creatures of humanoid or monstrosity type.

name: Foco em Magia
entries: Escolha uma escola de magia, como Ilusão. As magias dessa escola do personagem serão mais poderosas que o normal.
{@b Beneficio:} Adicione +2 na Classe de Dificuldade de todos os testes de resistência contra as magias da escola selecionada.
{@b Especial:} O personagem pode adquirir Foco em Magia diversas vezes. Seus efeitos não são cumulativos. Sempre que escolher esse talento, ele se aplica a uma escola de magia diferente.

name: Focused
entries: As a bonus action, you can enter a state of heightened focus which lasts for one minute. While focusing in this manner, whenever you make a Dexterity saving throw or a Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check, you can roll a {@dice d4} and add the number rolled to the saving throw or ability check, as long as you arent blinded. Once you enter this state, you cant do again until you finish a short or long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Focused
entries: As a bonus action, you can enter a state of heightened focus which lasts for one minute. While focusing in this manner, whenever you make a Dexterity saving throw or a Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check, you can roll a {@dice d4} and add the number rolled to the saving throw or ability check, as long as you aren't blinded. Once you enter this state, you cant do again until you finish a short or long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Focused Critical
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Improved Critical
entries: Your attack rolls with weapons and {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} can score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19 or 20 on the {@dice d20}.

name: Focused Critical
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Improved Critical
entries: Your attack rolls with weapons and {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} can score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19 or 20 on the {@dice d20}.

name: Focused Critical
entries: You've honed your combat skills to seize any opening that presents itself. When you choose this feat, select ranged weapon attacks or melee weapon attacks. You score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 with attack rolls of that type.

name: Focused Discipline
entries: Your diligence and focused training has granted you the following benefits:

items: Choose one skill proficiency granted to you by your class. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for ability checks made using that skill.
Choose one saving throw proficiency granted to you by your class. Whenever you make that saving throw, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

entries: If you lose this feat because you do not meet its prerequisite, you gain the Multidisciplinary feat instead.

name: Focused Disguise
entries: Your ability to change your shape is so advanced, it can even thwart some magical means. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on any saving throws against spell or spell effects designed to reveal your true nature, including divination spells.
Once per long rest, if you fail a Wisdom ({@skill Deception}) ability check, you can reroll the check; you must take the new roll.

name: Focused Fighting

otherSummary.entry: When Gaining the Level 2 Jaegar "Fighting Style" Feature

entries: You learn an additional {@filter Adrenaline Art|optionalfeatures|feature type=sgtteh:aa}, and you gain 1 additional Adrenaline Point.

name: Focused Hunter
entries: During hunts, you are capable of bursts of focus when you need them most. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain 1 Focus Point (adding to your existing Focus Points if you already have Focus Points), and learn one new Focus Art, choosing from {@optfeature Weapon Parry|SGttEH}, {@optfeature Dodge Step|SGttEH}, or any of the jaeger's Additional Focus Arts. You regain all expended Focus Points when you finish a short or long rest.

name: Focused Hunter
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Improved Focus
entries: You gain 1 Adrenaline Point (adding to your existing Adrenaline Points if you already have Adrenaline Points), and learn one new Adrenaline Art, choosing from {@optfeature Weapon Parry|SGttEH24}, {@optfeature Dodge Step|SGttEH24}, or any of the Jaeger's Additional {@filter Adrenaline Arts|optionalfeatures|feature type=sgtteh:aa}. You regain all expended Adrenaline Points when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Focused Multitasker
entries: You are able to concentrate on two spells simultaneously. When you do, you suffer the following penalties:

items: You can't cast spells or make weapon attacks.
The minimum DC for Constitution saving throws you make to maintain your {@condition concentration} when you take damage is 15.
At the start of each of your turns in combat, you must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or lose concentration on your choice of one of the two spells.

name: Focused Multitasker*
entries: You can maintain your concentration on two spells or effects that requires concentration, instead of one.

name: Focused Personas
entries: You've developed personas that help you focus your talents. Work with your DM to define two unique personas—identities with distinct appearances and personalities. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

Choose a tool and define a persona associated with it.While you are using your Shapechanging trait to assume the identity of that persona, you are proficient with that tool.If you are already proficient in it, your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make using that tool while assuming that persona.

Choose a skill you're proficient in and define a different persona associated with it. While you are using your Shapechanging trait to assume the identity of that persona, your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make using that skill.

name: Focused Personas
entries: You've developed personas that help you focus your talents. Work with your DM to define two unique personas—identities with distinct appearances and personalities. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Adept Persona
entries: Choose a tool and define a persona associated with it. Whenever you use your Shape-Shifter trait to assume the persona, you gain proficiency with the chosen tool and when you make an ability check with the chosen tool, you can roll {@dice 1d4} and add the number rolled to the ability check.

entries.name: Expert Persona
entries: Choose a skill you are proficient in and define a different persona associated with it. Whenever you use your Shape-Shifter trait to assume the persona, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in the chosen skill.

entries.name: Skin Cant
entries: You are fluent in {@language Skin Cant|ExploringEberron24}, a language used by the Changeling Travelers.

name: Foe Sense
entries: As an action, you can open your awareness to detect for creatures of your favored enemy type. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any creatures of your favored enemy type within 60 feet of you that are not behind total cover. You know the type of any being whose presence you sense, but not its identity. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

Additionally, by spending 1 uninterrupted minute in concentration (as if you were concentrating on a spell), you can sense whether any creatures of your favored enemy type are present within 5 miles of you. This feature reveals which are present, their numbers, and the creatures' general direction and distance (in miles) from you.

name: Following Suit
entries: When you first perform an activity as a demonstration, you have advantage on Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) checks to convince others to do the same.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Following Suit
entries: When you first perform an activity as a demonstration, you have advantage on Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) checks to convince others to do the same.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Font of Life
entries: You become a spring of healing and life, and excel at keeping things alive. Life Blossoms in your step, and death flees in your wake.

items: Every time you cast a healing spell, roll a {@dice d10}.
If you roll a 10, you do not expend the spell slot used to cast the spell.
If you roll a 1, The spell heals for the maximum amount at the level cast, and the spell slot is expended as normal.
Otherwise the spell slot is expended as normal.

Whenever there is an {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} creature (with 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}) within 60 feet of you, you can cast {@spell Healing Word|XPHB} at 1st level without expending a spell slot. You may do this an amount of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (Minimum of Once).
You recover all expended charges after a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
Casting {@spell Healing Word|XPHB} using this feature does not activate a {@dice d10} roll as described above.

name: Forager
entries: You've spent countless hours exploring the island searching for ingredients. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Survival} skill. If you already have this proficiency, you instead gain expertise with that skill, which means your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make using it.
You produce twice the number of common or uncommon ingredients when foraging.

name: Forceful Presence
entries: You can focus your vampiric presence to instill emotions in others. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Awe
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you give yourself {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}, {@skill Performance|XPHB}, and {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) checks for 10 minutes.
You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Daunt
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, make a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) check and choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw with a DC equal to the result of your {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} check. On a failed save, the creature has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} creature's turns, the creature repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature with an Intelligence of 3 or lower automatically succeeds on its saving throw against this effect.
You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Foreign Incantation

prerequisite.other: Linguist, The ability to cast a cantrip or spell

entries: You learn to use the properties of languages as you know to alter your incantations. When you cast a spell that involve a verbal component, you can choose one of the following effects. You can only use effects tied to languages you are proficient with.

entries.name: Abyssal
entries: When you cast a spell that requires concentration, you gain resistance against cold, fire, and lightning damage while you are concentrating on the spell.

entries.name: Celestial
entries: When you cast a spell that restores hit points to a creature other than you, you regain hit points equal to the spell's level + your spellcasting modifier.

entries.name: Deep Speech
entries: If you fail the check to maintain concentration of a spell, each creatures within 5 feet of you takes 1d6 psychic damage for each level of spell slot used to cast the spell.

entries.name: Draconic
entries: When you cast a spell that requires concentration, you gain a number of temporary hit points equal to the spell's level + your spellcasting modifier, which last until you stop concentrating on the spell.

entries.name: Giant
entries: When you cast a spell that involves one or more ranged spell attacks, you can instead turn all of them into melee spell attacks with range of 5 ft.

entries.name: Infernal
entries: When you cast a spell that involves a melee or ranged spell attack that targets a single creature, you can infuse it with hellish energy. On a hit, any healing the target receives until the start of your next turn is reduced by 1d4 for each level of spell slot used to cast the spell.

entries.name: Auran
entries: When you cast a spell that requires concentration, your movement speed increases by 5 feet  for each level of spell slot used to cast the spell while you are concentrating on the spell.

entries.name: Aquan
entries: When you cast a spell that requires concentration, you gain the ability to walk across liquid surfaces while you are concentrating on the spell.

entries.name: Ignan
entries: When you cast a spell that requires concentration, you can shroud yourself with flames. While you maintain concentration on that spell, a creature that touches you or hits you with a melee attack while within 5 feet of you takes fire damage equal to the spell's level + your spellcasting modifier.

entries.name: Terran
entries: When you cast a spell that requires concentration, you can strenthen your connection to the ground. While you maintain concentration on that spell and are standing on earth or stone, you cannot be pushed or knocked prone.

entries.name: Sylvan
entries: When you cast a spell while within 60 feet of a plant, you cast the spell as though you were in the plant's space, using your own senses.

name: Foresight of their Kindred
entries: The Rangers of the North still possess a measure of the foresight that their ancestors possessed in full. In the Twilight of the Third Age, this gift manifests as a sense of watchfulness, and of fear, arising to warn a Ranger of a danger that has not yet come to pass.

items: You have a number of foresight points equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). Whenever you or a creature that you can see make an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw, you can spend one foresight point to reroll the {@dice d20} and must use the new roll. You can choose to spend one of your foresight points after the roll, but before the outcome is determined. You can also spend one foresight point after a roll on the Journey Events table. Roll a {@dice d20}, and then choose whether the Loremaster uses their roll or yours. You regain your expended foresight points when you finish a long rest.

name: Forest Denizen
entries: You are familiar with the ways of the forest. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can discern if a plant or fungal growth is safe to eat.
You learn to speak, read, and write {@language Sylvan}.

You have advantage on Strength ({@skill Athletics}) and Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) checks you make to escape from being {@condition grappled} or {@condition restrained} as long as you are being {@condition grappled} or {@condition restrained} by nonmagical vegetation or a beast's action such as a giant frog's bite or a spider's web.

name: Forest Sage
entries: The Tenders value diversity among ideas, and although they began as a purely druidic order, they have since learned to accept many different ways of thinking about the natural world, especially regarding the application of magic. You are either a {@class wizard} who has learned to temper your arcane research with an eye to maintaining the delicate balance of natural forces, or you are a {@class druid} who has learned a new understanding of natural magic through study and experimentation. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can use your choice of Intelligence or Wisdom to make {@skill Animal Handling}, {@skill Arcana}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Survival} checks.

You can choose to learn two spells from either the druid or wizard spell list. Spells you choose must be of a level you can cast. The chosen spells count as spells of your class and are added to your spellbook if you are a {@class wizard} or your spells known if you are a {@class druid}.

name: Forge Heart
entries: You have achieved mastery of some of your people's sacred crafting skills. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in two of the following tools of your choice: {@item smith's tools|phb}, {@item mason's tools|phb}, {@item glassblower's tools|phb} or {@item jeweler's tools|phb}. If you are already proficient in the chosen tool your proficiency bonus with that tool is doubled.

Whenever you make an Intelligence ({@skill History}) check related to the origin of metal craftsmanship, such as a golden ring or bronze sword, you are considered proficient in the History skill and add double your proficiency bonus to the check instead of your normal proficiency bonus.

name: Forgemaster
entries: Your deftness with your tools of choice is unparalleled.

items: When you make a Manufacturing check with a tool with which you are proficient, you have advantage on the roll.
You gain proficiency with 2 tools of your choice.
Each hour you spend forging an item counts as 3 hours towards the item's completion.

name: Forger
entries: You are a master of creating false identities and documents. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with {@item forgery kit|phb|forgery kits}. If you are already proficient with them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.
If you spend at least 1 hour studying a person's handwriting, you gain advantage on checks made to mimic it.

You can protect yourself with multiple layers of identities and misdirection. When you forge a document, you can leave behind false clues that suggest a different person was the forger; this act doesn't take any extra time. Such false clues could involve blending a mimic of the person's handwriting with the intended one, adding fake prints of the target's fingers to the paper, or adding a secret message that somehow implies this person is the true culprit. When a reader spots that the document is forged, it also discovers these clues. Identifying that these clues are false requires an additional Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check against the same DC used to identify the original forgery.

name: Forger
entries: You are an expert with {@item Forgery Kit|phb|Forgery Kits}.
If you spend at least 1 hour studying a person's handwriting, you gain advantage on checks made to mimic it.

You can protect yourself with multiple layers of identities and misdirection. When you forge a document, you can leave behind false clues that suggest a different person was the forger; this act doesn't take any extra time. Such false clues could involve blending a mimic of the person's handwriting with the intended one, adding fake prints of the target's fingers to the paper, or adding a secret message that somehow implies this person is the true culprit. When a reader spots that the document is forged, it also discovers these clues. Identifying that these clues are false requires an additional Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check against the same DC used to identify the original forgery.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Foritfy
entries: When making temporary modifications to a campsite, battlefield, stronghold, or other area, you can add your proficiency bonus to checks related to construction or improvement of barriers, fortifications, or similar works. These works add your proficiency bonus to their armor class for the duration, and gain a number of temporary hit points equal to your level.
If a restraint or fortification you create has a DC to break it (such as a blocked doorway or tied-up creature), this DC increases by your proficiency bonus as well.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Fortified Undead

prerequisite.other: {@feat Spellbook|Adventurer} (School of Necromancy) or {@feat Acolyte: Grave|Adventurer}, 6th Level

entries: When you take this feat, choose two of the following fortifications, affecting all undead creatures you control:

items: The undead increase their maximum hit points by 5.
The undead gain a +1 bonus to damage rolls.
The undead gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls.

entries: You can choose the same benefit more than once. You can select this feat a second time after 12th level, and a third time after 18th level. Each time you do so you must choose two more fortifications.

name: Fortify
entries: When making temporary modifications to a campsite, battlefield, stronghold, or other area, you can add your proficiency bonus to checks related to construction or improvement of barriers, fortifications, or similar works. These works add your proficiency bonus to their armor class for the duration, and gain a number of temporary hit points equal to your level.
If a restraint or fortification you create has a DC to break it (such as a blocked doorway or tied-up creature), this DC increases by your proficiency bonus as well.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Fortifying Healer
entries: Your healing magic is augmented by the fortifying magic of resolute bravery. If you target one or more allies with a spell that allows them to regain hit points, those allies are immune to being frightened for a number of rounds = the level of the healing spell. In addition, one ally who healed hit points (your choice) gains inspiration. You must complete a short or long rest before you can grant inspiration again.

name: Fortifying Treatment
entries: During a short rest, choose one willing creature you can touch. For this short rest, when it rolls a hit die to regain hit points it regains the maximum value on the die instead of rolling. You must expend a use of your healer's hit for each die that is maximized.

In addition, at the end of a long rest, you can choose any number of creatures and expend 1 use from your {@item healer's kit|PHB} for each of them. For the next 24 hours, each creature must fail an additional death save in order to die. A creature can only gain this benefit once per long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Fortifying Treatment
entries: During a short rest, choose one willing creature you can touch. For this short rest, when it rolls a hit die to regain hit points it regains the maximum value on the die instead of rolling. You must expend a use of your healer's hit for each die that is maximized.

In addition, at the end of a long rest, you can choose any number of creatures and expend 1 use from your {@item healer's kit|PHB} for each of them. For the next 24 hours, each creature must fail an additional death save in order to die. A creature can only gain this benefit once per long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Fortune of the Thaumaturge
entries: Your connection to the Thaumaturge puts you in touch with forces outside mortal understanding, making others think you were born under a fortunate moon. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Fortune's Fortitude
entries: When you fail a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can expend and roll one {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die}, adding that number to your result. You can do this only once per {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}.
You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all uses of this ability when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Fortune of the Unknown
entries: When using the Fortune's Fortitude benefit, if you roll the highest or lowest number on the {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die}, you regain that {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die}. It still counts as a use of Fortune's Fortitude.

name: Four Arms
entries: You add two additional arms to your frame, for a total of four. At any one time, you can hold up to four one-handed objects, a pair of two-handed objects, or a twohanded object and two one-handed objects. Also, the weight you can carry is doubled, and you gain a climbing speed of 30 feet.

You are able to use your Them Bones trait if at least two of your hands are unoccupied, and using Them Bones occupies two of your hands. If all of your hands are unoccupied, you can use Them Bones for two different purposes at the same time, though doing so occupies all your hands.
Having four arms does not grant you any additional attacks, and your attacks and actions are unchanged except as listed here.

name: Fragment of Bakuryō
entries: A fragment of the koi dragon kaiju Bakuryō churns within you, granting you the following benefits:

items: You gain 2 Rampage Points.

As an action, or in place of one attack when you take the Attack action, you can expend 2 Rampage Points to conjure a roiling vortex of divine water. Choose one Huge or smaller creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw or become entrained in the vortex for 1 minute. A creature can choose to fail this saving throw. While entrained, the creature is lifted 30 feet above the surface on which it was stood (if any), has resistance to all damage except cold, force, and lightning damage, is {@condition restrained}, and can't breathe or speak. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a success, it escapes the vortex, falls to the ground if nothing else is holding is aloft, and the vortex disappears. You can end the vortex as a bonus action, choosing whether to drop the entrained creature or gently place it down.

name: Fragment of Iminada
entries: A fragment of the Undead kaiju Iminada roils within you, granting you the following benefits:

items: You gain 2 Rampage Points.

As a bonus action, you can expend 2 Rampage Points to magically teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet of yourself. Alternatively, you use an action and expend 2 Rampage Points to attempt to magically teleport one creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself. That creature must succeed on a Charisma saving throw (it can choose to fail) or be teleported to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of you. You can target one additional creature with this action for every 2 additional Rampage Points you expend.

name: Fragment of Magatsuchi
entries: A fragment of the Plant kaiju Magatsuchi blooms within you, granting you the following benefits:

items: You gain 2 Rampage Points.

As an action, or in place of one attack when you take the Attack action, you can expend 2 Rampage Points to unleash a torrent of amber-tipped leaves in a 20-foot cone originating from you. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 4d6} piercing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

name: Fragment of Nomi
entries: A fragment of the kabuto kaiju Nomi buzzes within you, granting you the following benefits:

items: You gain 2 Rampage Points.

Using the Attack action, you can expend 2 Rampage Points to throw one creature you are grappling up to 30 feet in any direction. If you're able to make multiple attacks with the Attack action, this throw replaces one of them. If the creature collides with an obstacle that prevents it from moving the full distance, it takes {@damage 3d6} bludgeoning damage before falling down.

name: Fragment of Raiko
entries: A fragment of the Elemental kaiju Raiko crackles within you, granting you the following benefits:

items: You gain 2 Rampage Points.

As an action, you can expend 1 Rampage Point to detonate a chaotic, magical burst of electricity. Each creature within 30 feet of you (including you) must make a Dexterity saving throw as bolts of lightning spiral through the air. The creature with the lowest result takes a number of d10s of lightning damage equal to your proficiency bonus. When you use this benefit, you can expend additional Rampage Points to grant a number of creatures of your choice advantage on the saving throw equal to the number of additional Rampage Points you expend.

name: Fraudulento
entries: O personagem sabe como encobrir a verdade.
{@b Beneficio:} Seu personagem tem vantagem em todos os testes de Disfarces e Falsificação.

name: Free Stride
entries: Your quick stride lets you carefully pick a path through rough terrain. Your speed increases by 10 ft. When you take the {@action Dash} action, difficult terrain costs you no extra movement this turn.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Free Stride
entries: Your quick stride lets you carefully pick a path through rough terrain. Your speed increases by 10 ft. When you take the {@action Dash} action, difficult terrain costs you no extra movement this turn.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Free Sword Mercenary's Will
entries: Your training with the Company of Free Swords has given you an increased stamina and an attitude that make you less likely to succumb to hardships. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Hold the Ground
entries: When you are moved without using your movement by a creature, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce the distance you are moved by up to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Resolute
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws that would apply a condition.

name: Freediver
entries: You have undergone extensive underwater training. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a swimming speed equal to twice your Constitution score (rounded up to the nearest 5 feet). If you already have a swimming speed, it instead increases by 10 feet.
You triple your Constitution modifier when calculating how long you can hold your breath.
You gain resistance to cold damage.

name: Freeruning
entries: When you take the {@action Dash} action, if you are wearing light or no armor, you can run on vertical surfaces, along the edges of thin barriers, or hop from one outcropping to another as if you were travelling along normal terrain. If you stop moving while running across a wall, you begin to fall.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Freerunning
entries: When you take the {@action Dash} action, if you are wearing light or no armor, you can run on vertical surfaces, along the edges of thin barriers, or hop from one outcropping to another as if you were traveling along normal terrain. If you stop moving while running across a wall, you begin to fall.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Frenzied Fighting
entries: You are adept at the frantic combination of barking, scratching, biting and general chaos that typifies some dogs when they are enraged. Once per long rest, you may cause each creature in a 15-foot cube originating from you to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 2d8 damage and is pushed 10 feet away from you. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn't pushed.

name: Frenzy Fever
entries: Research once again goes a step too far with the invention of a medicine that will give you the frenzy virus.

items: You are infected with a mutated version of the {@condition frenzy virus|MHMM}. You gain all the effects of the frenzy virus sentient race template on page 80 of the Monster Hunter Monster Manual except for the impaired healing effect. You can still heal from nonmagical means.

At your DM's discretion, whenever you hit a creature with your natural weapon attacks (claws or bite mainly), they can have the creature make a Constitution saving throw equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier. On a failed save the creature is infected with the frenzy virus (See page 80 of the Monster Hunter Monster Manual). On a successful save, the target is immune to your mutated version of the frenzy virus, forever.

entries: {@b Creator's Note}
Dungeon Masters, don't allow your players to intentionally infect other players' characters. This could be a great story and mechanical feat, but could potentially ruin a campaign if you let it.

name: Friend of the Forest
entries: After spending some time in forests, you have attuned yourself to the ways of the woods and the creatures in it. You learn the {@spell treeheal|ToH} (see the Magic and Spells chapter) cantrip and two other {@filter druid cantrips|spells|source=|level=0|class=druid} of your choice. You also learn the {@spell speak with animals} spell and can cast it once without expending a spell slot. Once you cast it, you must finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|short or long rest} before you can cast it in this way again. Your spellcasting ability for these spells is Wisdom.

name: Friend of the Winds
entries: Friend of the Winds

items: Your connection to the Elemental Plane of Air allows you to pull a guardian from it, to defend you in your time of need ().
You can use an action and begin concentrating as if on a spell to conjure an air guardian (the statistics for which are included here) at a point you can see with 30 feet of you.

This guardian is friendly to you and your companions, acts on its own turn in initiative order, adds half your total character level to its hit point maximum, adds your proficiency bonus 3 on its attack and damage rolls, and obeys any verbal commands you give it.
This guardian disappears after one minute, if you lose concentration, or if it reaches 0 hit points.
You can conjure this guardian twice, and regain all expended uses of this ability when you finish a long rest.

name: Friendly and Familiar
entries: Since you started your adventures, you have realised that your folk's custom of trading with foreigners may help you in your endeavours. Your nice manners and friendly demeanour easily gain the sympathies of those you meet, and your ability to inquire about the doings of strangers without letting curiosity get the better of you provides you with many opportunities to learn from those you meet along the way.

items: Increase the Fellowship rating of your Company by 1.

Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check you make. In addition, you have advantage on the first Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check you make when interacting with Dwarves, Elves, Hobbits, and Men (other than the Dúnedain).

name: Frighting Power
entries: When you deal critical damage to a creature, you impose disadvantage on the next saving throw that creature makes against being {@condition frightened} within 1 minute.

If the creature is immune to the {@condition frightened} condition, that immunity is ignored and the creature makes its next saving throw against being {@condition frightened} with advantage within 1 minute. If the creature fails that saving throw, it continues making its saves against being {@condition frightened} with advantage until the condition ends.

name: Frost Acclimation
entries: Your body has gotten used to the harsh cold, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain resistance to cold damage
You ignore difficult terrain caused by the cold

name: Frost Breath
entries: Your Dragon breath has been altered by the north, you gain the following benefits:

items: Your dragon breath now can inflict cold damage in a 15 foot cone in front of you, instead of your regular dragon breath damage.

When you use your dragon breath a creature takes 2d6 damage + your Proficiency bonus on a failed save, and half as much damage on a successful one. The damage increases to 3d6 at 5th level, 4d6 at 8th level, 5d6 at 11th level, and 6d6 at 17th level.
You can use your dragon breath twice between rest.

name: Frost Eyed
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Bright Eyed
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks in {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB}, and you do not have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks in {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB}.

entries.name: Ice Tracker
entries: You are proficient in the {@skill Survival} skill. You treat both snow and icy terrain as normal terrain. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@skill Survival} checks made in snow or ice.

name: Frost-Touched
entries: Your connection to the ancient frozen power of the Northlands grants you the following benefits.

entries.name: Frost Magic
entries: You know your choice of the {@spell Frostbite|XPHB} or {@spell Ray of Frost|XPHB} cantrip. Choose one level 1 spell that deals Cold damage from the Druid, Sorcerer, or Wizard spell lists. You always have that spell and the {@spell Gust of Wind|XPHB} spell prepared. You can cast each of these spells without expending a spell slot. Once you cast either spell in this manner, you can't cast that spell again until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast these spells using spell slots you have of the appropriate level. The spells' spellcasting ability is the ability increased by this feat.

prerequisite.other: You must be able to use at least one engineer gadget schematic

items: When you roll a 1 on a damage die for a gadget you control, you may reroll that die. You must use the result of the new roll.

When you use a gadget that effects an area, you can shield some creatures in the area from being affected by the gadget. Choose a number of creatures equal to your Intelligence modifier minus 2 (minimum of 1 creature). The creatures that you chose are unaffected by the gadget.

name: Galactic Bank: Trustee
entries: Your privileged association with the Galactic Bank has earned you the honorary title of "Trustee" and a Platinum Member bank account, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Line of Credit
entries: You can spend Credits you don't have via a line of credit to the Galactic Bank. The amount you can spend using your line of credit starts at 1,000 CR and increases when you reach character levels 5 (10,000 CR), 11 (50,000 CR), and 17 (100,000 CR). For every ten days that elapse without paying back the amount you owe, the total amount increases by 100 CR.

entries.name: Platinum Member Discounts
entries: Whenever you buy an item worth 100 CR or less, you receive a 20 percent discount on it.

entries.name: Faction Feats
entries: Veteran adventurers are likely to make enemies across the 'Verse, but if they're lucky, they might forge some alliances too. The greatest of these alliances are likely to be with factions, which provide work, services, and connections to spacers everywhere. Factions in Dark Matter are detailed in Chapter 1: The 'Verse.

Of course, such allies don't come free. Factions generally also require work and commitment from their members, which might come in the form of small tasks, important favors for higher ranking members, or even regular obligations for the organization. For their efforts, adventurers gain specific and useful skills from their factions, as represented by Faction feats.

entries.name: Gaining a Faction Feat
entries: The GM can award you a Faction feat for joining a faction or completing a quest for one. If allegiance to a faction is important to your backstory, the GM can also replace the feat granted by your background with an appropriate Faction feat.

items: You gain proficiency with one gaming set of your choice, or you choose a {@item gaming set|phb} with which you already have proficiency and double your proficiency bonus for each ability check you make with it.

Whenever you win a game with a {@item gaming set|phb} with which you are proficient, you have advantage on all Wisdom ({@skill insight}) and Charisma ({@skill deception}) checks you make against the creatures you beat for the next hour.

During a short or long rest, you may try to rally others' spirits by playing a short game with them. A number of creatures equal to your proficiency bonus including you roll {@dice 1d4} on the gambler's table, and gain the characteristics described until they next finish a short or long rest.

items.caption: Gambler's Table
rows: You subtract {@dice 1d4} from the next saving throw you make.
Your movement speed increases by 5 feet.

Whenever you fail an ability check or saving throw, you may roll {@dice 1d6} and add it to the result, potentially transforming it into a success. If you transform the roll into a success, you may not use this feature again.

name: Gambler
entries: Always keen for probabilities and risk, you often trust your safety and fortune to the hands of fate. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in all gaming sets and have advantage on ability checks you make for games of chance.

Once on each of your turns, before you roll damage, you can place stakes on the roll. Choose less than the average, or higher than or equal to the average. If you choose correctly, you can add one additional die of damage to the roll. If you choose incorrectly, you must remove the damage die with the highest number.

name: Gambler
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Gaming Sets
entries: You gain proficiency with all Gaming Sets and have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks you make for games of chance.

entries.name: Losing Streak
entries: Record whenever you roll a 9 or lower on the {@dice d20} for a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}. Roll the d20s for {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} and {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} sequentially and record them in order. If you roll 9 or lower three or more times consecutively, you can immediately change the {@dice d20} roll to a 20. If this was an attack roll, it doesn't score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}. Once you use this feat to change a {@dice d20} roll, discard your recorded rolls.

name: Gambler
entries: Your itch for high-stakes speculation grants you the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in three types of gaming sets of your choice.

When you roll initiative, you can choose a number between 2 and 19 as your lucky number. Once per combat when you make an attack roll and the roll on the d20 equals your lucky number, you can cash it in, turning the roll into a critical hit. Add the ability modifier of the score increased by this feat to the damage of the attack. If initiative ends and your lucky number did not appear, you take psychic damage equal to your level, and you cannot choose that number again until you finish long rest.

name: Gambler
entries: Spending countless hours winning and losing coin in alestained taverns has forged you into a consummate gambler and chance-seeking addict. You gain the following benefits and features:

items: You gain proficiency with two types of {@filter gaming sets|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=gaming set} of your choice.
You have advantage on Charisma ({@skill Deception}) checks to bluff opponents in games of chance, and Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) checks to convince others to join you for a game.
You have a reputation as a card shark in some circles. Some folks may avoid playing you for this reason, while other higher-stakes gamblers may seek you out specifically.
When you take the Carousing downtime action, you may reroll your result once, but must keep the results of the second roll.

name: Gambler
entries: Always keen for probabilities and risk, you often trust your safety and fortune to the hands of fate. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in all {@item gaming set|PHB|gaming sets} and have advantage on ability checks you make for games of chance.

Once on each of your turns, before you roll damage, you can place stakes on the roll. Choose less than the average, or higher than or equal to the average. If you choose correctly, you can add one extra die of damage to the roll. If you choose incorrectly, you must remove the damage die with the highest number.

name: Gash
entries: When you score a critical hit that deals slashing damage to a creature, you grievously wound it. Until the start of your next turn, the target has disadvantage on all attack rolls.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Gatekeeper Initiate
entries: You have learned a certain number of secrets and techniques of the Gatekeeper druidic order. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Gatekeeper Proficiency
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Arcana|XPHB} skill.

entries.name: Protection Against Aberrations
entries: When you make a saving throw against the magic abilities of an Aberration or a spell cast by an Aberration, you can roll {@dice 1d4} and add it to your saving throw.

entries.name: Gatekeeper Spells
entries: The secrets you've learned allow you to always have certain spells at the ready. When you have spell slots of a level specified in the Gatekeeper Spells table, you thereafter have the spells listed for that level and lower prepared.

name: Geneseed
entries: You unlock an uncanny understanding of your people's influence on modern evolution, which grants you the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in your choice of Alchemist's Supplies, Medicine, or Animal Handling.

You learn the {@spell command} spell, and can cast it an unlimited number of times with this trait. You can only target aberrations, beasts, or plants with this spell, and the target must have a challenge rating equal to or lower than half your level. When you cast command with this feature, you and the target do not need to share a language. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

name: Genius
entries: Every successful starship needs at least one person with uncanny knowledge about most things. As one of those people, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in four of the following skills: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill Data|DarkMatter}, {@skill History}, {@skill Nature}, {@skill Religion}, or {@skill Technology|DarkMatter}.
You can reroll an Intelligence check. If you do so, you must use the new roll, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Geomancer
entries: You specialize in the magic of the earth, commanding earthen arms and armor and beckoning quakes from the ground beneath you. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have {@variantrule spell prowess|TEB} with {@book geomancy spells|TEB|2|Geomancy Spells}
The spells {@spell bones of the earth|XGE},* {@spell mold earth|XGE},* {@spell shield of faith}, and {@spell stone shape} are added to the spell list of your spellcasting class.

Whenever you cast a geomancy spelL you gain a +1 bonus to AC and temporary hit points equal to half of your proficiency bonus, both of which last until the end of your next turn or until you roll initiative.
Whenever you make a saving throw to maintain concentration on a geomancy spell, you roll {@dice 1d4} and add it to the result.

name: Ghostlight Medium
entries: You formed a mystical connection to the Ghostlight Express that affords you insight into the nature of spirits, granting the following benefits.

entries.name: Ghostly Touch
entries: When you damage a creature with the Incorporeal Movement trait, you can ignore the creature's damage {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}, if any.

entries.name: Spirit Sense
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can sense any Undead within 60 feet of you, or any creatures in the Ethereal Plane that overlaps that area. You learn the distance and direction to any creatures you detect (or an Ethereal creature's equivalent position on your plane). Once you detect a creature with this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Ghostly Magic
entries: Your soul is especially powerful, and you can channel its power into a semblance of mortal magic. You learn the {@spell mage hand} cantrip, and can make the hand that it conjures invisible.

You also learn the {@spell blink} and {@spell invisibility} spells, each of which you can cast once at its lowest possible spell level without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast those two spells in this way when you finish a long rest. Choose Wisdom or Charisma as your spellcasting ability for all three spells.

name: Ghoulish Agility
entries: You become exceedingly nimble. Your jump distance and height triple, and you gain a climbing speed of 30 feet. If at least one of your hands is unoccupied, you can stoop into a beastly gait as you run, increasing your land movement speed by 10 feet
Additionally, you can use the {@action Dodge} action as a bonus action. Once you do so, you must finish a short or long rest before you can do so again.

items.name: Large
items.entry: Your are one size larger and the weight of your body is multiplied by 4.

name: Giant Foe
entries: Your experience fighting giants, such as ogres, trolls, and frost giants, has taught you how to avoid their deadliest blows and how to wield mighty weapons to better combat them. You gain the following benefits:

items: If you normally have disadvantage on attack rolls made with {@filter weapons with the Heavy property|items|source=|type==sand|property=heavy} due to your size, you don't have disadvantage on those attack rolls.
When a giant attacks you, any critical hit from it against you becomes a normal hit.

Whenever you make an Intelligence ({@skill History}) check related to the culture or origins of a giant, you are considered proficient in the {@skill History} skill and add double your proficiency bonus to the check, instead of your normal proficiency bonus.

name: Giant Slayer
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Duck and Weave
entries: If you are within 5 feet of a Large or larger creature, you can take the {@action Dodge} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: The Bigger They Are
entries: You're adept at knocking Large or larger creatures off their feet. When you use the {@itemMastery Topple} Weapon Mastery feature against a creature of Large or larger size, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its save.

name: Giantborn
entries: The blood of the first orcs, giants among mortals, flows through your veins, granting you the following benefits:

items: Immediately after you use your Relentless Endurance trait, you can spend a number of Hit Dice up to half your level to heal yourself. Roll the dice, add your Constitution modifier to each roll, and regain a number of hit points equal to the total (minimum of 1). For the next ten minutes, your size is increased by one category—from Medium to Large, for example. While enlarged, you have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, and your attacks deal 1d4 extra damage.

name: Gift of Bakuryō
entries: You have been blessed with a minor boon of power from the koi dragon kaiju Bakuryō, granting you the following benefits:

items: You gain 2 Rampage Points.

You learn the {@spell sacred flame} cantrip. You also learn the {@spell calm waters|WrathOfTheKaiju} and {@spell ice moon|WrathOfTheKaiju} spells, and you can expend 1 Rampage Point to cast either one without material components, using Constitution as your spellcasting ability. If you have the Spellcasting or Pact Magic class features, you can use that feature's spellcasting ability instead, and you can cast these spells with any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. When you cast {@spell calm waters|WrathOfTheKaiju} or {@spell ice moon|WrathOfTheKaiju} with this feat, you can expend additional Rampage Points; the level of the spell increases by 1 for each additional point you expend in the casting (maximum 9th-level spell).

name: Gift of Iminada
entries: You have been blessed with a minor boon of power from the bakekujira kaiju Iminada, granting you the following benefits.

items: You gain 2 Rampage Points.

You learn the {@spell spare the dying} cantrip. You also learn the {@spell cure wounds} and {@spell inflict wounds} spells, and you can expend 1 Rampage Point to cast either one without material components, using Constitution as your spellcasting ability. If you have the Spellcasting or Pact Magic class features, you can use that feature's spellcasting ability instead. When you cast {@spell cure wounds} or {@spell inflict wounds} with this feat, you can expend additional Rampage Points; the level of the spell increases by 1 for each additional point you expend in the casting (maximum 9th-level spell).

name: Gift of Magatsuchi
entries: You have been blessed with a minor boon of power from the Plant kaiju Magatsuchi, granting you the following benefits.

items: You gain 2 Rampage Points.

You learn the {@spell earthen fist|WrathOfTheKaiju} cantrip. You also learn the {@spell earthen uppercut|WrathOfTheKaiju} and {@spell entangle} spells and can expend 1 Rampage Point to cast either one without material components, using Constitution as your spellcasting ability. If you have the Spellcasting or Pact Magic class features, you can use that feature's spellcasting ability instead, and you can cast these spells with any spell slots you have. When you cast {@spell earthen uppercut|WrathOfTheKaiju} or {@spell entangle} with this feat, you can expend additional Rampage Points; the level of the spell increases by 1 for each additional point you expend in the casting (maximum 9th-level spell).

name: Gift of Nomi
entries: You have been blessed with a minor boon of power from the kabuto kaiju Nomi, granting you the following benefits:

items: You gain 2 Rampage Points.

You gain proficiency in the Athletics skill. If you already have proficiency in that skill, you gain expertise instead; your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability checks you make using the skill.

You can use a bonus action and expend 1 Rampage Point to attempt to grapple or shove a creature within your reach. When you use this benefit, you can expend 1 additional Rampage Point to impose disadvantage on your target's ability check made to contest your grapple or shove.

name: Gift of Raiko
entries: You have been blessed with a minor boon of power from the Elemental kaiju Raiko, granting you the following benefits.

items: You gain 2 Rampage Points.

You learn the {@spell shocking grasp} cantrip. You also learn the {@spell flash|WrathOfTheKaiju} and {@spell wind drake|WrathOfTheKaiju} spells, and you can expend 1 Rampage Point to cast either one without material components, using Constitution as your spellcasting ability. If you have the Spellcasting or Pact Magic class features, you can use that feature's spellcasting ability instead, and you can cast these spells with any spell slots you have.
