At the end of the 10 minutes, you identify any objects within that area that are magical or cursed. You also gain a mental image of events that occurred in that area within the last 24 hours, including creatures that entered or left, objects they interacted with, and actions they took. These visions do not include sound or other sensory information. Creatures and objects obscured from divination magic appear as voids of darkness, and you are unable to identify their size or shape. Once you use this benefit, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

When you perform this ritual, you can extend it into a much deeper meditation in order to peer further into an area's history. If you concentrate for 8 hours rather than 10 minutes, you gain a mental image of all events that occurred in that area within the last month. You can repeat this 8 hour ritual daily to delve deeper into the past. For each consecutive day you repeat the ritual, you look one month further back in time.

name: Hit Die
entries: You gain a Hit Die, a {@dice d6}, and your hit points maximum increases by {@dice 1d6} (or 4) + your Constitution modifier.

entries.name: Special
entries: You may take this feature multiple times.

name: Hoard Away From Hoard
entries: You like the feeling of having large sums of gold near you when you rest. You gain the following benefits:

items: Whenever you take a long rest with a certain amount of gold pieces in your possession, you roll the corresponding die and gain temporary hitpoints equal to the roll.

name: Holmganga Master
entries: Your experience in dueling gives you the following benefits.

entries.name: Battle Primed
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} at the start of a Holmganga or other duel.

entries.name: Duel Intimidation
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can make a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check against your holmganga opponent. If the check succeeds (GM's discretion), you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on your next attack against the target, and the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its next attack against you.

name: Holy Acolyte
entries: When you gain this feat, select a Divine Domain from the Cleric subclasses. You may choose not to select a domain when you gain this feat.

You gain the Channel Divinity feature of the selected domain. If you didn't select a Divine Domain when you gained this feat, you gain the Turn Undead Channel Divinity feature that all clerics gain at 2nd level instead. Once you've used the chosen Channel Divinity, you must then finish a short or long rest before using it again.

If the Channel Divinity references your Cleric level, it uses your Proficiency Bonus instead. If the Channel Divinity forces a saving throw, the DC is equal to 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Wisdom modifier.

name: Holy Aura
entries: When you use your {@feat Ward of Faith|TalentTrees} to protect a creature, you can choose to imbue them with a holy aura which lasts 1 minute and manifests as a aura which gives off dim light and protects a 10 foot radius sphere around it. When a creature of the type chosen for the {@feat Ward of Faith|TalentTrees} attempts to enter or leave the aura, it must make a Wisdom saving throw or be stopped by the barrier and take {@dice 2d8} radiant damage, or half as much on a successful save.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Holy Aura
entries: When you use your {@feat Ward of Faith|TalentTreesMod} to protect a creature, you can choose to imbue them with a holy aura which lasts 1 minute and manifests as a aura which gives off dim light and protects a 10 foot radius sphere around it. When a creature of the type chosen for the {@feat Ward of Faith|TalentTreesMod} attempts to enter or leave the aura, it must make a Wisdom saving throw or be stopped by the barrier and take {@dice 2d8} radiant damage, or half as much on a successful save.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Homebrew Technologist
entries: Choose two trivial and one simple complexity gadget schematic from the engineer's list. You learn and can use these schematics as if you were an engineer. If the gadgets have an activated effect that requires a short or long rest to reset, you must finish a long rest before you can use it again.

name: Homebrewer
entries: You gain proficiency with {@item alchemist's supplies|PHB} if you don't already have it. Using a set of {@item alchemist's supplies|PHB} over the course of 10 minutes, you can brew potions. You gain a number of reagent dice equal to your proficiency bonus and can expend them to brew any potions available to an alchemist of 3rd level. These potions retain potency for 24 hours, after which they become inert. If you have the {@classFeature Reagent|Alchemist|VSS|3} feature from the alchemist class, you can also use these reagent dice to add additional damage to a bomb's damage roll.

name: Honed Reflexes
entries: You have become adept at laying ambushes and quickly escaping danger. You can take two turns during the first round of any Combat. You take your first turn at your normal initiative and your second turn at your initiative minus 10. You canâ€™t use this feature when you are surprised.

name: Honorable*
entries: By the power of Sigalo, you become better at doing the honorable thing. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain advantage against fear effects.
Each allied creature within 5 feet of you confers a +1 bonus to all attack you would make while in melee range of the target, to a maximum of +3.

name: Hook
entries: When you hit a creature with a {@item trident|PHB}, {@item war pick|PHB}, or {@item sickle|PHB} on your turn, you can use your bonus action to attempt to {@action grapple} the targeted creature.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Hook
entries: When you hit a creature with a {@item trident|PHB}, {@item war pick|PHB}, or {@item sickle|PHB} on your turn, you can use your bonus action to attempt to {@action grapple} the targeted creature.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Hope of Dawn
entries: Your faith shines forth like the inviting warmth of dawn, bringing hope and confidence to all around you. You gain a pool of {@dice d6}s equal to your Proficiency bonus that you and allies can draw upon to turn the tide against the darkness.

When you or an ally within 30 feet make a saving throw, you can expend a {@dice d6} to add to the save. You can do so after the roll, but before the outcome is determined. If the roll is added to an ally's roll, if you are rolling a save against the same effect, you also add the {@dice d6} to your save. The die is doubled to a {@dice d12} when being used to save against the {@condition frightened} condition.
You can additionally use these dice in the following ways:

items: Expend 1 die to cast {@spell light}
Expend 3 dice to cast {@spell daylight}

entries: You regain all expended dice from this feature when you complete a long rest.

name: Horde Breaker
entries: You learn the way to fight against a large number of foes simultaneously. Once on each of your turns when you make a weapon attack, you can make another attack with the same weapon against a different creature that is within 5 feet of the original target and within range of your weapon.

You can select this feat a second time after 7th level, and a third time after 11th level. Each time you do so you can make another attack with the same weapon against a different creature that is within 5 feet of both of the original targets and is within reach of your weapon.

name: Hordemaster
entries: You've learned how to summon and command hordes of rats to devour your foes, granting you the following benefits:

As an action, you can summon a number of {@creature giant rat|SSGRF|giant rats} equal to your proficiency bonus, which appear in unoccupied spaces that you can see within 30 feet of you. The summoned rats are friendly to you and your companions. In combat, the rats share your initiative count, but they each take their turns immediately after yours in any order you choose.

On each of your turns, you can use a bonus action to command any of the rats within 30 feet of you (if you control multiple creatures, you can command any or all of them at the same time, issuing the same command to each one). You decide what action the rats will take and where they will move during their next turn, or you can issue a general command, such as to guard a particular area or run up and attack a specific creature.

If you issue no commands, they can move and use their reaction on their own, but the only action they take on their turn is the {@action Dodge} action. Once given an order, the rats continue to follow it until their task is complete or they end their turn more than 30 feet away from you. Each rat disappears after it drops to 0 hit points, after 10 minutes have passed, or you use this feature to summon more rats.

Once you summon rats this way, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a spell slot of 1st level or higher. When you summon rats this way, you create a number of rats equal to twice the level of the spell slot expended.

name: Horn Maestro
entries: Thanks to extensive practice with the {@item hunting horn|AGMH}, you gain the following benefits:

items: Your hunting horn's chord length is increased by 1.
You can now complete a hunting horn's melody as a bonus action.
{@i Fortissimo!} Your hunting horn's single note melody effect is doubled.

name: Horn Pit Gladiator
entries: You have honed your skills in the brutal Horn Pits of Kihōsō City. You gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Single Combat
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can mark that creature as your target for single combat for 1 minute. You can only have one creature marked in this way at a time, and you can mark creatures in this way a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. You regain all expended uses of this feature when you finish a long rest.
Marking a creature grants the following benefits:

items.name: Retaliation.
items.entry: If the marked creature attacks a creature other than you while it is within your reach, you can use your reaction to make a weapon attack against the marked creature, and you have advantage on the attack.

items.name: Pursuit.
items.entry: At the end of the marked creature's turn, you can use your reaction to move up to your speed towards it, ending your movement as close to it as possible.

items.name: Victory.
items.entry: If you reduce the marked creature to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to twice your proficiency bonus.

name: Hound the Foes
entries: When you hit a target in melee with a critical hit, their speed becomes 0 for their next turn.You may move to engage a different target within 15 feet as a bonus action, without provoking opportunity attacks.

name: Howling Melody
entries: You may cast the spell {@spell Dissonant Whispers} once per short rest without spending a spell slot and may cast this spell at first level.

name: Hulking Figure
entries: You are a broad and formidable size for your race, either due to extensive training or natural build. You gain the following benefits:

items: You count as one size larger (to a maximum size of large) when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, and lift.

When you hit a creature with a melee attack, if you used your strength modifier to hit the creature, you deal an additional {@damage  1d4} damage. This damage is of the same type as the weapon attack.
Whenever you attempt a Charisma (intimidation) check against a creature of your size or smaller, you can add your Strength modifier to the result.

name: Hulking Figure
entries: Either from extensive training or a natural build, you have a broad and formidable size for your species. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Brutal
entries: Once per turn, you can deal an extra {@damage 1d4} Bludgeoning damage to a target you hit with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

entries.name: Intimidating
entries: When you make a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}, {@skill Performance|XPHB}, or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check, you can also add your Strength modifier to the roll.

entries.name: Powerful
entries: You count as one size larger (to a maximum size of Large) when determining your carrying capacity.

name: Hulking Mimic
entries: In a process that takes roughly 24 hours, you gorge yourself on over a ton of food and enter into a deep, transformative slumber. During this time, your body surges in size. When you awaken, you gain the following benefits:

items: Your size becomes Large. While you are Large, when you use your {@variantrule Object|XPHB} Form species trait, you can transform only into

entries: Large objects.

items: When you hit a target with an unarmed strike using your pseudopods (or your pseudopod blade, if you have the Mimic Blade feat), you deal an extra {@damage 1d4} damage

name: Hungry Hungry Goo
entries: Your deepen your primal appetite. Your hunger drives you forward, giving you the following benefits:

items: You can engulf creatures that are one size larger than you.
When you hit a creature with a pseudopod attack, you can use a bonus action to attempt to grapple the same creature as a bonus action until the end of your turn.

When a creature fails its saving throw against your Engulf trait, you can move into its space to trap it in your body instead. The engulfed creature can't breathe and is restrained. While engulfing a creature or object, your speed is halved. When you move, the engulfed creature or object moves with you. You can only have one creature or object engulfed this way at a time. A trapped creature can try to escape by taking an action to make a Strength check (same DC as for Engulf). On a success, the creature escapes and enters a space of its choice within 5 feet of you.

name: Hunt Master
entries: A master of hunting, tracking, and harvesting usable materials from monsters and beasts, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with hunter's supplies. If you are already proficient with them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.
You have advantage on hunter's supplies and Wisdom (Survival) checks made to harvest useable parts from monsters. This feature does not apply to downtime activities outside of of games.
When you roll a natural 20 on a hunter's supplies check in downtime, you gain one extra success than you normally would.

name: Hunted

otherSummary.entry: You can only take this feat during character creation

entries: You are pursued by those who would kill you on sight or drag you to an ill-fated end. Perhaps you are fleeing the consequences of a terrible crime, or your name is on the lips of an underworld kingpin. The constant paranoia grants you a +5 bonus to your passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) score and allows you to instantly awaken whenever a creature moves within 30 feet of you. However, you rarely sleep soundly. Roll a d20 whenever you take a long rest; on a 1, you instead only gain the benefits of a short rest.
If you are confident that you are permanently freed of your pursuers, such as if you escape to another plane of existence or watch your hunter die, you lose this feat.

name: Hunter
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Improved Tracking
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) and Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks to follow or identify tracks.

entries.name: Greater Stealth
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} when on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks while outdoors.

name: Hunter of Hunters
entries: You are adept at hunting monstrous prey, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Dead Aim
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can scrutinize a creature to spot its vulnerable points. The next time you deal damage to the creature before the start of your next turn, you ignore the creature's damage {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}, if any.

entries.name: Studied Quarry
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks made to recall information about a creature.

name: Hunter's Insight

prerequisite.other: Level 9 or higher, Hunter's Mark spell and Favored Enemy class feature

entries: {@spell Hunter's Mark} no longer requires concentration when used on one of your favored enemies. When a creature affected by your Hunter's Mark has to make a saving throw against one of your Master Strikes you can roll a {@dice d6} and subtract it from the creature's roll. You can't do this more than once for each cast of the spell.

name: Hunting Hound
entries: You are a natural at seeking the quarry of your allies. You have advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of your allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated

name: Huntsman's Blessing*
entries: Your study of Fey lore has unlocked a fey power that few others possess. Drawing on your ancestry, you can momentarily stride through the Nexus of Yastah to shorten your path from one place to another. You gain the Following Benefits:

items: You learn to speak, read, and write Sylvan if you cannot already.
You learn the cantrip {@spell Blink Step|yastah}, and case use the spells {@spell Misty Step|yastah} and {@spell Blink|yastah} once per day without expending a Spell Slot.

name: Hurl Through Hell
entries: When you or your familiar hit a creature with an attack within 5 feet of your familiar, you can command your familiar to instantly transport the target through the lower planes. Both your familiar and the creature disappears and hurtles through a nightmare landscape. Your familiar must be a fiend in order to use this ability. At the end of your next turn, the target returns to the space it previously occupied, or the nearest unoccupied space. If the target is not a fiend, it takes 10d10 psychic damage as it reels from its horrific experience. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

name: Hybrid Shape
entries: You gain the ability to take on attributes of beasts you've seen. Choose a creature from the {@feat Minor Beast Shape|Adventurer} feat. As a bonus action, you can expend one use of your {@feat Beast Shape|Adventurer} to take on a hybrid form rather than fully transform into the creature. While in this hybrid shape you gain temporary hit points equal to the creature's hit points. These hit points last for 1 minute, and while you have these temporary hit points you gain the creature's special abilities, actions, movement, climbing, swimming, and flying speed.

name: Hydromancer
entries: You specialize in the magic of water, commanding seas, rivers, glaciers, and steam geysers all as one. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have {@variantrule spell prowess|TEB} with {@book hydromancy spells|TEB|2|Hydromancy Spells}
The spells {@spell create or destroy water}, {@spell maelstrom|XGE},* {@spell shape water|XGE},* and {@spell tsunami} are added to the spell list of your spellcasting class.
The range for your hydromancy spells is increased by 30 feet, unless the spell's range is Self. This also increases the range of Touch spells.

When a hydromancy spell that you cast pushes or pulls a creature, it moves that creature 10 extra feet. When one knocks a creature {@condition prone}, you can choose to also push that creature 10 feet away from you. When one reduces a creature's speed, it is reduced by 10 additional feet. When one creates liquid water, it creates twice as much.

name: I Fought, I Lived
entries: You confronted a horror from beyond this world or spawned by terrible magic. It disregarded you as a puny mortal, but it learned its mistake the hard way when you sent it back to wherever it came from with good, old-fashioned muscle, courage, and a really, really large axe.
You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Defiant Strike
entries: While you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB} and hit with a spell or weapon attack, you can choose to treat the attack's damage roll as having rolled the maximum damage possible. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Indomitable Heart
entries: If you have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition at the start of your turn, roll a {@dice d20}. On a 10 or higher, you no longer have that condition.

name: I Hid from the Terror
entries: That night is a blur. A strange presence, an overwhelming terror, and a confused jumble of screams mixed with faint memories of something terrible and hungry. You hid from it, finding a place too small for it to reach. The sounds of that night, and the awful aftermath you found that morning, will remain with you to the end of your days and beyond.
You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Shadowed Strike
entries: If attacking would end the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition on you, you can make an attack and keep that condition. You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Beneath Notice
entries: When you attempt to hide from a creature that is larger than you, you can hide if you are lightly obscured or more than 30 feet away from it. You gain the benefits of being hidden against such creatures, but you do not hide from other creatures.

entries.name: Merge into Shadows
entries: Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks made to detect you while you have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

name: I Opened the Gate
entries: You didn't mean for things to turn out this way. You were curious and perhaps ignored a few signs, but it's hard to take ancient curses seriously. Musty old books say a lot of things, and most of them turn out to be mere fables. Most of them. The one book you read turned out to be the key to unleashing some ancient evil. Now it's in the world, and it's up to you to find it and send it back.
You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Delver into Forgotten Lore
entries: You learn three languages of your choice.

entries.name: Foul Arcana
entries: You can tap into a brief glimpse of the mythos to empower a spell, at the cost of overwhelming your mind with a horrifying, cosmic insight. When you cast a spell, you can give that spell's save DC a +2 bonus but you have the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn. You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: I Pierced the Illusion
entries: You came across something strange and awful, made all the more terrible by its hidden nature. A town might have seemed innocent until it dragged unwitting visitors to their carefully tended sacrificial garden, or the family that took you in on a dark, stormy night were actually hungry cannibals. You survived because you saw their disguise and escaped or struck first.
You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Clear Senses
entries: If you have the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition at the start of your turn, roll a {@dice d20}. On a 10 or higher, you no longer have that condition.

entries.name: Ear for Falsehood
entries: When an NPC speaks to you, you can use this ability to determine if they are lying. You learn nothing about the truth they conceal or why they are lying, simply that there is a knowing falsehood in their statement. You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Subtle Interrogation
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Insight checks made against creatures that you are speaking with.

name: I Survived to Tell the Tale
entries: You encountered something dreadful, a horrible creature or bizarre ritual that set you down the path to becoming an investigator of the strange. Your quick feet and instinct for survival carried you through that day and are your best assets.
You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Instinct to Survive
entries: When you take damage that would reduce you to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can immediately regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your level. When you use this benefit, you cannot use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Superior Speed
entries: You gain a +10 bonus to {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Wriggle Free
entries: If you would gain the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition, roll a {@dice d20}. On a 10 or higher, you instead do not gain it.

name: Icarian
entries: Your wings grow large and strong. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your flying speed is doubled.

name: Ice Mastery
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Fimbulwinter's Grasp
entries: Your cold spells carry the strength of Fimbulwinter. Whenever you deal Cold damage to a creature with a spell of at least 1st level, you can choose one of the following additional effects.

items: The creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity checks for 1 minute as a terrible cold numbs its body.

The creature is coated in ice. It has the {@condition Restrained} condition until it succeeds on a Dexterity saving throw to free itself (equal to your spell saving throw DC) or takes at least 10 points of Bludgeoning or Fire damage. It can make the save to end this effect at the end of each of its turns.

The creature has {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Cold damage for 1 minute. It can make a Constitution saving throw (equal to your spell saving throw DC) to end this effect at the end of each of its turns.

entries: You can use Fimbulwinter's Grasp a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Ice to meet you
entries: Your presence is cold and intimidating.

items: You have advantage on all intimidation checks, and can use Strength (Intimidation) checks instead of Charisma (Intimidation) Checks.

Once per long rest you can try to make an intimidation check, contested by a creature's Wisdom (Insight) check. If they fail, they are afraid of you for 1 minute and their speed become 0. They can use an action on subsequent turns to repeat their check, ending the effect on a success.

name: Iconoclast
entries: Your people may not deny that the gods exist, but most deny their altruism. You have trained as an iconoclast, learning to hunt down the corrupt servants of these equally corrupt deities. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have resistance to radiant damage.

When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Wisdom saving throw to take only half damage, you can use your reaction to instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

name: Illusion Art
entries: You master the arts of illusion, mastering a special art to create them through a unique method. You gain the following benefits:

items: {@b Mind Tricks.} You learn the {@spell minor illusion|PHB} cantrip and cast it without a material component, using a spellcasting ability modifier of your choice. When you form a weapon with minor illusion, you can use it as if it were a real weapon for the duration. On hit, it does psychic damage instead of its normal damage type.
You gain the {@b Illusion Steps} special bonus action (below).

entries.name: Illusion Steps
entries: {@italic Active Ability (Bonus Action, Supernatural)}

You can cast {@spell mirror image|PHB} as a bonus action without expending a spell slot. When cast this way, it conjures a number of duplicates equal to your proficiency bonus. When you cast this ability or as a bonus action while it is active, you can move one or more of the duplicates out of your space, moving up to your movement speed. A duplicate outside of your space looks just like you and mimics your action, but if you attack or interact with anything while it is not in your space, it is revealed as an illusion until to returns to your space.
If you start your turn with one or more duplicate not in your space, you can either recall them to your space or swap positions with one (destroying the duplicate in the process).
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you complete a long rest.

name: Illusory Master
entries: Your experience with illusory magic has granted you greater understanding of its art. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on saving throws against illusions.
When you hit a creature with an attack on your turn, that creature can't turn invisible until the start of your next turn.
You can cast {@spell disguise self} using your Firbolg Magic trait at will, without expending a spell slot.

name: Illusory Master
entries: Your experience with illusory magic has granted you greater understanding of its art. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on saving throws against illusions.
When you hit a creature with an attack on your turn, that creature can't turn {@condition invisible} until the start of your next turn.
You can cast {@spell disguise self} using your Firbolg Magic trait at will, without expending a spell slot.

name: Illusory Reality

prerequisite.other: {@feat Spellbook|Adventurer} (School of Illusion) or {@feat Acolyte: Trickery|Adventurer}, 14th Level

entries: You have learned the secret of weaving shadow magic into your illusions to give them a semireality. When you cast an illusion spell of 1st level or higher, you can choose one inanimate, nonmagical object that is part of the illusion and make that object real. You can do this on your turn as a bonus action while the spell is ongoing. The object remains real for 1 minute. For example, you can create an illusion of a bridge over a chasm and then make it real long enough for your allies to cross. The object can't deal damage or otherwise directly harm anyone.

name: Illusory Step

prerequisite.other: {@feat Spellbook|Adventurer} (School of Illusion) or {@feat Acolyte: Trickery|Adventurer}, 10th Level

entries: You can create an illusory duplicate of yourself as an instant, almost instinctual reaction to danger. When a creature makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to interpose the illusory duplicate between the attacker and yourself. The attack automatically misses you, then the illusion dissipates. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Immortal
entries: According to legend, a human can achieve immortality by replacing their heart with a mote of celestial radiance. The secret to immortality, including the elixirs and rituals needed to achieve it, is protected by a small, clandestine sect of immortal mystics, each of who only know one component of the process. There are perhaps only a dozen true immortals in the world, but as many as hundreds if every tale can be believed.

entries.name: Ageless
entries: You don't age, can't be aged magically, and suffer none of the frailty of old age. You can't die of old age.

entries.name: Immortal Resilience
entries: You have advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end diseases and the {@condition poisoned} condition yourself. You also have resistance to poison damage.

name: Impact Expert
entries: You have mastered heavy blows with bludgeoning weapons. When you hit a creature with a maul or greatclub, you gain a charge of momentum until the end of your current turn. You can expend your momentum charges as a bonus action on one of the following abilities.

entries.name: Knock Back
entries: Requires 1 or more charges of momentum: You push a creature within reach of you 5 feet per charge of momentum directly away from you. The distance they are pushed decreases by 5 feet for every size larger than you they are (for example, if you are Medium pushing a Large creature, you need to push them 10 feet to move them 5 feet).

entries.name: Take Down
entries: Requires 2 charges of momentum: You force a creature within reach of you to make a Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

entries.name: Bonk!
entries: Requires 1 or more charges of momentum: You expend the momentum slamming into a creature within 5 feet of you, dealing 1d4 bludgeoning damage per charge of momentum.

name: Impaired Vision

otherSummary.entry: You can only take this feat during character creation

entries: Due to injury, illness, or incident of birth, you are unable to see as others can. Instead, you rely on a highly trained sense of hearing, and on aids like white canes to navigate. Your actual condition might range from total blindness to varying types of low vision, which grants you the following traits:

items: You have the {@condition blinded} condition. However, attack rolls do not have advantage against you due to this condition.

You have {@sense blindsight} with a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn't behind {@quickref cover||3||total cover}. Moreover, you can see an invisible creature within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you.

You can cast spells that require you to see a target or area, provided that the target or part of the area is within 30 feet, you have a direct line of sight to the target or area, and you can hear the target if it is a creature. If the target or area is further than 30 feet from you, you can make an ability check using your spellcasting ability. The DC equals 10 + the spell's level. On a successful check, you cast the spell normally. On a failure, the spell fails and has no effect.
You are immune to spells and effects, such as a medusa's Petrifying Gaze, that require you to see.

entries: If your visual impairment is ever remedied, such as through the use of a {@spell regenerate} spell, you lose the benefits of this feat. The GM should discuss with you whether or not removing your impairment is appropriate for your character—it is always a possibility, but never a requirement.

name: Impenetrable
entries: While you are wearing heavy armor you have tolerance to slashing and piercing damage. Additionally, your max jump distance is not halved.

name: Imposing
entries: When you're in the presence of the creature you're intimidating, you can use Strength instead of Charisma for your {@skill Intimidation} checks. When you are not, you can use Intelligence instead.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Imposing
entries: When you're in the presence of the creature you're intimidating, you can use Strength instead of Charisma for your {@skill Intimidation} checks. When you are not, you can use Intelligence instead.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Impossible Wielder
entries: Training in advanced, unorthodox techniques has accelerated your mastery in the martial arts, granting you the following benefits:

entries.name: Weapon Training
entries: You gain proficiency with a Martial weapon of your choice.

entries.name: Mastery
entries: You learn one {@variantrule Advanced Weapon Masteries|RyokoGuideToYokaiRealms|Advanced Technique} of your choice from any {@filter Technique Tree|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=AWM;FWM;HWM;IWM;LWM;LRWM;PWM;RWM;SCWM;SWM;TWM;VWM}{@sup *}. You must meet the prerequisites for the technique to learn it.
{@note *See Ryoko's Guide to the Yokai Realms}

entries.name: Armoury of One
entries: While you are wielding no weapons with the {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light} property, you can wield a {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light} weapon using your mouth or tail (if applicable) for 1 minute. When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action while wielding a weapon in this way, you can make one additional attack using this weapon. You don't add your ability modifier to the damage of this extra attack unless that modifier is negative. Once you have wielded a weapon in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Improved (un)Holy Tattoo
entries: Your tattooed holy symbol is imbued with divine power.
{@b Benefit}:

items: Caster's Spell and Ability Save DC for Paladin/Cleric DC increases by +1
Using a tattoo grants a +2 AC and +1 to saves until the beginning of your next turn, as you flare with a holy vigor. You also gain 5hp (Does not stack)

name: Improved Assistance
entries: You gain an additional assistance dice, your assistance dice turn from d6 to d8, and you regain all of your expended assistance dice when you finish a short or long rest. You can select this feat a second time after 10th level and a third time after 15th level. Each time you do so, you gain an additional assistance dice, and your assistance dice become one step larger (such as from d8s to d10s).

name: Improved Attunement
entries: Your superior understanding of magic items allows you to master their use. You can now attune to up to four, rather than three, magic items at a time. You can select this feat a second time after 15th level, and a third time at 20th level. Each time you do so, you can attune to one additional magic item.

name: Improved Beast Shape
entries: You gain the ability to use Beast Shape on your turn as a bonus action, rather than as an action. You can directly transform from one form to another as a bonus action. You can transform into beasts of CR 1, and can stay in beast shape for 1 hour. The beast cannot have a flying or swimming speed.
If you have the {@feat Greater Favored Enemy|Adventurer} feat, you can transform into creatures of your favored enemy type as well as beasts.

You can select this feat a second time after 6th level, a third time after 9th level, a fourth time after 12th level a fifth time after 15th level, and a sixth time after 18th level. Each time you do so the CR of beasts you can transform into increases by 1 (such as from CR 1 to CR 2), and the duration of your beast shape increase by 1 hour.

name: Improved Breath Weapon
entries: Extensive training has granted you greater control over your Breath Weapon, allowing you to enhance its power and speed.

items: When you roll to regain the use of your breath weapon trait, you regain it on a 5 or 6 on the {@dice d6} dice roll.

You gain a number of empower points equal to your proficiency bonus. Each time you use your Breath Weapon trait you can expend an empower point and choose one of the following benefits: You can use your breath weapon as a bonus action, its damage is increased by {@dice 2d6}, or its range is doubled (30-foot cone or 60-feet long line that is 10 feet wide). You can only gain each benefit once per use of your breath weapon, but you can expend more empower points to gain multiple different benefits at once.

entries: You regain one empower point after finishing a short rest, and all of them after finishing a long rest.

name: Improved Breath Weapon
entries: Extensive training has granted you greater control over your racial breath weapon, allowing you to enhance its speed, power, and range.

items: When you roll to regain the use of your Breath Weapon trait, you regain it on a 5 or 6 on the d6 die roll.
You gain a number of empower points equal to your proficiency bonus. When you use your Breath Weapon trait you can expend an empower point and choose one of the following benefits:
You can use your breath weapon as a bonus action
Its damage is increased by 2d6 or its range is doubled (30-foot cone or 60-feet long line that is 10 feet wide while you are in your original form).
You can only gain each benefit once per use of your breath weapon, but you can expend more empower points to gain multiple different benefits at once.

entries: You regain one empower point after finishing a short rest, and all of them after finishing a long rest.

entries.caption: Draconic Ancestry
rows: Fang ({@b Officially do not have a Breath Weapon})

name: Improved Critical
entries: Your weapon attacks with your bonded weapon score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20. You can select this feat a second time after 15th level. When you do so, your weapon attacks with your bonded weapon score a critical hit on a roll of 18-20.

name: Improved Familiar
entries: You learn to use your magic to create a more powerful familiar. With 8 hours of work and the expenditure of 50 gp worth of rare herbs and fine food, you can transform your familiar into a more powerful companion. Your familiar can take the form of any beast of CR 1/4. If you have the {@feat Favored Enemy|Adventurer} feat, and do not have humanoids as your favored enemy, your familiar can take the form of creatures of your favored enemy type as well as beasts.

Your familiar can attack, but loses Multiattack action, if it has one. Additionally, if you have the Extra Attack feat, when you take the Attack action, you can forgo one of your own attacks to allow your familiar to use its reaction to make one attack of its own. If your familiar's new form is capable of casting spells, it is unable to cast any of them.

You can select this feat a second time after 7th level, a third time after 11th level, a fourth time after 15th level, and a fifth time after 19th level. The CR of beasts you can summon as familiars into increases to CR 1/2 after the second time, CR 1 after the third time, CR 2 the fourth time, and CR 3 the fifth time.

items: When you cast the {@spell find familiar} spell, you can choose one of the special forms available to warlocks with the pact of the chain, in addition to the normal options.
Your familiar's hit points become (3 + {@spell find familiar}'s spellcasting ability modifier) times your character level, unless it is higher.
Your familiar's Intelligence score increases to 6, unless it is higher and can speak, and read any languages you know.
When you are wielding a {@item Hammer|AGMH}, you can use its hammer {@optfeature charge (H)|AGMH} property when you move 15 feet instead of 20.
If you jump when performing a hammer charge, you perform a spinning hammer charge that allows you to pass through a hostile creatures space without provoking opportunity attacks.

You can add the extra damage from the hammer charge to 1 additional attack on this turn for every 5 feet you jump during the charge, so long as the attacks target a creature you passed through during the spinning hammer charge.

name: Improved Health
entries: Your hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to your level + 1, and all of your current and future hit dice become d10s. You can select this feat a second time, increasing your hit point maximum by by an amount equal to your level + 1, and improving your hit dice to a d12.

name: Improved Paralytic Claws
entries: A creature that fails its save against your Paralytic Claws ability is {@condition paralyzed} instead of {@condition incapacitated}. Additionally, you can use this trait successfully twice before requiring a short or long rest to refresh its usage, instead of using it successfully once and requiring a long rest.

name: Improved Smite
entries: The maximum for your {@feat Smite|Adventurer} damage increases to 10d8 (9th-level spell slot). Additionally, if you have the {@feat Greater Favored Enemy|Adventurer} feat, your melee weapon attacks against creatures that are the type of your Greater Favored Enemy deal an additional 1d8 radiant damage.

name: Improved War Magic

prerequisite.other: {@feat War Magic|Adventurer}, The ability to cast a spell, 18th Level

entries: When you use your action to cast a spell, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

name: Inabalável
entries: Você pode se recuperar rapidamente de acertos críticos.

{@b Beneficio:} Depois de receber um acerto crítico, você pode gastar um Dado de Vida (Hit Die) como reação após receber o dano. Se você estiver inconsciente, não poderá usar essa habilidade. Isso conta contra o número total de Dados de Vida (Hit Dice) que você pode usar por dia.

name: Inanimate Shapes
entries: Your shapeshifting skills have improved, and now you can transform into objects that make your size more compact. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can now transform into creatures and objects of Medium size or smaller. When you do so, your statistics are changed based on the description below.

You can now use your Shapechanger trait to turn into an object. When you transform into an object, your equipment melds into your form, your speed is reduced to 5 feet, and you can't speak or use any actions for anything other than casting {@spell message} or transforming into another form.
While you're in an object form and remain motionless, you are indistinguishable from a normal object, gaining a +10 bonus to {@skill Stealth} checks.

entries: Based on your size, your statistics may change in following ways:

items: Small. Your size in all dimensions is halved and your weight is reduced to one eighth. Additionally, your base speed is reduced to 25 feet, and your weapon damage rolls are reduced by {@dice 1d4} (minimum 1).

Tiny. Your size in all dimensions is quartered and your weight is reduced to one sixtyfourth. You have disadvantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. Additionally, your base speed is reduced to 15 feet, and your weapon damage rolls are reduced by {@dice 2d4} (minimum 1).

name: Incessant Barking
entries: You have a bark that is hard to ignore, driving foes to distraction. Once per long rest you may affect all creatures within a 15 feet cube. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 2d8} damage and must immediately use its reaction, if available, to move as far as its speed allows away from you. The creature doesn't move into obviously dangerous ground, such as a fire or a pit. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage and doesn't have to move away. A {@condition deafened} creature automatically succeeds on the save.

items: Once per day, you ignore the effects of the first level of Exhaustion/Fatigue incurred for 12 hours.
Each Long Rest you reduce your level of Exhaustion by 2.

name: Indomitable
entries: You gain the ability to reroll a saving throw that you fail. If you do so, you must use the new roll, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest. You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do so, you gain another use of this ability.

name: Industrious
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Hardworking
entries: Choose one skill with which you have proficiency. When you gain a level, you replace the skill you chose with a different one.

Whenever you fail an ability check using  that skill, you can roll a {@dice d6} and add it to the roll, potentially turning the failure into a success. You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Strong Core
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws you make to avoid the {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} condition.

name: Inexhaustible
entries: Whether through natural fortitude or intensive training, you are inexhaustible. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
As a bonus action on your turn, you gain temporary hit points equal to 1d10 + your Constitution modifier. Once you use this ability, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.
When you finish a long rest, your exhaustion level is reduced by 2 (instead of 1), provided that you have ingested food and drink.

name: Inexhaustible
entries: Whether through natural fortitude or intensive training, you are inexhaustible. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
As a bonus action on your turn, you gain temporary hit points equal to 1d10 + your Constitution modifier. Once you use this ability, you must finish a short or long rest before you can do so again.
When you finish a {@quickref resting||2|0|long rest}{@sup {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB|'24}}, your {@condition exhaustion} level is reduced by 2 (instead of 1).

name: Infernal Attunement
entries: Attuning more into your infernal heritage, you evolve into a form capable of doing great things. With that, you gain the benefits as listed below:

items: Choose one of the following:

Your body grows new tools at your disposal, similar to the fiend you are related to. You gain a new natural weapon, which deals {@damage 1d6} + your Strength modifier slashing, piercing or bludgeoning damage, as appropriate for the appendage(s) created or upgraded by this feat. In case of gaining new limbs, you can make them appear and dissapear as a bonus action.
Your connection to the depths of hell grows stronger. Pick a 2nd-level spell from the Warlock spell list. You can cast this spell once per long rest.

You can manifest your rage as a beam of brimstone darkness. When you take the {@action Attack} action, you can replace one of your attacks with shooting a beam of brimstone out of your mouth. The laser is a 5 feet wide, 30-foot line that damages anyone and anything in its path. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw against a DC equal to 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus. A creature takes {@dice 2d6} radiant damage on a failed save, or half that on a success.

name: Infernal Bulwark
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Devil's Flesh
entries: Your skin thickens and assumes a scaled, leathery texture. While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|XPHB}, your base {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} equals 10 plus your Dexterity modifier plus the modifier of the ability increased by this feat.

entries.name: Infernal Protection
entries: You always have the {@spell Armor of Agathys|XPHB} spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. When you cast it without a spell slot using this feature, you cast this spell as its level 2 version, and it deals Fire damage instead of Cold damage. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

entries.name: Vengeful Surge
entries: Whenever a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself forces you to make a saving throw and you succeed, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to deal {@damage 1d10} Fire damage to that creature.
You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Infernal Dragoon
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Devilish Aura
entries: Your close association with diabolic powers unsettles others. You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to manifest an aura of fear in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from yourself. Each creature of your choice in that area makes a Charisma saving throw (DC 8 plus the modifier of the ability increased by this feat plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, it has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, a creature is unaffected, and it is immune to this ability for 24 hours.

entries.name: Devil's Favor
entries: You can call on your infernal patron to aid you. When you make a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can add a +2 bonus to the roll. Once you use this benefit, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Diabolic Empowerment
entries: You always have the {@spell Magic Weapon|XPHB} spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. When you cast it without a spell slot using this feature, the spell's duration becomes 8 hours for that casting. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

name: Infernal Pact
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Infernal Resistance
entries: You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire damage or Poison damage (choose when you select this feat).

entries.name: Infernal Sight
entries: You gain {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 30 feet. This {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} is unimpeded by magical {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}.

entries.name: Silver-Tongued
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Deception|XPHB} skill.

name: Infernal Wings
entries: Your infernal heritage owns wings, and now whether suddenly, through arcane experimentation, or drinking fiendish blood, you have them too.

items: You grow bat wings from your back, those giving you a flight speed of 30 feet. You can make them appear and dissapear as a bonus action.

name: Infinite Armory
entries: Your {@feat Weapon Bond|Adventurer} ritual can now be used to bond with multiple weapons, and is not replaced when you bond with an additional weapon. When you summon your weapon, you choose which bonded weapon to summon. Summoning a bonded weapon can now be done as part of making an attack instead of as a bonus action.

name: Infused Magic

prerequisite.other: The ability to cast a spell or cantrip

entries: You gain the ability to channel your spells into objects for later use. When you cast a spell with a casting time of 1 action, you can increase its casting time to 1 minute. If you do so and hold a nonmagical item throughout the casting, you cast the spell, but none of the spell's effects occur. Instead, the spell transfers into that item for later use if the item doesn't already contain a spell from this feature. Any creature holding the item thereafter can use an action to activate the spell if the creature has an Intelligence score of at least 6.

When activated, the spell is cast using your spellcasting ability, targeting the creature that activates the item. If the spell targets more than one creature, the creature that activates the item selects the additional targets. If the spell has an area of effect, it is centered on the item. If the spell's range is self, it targets the creature that activates the item. If the spell requires concentration, the creature that activates the item must concentrate on it.

When you infuse a spell in this way, it must be used within 8 hours. After that time, its magic fades and is wasted. You can have a limited number of infused spells at the same time. The number equals your spellcasting modifier.

name: Infusion Adept

prerequisite.other: proficiency in one type of artisan's tools

entries: Matching your skill in craftsmanship or magic with curiosity in the other, you have experimented with enhancing items: you learn two {@filter Artificer Infusion|optionalfeatures|feature type=AI} options of your choice from the artificer class. If the infusion has a prerequisite of any kind, you can choose that infusion only if you're an artificer who meets the prerequisite.
Whenever you gain a level, you can replace one infusion you know with another one from the artificer class.

You can touch one nonmagical object at the end of a long rest and imbue it with one of your artificer infusions learned in this way, turning it into a magic item. See the artificer class in Chapter 1 of Tasha's Cauldron of Everything for how infusions work. You can infuse only one nonmagical object at a time (if you're an artificer, this does not count towards the maximum number of objects you can infuse). If you try to infuse a new item, the first infusion immediately ends, and then the new infusion applies.

name: Infusion Initiate
entries: Your inventiveness has granted you the ability to imbue mundane items with magic.

You learn three {@filter infusion options|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=AI} of your choice from the artificer class. If the infusion has a prerequisite of ayn kind, you can choose that infusion only if you're an artificer who meets the prerequisite.
If you already have the {@classFeature Infuse Item|Artificer|TCE|2} feature, your maximum number of infused items increases by 2; otherwise, you may only have two infused items at a time.

Whenever you reach a level that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can replace one of these infusions with another one from the artificer class. The infused magic vanishes from an item if you give up your knowledge of that infusion for another one.

name: Inner Peace
entries: You've managed to unlock your spirit's inner ki, granting you the following:
You can use a d4 + Dexterity modifier for unarmed attacks you make
You gain two Ki points, which are added to any Ki you might have. You regain any spent Ki on a short rest.
You learn one of the following abilities, which are fueled by your Ki:
{@b Flurry of Blows}
Immediately after you take the Attack action on your turn, you can spend 1 ki point to make two unarmed strikes as a bonus action.
{@b Patient Defense}
You can spend 1 ki point to take the Dodge action as a bonus action on your turn.
{@b Step of the Wind}
You can spend 1 ki point to take the Disengage or Dash action as a bonus action on your turn, and your jump distance is doubled for the turn.

name: Inner Power

feature: At least 1 psi or ki point

entries: Your body is powered by the inner powers that course through it. Your maximum psi or ki points (if you have both, your choice of which) increases by 1. At the end of your turn after expending one or more psi or ki points during your turn (not counting temporary or free points, such as those from Psionic Mastery), you heal for a number of hit points equal to the psi or ki points spent.

name: Inner Resilience
entries: Your internal discipline gives you access to a small pool of {@classFeature Ki|Monk||2} points. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have 3 Ki points, which you can spend to fuel the {@classFeature Ki|Monk||2||Patient Defense} or {@classFeature Ki|Monk||2||Step of the Wind} features from the monk class. When you spend a Ki point, it is unavailable until you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|short or long rest}, at the end of which you draw all of your least 30 minutes of the rest meditating to regain your Ki points.
If you already have Ki points, your Ki point maximum increases by 3 instead.

name: Innovator's Upgrade
entries: You've honed your mind into a nonstop analytical machine. You can select an additional {@filter upgrade|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=IS:C;IS:F;IS:G;IS:I;IS:O;IS:P;IS:T;IS:Re;IS:Ru;IS:W} from your subclass list. You can select this feat multiple times, selecting a different upgrade each time.

name: Inquisitive Empathy
entries: Naturally curious, you have honed your telepathic powers to sense how other creatures are feeling at a given moment. You can probe deeper into a creature's mind, but only rarely. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can cast {@spell detect thoughts} spell at will, without expending a spell slot or material components. Once you probe deeper into a creature's mind using this spell, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest. When you cast {@spell detect thoughts} with this feat, you cannot detect the presence of creatures you can't see. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

name: Insect Glaive Mastery
entries: You master fighting with an {@item insect glaive|AGMH}, gaining the following benefits:

items: When you use the insect glaive standing leap property, you can now use the Attack action as part of the same action, instead of a single weapon attack. Additionally, if you use the standing leap property to jump into the air, the distance you can jump is doubled.

When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack from your insect glaive, while you are in the air, you can move up to 10 feet in any direction. This movement does not count against your normal movement speed or the amount of movement you gain from the standing leap property.

name: Insectoid
entries: Insectoids bear one or two insectlike features, such as prominent compound eyes or chitinous plates, but almost always have a pair of sensitive antennae atop their heads. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Blindsight
entries: Due to your antennae, you have {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} with a range of 10 feet.

entries.name: Regenerative
entries: If any part of your body is amputated, but its amputation doesn't kill you, that body part fully regrows over the course of 24 hours.

name: Insectoid
entries: Insectoids bear one or two insectlike features, such as prominent compound eyes or chitinous plates, but almost always have a pair of sensitive antennae atop their heads.

entries.name: Blindsight
entries: Due to your antennae, you have {@sense blindsight} with a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn't behind {@quickref cover||3||total cover}, even if you're {@condition blinded} or in darkness. Moreover, you can see an {@condition invisible} creature within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you.

entries.name: Regenerative
entries: If any part of your body is amputated, but its amputation doesn't kill you, you can fully regrow that part of your body in 24 hours.

name: Insidious Mimic
entries: It's almost impossible for anyone to determine you're actually a mimic, even using magic. When you use your {@variantrule Object|XPHB} Form species trait to adopt a form other than your natural form, you become immune to magic that allows other creatures to read your thoughts, determine whether you are lying, learn your alignment or creature type, or otherwise discern your true form.

name: Insightful
entries: You possess keen insight into how other people think and feel. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Insight} skill. If you are already proficient in the skill, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.

You can use your action to try to get uncanny insight about one humanoid you can see within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check contested by the target's Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check. If your check succeeds, you have advantage on attack rolls and ability checks against the target until the end of your next turn.

name: Insightful Collector
entries: Your expeditions, transactions, and mercantile activities on behalf of the Augustine Trading Company have put you in contact with collectors of historical artifacts, relics, and tomes. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Object Intuition
entries: You can take a {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine one magical object and learn its properties and how to use it without attuning to it or taking a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} in physical contact with it, but you don't learn any curse the item might bear. There is a cumulative 5% chance for every rarity above Common that you misidentify the nature and the power of the object.

entries.name: Rare Find
entries: You begin play in possession of a Common magic item. Work with your GM to decide on which object fits your character and the campaign.

name: Inspirational
entries: You've had some training in performance, allowing you to inspire others with your musical prowess. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with one {@item musical instrument|PHB} of your choice, and you can use that instrument as a spellcasting focus for any spell you cast that uses Charisma as its spellcasting ability.
Whiel you are playing an instrument you are proficient with, you can cast the {@spell guidance} cantrip, and you can target a creature within 30 feet of you that can hear you.

name: Inspirational
entries: Whenever you use the Help action, the target can add your proficiency bonus to the attempted ability check or attack. You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining any expended uses at the end of a long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Inspirational
entries: Whenever you use the Help action, the target can add your proficiency bonus to the attempted ability check or attack. You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining any expended uses at the end of a long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Inspirational Caster
entries: Your impressive and inspiring spells rally allies to your cause.

items: You gain proficiency in your choice of Intimidation or Persuasion.

If you target allies with a spell that does not cause damage, those allies gain advantage on saving throws to resist effects that cause charm or fear for a number of rounds equal to your Charisma ability modifier, in addition to the normal effect of the spell.

name: Inspired Protector
entries: Once per long rest, you can spend 10 minutes working on defensive maneuvers with one ally you've chosen to protect. At the end of the 10 minutes, you gain a limited ability to use a fighter's {@optfeature Protection} and {@optfeature Interception|TCE} fighting styles to protect that ally. You may use each of these fighting styles twice, plus an additional number of times equal to the chosen ally's Charisma modifier (minimum 1).
This ability to protect your ally lasts until the chosen ally is reduced to zero hit points or until you finish a long rest.

name: Inspiring Leader (Alternate)
entries: If you do not have a Leadership Ability, choose Wisdom or Charisma to be your Leadership Ability and modifier.

Over the course of 10 minutes, which can be during a short or long rest, you can inspire allies and shore up their resolve to fight. When you do, creatures equal to 1 + your Leadership modifier that can hear you within 30 feet gain temporary hit points equal to your level + your Leadership modifier.
A creature can't gain temporary hit points from this feat again until it finishes a short or long rest.

name: Inspiring Leader
entries: You gain the following benefit and the first two available Tiers of the Inspiring Leader Feat:
{@b The Tiers of the Inspiring Leader Feat:}

name: Inspiring Leader
entries: You can spend 10 minutes inspiring your companions, shoring up their resolve to fight. When you do so, choose up to six friendly creatures (which can include yourself) within 30 feet of you who can see or hear you and who can understand you. Each creature can gain temporary hit points equal to your level + your Charisma modifier. A creature can't gain temporary hit points from this feat again until it has finished a short or long rest.

name: Inspiring Musician
entries: Even the music you play hums the tune of enchantments. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Dexterity or Charisma score by 1, up to a maximum of 20.
You gain the proficiency in the {@skill Performance} skill. If you are already proficient in the skill, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.
Your legs and wings count as musical instruments. When you make an ability check to play music with them, you are considered proficient with them.

You can spend 10 minutes playing a mystical tune for your companions, bolstering their morale for the next fight. When you do so, choose up to six friendly creatures (which can include yourself) within 30 feet of you who can see or hear you. Once until it finishes a short or long rest, when the creature makes an attack roll, ability check or saving throw, it can roll a {@dice d6} and add the number rolled to the roll. A creature can't benefit from this feat again until it has finished a short or long rest.

name: Inspiring Word
entries: The range of your {@action Help} action increases by 10 ft (when aiding allies in attacking a creature, you can choose enemies who are up to 10 feet farther away from you than normal, allowing you to help at a 15 foot range, instead of 5).
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Inspiring Word
entries: The range of your {@action Help} action increases by 10 ft (when aiding allies in attacking a creature, you can choose enemies who are up to 10 feet farther away from you than normal, allowing you to help at a 15 foot range, instead of 5).
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Instinctive Charm

prerequisite.other: {@feat Spellbook|Adventurer} (School of Enchantment) or {@feat Acolyte: Trickery|Adventurer}, 6th Level

entries: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to divert the attack, provided that another creature is within the attack's range. The attacker must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the attacker must target the creature that is closest to it, not including you or itself. If multiple creatures are closest, the attacker chooses which one to target. On a successful save, you can't use this feature on the attacker again until you finish a long rest.
You must choose to use this feature before knowing whether the attack hits or misses. Creatures that can't be charmed are immune to this effect.

name: Integrated Arcana
entries: You have tapped into the arcane power that gives you life, allowing you to produce a number of magical effects. You learn {@filter one cantrip of your choice from the sorcerer spell list|spells|level=0|class=sorcerer}. You also learn the {@spell enhance ability} and {@spell levitate} spells. You regain the ability to cast these two spells in this way when you finish a long rest. Constitution is your spellcasting ability for all three spells.

name: Integrated Heatsink
entries: You have discovered a method to forgo stamina loss in favour is generating heat.

Upon using the overdrive ability, instead of destroying the available hit dice you may instead deal fire damage in a 5ft radius centered on yourself equal to rolling the number of hit die. Creatures beside yourself may roll a Dexterity Saving Throw against a DC equal to 10 + your proficiency and constitution modifier, halving the damage on a success.
The damage dealt to you cannot be reduced by any means.

name: Interception
entries: If you use the reaction of a shield to block an attack and it still hits the target, swap places with the target. The attack now targets you instead of the target.

name: Interchangeable parts - Chemical Sprayer (Arm)
entries: A rural adaptation usually used in conjunction with a basic fluid dispensary, this module allows a Babbage to pump a directed stream or spray of liquid from a separate tank. While often used to distributing pesticides, black-market modifications exist which convert it into an effective - if dangerously unreliable - flamethrower. A standard chemical thrower runs about 50gp. The availability and cost of the flamethrower variant is up to your DM's discretion.

name: Interchangeable parts - Fluid Dispensary (Chest)
entries: Popular within high society, this simple tank allows up to 5 gallons of liquid to be stored within the Babage's chest, and heated or cooled as it is dispensed. Many models also contain a system of filters, which can be used to purify water, or brew drinks such as coffee of tea. A basic dispensary costs about 50gp, but more advanced models with filters can run higher.

name: Interchangeable parts - Grapple Attachment (Arm)
entries: This forearm sports a detachable hand, which is connected to it by a 50ft spool of rope or chain. The hand can be launched from the forearm using powerful springs to grab hold of far away objects, and then automatically retracted by an built-in wench, doing so requires an action, and the spring must be re-wound after each use which requires a full minute. In a pinch, the partially retracted hand may be used as an improvised flail, but doing so is likely to damage the mechanism. This complex attachment often costs as much as 300g.

name: Interchangeable parts - Ground Stabilizers (Legs)
entries: This module includes powerful pistons and ground clamps that allow a Babbage to lock themselves in place despite incredible forces. As a free action on your turn, the stabilizers can be activated, making you immune to forced movement that doe snot include teleportation, and incapable of being knocked prone. While the stabilizers are activated, your speed is reduced to 0. Deactivating the stabilizers is a bonus action. The price-range for this module is usually no more than 50-100gp.

name: Interchangeable parts - Integrated Tool (Arm)
entries: This limb replaces your existing forearm and can be designed to function as any onehanded tool or weapon when activated as a free action, or serve as a normal hand when deactivated. It is a DC 20 investigation check to recognize the weapon while deactivated. The cost of an integrated tool generally starts at around 50gp, plus the cost of a normal tool or weapon of that type.

name: Interchangeable parts - Low-light Optics (Eye)
entries: These optical sensors have been specially calibrated to function in low-light environments, granting you darkvision out to a range of 60 ft. Low light optics usually cost about 50gp in a fair market.

name: Interchangeable parts - Mining Drill (Arm and Chest)
entries: This industrial attachment replaces your arm with a heavy mining drill, capable or breaking through mineral deposits at a rate of 3 ft an hour. The Drill requires fuel to operate, which is provided by a large chest-mounted tank, and must be replenished after 5 hours of continuous use. Used as a weapon, the drill deals 2d12 slashing damage on a hit, but using against soft targets is ill advised, as the fleshy viscera of gore tends to damage the mechanism almost immediately. Costs about 300gp on a good day.

name: Interchangeable parts - Phonographic Recorder (Chest)
entries: This intricate device sits within a specialized compartment of the chest and is capable of recording music or conversations onto a wax or copper cylinder and playing them back. Popular among aristocrats, the device itself costs about 150gp, with canisters costing anywhere between 5-20 gp depending on the quality.

name: Interchangeable parts - Welding Torch (Arm)
entries: This modification allows one of your fingers to function as a blow torch to light fires or heat metal. It includes a small reinforced fuel tank in the forearm, which must be refilled after approximately 1 hour of continuous use. Adjusting the burner reduces the flame's heat, but allows it to shed bright light in a similar manner to a torch, and last for up to 5 hours. A welding torch attachment in safe and usable conditions can run anywhere from 150-200gp, but less... dependable versions often go for cheaper.

name: Interior Camouflage
entries: Your ability to alter your shape, texture, and coloration improves to become reactive as you move, allowing you to camouflage yourself inside normal buildings with ease. You can take the {@action Hide|XPHB} action in most normal buildings even when other creatures can see you. In addition, you gain advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks so long as you remain in one spot without moving or taking actions. You can't use this ability to hide in natural environments, and the GM may decide that you can't hide in buildings with exceptionally unusual decor.

name: Internal Plating
entries: You've developed additional chitin plates inside your body and can move them to unexpected places to protect your vitals from critical strikes. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain resistance to piercing damage.
When you are subjected to a critical hit, roll a {@dice d20}. On a 10 or higher, the critical hit becomes a normal hit instead

name: Interrogator
entries: After you succeed on an {@skill Intimidation} check against a creature, you and your allies have advantage on {@skill Insight}, {@skill Persuasion}, and {@skill Deception} checks against that creature for 1 minute.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Interrogator
entries: After you succeed on an {@skill Intimidation} check against a creature, you and your allies have advantage on {@skill Insight}, {@skill Persuasion}, and {@skill Deception} checks against that creature for 1 minute.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Intimidating Leader

otherSummary.entry: proficiency in {@skill Intimidation}

entries: You use fear and intimidation to rally those who follow you into battle. You gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Fearsome Rally
entries: When another creature within 30 feet of you that can also see or hear you fails a saving throw to resist the {@condition Charmed} or {@condition Frightened} condition, you can use a reaction to make an {@skill Intimidation} check against the same save DC. On a success, the creature is not Charmed or Frightened.
You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses of this feature each time you finish a long rest.

activation.condition: When another creature within 30 feet of you that can also see or hear you fails a saving throw to resist the Charmed or Frightened condition

name: Intimidating Size
entries: Your towering stature is unsettling to others. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Strength score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
When you use threats of violence or demonstrate your physical power to frighten another, you can add your Strength modifier instead of your Charisma modifier to your Intimidation ability check.
When you make an Intimidation ability check against a creature your size or smaller you gain advantage.

entries.name: Credits
entries: The Intimidating Size optional feature is based on the book {@link Saurian, an Original Race for D&D 5e|https://www.dmsguild.com/product/203521/Saurian-an-Original-Race-for-DD-5e}. Please credit if you repost elsewhere.

name: Intimidating Size
entries: Your towering stature is unsettling to others. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Strength score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
When you use threats of violence or demonstrate your physical power to frighten another, you can add your Strength modifier instead of your Charisma modifier to your Intimidation check.
When you make an Intimidation check against a creature your size or smaller, your roll has advantage.

name: Intrepid Captain
entries: With you at the bridge, the crew operates like a welloiled machine, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: All Hands on Deck
