entries: When you take an action from the {@variantrule Captain|DarkMatter24} Crew Role, you can take another action from that role as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Dauntless Command
entries: While you are in the {@variantrule Captain|DarkMatter24} Crew Role, the ship's crew members have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Galactic Diplomat
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Persuasion|XPHB} skill. If you are already proficient in the skill, you have {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it.

entries.name: Ship Feats
entries: Life on a starship is arduous, and those without proper training can find themselves completely unprepared to face the challenges posed by deep space. Even a simple run-in with a spaceshark or a pack of var'zuul grubs can spell disaster for the uninitiated. Ship feats each correspond to a Crew Role aboard a starship and represent training and expertise in that role. Ship roles are detailed in the Ships chapter.

entries.name: Gaining a Ship Feat
entries: The GM can grant you a Ship feat to solidify your chosen role aboard the ship or to award you for excellence in a particular role.

name: Inventive Adept
entries: You have spent many days tinkering with various inventions, tool sets, and arcane forces. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with {@item tinker's tools|PHB}. If you are already proficient, then whenever you make an ability check with tinker's tools you treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

You learn one {@filter Infusion|optionalfeatures|feature type=llaart:inf} of your choice from those available to the {@loader Alternate Artificer|class/LaserLlama; Alternate Artificer.json}. At the end of each long rest, you can infuse this Infusion into one object, following the Infusion rules outlined in the Alternate Artificer class.

name: Inventor
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Gadgets
entries: You gain two Gadgets of your choice from the "{@filter Gadget Options|optionalfeatures|source=|feature type=g}" available to the {@class Gadgeteer|DarkMatter24} class that don't have a prerequisite, other than the {@optfeature Magic Item|DarkMatter24} Gadget. Whenever you gain a level, you can replace one of your Gadgets with another one for which you qualify.
No other creature can use your Gadgets. If one of your Gadgets is lost, you can replace it with a new one when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
If a Gadget requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Intelligence and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

name: Inventor
entries: You have studied the secrets of tinkering and inventing new magitech, and are an expert in the practice of both, gaining the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with tinker's tools. If you are already proficient with them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.

You have advantage on Intelligence (Arcana, Investigation) checks made to invent or figure out how both mundane machines and magitech work. This feature applies to research and experimentation performed during downtime, as long as your line of inquiry relates to figuring out or inventing a machine or a piece of magitech.

As an action and using at least one free hand, you can sabotage an invention, a piece of magitech, or a crossbow, causing it to cease to function for one round the next time it is used (or starting on its wielder or wearer's next turn, if it is currently in use). If the item is currently being held, used, or worn by another creature who is aware of your presence, you must first win a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check contested by the target's Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) in order to sabotage it. Otherwise the DM may require you to make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check to see if your sabotage is noticed.

name: Inventor's Mind
entries: You've honed your mind to into a nonstop analytical machine.

items: You can select an additional upgrade from your subclass list. This upgrade cannot be a level restricted upgrade.

name: Investigador
entries: O personagem sabe como descobrir informações.
{@b Beneficio:} Seu personagem recebe +2 de bônus em todos os testes de {@skill Persuasion} para obter informação e {@skill Investigation}.

name: Investigator
entries: You have an eye for detail and can pick out the smallest clues. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Investigation} skill. If you are already proficient in the skill, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.
You can take the {@action Search} action as a bonus action.

name: Iron Gut
entries: You eat like a giant and drink like a fish. Years of punishing your stomach and liver have led to a powerful fortitude. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on Saving Throws against being {@condition poisoned}.
Upon completing a long rest, you regain 1 additional spent Hit Dice.
As an action, you can spend Hit Dice to heal yourself, as if you have taken a short rest. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1) per long rest.

name: Iron Gut
entries: You can eat like a hill giant and drink like a fish. Years of punishing your stomach and liver have led to a powerful fortitude. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Inured to Poison
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Everything Looks Delicious
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks to forage for food.

entries.name: Quick to Recover
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend one of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, roll the die and add your Constitution modifier, and regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the roll's total. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Iron Hero
entries: You have resolved yourself to save the day when all hope seems lost. You gain the following benefits:

items: When you are attacked by a creature that has a CR higher than your level, you gain a +2 bonus to your Armor Class.
You have advantage on attack rolls against any creature that has reduced one of your allies to 0 hit points in the last round.

If a hostile creature you can see takes a legendary action, you can use your reaction to intercede, preventing the legendary action from happening. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Iron Hero
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Underdog's Resolve
entries: When you are attacked by a creature that has a CR higher than your level, you gain a +2 bonus to your {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} for that attack.

entries.name: Vengeful Strike
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against any creature that has reduced one of your allies to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} since the end of your last turn.

entries.name: Heroic Intervention
entries: When an enemy you can see takes a Legendary Action, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to intercede, preventing the Legendary Action from happening. You can take this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Iron Hero
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Underdog's Resolve
entries: When you are attacked by a creature that has a CR higher than your character level, you gain a +2 bonus to your {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} for that attack.

entries.name: Vengeful Strike
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against any creature that has reduced one of your allies to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} since the end of your last turn.

entries.name: Heroic Intervention
entries: When an enemy you can see takes a Legendary Action, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to intercede, preventing the Legendary Action from happening. You can take this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Iron Hero
entries: You have resolved yourself to save the day when all hope seems lost. You gain the following benefits:

items: When you are attacked by a creature that has a CR higher than your level, you gain a +2 bonus to your Armor Class.
You have advantage on attack rolls against any creature that has reduced one of your allies to 0 hit points in the last round.

If a hostile creature you can see takes a legendary action, you can use your reaction to intercede, preventing the legendary action from happening. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Iron stomach
entries: Your stomach's tolerance levels are incredible.  You have toughened your stomach and mouth to the point that you can consume things normally  impossible to digest.

items: You are not subject to potion miscibility misfire results.
You and can chew up and consume objects the size of your fist or smaller once a day as meal.
You are immune to being diseased or poisoned via ingestion.
Gain advantage on {@condition intoxicated} checks

name: Iron Ward
entries: Your arcane ward has resistance against damage from spells, and you have advantage on saving throws against spells while your {@feat arcane ward|Adventurer} has 1 or more hit points.

If you have the {@feat Martial Arts|Adventurer} feat, you gain the ability to deflect melee and ranged spell attacks using your deflect ability from the {@feat Martial Arts|Adventurer} feat while your {@feat arcane ward|Adventurer} has 1 or more hit points.

name: Ironspire Veteran
entries: You have trained in the ways of the ironspire warriors, who cut their teeth in fierce battles with mighty, flying ironwyrms. You gain the following benefits:

items: Attacking at long range doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged weapon attack rolls.

The first time you hit a Huge or smaller airborne creature with an attack roll using a thrown or melee weapon on your turn, that creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw or fall {@condition prone} (DC = 8 + the modifier of the ability you increase with this feat + your proficiency bonus).
When you score a critical hit against an airborne creature, that creature falls {@condition prone}.

name: Ironwood Dryad
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Barkflesh
entries: While you aren't wearing any armor, your {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} equals 15. You can use a {@item Shield|XPHB} and still gain this benefit.

entries.name: Natural Regeneration
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can heal your ironwood flesh. Expend one of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, roll the die, and regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the roll plus your Constitution modifier. You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Isetsu Magic
entries: Your connection with the ocean allows you to wield a measure of water magic, granting you the following benefits:

items: You learn the {@spell water whip|RyokoGuideToYokaiRealms} cantrip.

You can cast the {@spell riptide|RyokoGuideToYokaiRealms} and {@spell water breathing} spells without expending a spell slot. Once you cast {@spell riptide|RyokoGuideToYokaiRealms} or {@spell water breathing} with this feat, you can't cast that spell with it again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast either of those spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells when you cast them with this feat (choose when you select this feat).

name: Jack of All Tools
entries: You learn to wield tools with precision and efficiency, improvising where necessary.

items: You gain proficiency with 3 tools of your choice.

When you make a Manufacturing check using a tool with which you are not proficient, you can add half your proficiency bonus instead, and do not suffer any disadvantage due to not having proficiency with the tool.
Each hour you spend manufacturing an item counts as 2 hours towards the item's completion.

name: Jack of All Trades
entries: You can add half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to any ability check you make that doesn't already include your proficiency bonus.

name: Jack of Trades
entries: You gain proficiency with three tools, instruments, or gaming sets of your choice.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Jack of Trades
entries: You gain proficiency with three tools, instruments, or gaming sets of your choice.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Jeweler
entries: You have mastered not only the art of beautiful and finely crafted jewelry, but also the finer points of improving spellcasting focii. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with jeweler's tools. If you are already proficient with them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.

As an action, you can assess someone's social status and lifestyle based on their clothing and accessories. Additionally, if you spend 1 minute examining a gemstone or a piece of jewelry, you can accurately estimate its value and, in the case of jewelry and at the discretion of the DM, you gain one further piece of information about it: its age, cultural origins, or some other snippet of potentially useful information.

Over the course of a short or long rest, you can polish and shine a single focus or holy symbol made of metal or gemstone and choose one of the following effects. Until your next short or long rest, whenever someone casts a spell for which these effects are applicable and using this focus, the chosen effect is applied to the spell (whether it triggers or not). Once a number of spells equal to your proficiency modifier have been modified this way, the focus loses the benefits of this feature until it is again shined and polished by someone with this feat.
You may reroll a single damage or healing die.
Add a +1 bonus to the spellcaster's first concentration check for this spell.

name: Jeweler
entries: You are an expert with {@item Jeweler's Tools|phb}.
Your knowledge of gems and gem-based objects allows you to identify their shatter points. You deal double damage to such objects with your weapon attacks.

As part of a long rest, you can create one or more fake gemstones. When you create them, you can set a gold value for them to appear to have; their combined value can't be more than your proficiency bonus × your Intelligence modifier × 100 (minimum of 300 gp). In addition, make an Intelligence check using your jeweler's tools; the total of your check becomes the DC for someone else's attempt to identify the fake gems for what they are.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Jewelry Expert
entries: You are an expert in all things gem-related. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with {@item jeweler's tools|phb}. If you are already proficient with them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.
Your knowledge of gems and gem-based objects allows you to identify their shatter points. You deal double damage to such objects with your weapon attacks.

As part of a long rest, you can create one or more fake gemstones. When you create them, you can set a gold value for them to appear to have; this value can't be more than your proficiency bonus × your Intelligence modifier × 100 (minimum of 300 gp). In addition, make an Intelligence check using your jeweler's tools; the total of your check becomes the DC for someone else's attempt to identify the fake gems for what they are.

name: Jinx
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Mutual Misery
entries: When you roll a 1 on the {@dice d20} for a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, choose a creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} it makes within the next minute.

entries.name: Unlucky Number
entries: Whenever an enemy rolls a 13 on the {@dice d20} for an attack against you or on a saving throw against a spell that you cast, the {@dice d20} roll becomes a 1.

name: Jinxed

otherSummary.entry: You can only take this feat during character creation

entries: You were born under an unfortunate star, or were afflicted with a hex that has permanently damaged your luck. Choose a number from 2 to 19. Whenever you roll that number on an ability check or attack roll, the d20 roll becomes a 1. Additionally, when a creature rolls that number on an attack or a contested ability check against you, the d20 roll becomes a 1.

name: Jötunn Magic
entries: You awaken your primordial blood, gaining the following benefits:

items: You learn the {@spell faerie fire} spell and one 1st-level spell of your choice. The 1st-level spell must be from the divination or evocation school of magic. You can cast each of these spells without expending a spell slot Once you cast either of these spells in this way, you can't cast that spell in this way again until you finish a long rest. If you have the Spellcasting or Pact Magic feature, this spell is also added to your spell list. The spells' spellcasting ability is the ability increased by this feat.

name: Juggernaut Plating
entries: Your armor is a part of you, strengthened by your life force. You gain the following benefits.

items: Increase your Strength or Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

When you use Integrated Protection to don {@filter light or medium armor|items|type=light armor;medium armor}, you can add your Constitution modifier to your Armor Class instead of your Dexterity modifier (to a maximum of +2 when using medium armor).

When you use Integrated Protection to don {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor}, you have advantage on Strength saving throws and Strength ({@skill Athletics}) checks to resist being knocked prone or moved against your will.
While it's incorporated into your body, your armor can't be targeted by any effect (such as {@spell heat metal} or the antennae of a {@creature rust monster}) against your will

name: Juggernaut Plating
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Resilient Armor
entries: While you remain alive, armor you have donned can't be targeted by any effect (such as the {@spell Heat Metal|XPHB} spell or the antennae of a rust monster) against your will.

entries.name: Adamantine Body
entries: Any {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} against you becomes a normal hit.

name: Jump Scare
entries: When an adjacent creature believes you are a normal object, rather than a mimic, you can scare them as an {@variantrule Action|XPHB} by suddenly revealing that you're a mimic. The creature must attempt a Will saving throw with a DC of 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier. On a failure, they're {@condition Frightened|XPHB} until the end of their next turn.

name: Jumper
entries: You gain the following benefits:

items.name: Movement Speed
items.entry: You gain movement equal to half your movement speed whenever you take an action other than the magic action or the attack action.

items.name: Jumping
items.entry: Your max jump distance is doubled.

name: Jumper
entries: You can make a running long jump or a running high jump after moving only 5 feet on foot, rather than 10.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Jumper
entries: You can make a running long jump or a running high jump after moving only 5 feet on foot, rather than 10.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Kaiju Brawler

prerequisite.other: {@feat Expert Grappler|WrathOfTheKaiju} and {@feat Blessing Of The Colossus|WrathOfTheKaiju} Feats

entries: The magic of your boon is magnified, allowing you the power to grapple with gods. You gain the following benefits:

items: When you use the Blessing of the Colossus feat to increase your size, you grow to Huge if there is room, and your weapon attacks deal an extra {@damage 1d8} damage on a hit instead of {@damage 1d4}.

While you are Huge or larger, if you use the Attack action on your turn to shove a creature and knock it {@condition prone}, you can make one weapon attack against that creature as a bonus action on that turn.

name: Kaiju Conduit

prerequisite.other: A Feat that grants Rampage Points

entries: You have an uncanny connection to kaiju, their power manifesting with unusual potency within you. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain 3 Rampage Points.

entries: This feat can be taken multiple times.

name: Kaiju Hunter
entries: You are practised in the ways of fighting colossal creatures, granting you the following benefits:

items: Mounting a creature costs you only 5 feet of movement, rather than half your speed.
You can {@action brace} yourself by spending only 5 feet of movement, instead of half your speed.
You have {@b advantage} on ability checks to {@action Identifying Vulnerable Areas|RyokoGuideToYokaiRealms}.
You ignore the difficult terrain caused by moving on a creature more than two sizes larger than you.

Immediately after a creature you can see that is at least one size larger than you hits or misses you with a melee attack roll, you can use your reaction to make a weapon attack against that creature.

name: Karasu Trickery
entries: You are a virtuoso of mischief and trickery even among karasu, granting you the following benefits:

items: Whenever you and at least one other creature you can see make an ability check or saving throw at the same time, such as rolling for initiative, a contested check, or a saving throw against an area of effect, you can swap your result on the d20 for the other creature's. You receive their result, and they receive yours. Once you use this benefit, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Keen Mind
entries: You can accurately recall anything you have seen or heard within the past month, you always know which way is north, and you always know the number of hours left before the next sunrise or sunset.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Keen Mind
entries: You can accurately recall anything you have seen or heard within the past month, you always know which way is north, and you always know the number of hours left before the next sunrise or sunset.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Keen Mind
entries: You gain the following benefit and the first two available Tiers of the Keen Mind Feat:
{@b The Tiers of the Keen Mind Feat:}

name: Keen Mind
entries: You have a mind that can track time, direction, and detail with uncanny precision. You gain the following benefits:

items: You always know which way is north.
You always know the number of hours left before the next sunrise or sunset.
You can accurately recall anything you have seen or heard within the past month.

name: Keen Senses
entries: You can clearly make out fine details or written text from a document, object, or surface and clearly overhear any bits of lightly spoken conversation as long as it is within a number of feet equal to your passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) score.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Keen Senses
entries: You can clearly make out fine details or written text from a document, object, or surface and clearly overhear any bits of lightly spoken conversation as long as it is within a number of feet equal to your passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) score.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Kenku Know-How
entries: Your desire to fly pushes you to elevate yourself and your allies, albeit in different ways. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can take the {@action Help} action as a bonus action.

When you take the {@action Help} action to assist a creature with an ability check that uses a skill or tool check you are proficient with, the creature may add your Intelligence modifier to the check (minimum +1).

name: Khesh'dar Training
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Swift and Silent
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Stealth|XPHB} skill.

entries.name: Master of Shadows
entries: You gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} with the {@skill Stealth|XPHB} skill.

entries.name: Fade Away
entries: When you take the {@action Hide|XPHB} action, the DC for a successful check is reduced to 10. All other restrictions still apply.

name: Khyber Dragonmark
entries: You possess a Khyber Dragonmark, the largest and most powerful expression of an aberrant dragonmark. This provides the following benefits:

items: Choose {@filter one 4th-level|spells|level=4|class=sorcerer} and {@filter one 5th-level spell from the Sorcerer spell list|spells|level=5|class=sorcerer}. At 15th level, choose {@filter a 6th-level sorcerer spell|spells|level=6|class=sorcerer}. You can cast each of these spells once without expending a spell slot. Constitution is your spellcasting ability for these spells. You regain the ability to cast these spells in this way when you finish a long rest.

You can now control the flow of your life force to better command the power within your aberrant mark to suit your goals. Along with the benefit you gain from your Aberrant Dragonmark, each time you cast one of your aberrant spells, you can choose to spend two additional Hit Dice to affect your spell with one Metamagic option from the following list: {@optfeature Careful Spell}, {@optfeature Extended Spell}, or {@optfeature Subtle Spell}. Immediately after you cast the spell, roll those Hit Dice. You take damage equal to the total.

name: Ki Adept
entries: You have studied the ways of monks and have gained some of their understanding. You gain the following benefits:

items.name: Ki Power
entries: You gain 2 Ki points to fuel abilities that use Ki (these points are added to any Ki points you have from another source). You regain any expended Ki points when you finish a short or long rest.

items.name: Flurry of Blows
entries: Immediately after you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can spend 1 ki point to make two unarmed strikes as a bonus action. You can use your Dexterity modifier for attack and damage rolls with these unarmed strikes, which deal {@damage 1d4} bludgeoning damage on a hit (scaling up with your Martial Arts die type, if you have that feature from your class).

items.name: Patient Defense
entries: You can spend 1 ki point to take the {@action Dodge} action as a bonus action on your turn.

items.name: Step of the Wind
entries: You can spend 1 ki point to take the {@action Disengage} or Dash action as a bonus action on your turn, and your jump distance is doubled for the turn.

items: If you already gained these abilities from your class, you can roll a {@dice d4} whenever you use one of them. If you roll a 4, you do not expend a Ki point for using that ability.

name: Ki Initiate
entries: You've gained a more worldly knowledge, bringing you a new understanding of both your mind and body. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your walking speed increases by 10 feet while you are not wearing armor or using a shield.

You learn to use the following ki abilities from the monk class: {@classFeature Flurry of Blows|Monk|PHB|2}, {@classFeature Patient Defense|Monk|PHB|2}, {@classFeature Step of the Wind|Monk|PHB|2}, and {@classFeature Quickened Healing|Monk|PHB|4|TCE}. If an ability refers to a Martial Arts die and you don't have the {@classFeature Ki|Monk|PHB|2} feature, the die is a {@dice d4}.
You gain 2 ki points to spend on ki features (these points are added to any ki points you might have from another source). You regain all expended ki points whenever you finish a short or long rest.

name: Kinsect Mastery
entries: You can use an action to have your {@item insect glaive|AGMH|kinsect} act as if it was summoned by the {@spell find familiar} spell, with the following differences:

items: It can only be used in this way for a total of 1 hour each day.
It cannot be dismissed, instead you can use an action to call it back to you.
It uses the stat block of a {@creature hawk} (MM p.330).
When its hit points reaches 0 it reappears on your insect glaive at full hit points and will resume what it was last doing unless told otherwise.
It can use its action to absorb a creature's essence in the standard order, but it can return this essence to you or one other creature you designate as an action.
While being used in this way, you cannot use it to attack as part of your Attack action.

name: Kitsune's Blessing
entries: You possess natural magic beyond that of a typical kitsune. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can cast spells while transformed using your Shapeshifter trait without requiring material components, unless they have a gold cost.

While transformed using your Shapeshifter trait, you can use your fox's bite to make unarmed strikes, using Strength or Dexterity for your attack and damage rolls. When you hit with it, the strike deals piercing damage equal to {@damage 1d6} + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice).
You gain the Multiattack action. While transformed using your Shapeshifter trait, you can use an action to make a number of unarmed strikes equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded up).
While transformed using your Shapeshifter trait, your AC equals 12 + your Dexterity modifier.

name: Knight of Lolth
entries: You have mastered techniques of waging war when mounted on a monstrous spider. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can cast the find steed spell without expending a spell slot, and you must finish a long rest before you can cast it in this way again. The steed you summon must be a giant spider.
While mounted, you deal extra damage with your melee attacks equal to your proficiency bonus.
When your mount is hit with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to make one melee attack against the creature that hit your mount.

name: Knock About
entries: Once per turn, when you take the {@action Attack} action and hit a creature with a two-handed or versatile weapon wielded in two hands you can push the target 5 feet if the target is no more than one size larger than you.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Knock About
entries: Once per turn, when you take the {@action Attack} action and hit a creature with a two-handed or versatile weapon wielded in two hands you can push the target 5 feet if the target is no more than one size larger than you.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Knowledge of Materials
entries: You have detailed knowledge of the various kinds of materials that appear in the world. You automatically recognize and know the rarity of most woods, textiles, minerals, gems and metals, and have advantage on checks to recall information about them.

You can also spend 10 minutes examining a structure to discern its age and locate possible weak points based on mineralogical clues. When you deal damage to an object you have examined in this way, you can deal maximum damage instead of rolling.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Knowledge of Materials
entries: You have detailed knowledge of the various kinds of materials that appear in the world. You automatically recognize and know the rarity of most woods, textiles, minerals, gems and metals, and have advantage on checks to recall information about them.

You can also spend 10 minutes examining a structure to discern its age and locate possible weak points based on mineralogical clues. When you deal damage to an object you have examined in this way, you can deal maximum damage instead of rolling.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Knowledge of Monsters
entries: You have detailed knowledge of the various kinds of beasts, dragons, and monstrosities that inhabit the world. You have advantage on checks to recall information about a beast, dragon, or monstrosity or discern ones intentions. When you do so, in addition to what you would normally learn, you can also determine the creatures skills and abilities, common attacks, and if the creature is considered especially dangerous to a party of your level, though you dont necessarily learn the specifics of the creatures statistics.
In addition, you know if any portion of any creature is regarded as particularly valuable and have advantage on checks to harvest parts of the corpses of creatures.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Knowledge of Monsters
entries: You have detailed knowledge of the various kinds of beasts, dragons, and monstrosities that inhabit the world. You have advantage on checks to recall information about a beast, dragon, or monstrosity or discern ones intentions. When you do so, in addition to what you would normally learn, you can also determine the creatures skills and abilities, common attacks, and if the creature is considered especially dangerous to a party of your level, though you don't necessarily learn the specifics of the creatures statistics.
In addition, you know if any portion of any creature is regarded as particularly valuable and have advantage on checks to harvest parts of the corpses of creatures.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Knowledge of Plants & Oozes
entries: You have detailed knowledge of the various kinds of plant creatures and oozes that inhabit the world. You have advantage on checks to recall information about a plant creature or ooze or discern ones intentions. When you do so, in addition to what you would normally learn, you can also determine the creatures skills and abilities, common attacks, and if the creature is considered especially dangerous to a party of your level, though you dont necessarily learn the specifics of the creatures statistics.

In addition, you know the most valuable types of plants and fungi by sight, and can more easily identify dangerous habitat features in an area. You have advantage on perception checks against natural dangers such as mushroom spores, poisonous shrubs, carnivorous plants, grasping vines, etc.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Knowledge of Plants & Oozes
entries: You have detailed knowledge of the various kinds of plant creatures and oozes that inhabit the world. You have advantage on checks to recall information about a plant creature or ooze or discern ones intentions. When you do so, in addition to what you would normally learn, you can also determine the creatures skills and abilities, common attacks, and if the creature is considered especially dangerous to a party of your level, though you don't necessarily learn the specifics of the creatures statistics.

In addition, you know the most valuable types of plants and fungi by sight, and can more easily identify dangerous habitat features in an area. You have advantage on perception checks against natural dangers such as mushroom spores, poisonous shrubs, carnivorous plants, grasping vines, etc.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Knowledge of Society
entries: Your have learned much about the history of cultures and societies. When you see a coat of arms, livery, logo, insignia, or other piece of identifying information for a noble lineage, guild, country, corporation, or other organization, you have advantage on checks to identify it and on checks to recreate or incorporate such an item into a disguise. While disguised in this way, you have advantage on blending in with the locals.
Additionally, when you hear a creature speak, you can tell what language it is speaking. If you know the language, you can tell what dialect it uses and ascertain roughly where the creature is from.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Knowledge of Society
entries: Your have learned much about the history of cultures and societies. When you see a coat of arms, livery, logo, insignia, or other piece of identifying information for a noble lineage, guild, country, corporation, or other organization, you have advantage on checks to identify it and on checks to recreate or incorporate such an item into a disguise. While disguised in this way, you have advantage on blending in with the locals.
Additionally, when you hear a creature speak, you can tell what language it is speaking. If you know the language, you can tell what dialect it uses and ascertain roughly where the creature is from.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Kobold Breath
entries: Dragonwrought kobolds have strong ties to their dragon ancestors, and some can even use a racial breath weapon.

items: You gain the Breath Weapon trait from the half dragon (page 10). Its damage type, save type, and shape are determined by your dragonwrought dragon ancestor.

You gain a number of empower points equal to your proficiency bonus. When you use your Breath Weapon trait you can expend an empower point and choose one of the following benefits: You can use your breath weapon as a bonus action, its damage is increased by 2d6 or its range is doubled (30-foot cone or 60-feet long line that is 10 feet wide). You can only gain each benefit once per use of your breath weapon, but you can expend more empower points to gain multiple different benefits at once.

entries: You regain one empower point after finishing a short rest, and all of them after finishing a long rest.

name: Kobold Inventor
entries: You are resourceful and clever for a kobold, although quite eccentric as well. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your created traps (found on page 84 of Xanathar's Guide to Everything) deal double the standard damage. You can create a trap once outside your short rests, and within 1 minute. You regain the ability to make a trap this way after finishing a short or long rest.

You carry six of your inventions with you, and you can use each of the options listed in the {@table Kobold Inventions|CotDDPRaS} table as an action once. Their DC is 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier. All initial damage caused by your inventions increases by an additional 1d6 at 8th level, 12th level, 16th level and 20th level. You also add your proficiency bonus to the attack rolls of your insect swarms. You can choose to panic and use one of your inventions as a bonus action instead of an action, however you must then roll a d6 die to determine which invention you use. If you roll a used invention, then nothing happens. While using an invention this way, you can choose not to cause its effects. You can only use one invention each turn. After finishing a long rest, and spending 10 minutes to forage and prepare, you can regain all expended uses of your inventions.

entries: These inventions look like a mess of scrap or alchemy, therefore others are unwilling to purchase them. Other creatures are unable to use your inventions.

name: Kobold Inventor
entries: You are resourceful and clever for a kobold, although quite eccentric as well. You gain the following benefits:

items: The damage of your created traps ({@i Xanathar's Guide to Everything} page 84) is doubled. As an action, you can also create a temporary makeshift trap outside a short rest, which follows the same rules as your normal traps but only lasts 1 hour, and afterwards you regain the ability to do so after finishing a short or long rest.

You carry six of your inventions with you, and you can use each of the options listed in the Kobold Invention table as an action once. Their DC is 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier. All initial damage caused by your inventions increases by an additional 1d6 at 8th level, 12th level, 16th level and 20th level. You also add your proficiency bonus to the attack rolls of your insect swarms. You can choose to panic and use one of your inventions as a bonus action instead of an action, however you must then roll a d6 die to determine which invention you use. If you roll a used invention, then nothing happens. While using an invention this way, you can choose not to cause its effects. You can only (try to) use one invention each turn. After finishing a long rest, and spending 10 minutes to forage and prepare, you regain all expended uses of your inventions.

entries: These traps and inventions look like a mess of scrap, and others are unwilling to buy them and unable to use them.

entries.caption: Kobold Inventions
rows: {@b Acid.} You hurl a flask of volatile acid to a location within 20 feet of you. Those within 10 feet of that location must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 3d6 acid damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
{@b Pocket Sand.} You throw sand at a creature within 5 feet of you. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be blinded until the end of your next turn.

{@b Scorpion on a Stick.} You attack a creature within 5 feet of you with a scorpion tied to the end of a 5-foot-long pole. The target automatically suffers 1 piercing damage and it must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 3d6 poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. On a failed save the target is also poisoned for 1 minute. The affected target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

{@b Skunk in a Cage.} You release a skunk into an unoccupied 5-foot-square space within 20 feet of you, which immediately sprays a random creature within 5 feet of it. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target retches and can't take actions for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, and whenever it takes damage, ending the effect on a success.

{@b Volatile Fire.} You hurl a flask of fire to a creature within 20 feet of you, who must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the target suffers 2d6 initial fire damage, and 1d6 additional fire damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature can take an action to extinguish the flames.

{@b Wasp Nest in a Bag.} You throw a basket into a 5-foot-square space within 20 feet of you. A swarm of insects (wasps) emerges from it, taking its turn after yours. On its turn, the swarm attacks the creature that was closest to (or inside) the space the basket landed in when you threw it, until that creature (or the swarm) is reduced to 0 hit points, after which the swarm disperses.

name: Koradi Warrior Training
entries: You have undergone training in the weapons and tactics employed by your clan's warriors. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with {@item blowgun|PHB|blowguns}, {@item scimitar|PHB|scimitars}, and {@item shortbow|PHB|shortbows}.

You know traditional methods of concealing and obscuring the source of attacks made using koradi weapons. When you make a ranged attack from concealment using a {@item blowgun|PHB}, {@item longbow|PHB}, or {@item shortbow|PHB} that would reveal your location, you can make a Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check contested by the target's Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check. On your success your position is not revealed. You automatically fail this check if you have already made another attack against the target since the start of your turn.

name: Kraken Anatomy
entries: Your tentacles are covered in octopus suckers and sturdy enough that fewer are needed to support you, giving you an iron grip and an unparalleled advantage when wrestling. You gain the following benefits:

items: You cannot be disarmed, you have advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to escape from being {@condition grappled} or {@condition restrained}, and creatures have disadvantage on ability checks and saving throws made to escape from your grapples.
You have two extra arms (tentacles) that you can use as normal or hide inside your body while they aren't holding anything. These arms can't be used to wield shields or weapons.
Your base swimming speed increases by 10 feet.

name: Kusarigama Master
entries: You have mastered the use of the {@item Kusarigama|RyokoGuideToYokaiRealms}, learning additional techniques to trip and harass your foes. You add your ability modifier to the damage roll made with a kusarigama's counterweight. In addition, when you make this attack against a Medium or smaller target, you can choose to deal no damage. If you do, the target makes a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check (target's choice), contested by your attack roll. If it fails the contest, choose one of the following effects:

items: The target is disarmed of one object it is holding of your choice, which is pulled towards you and falls at your feet.
The target is knocked {@condition prone}.

The target is pulled 5 feet towards you. If that leaves it within your reach, it is {@condition grappled} by you. While a creature is {@condition grappled} in this way, you can't make attacks using the kusarigama's counterweight.

name: Labyrinthine Mind
entries: Your body and mind have adapted to darkness, and you are capable of discovering hidden paths, though you risk the madness of Baphomet in doing so. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain {@sense darkvision} out to 60 feet.
You can perfectly recalled any path you have traveled.

When you reach 5th level, you can use your action to attempt to discover the shortest route to a location by rolling a percentile dice. If you roll a number equal to or lower than your level, you immediately cast the {@spell find the path} spell without expending a spell slot or material components. If you fail to cast this spell, you suffer from an effect from the {@table short-term madness|DMG} table for 1 minute, using the number you rolled on the percentile dice to determine the effect, and you can't use this ability again until you finish a long rest. If you successful cast this spell, you can't use this ability again for {@dice 1d6} days.

name: Lakshay: Oni
entries: Affiliation with Lakshay grants the Ship feat {@feat Battleframe Dragoon|darkmatter24} instead of a Faction feat. Only once a Dragoon has proven their prowess do they gain the rank of Oni and the following benefits.

entries.name: Battleframe Expertise
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Piloting|DarkMatter24}) checks you make while piloting a Battleframe.

entries.name: Fearsome Reputation
entries: When you take the {@action Influence|XPHB} action, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB} and {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) checks you make against a creature that recognizes your rank of Oni.

entries.name: Oni's Skill
entries: You can add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to one damage roll or saving throw you make, or to your AC against one attack that hits you, potentially causing it to miss. Once you add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} in this way, you can't do so again until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Faction Feats
entries: Veteran adventurers are likely to make enemies across the 'Verse, but if they're lucky, they might forge some alliances too. The greatest of these alliances are likely to be with factions, which provide work, services, and connections to spacers everywhere. Factions in Dark Matter are detailed in Chapter 1: The 'Verse.

Of course, such allies don't come free. Factions generally also require work and commitment from their members, which might come in the form of small tasks, important favors for higher ranking members, or even regular obligations for the organization. For their efforts, adventurers gain specific and useful skills from their factions, as represented by Faction feats.

entries.name: Gaining a Faction Feat
entries: The GM can award you a Faction feat for joining a faction or completing a quest for one. If allegiance to a faction is important to your backstory, the GM can also replace the feat granted by your background with an appropriate Faction feat.

name: Lance Master
entries: You use maximize the effectiveness of a lance, gaining the following benefits:

entries.name: Impaled Movement
entries: While you are mounted, if you strike a creature smaller than your mount with a lance, you can push that creature until the end of your turn, you make another attack, or you move in something other than a straight line. This movement counts as if you are grappling the creature for the duration of the movement, and your mounts movement speed is reduced to half while pushing them.

entries.name: Piercing Charge
entries: When you hit an attack with a lance after traveling at least 10 feet, you can make an additional attack at another creature behind the target hit with disadvantage, as long as they are in reach of your weapon (you can move between attacks, but only in a straight line) with disadvantage. You can continue to repeat this until you miss, run out of movement, or run out of creatures in a line to hit.

entries.name: Expert Handling
entries: A lance no longer requires two-hands when you aren't mounted.

name: Laser Swordmaster
entries: You are a trained and practiced sage of the laser sword, a subtle, yet elegant weapon. As such, you gain the following benefits:

items: When you are wielding an {@item antimatter dagger|DarkMatter}, {@item laser halfsword|DarkMatter}, or {@item laser sword|DarkMatter} with which you are proficient and another creature hits you with a ranged blaster attack or an attack from one of these weapons, you can use your reaction to add your proficiency bonus to your AC for that attack, potentially causing the attack to miss you.

When you score a critical hit with an {@item antimatter dagger|DarkMatter}, {@item laser halfsword|DarkMatter}, or {@item laser sword|DarkMatter}, instead of rolling the weapon's damage dice twice, you deal the weapon's maximum damage and add the weapon's damage dice once.

name: Laser Swordsmaster
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Cauterizing Critical
entries: When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} with an {@item Antimatter Dagger|DarkMatter24}, {@item Laser Claws|DarkMatter24}, {@item Laser Sword|DarkMatter24}, or {@item Laser Greatsword|DarkMatter24}, you can rake the target with the blade. Instead of rolling the attack's damage dice twice, you add the attack's maximum damage to the roll.

entries.name: Deflect Blaster
entries: If you're holding an {@item Antimatter Dagger|DarkMatter24}, {@item Laser Claws|DarkMatter24}, {@item Laser Sword|DarkMatter24}, or {@item Laser Greatsword|DarkMatter24}, and another creature hits you with a ranged attack using a blaster, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to your {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} for this attack. If this causes the attack to miss, you can deflect the blaster bolt toward a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier of the score increased by this feat and your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or take damage as if hit by the triggering attack.

name: Last Breath*
entries: When you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can drop to 1 hit point instead. You can't use this feature again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Last Dying Breath
entries: Your physique allows you a few moments of clarity before unconsciousness, you gain the following benefits:

items: When you take damage that reduces you to 0 hit point or lower, and you are not killed outright, you get an extra turn. During that turn you can only use your action, it has to be the Attack Action (Weapon Attacks only). You then fall unconscious and must immediately roll a death saving throw. Once you used this ability you can't use it again until you've taken a long rest.

name: Last Stand
entries: Power lies latent in your blood—power that can only be released in moments of true desperation. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Ability Score Increase
entries: Increase your Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

entries.name: Out with a Bang
entries: When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, energy explodes from your body in a destructive wave. Each creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB} originating from you must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus). Creatures of your choice have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes a number of d10s of Force damage equal to twice your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and is knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only. Once the explosion happens, it can't happen again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Lasting Magic
entries: Whenever you unwillingly lose concentration on a spell, the spell's effects last until the end of your next turn, instead of ending immediately. If the spell summoned creatures with their own initiative, it lasts until the end of their next turn instead.

Additionally, whenever you cast a spell with a duration of 1 minute or longer, you may choose to double its duration, to a maximum of 24 hours. After you've done so, you may not do so again until you finish a long rest.

name: Latent Psionics
entries: Unlike others of your kind, the quiet hum of psionic power stirs in the back of your mind, flaring to life when you command it. You gain a pool of 6 psionic power points, which fuel your psionic abilities. You regain all expended power points when you finish a long rest.

You can spend power points to cast spells. When you gain this feat, you choose whether your spellcasting ability for these spells is Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma; once chosen, this selection can't be changed.

items: 0 Points: {@spell mage hand}, {@spell minor illusion}
2 Points: {@spell command}, {@spell disguise self}, {@spell silent image}
3 Points: {@spell detect thoughts}

name: Latent Psionics
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Empathy
entries: You can take the {@action Magic|XPHB} action to probe the mind of a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. You learn the creature's emotional state.

entries.name: Improved Psionic Blast
entries: Your Psionic Blast deals an extra {@damage 1d10} Psychic damage.

entries.name: Minor Kinesis
entries: You learn the {@spell Mage Hand|XPHB} cantrip, and the hand is {@condition Invisible|XPHB} when you cast the cantrip with this benefit. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell when you cast them with this property (choose when you attune to this item).

name: Lay on Hands
entries: You gain a pool of two d10 dice that you replenishes when you take a long rest.

As an action, you can touch a creature and heal it by expending dice from the pool, up to the maximum amount remaining in your pool. Roll the dice you spend, add them together, and restore a number of hit points equal to the total.

Alternatively, you can expend one dice from your pool of healing to cure the target of one disease or neutralize one poison affecting it. You can cure multiple diseases and neutralize multiple poisons with a single use of Lay on Hands, expending hit points separately for each one. This feat has no effect on undead and constructs.
If you have the {@feat Martial Arts|Adventurer} feat, you can spend 1 ki to replace one unarmed strikes with a use of this feature.
You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do so, your pool of d10s for this feature increases by two.

name: Lead from the Front
entries: Each unit you control has +2 to Power.

name: Lead the Hunt
entries: When you cast {@spell Hunter's Mark} on a target, choose a willing creature within 30 feet. That creature gains a {@damage 1d4} damage bonus to attacks against the same target for the duration of the effect.

name: Leadership
entries: You can spend 10 minutes inspiring your companions, shoring up their resolve to fight. When you do so, choose up to six friendly creatures (which can include yourself) within 30 feet of you who can see or hear you and who can understand you. Each creature can gain temporary hit points equal to your level + your Charisma modifier. A creature can't gain temporary hit points from this feat again until it has finished a short or long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Leadership
entries: You can spend 10 minutes inspiring your companions, shoring up their resolve to fight. When you do so, choose up to six friendly creatures (which can include yourself) within 30 feet of you who can see or hear you and who can understand you. Each creature can gain temporary hit points equal to your level + your Charisma modifier. A creature can't gain temporary hit points from this feat again until it has finished a short or long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Leading by Example
entries: After you perform an action, as a bonus action, you can select a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier within 30 feet of you to attempt to inspire to follow suit. If, on their subsequent turn, any of them perform the same action as you, such as attacking the same enemy, or performing the same skill check, they have advantage on any rolls involved with doing so.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Leading by Example
entries: After you perform an action, as a bonus action, you can select a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier within 30 feet of you to attempt to inspire to follow suit. If, on their subsequent turn, any of them perform the same action as you, such as attacking the same enemy, or performing the same skill check, they have advantage on any rolls involved with doing so.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Learned Caster
entries: Gain the first two available Tiers of the Learned Caster feat:
{@b The Tiers of the Learned Caster Feat:}

name: Learning from History

prerequisite.other: {@feat Linguist|TalentTrees} or {@feat Objects of Legend|TalentTrees} or {@feat Martial Adept|TalentTrees}

entries: When in a historically significant area, like a city, ruin, battlefield, or stronghold, or when preparing to enter one, you can spend 10 minutes regaling creatures around you with tales of the locale's past; Until the next long rest, you and each creature that listens to the entirety of this lesson gains advantage on initiative checks while in the area.

In addition, you can choose a number of creatures up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1) and give each of them a Historical Accuracy die (a {@dice d6}). Once within the next 8 hours, the creature can roll the die and add the result to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes. A creature can only have one Historical Accuracy die at a time and can't use more than one per long rest per location.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Learning from History

prerequisite.other: {@feat Linguist|TalentTreesMod} or {@feat Objects of Legend|TalentTreesMod} or {@feat Strategist|TalentTreesMod}

entries: When in a historically significant area, like a city, ruin, battlefield, or stronghold, or when preparing to enter one, you can spend 10 minutes regaling creatures around you with tales of the locale's past; Until the next long rest, you and each creature that listens to the entirety of this lesson gains advantage on initiative checks while in the area.

In addition, you can choose a number of creatures up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1) and give each of them a Historical Accuracy die (a {@dice d6}). Once within the next 8 hours, the creature can roll the die and add the result to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes. A creature can only have one Historical Accuracy die at a time and can't use more than one per long rest per location.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Leatherworker
entries: You have studied the secrets of Leatherworking and are an expert in its practice, gaining the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with leatherworker's tools. If you are already proficient with them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.
For the purposes of researching any special properties of a specific type of monster hide, you may use leatherworker's tools (Intelligence or Wisdom) instead of Investigation.
Your mastery of leather work has allowed you to optimize your personal storage through tweaking your clothing, belt, and bag. You gain 1 additional belt slot and 3 backpack slots.

name: Leatherworker
entries: You are an expert with {@item Leatherworker's Tools|phb}.
Scavenging leather from an animal takes you half as much time.

As part of a long rest, you can use leather pieces to augment a set of medium or heavy armor. For 8 hours, the armor doesn't cause its wearer to suffer disadvantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Leech-Craft
entries: You are skilled, according to ancient traditions, in the healing of wounds and sickness. As an action, you can spend a craft slot to tend to a creature within 5 feet of you and make a {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Medicine}) check. You can spend one use of a {@item healer's kit|PHB} to replace the {@dice d20} roll with a 10. If you succeed, the creature regains a number of hit points equal to your check result minus 10 (minimum 1 hit point).
When you reach 5th level, on a successful check you can alternatively cure the target of one disease or neutralise one poison affecting it.

name: Legacy of Scyllaea
entries: Echoes of the power your people once possessed awaken inside of you, granting you the following benefits:

items: You learn the {@spell detect magic} spell and can cast it at will, without expending a spell slot.

You can cast {@spell magic missile} once using this feature without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a long rest. When casting magic missile, whenever you would roll a d4, roll a d6 instead.

entries: Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

name: Legendary Might
entries: You have always found ways to leverage your great might for additional benefits. You gain the benefits on the table below that correspond to your Strength modifier and lower.
Should your Strength modifier increase, the benefits that you gain from this Feat also increase with your modifier:

rows: You count as one size larger for the purpose of carrying capacity, the size of creatures you can {@action Grapple}, and the weight you can push, pull, lift, or drag at one time.
You can make Strength ({@skill Intimidation}) checks in place of Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) checks.
You gain a climbing speed or a swimming speed equal to your walking speed.
Whenever you make an {@skill Athletics} check, you treat a d20 roll of 7 or lower as an 8.
When you are forced to make a Constitution saving throw, you can choose to make a Strength saving throw instead.

name: Legerdemain

prerequisite.other: {@feat Thief of Order|TalentTrees} or {@feat Thief of Propriety|TalentTrees} or {@feat Thief of Focus|TalentTrees}

entries: When you use your action to make a {@skill Sleight of Hand} check or to take the {@action Use an Object} action, you can make an additional {@skill Sleight of Hand} check or {@action Use an Object} an additional time.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Legerdemain

prerequisite.other: {@feat Thief of Order|TalentTreesMod} or {@feat Thief of Propriety|TalentTreesMod} or {@feat Thief of Focus|TalentTreesMod}

entries: When you use your action to make a {@skill Sleight of Hand} check or to take the {@action Use an Object} action, you can make an additional {@skill Sleight of Hand} check or {@action Use an Object} an additional time.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

items: Your Scoridra grows a third head. The new third head will have it's own name, personality, be of the same age and gender as the main body and will obtain all knowledge that is retained by it's siblings. In addition this new head the Scoridra may choose to be proficent in any skill it is not already proficient in.
Your melee weapon attacks gain +1 to the damage for each adjacent ally to you.
You can use 10 feet of movement to swap places with a willing, adjacent ally. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks for either of you.
When you score a critical hit with a melee weapon attack, you can roll one of the weapon's damage dice one additional time and add it to the extra damage of the critical hit.

You weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20. If they already do, then your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 18-20. If they already do, then your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 17-20.

name: Lethal Body
entries: You possess potent vampiric strength, turning your bare hands into deadly weapons.

entries.name: Crushing Blows
entries: You can deal {@damage 1d8} extra damage when you hit a target with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. The extra damage is the same type dealt by that strike.

entries.name: Iron Grip
entries: A creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on ability checks and saving throws to escape your grapple.

name: Leviathan Suit
entries: You are equipped with an advanced aqua suit bestowed upon nautilid warriors, known as a Leviathan Suit. You gain the following benefits while wearing your suit:

items: You can integrate two one-handed weapons or one two-handed weapon into your suit. When you draw an integrated weapon, it snaps to your hand and you can't be disarmed of it. You can switch which weapons are integrated when you take a long rest.

You can attempt to move through a hostile creature's space as a bonus action. When you do so, make an opposed Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check against the target. On a success, you move into the target's space and push the target up to 10 feet in any direction you choose.

name: Leviathan Suit
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Integrated Weapons
entries: You can integrate a weapon directly into your Aqua Suit, or you can integrate two weapons (one into each arm) if neither has the {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} property. When you draw an integrated weapon, it snaps to your hand and you can't be disarmed of it. You can switch which weapons are integrated when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Sonar
entries: While wearing your Aqua Suit, you have {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} with a range of 10 feet. The range increases to 30 feet if you are underwater.

name: Lewd*
entries: It's pretty simple when you think about it. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage when using Persuasion against males of any species.
When using a Bonus Action to change your size, you can be considered Small if below 3ft.

name: Ley Adept
entries: You've focused on harnessing the power of ley lines, improving your powers. You can now attune to Lesser and Moderate Mana Ley Lines, following the same rules regarding Moderate Mana Ley Lines as those for Lesser Mana Ley Lines described in the {@feat Ley-Touched|CoH-LLN} feat.

items.name: Moderate Ley Powers.
items.entry: You learn one {@filter Moderate Ley Power|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=Moderate LP} of your choice from the ones presented in this document. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can replace the ley power you learned from this feat with another {@filter Moderate Ley Power|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=Moderate LP} from the list above.

items.name: Mana Points.
items.entry: You gain two mana points, which you add to the points you have from the {@feat Ley-Touched|CoH-LLN} feat.

items.name: Mana Limit.
items.entry: You can spend up to 4 mana points on a ley power at a time.

name: Ley Expert
entries: You've become an expert on utilizing ley magic. You can now attune to Lesser, Moderate or Greater Mana Ley Lines, following the same rules regarding Greater Mana Ley Lines as those for Lesser Mana Ley Lines described in the {@feat Ley-Touched|CoH-LLN} feat.

items.name: Greater Ley Powers.
items.entry: You learn one {@filter Greater Ley Power|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=Greater LP} of your choice from the ones presented in this document. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can replace the ley power you learned from this feat with another {@filter Greater Ley Power|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=Greater LP} from the list above.

items.name: Mana Points.
items.entry: You gain two mana points, which you add to the points you have from the {@feat Ley-Touched|CoH-LLN} feat.

items.name: Mana Limit.
items.entry: You can spend up to 6 mana points on a ley power at a time.

name: Ley Initiate
entries: You see ley lines and can draw on their power. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can sense the presence of every ley line within 1 mile of your location. If you have line of sight to the line itself, it's visible to you in some obviously magical fashion.
You can tap ley lines for their inherent powers.

When you finish a short rest within 1 mile of a ley line, you can regain one expended spell slot whose level is no higher than your Intelligence or Wisdom modifier (your choice, minimum of 1st level). You can't use this ability again until you finish a long rest.

name: Ley Master
entries: You've mastered the art of attuning and drawing power from ley lines. You can now attune to Lesser, Moderate, Greater or Major Mana Ley Lines, following the same rules regarding Major Mana Ley Lines as those for Lesser Mana Ley Lines described in the {@feat Ley-Touched|CoH-LLN} feat.

items.name: Major Ley Powers.
items.entry: You learn one {@filter Major Ley Power|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=Major LP} of your choice from the ones presented in this document. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can replace the ley power you learned from this feat with another {@filter Major Ley Power|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=Major LP} from the list above.

items.name: Mana Points.
items.entry: You gain two mana points, which you add to the points you have from the {@feat Ley-Touched|CoH-LLN} feat.

items.name: Mana Limit.
items.entry: You can spend up to 8 mana points on a ley power at a time.

name: Ley-Bound
entries: You instinctively feel the flow of ley line energy and draw insight from it. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks made to track a creature overland or to forage for food and water.
When you finish a long rest within 1 mile of a ley line, you gain {@variantrule inspiration|PHB}. If unused, this {@variantrule inspiration|PHB} fades away after your next long rest.

When you finish a long rest within 1 mile of a ley line, you can infuse ley energy into a token in your possession. If you make a saving throw while you have the infused token in your possession, you can use your reaction to roll a {@dice d4} and add the result to your saving throw. You can trigger this ability after rolling the {@dice d20} but before success or failure is revealed. You can't use this ability again until you finish a long rest.

name: Ley-Touched
entries: You've studied the natural magic of the world and learnt of ways to harness it, or you might have come into contact with a ley line or nexus, an event that altered your very being.

When you gain this feat, you become attuned to a Lesser Mana Ley Line. This attunement does not count against the number of items you can attune to at a time, and it doesn't end by you being more than 100 feet away from the ley line, or if another creature attunes to the same ley line. You can only be attuned to one ley line at a time, and if you attune to a new one, the attunement with the previous one ends.

While attuned to a ley line, you always know the closest direction towards its location as long as you're on the same plane of existence as it. Over a short rest, you can attune to another Lesser Mana Ley Line while you are within the area affected by it.

{@b Lesser Ley Powers.} You learn two {@filter lesser ley powers|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=Lesser LP} of your choice from the ones presented in this document. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can replace a ley power you learned from this feat with another {@filter Lesser Ley Power|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=Lesser LP} from the list above.

{@b Ley Power DC.} If a ley power you learn from this feat or any {@filter feat that has this feat as a prerequisite|feats|source=CoH-LLN} requires a saving throw, the save's DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice when you gain this feat).

{@b Mana Points.} You gain a number of mana points equal to your proficiency bonus, representing your prowess over ley magic and your innate connection with the land. You can never have more mana points than your proficiency bonus, unless you gain extra mana points from {@filter feats that have this feat as a prerequisite|feats|source=CoH-LLN}. You can use these points only with the ley powers you gain from this feat and with any ley powers you gain from {@filter feats that have this feat as a prerequisite|feats|source=CoH-LLN}. You regain all spent mana points when you finish a long rest. In addition, once per day when you finish a short rest within the area affected by a ley line you are attuned to, you can choose to regain spent mana points up to your proficiency bonus.
{@b Mana Limit.} You can spend up to 2 mana points on a ley power at a time.

name: Liar's Liar
entries: You can use your {@skill Deception} bonus for your {@skill Insight} checks and you have advantage on checks to determine if someone is lying or attempting to pass themselves off as a different person.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Liar's Liar
entries: You can use your {@skill Deception} bonus for your {@skill Insight} checks and you have advantage on checks to determine if someone is lying or attempting to pass themselves off as a different person.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Liderança
entries: O personagem é um indivíduo que as pessoas desejam seguir. Ele tem se esforçado um pouco para recrutar parceiros e seguidores.

{@b Beneficio:} Seu personagem é capaz de atrair companheiros leais e seguidores devotados, subordinados que o auxiliarão. O Mestre pode indicar todas as informações sobre os tipos de parceiros e a quantidade de seguidores que seu personagem consegue recrutar.

name: Lifelong Learner
entries: You have made a vow to never stop learning, no matter how educated you are. You gain the benefits from the table below that correspond to your Intelligence modifier and lower.
If your Intelligence modifier increases, the benefits you gain from this Feat also increase with your modifier:

rows: You learn to speak, read, and write one additional language of your choice.
You can make Intelligence ({@skill Persuasion}) checks in place of Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) checks.
You gain proficiency in either {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, or {@skill Religion}.
Whenever you make an Intelligence check to recall your knowledge of something, you treat a d20 roll of 7 or lower as an 8.
Whenever you are forced to make a Wisdom saving throw, you can choose to make an Intelligence saving throw instead.

name: Lifelong Learner
entries: You have made a vow to never stop learning, no matter how old or intelligent you become. You gain the benefits in the table below depending on your Intelligence modifier. Should your Intelligence modifier increase, through the Ability Score Increase feature or magic item, you gain additional benefits.

rows: You learn to speak, read, and write one additional language of your choice.
You gain proficiency with one set of {@item artisan's tools|phb} of your choice.
You gain proficiency in a skill of your choice
Choose one of your skill proficiencies. You treat a roll of 7 or lower on the {@dice d20} as an 8 when you make an ability check with that skill.
When you are forced to make a Wisdom saving throw, you can choose to make an Intelligence saving throw instead.

name: Lifesaver
repeatableNote: Yes, but you must choose the other option for miraculous recovery

items.name: Emergency Attention
items.entry: Immediately before you take the help action to attempt to stabilize a creature you can halve the creature's negative hit points (The hit points must be less than zero). You can use this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and regain all uses on a long rest.

items.name: Miraculous Recovery
items.entry: For every healing die that rolls the highest number it can roll, add a die of that type. This only applies when you are healed or when you heal a creature other than you (choose when you gain this feat).

name: Light Armor Master
entries: You have practiced moving in light armor to gain the following benefits:

items: Your speed increases by 5 feet while you aren't wearing medium or heavy armor.
Once on each of your turns, you can choose for a 5-foot portion of your movement to not provoke opportunity attacks.

name: Light Armor Master
