items: When you cast a sorcerer spell you can spend one hit dice. If you do, the expended spell slot counts as a spell slot of one level higher (to a maximum of 9th), and you take 1d6 necrotic damage. This damage ignores resistance and immunity.

name: Redirection
entries: When you deflect an attack using your {@feat Martial Arts|Adventurer} and reduce the damage to 0, you can cause that attack to target one creature of your choice, other than the attacker, that you can see within range of the attack, using the same attack roll and damage.

name: Reflexive Tattoo
entries: You can reflexively use your tattoos in response to a threat.
{@b Benefit}:

items: You may now use the powers of your tattoo(s) also as a bonus action during an encounter, or if you they already can be used as a bonus action as a reaction.
Add 2 to your tattoo pool.

entries: {@b Normal}: Using a tattoo power is an action.

name: Reflexos de Combate
entries: O personagem é capaz de reagir rápida e repetidamente contra os oponentes que baixam a própria guarda.

{@b Beneficio:} Quando os oponentes se descuidam e baixam a guarda, o personagem poderá realizar uma quantidade de ataques de oportunidade equivalente ao seu modificador de Destreza. No entanto, somente é possível executar um ataque de oportunidade em cada situação capaz de provocá-los.

name: Reforged
entries: You have meditated and philosophized extensively on what it means to be a living creature. You were forged, not born, it is true, but you have a living soul. By taking this feat you have come to an epiphany that radically alters your body to reflect the change to your identity. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your body sheds any armor it once had, leaving you a humanoid comprised solely of livewood musculature. You no longer benefit from the Integrated Armor, Model Type, or Remodeling racial traits. Because of this, you may now wear armor.

You lose any feat that requires a specific warforged model type to function or had them listed as a prerequisite. In their place you gain an Ability Score Improvement, as the class feature, for each feat lost this way.
You retain the ability to use warforged components, except those that require attunement by warforged with specific model types.
If your game uses the Construct Nature variant rules, you gain the normal effect of healing magic from all sources.
You gain proficiency in two of the following skills: Deception, Insight, Persuasion.

name: Regal Presence
entries: You begin to grow into a myconid sovereign. The range of your rapport spores increases to 150 feet, and you can allow creatures you choose within that radius to telepathically respond to you and communicate with one another. Your maximum lifespan increases to 250 years.

You also learn the {@spell command} and {@spell calm emotions} spells, and can cast each once per long rest, though you can target plants with these spells any number of times. Each spell cast in this way has a range of 300 feet and requires no components; any requisite communication is carried through your Rapport Spores.

name: Rejuvenating Gorge
entries: You are able to repair yourself and replace damaged flesh by gorging on unusually large amounts of food. During a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can consume up to 7 days worth of food to regain hit points equal to your Constitution modifier × the number of days' worth of food you consumed. At 12th level, you can eat up to 10 days worth of food, and at 16th level you can eat up to 14 days worth of food. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, after which you must take a long rest before you can recover hit points via a rejuvenating gorge again.

items: When you miss an attack roll against a target, you gain a +1 cumulative bonus to attack rolls you make against that target until you hit within the next minute, or you attack another target. The maximum bonus to attack rolls you can receive from this feature is +3.

Every successful consecutive attack roll you make against a target adds a cumulative +1 to your damage rolls. This bonus damage only applies to damage rolls from attacks you make against that target and is lost when you miss your target or you attack another target. The maximum bonus damage you can have from this feature is +5.
You can use your use bonus action heighten your reflexes. When you do, you can make up to two opportunity attacks without using your reaction until the start of your next turn.

name: Relentless Protector
entries: Your faith guides you to shield others from harm, throwing yourself into harm's way with relentless dedication to keep those around you from harm. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain the {@optfeature Protection} Fighting Style. If you already know the {@optfeature Protection} Fighting Style, you can learn another Fighting Style of your choice from the {@filter Fighter Fighting Styles|optionalfeatures|feature type=fs:f}.

name: Reliable Skill
entries: Choose an ability score. For any skill check using this ability and in which you are proficient, if your total for that check is less than your chosen ability score, you can use that score in place of the total. You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do so, you must choose a different ability score.

name: Remarkable Recovery
entries: Your body has the ability to recover quickly from terrible injuries, and is unusually receptive to healing magic. You gain the following benefits:

items: When you are successfully stabilized while dying, you regain hit points equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).
Whenever you regain hit points as a result of a spell, potion, or class feature (but not this feat), you regain additional hit points equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).

name: Remedy Injury
entries: You can use your knowledge of medicine to treat minor status conditions. As an action, you can use 5 charges of a {@item healer's kit|PHB} to tend to a creature, ending a temporary conditon afflicting it. These conditions can be {@condition blinded}, {@condition deafened}, or {@condition frightened}.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Remedy Injury
entries: You can use your knowledge of medicine to treat minor status conditions. As an action, you can use 5 charges of a {@item healer's kit|PHB} to tend to a creature, ending a temporary condition afflicting it. These conditions can be {@condition blinded}, {@condition deafened}, or {@condition frightened}.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Remise
entries: When you attack a creature with a light melee weapon during your turn and miss, you can use your bonus action to make another attack with the weapon against the same creature.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Remise
entries: When you attack a creature with a light melee weapon during your turn and miss, you can use your bonus action to make another attack with the weapon against the same creature.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Repairer
entries: The character can, when taking a short rest, spend a number of minutes of said rest tinkering with weapons (the number of minutes spent is the number of weapons tinkered with times 10). These weapons will have a bonus of +1 to hit on the next number of attack rolls made with the weapon equal to the character's proficiency modifier.

name: Repository of Lore
entries: Through your vast and detailed study of lore and rote memorization of primary sources, you have become a living historical archive. As an action, you can consult your accumulated knowledge on a topic. To do so is like consulting a bestiary, travel guide, or library inside your own mind. The DM will give you the text of the relevant entry, though it may not always be immediately or obviously applicable to your situation. You cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

For example, you might use this feature to quote a biology book mentioning the poisonous fangs of a creature you're fighting, or recall a legend that the ancient men of Ardven Hall used to build their houses deep underground.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Repository of Lore
entries: Through your vast and detailed study of lore and rote memorization of primary sources, you have become a living historical archive. As an action, you can consult your accumulated knowledge on a topic. To do so is like consulting a bestiary, travel guide, or library inside your own mind. The DM will give you the text of the relevant entry, though it may not always be immediately or obviously applicable to your situation. You cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

For example, you might use this feature to quote a biology book mentioning the poisonous fangs of a creature you're fighting, or recall a legend that the ancient men of Ardven Hall used to build their houses deep underground.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Reptilian Instincts
entries: You have inherited the wisdom & cunning from your ancient ancestors, and it enhances your abilities. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your eyes improve, and become accustomed to darkness. You gain {@sense darkvision} up to 60 feet.

You learn how to make any simple or martial weapon using your Cunning Artisan feature in addition to the previous options. Furthermore, you can also create {@dice 1d4} pieces of ammunition for one of these weapons instead.
You gain proficiency in Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival}). If you already had proficiency in the skill you chose, you gain Expertise instead.

name: Reptilian Regeneration
entries: You live a dangerous lifestyle, and your body had to adapt to survive, allowing you to heal grievous wounds.

items: On a short rest, if you choose to expend hit dice, you gain an additional amount of hit points equal to your proficiency bonus per hit die rolled. Additionally, you regrow severed body parts (fingers, legs, tail, and so on) within {@dice 1d4} days.

As a bonus action, you can release a surge of regeneration in your body. You regain a number of hit points equal to {@dice 2d6} + half your level. You can't regain hit points this way again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Reptilian Regeneration
entries: You live a dangerous livestyle, and your body had to adapt to survive, allowing you to heal grievous wounds.

items: Increase your Constitution score by 1, to a max. of 20.

On a short rest, if you choose to expend Hit Dice, you regain an additional amount of hit points equal to your proficiency bonus per Hit Die rolled. You regrow severed body parts (fingers, legs, tail, and so on) within 1d4 days.

You can release a surge of regeneration in your body as a bonus action. You regain a number of hit points equal to 2d6 + half your level (rounded down). You can't regain hit points this way again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Reptiloid
entries: You bear the abrasive skin, slitted eyes, and forked tongue of a reptile, which grant you the following benefits:

items: You can go twice as long as other humans without eating or drinking.
You can speak, read, and write Draconic.

You can use your action to spit acid from your mouth. When you do so, make a ranged attack roll against a creature within 30 feet. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d8} acid damage for each point of your proficiency bonus. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Reptiloid
entries: You bear the abrasive skin, slitted eyes, and forked tongue of a reptile, which grant the following benefits.

entries.name: Acid Spit
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with spitting a lob of acid from your mouth. This is a special ranged attack with a range of 60 feet. You are proficient with it, and you add your Dexterity modifier to its attack and damage rolls. On a hit, the target takes {@dice 1d10} {@item Acid|XPHB} damage. This damage increases by {@dice 1d10} when you reach character levels 5 ({@dice 2d10}), 11 ({@dice 3d10}), and 17 ({@dice 4d10}).
You can use your Acid Spit a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Reptilian Resistance
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Acid, Fire, or Poison damage (choose when you select this species).

name: Reptiloid
entries: You bear the abrasive skin, slitted eyes, and split tongue of a reptile—perhaps due to a dragonborn or kobold parent—which grant you the following racial traits:

entries.name: Acid Spit
entries: When you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with a lob of acid from your mouth. This is a special ranged attack with a range of 30 feet. You are proficient with it, and you add your Dexterity modifier to its attack and damage rolls. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d10} acid damage. This damage increases by {@dice 1d10} when you reach 5th level ({@dice 2d10}), 11th level ({@dice 3d10}), and 17th level ({@dice 4d10}).
You can use your Acid Spit a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Researcher
entries: If you have reference materials or other similar resources, you can add half your proficiency bonus (rounded up) to Intelligence checks that you aren't proficient with.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Researcher
entries: If you have reference materials or other similar resources, you can add half your proficiency bonus (rounded up) to Intelligence checks that you aren't proficient with.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Resilient
entries: Choose one ability score. You gain proficiency in saving throws using the chosen ability.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Resilient
entries: Choose one ability score. You gain proficiency in saving throws using the chosen ability.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Resilient

choose.entry: Increase the chosen ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

entries: Choose one ability score. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in saving throws using the chosen ability.

name: Resist Death
entries: When you are reduced to 0 hit points and would fall unconscious, you can instead remain conscious. You still must make death saving throws, and you suffer the normal effects of taking damage while at 0 hit points. At the start of each of your turns, you gain a level of exhaustion if you at 0 hit points and conscious.
If you have the Rage feat, you do not gain the levels of exhaustion until your rage ends.

name: Resistant
entries: Choose one of the following damage types: acid, cold, fire, lighting, poison, or thunder. You gain resistance to damage of the chosen type.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Resistant
entries: Choose one of the following damage types: acid, cold, fire, lighting, poison, or thunder. You gain resistance to damage of the chosen type.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Resolute Caster
entries: Your magic takes on a life of its own when it matters most. Your spells with a duration of concentration remain in effect after you lose concentration until the start of your next turn. This is true whether you lost concentration from taking damage, from being knocked unconscious, or even from being killed. (In the case of your death, the spell ends at the point when your next turn would have begun, if you were alive to take it.)

name: Resolution of the Syndicate
entries: Membership in the Ebon Syndicate provides perks—one of which is the motivation that comes with the understanding that the Syndicate kills those who fail too often. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Quick Strike
entries: On your first turn after an {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} roll, add {@dice 1d4} to the first damage roll you make. This extra damage increases to {@dice 2d4} at character level 9, and to {@dice 4d4} at character level 16.

entries.name: Resilient
entries: Your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum increases by an amount equal to your character level when you gain this feat. Whenever you gain a character level thereafter, your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum increases by an additional 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}.

name: Resourceful
entries: You've always hated leaving anything to waste and have always made sure you get the most out of any situation.

items: You gain proficiency in the {@item harvesting kit|HHHVI} and the {@item herbalism kit|PHB}.
You ignore any penalties for harvesting a creature that died a {@book particularly violent death|HHHVI|2|Particularly violent deaths}.
Both {@book appraising|HHHVI|2|Appraising} and {@book harvesting|HHHVI|2|Harvesting} a creature take half the time than it normally would.

name: Resuscitation
entries: You can attempt to resuscitate a humanoid or beast, which recently died. If a creature has been dead for one minute or less, and still contains most, or all, of its vital organs, you can attempt to conduct surgery on it. The surgery requires 1 hour to complete and uses up 10 charges of a {@item healer's kit|PHB}. If the surgery is completed without interruption, the creature is brought back to life at 1 hit point. It also suffers from three levels of exhaustion and can't be brought back to life by the use of this talent again until it finishes a long rest. If the surgery is interrupted before completion, the time taken by the surgery does not count against the time limit of spells such as revivify.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Resussitation
entries: You can attempt to resuscitate a humanoid or beast, which recently died. If a creature has been dead for one minute or less, and still contains most, or all, of its vital organs, you can attempt to conduct surgery on it. The surgery requires 1 hour to complete and uses up 10 charges of a {@item healer's kit|PHB}. If the surgery is completed without interruption, the creature is brought back to life at 1 hit point. It also suffers from three levels of exhaustion and can't be brought back to life by the use of this talent again until it finishes a long rest. If the surgery is interrupted before completion, the time taken by the surgery does not count against the time limit of spells such as revivify.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Retaliation
entries: When you are hit by a melee attack, you can use your reaction to attack that creature immediately after its attack, provided that you can see the creature and that you can reach it with a melee attack.
If you have the {@feat Favored Enemy|Adventurer} feat and the creature is the type of your favored enemy, you can use this feature even if the attack missed you.

name: Retriever
entries: You are a natural at seeking and returning desired items. You gain advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) checks

name: Reveler
entries: You are the life of the party. Your hedonistic indulgences, be they drinking, feasting, or debauchery, are sure to lead others to follow.

items: You gain advantage on Constitution saving throws against poison from alcohol.

You gain proficiency in one of the following musical instruments: {@item pan flute|phb|pan pipes}, {@item flute|phb|double flute}, {@item lyre|phb}, {@item drum|phb}, or your voice as if it were a musical instrument.

When you are in a social area, such as a market square, fighting pit, or an inn, populated with ten or more creatures that can see and hear you, you can make a {@skill Performance} (Charisma) skill check against a DC of 5–20 (at the GM's discretion based on the crowd). If you succeed, for the next hour you have advantage on any ability check to interact socially with a creature in the area. If you fail, you cannot use this feature in the same area for 24 hours. Any creature that can't be {@condition charmed} is immune to these effects.

name: Reveling Fool
entries: You joined a troupe of madcap revelers and learned to take on the guise of a fool, channeling otherworldly laughter and joviality. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Fool's Mask
entries: By donning a jovial mask and a fool's, jester's, or clown's costume, you take on a new identity that hides your own. In the guise of the fool, you can get away with minor transgressions against people in positions of authority or station.

entries.name: Jester's Repartee
entries: You always have the {@spell Tasha's Hideous Laughter|XPHB|Hideous Laughter} spell prepared, and your spellcasting ability for it is Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma (choose the ability when you select this feat). You can cast it once without Material components or a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have.

name: Reward
entries: You choose a reward (see {@book Chapter 4|TLotRR|3|Rewards}).

entries.name: Special
entries: You may take this feature multiple times.

name: Rifle Master
entries: Rifles are complex weapons, but you know just how to make every shot count. You gain the following benefits when wielding a rifle or carbine:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to damage rolls with these weapons.
You can reroll 1s and 2s to damage with these weapons.
If you roll a critical hit or deal a killing blow with these weapons, you can use your reaction to take an additional shot at a creature within 10 feet of the creature hit.
The normal range of these weapons increases by 10, and the long range increases by 30.

name: Rigor

prerequisite.other: {@feat Heedful|TalentTrees} or {@feat Memetic Memory|TalentTrees} or {@feat Predict Strike|TalentTrees}

entries: Once per short rest you can replace a roll you make for an {@skill Investigation} check with a 20. You can do so after you make the roll, but before you know if the check succeeded or failed.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Rigor

prerequisite.other: {@feat Heedful|TalentTreesMod} or {@feat Memetic Memory|TalentTreesMod} or {@feat Predict Strike|TalentTreesMod}

entries: Once per short rest you can replace a roll you make for an {@skill Investigation} check with a 20. You can do so after you make the roll, but before you know if the check succeeded or failed.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Rime Hydromancer
entries: You have learned techniques to direct your hydromancy through ice and snow, and to direct cold spells through bodies of water, gaining the following benefits:

items: You learn the {@spell water walk|PHB} spell and cast it once without expending a spell slot or providing material components. When you cast the spell in this way, it is only capable of targeting yourself, only allows you to move across the surface of liquid water, and leaves shards of ice in your wake. You regain the ability to cast this spell in this way when you finish a long rest.
You can treat a body of snow or ice as a body of water when casting spells with the hydromancy tag.
When you cast a spell that deals cold damage, it gains the hydromancy tag with a hydromancy radius of 30 feet.
While you are fully submerged in water, you have resistance to cold damage.

name: Rime Hydromancer
entries: You have learned techniques to direct your hydromancy through ice and snow, and to direct cold spells through bodies of water, gaining the following benefits:

items: You learn the {@spell water walk|PHB} spell and cast it once without expending a spell slot or providing material components. When you cast the spell in this way, it is only capable of targeting yourself, only allows you to move across the surface of liquid water, and leaves shards of ice in your wake. You regain the ability to cast this spell in this way when you finish a long rest.
You can treat a body of snow or ice as a body of water when casting spells with the hydromancy tag.
When you cast a spell that deals cold damage, it gains the hydromancy tag with a hydromancy radius of 30 feet.
While you are fully submerged in water, you have resistance to cold damage.

name: Rimecaster

prerequisite.other: A race or background from a cold climate

entries: You are from an area with a cold climate and have learned to adapt your magic to reflect your heritage. You gain the following benefits:

items: When you cast a {@filter spell that deals damage|spells|source=|damage type=acid;bludgeoning;cold;fire;force;lightning;necrotic;piercing;poison;psychic;radiant;slashing;thunder}, you can use a reaction to change the type of damage the spell deals to cold damage.

When you cast a {@filter spell that deals cold damage|spells|source=|damage type=cold}, you gain resistance to cold damage until the start of your next turn. If you already have resistance to cold damage, you are immune to cold damage until the start of your next turn instead.

name: Ring-Bound
entries: You have acquired a ring-magic-imbued ring as a token of respect. You gain the following benefits.

items: You have advantage on saving throws against transmutation spells.

You can physically bind your ring token to a weapon with 1 hour of work that can be completed during a short rest. While the ring is attached to the weapon, you can use a bonus action to make the weapon magical until the start of your next turn. After activating this ability twice, you must complete a short or long rest before using it again.

Ring wardens and others who respect the traditions of ring magic are favorably disposed toward you. Their starting attitude toward you automatically improves by one step, and you have advantage on Charisma checks related to social interaction with such creatures.

name: Ring-bound
entries: You have acquired a magic-imbued ring as a token of respect. You gain the following benefits from the ring:

items: You have advantage on saving throws against transmutation spells.

You can physically bind your ring to a weapon with 1 hour of work that can be completed during a short rest. While the ring is attached to the weapon, you can use a bonus action to make the weapon magical until the start of your next turn. After activating this ability twice, you must finish a short or long rest before using it again.

{@class wizard||Ring wardens|Ring Warden|KPDM} and others who respect the traditions of ring magic are favorably disposed toward you. Their starting attitude toward you automatically improves by one step, and you have advantage on Charisma checks related to social interaction with such individuals.

name: Rising Blossom Sectary
entries: You are a courageous member of the Rising Blossoms, a faction of rebels and iconoclasts dedicated to changing the world for the betterment of the people. You gain the following benefits:
You gain proficiency in the Stealth skill.

items: When you make a saving throw to avoid or end the {@condition charmed} or {@condition frightened} condition, you can grant yourself advantage on the save. You can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

When you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can use your reaction to target one creature within 30 feet of you that is {@condition charmed} or {@condition frightened} by the creature you hit; the condition ends for that creature.

name: Rites
entries: You have learned the basic rites and sacraments of your faith. By spending 1 hour in prayer and expending 15 gp worth of powdered silver, you can sanctify a vial of {@item holy water|PHB}. It retains its purity for up to 24 hours, before reverting to normal water.

In addition, your pleas to the gods to grant divine guidance. As an action, you can give a blessing to a number of creatures of your choice that can hear you equal to your Wisdom modifier. Each of these creatures can add {@dice 1d4} to the result of an ability check that it makes within the next 10 minutes. Once you have provided this blessing you cannot do so again until you complete a long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Rites
entries: You have learned the basic rites and sacraments of your faith. By spending 1 hour in prayer and expending 15 gp worth of powdered silver, you can sanctify a vial of {@item holy water|PHB}. It retains its purity for up to 24 hours, before reverting to normal water.

In addition, your pleas to the gods to grant divine guidance. As an action, you can give a blessing to a number of creatures of your choice that can hear you equal to your Wisdom modifier. Each of these creatures can add {@dice 1d4} to the result of an ability check that it makes within the next 10 minutes. Once you have provided this blessing you cannot do so again until you complete a long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Rites of Revenge
entries: You are able to use minor mysticism in your pursuit of those who have wronged you. You learn the {@spell true strike} cantrip and can cast it with a bonus action instead of an action, but afterwards you must finish a short or long rest before you can cast it with a bonus action again. You also learn the {@spell hunter's mark} spell, which you can cast twice at its lowest possible spell level without expending a spell slot.
You regain all expended castings of {@spell hunter's mark} when you finish a long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

name: Ritual Caster
entries: Choose a class: {@class bard}, {@class sorcerer}, {@class warlock}, or {@class wizard}. You acquire a ritual book containing two 1st-level ritual spells of your choice from the chosen class and you learn to cast these spells as rituals. You must be holding the book to do so. Your spellcasting ability for these spells is the same as that of the chosen class. You can take this option multiple times, but must choose a new class each time.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Ritual Caster
entries: Choose a class: {@class artificer|TCE}, {@class bard}, {@class sorcerer}, {@class warlock}, or {@class wizard}. You acquire a ritual book containing two 1st-level ritual spells of your choice from the chosen class and you learn to cast these spells as rituals. You must be holding the book to do so. Your spellcasting ability for these spells is the same as that of the chosen class. You can take this option multiple times, but must choose a new class each time.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Ritual Caster
entries: You have learned a number of spells that you can cast as rituals. These spells are written in a ritual book, which you must have in hand while casting one of them.
Any spells that take a minute or more to cast are also considered a ritual.

When you choose this feat, you acquire a ritual book holding two 1st-level spells of your choice. Choose one of the following classes: {@filter bard|spells|level=1|class=bard|components & miscellaneous=ritual|source=yastah}, {@filter cleric|spells|level=1|class=cleric|components & miscellaneous=ritual|source=yastah}, {@filter druid|spells|level=1|class=druid|components & miscellaneous=ritual|source=yastah}, {@filter sorcerer|spells|level=1|class=sorcerer|components & miscellaneous=ritual|source=yastah}, {@filter warlock|spells|level=1|class=warlock|components & miscellaneous=ritual|source=yastah}, or {@filter wizard|spells|level=1|class=wizard|components & miscellaneous=ritual|source=yastah}. You must choose your spells from that class's spell list, and the spells you choose must have the ritual tag. The class you choose also determines your spellcasting ability for these spells: Charisma for bard, sorcerer, or warlock; Wisdom for cleric or druid; or Intelligence for wizard.

If you come across a spell in written form, such as a magical spell scroll or a wizard's spellbook, you might be able to add it to your ritual book. The spell must be on the spell list for the class you chose, the spell's level can be no higher than half your level (rounded up), and it must have the ritual tag. The process of copying the spell into your ritual book takes 2 hours per level of the spell, and costs 50 gp per level. The cost represents material components you expend as you experiment with the spell to master it, as well as the fine inks you need to record it.

name: Ritual Collector
entries: If you come across a ritual spell in written form, such as a spell scroll or a wizard's spellbook, you might be able to add it to your ritual book if it is on the spell list of a class you've chosen with ritual caster and the spell's level is no higher than half your level (rounded up). The process of copying the spell into your ritual book takes 2 hours and 50 gp per level of the spell.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Ritual Collector
entries: If you come across a ritual spell in written form, such as a spell scroll or a wizard's spellbook, you might be able to add it to your ritual book if it is on the spell list of a class you've chosen with ritual caster and the spell's level is no higher than half your level (rounded up). The process of copying the spell into your ritual book takes 2 hours and 50 gp per level of the spell.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Roaming Bones
entries: Additionally, you can use a bonus action to detach or re-attach one of your hands, which allows the hand to wander freely by walking on its fingertips. This detached hand has a movement speed and climb speed of 30 feet, and can move up, down, and across vertical surfaces and upside down along ceilings. The hand has a Strength score of 5, a hit point maximum equal to twice your total character level, and otherwise uses your statistics and AC. You cannot detach a hand in this way while using your Them Bones trait, or use Them Bones while a hand is detached.

You have a psychic link with your detached hand, and can command it to move or take actions on your turn with no additional action from you. A hand detached in this way retains animation up to 1,000 feet away from you. A detached hand can take the {@action Dodge}, {@action Disengage}, {@action Dash}, or {@action Help} actions, but no other actions.

You mentally receive visual and auditory information from the detached hand, which can see and hear as any other creature, in addition to having darkvision out to 30 feet. While the hand is detached, you know its exact location relative to you, as long as you are on the same plane of existence.

name: Rod Expert
entries: You've mastered the use of a {@item Rod|XPHB} as an Arcane Focus. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Close-Ranged Focus
entries: If the target of a cantrip you cast using a {@item Rod|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} is within 20 feet of you when you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll, even if the new roll is a 1 or a 2.

entries.name: Unshakeable Casting
entries: When you make a ranged spell attack roll while using a {@item Rod|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}, you do not have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the roll if you are within 5 feet of an enemy.

entries.name: Rough & Tumble
entries: When you make a ranged spell attack while using a {@item Rod|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to make a melee attack with your {@item Rod|XPHB}. It counts as a {@item Club|XPHB} for the purposes of the attack.

name: Roguean
entries: You hail from an icy, desolate world, thrown away from its home star by some catastrophic event. Surviving the interminable harshness of your rogue world gives you the following benefits:

items: You have resistance to cold damage.
You take no damage from the extreme temperatures of space and other harsh environments.

You have {@sense darkvision}, the ability to see in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

name: Roguean
entries: You hail from an icy, desolate world, thrown away from its home star by some catastrophic event. Surviving the interminable harshness of your home gives you the following benefits.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@spell Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Cold Resistance
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage.

entries.name: Extremophile
entries: You take no damage from cold Extreme Temperatures (see Glossary). Extremely hot conditions affect you normally.

name: Roguean
entries: You hail from an icy, desolate land, prone to dramatic swings in temperature. Surviving the interminable harshness of your home gives you the following racial traits:

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You can see in {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} within 60 feet of you as if it were {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light}, and in darkness as if it were {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light}. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

entries.name: Cold Resistance
entries: You have resistance to cold damage.

entries.name: Extremophile
entries: You can tolerate temperatures as low as -100 degrees Fahrenheit and as high as 300 degrees Fahrenheit.

name: Roguish Initiate
entries: You have spent time honing talents associated with the criminal underworld. You gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Cunning Adept
entries: Choose one of the following actions: {@action Dash}, {@action Hide}, or {@action Use an Object}. You can take that action as a bonus action on each of your turns.

entries.name: Thieves' Cant
entries: You learn to speak the jargon, write secret symbols of, and decode messages in {@language Thieves' Cant}.

entries.name: Arm's Length
entries: When you are targeted by a melee weapon attack, as a reaction you actively keep your attacker at arm's length. The attack against you has disadvantage and the attacking creature may not make attacks of opportunity against you until the end of your next turn. You may use Arm's Length a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. Use of Arm's Length is recovered when you complete a long rest.

entries.name: Recuperate
entries: You draw on your fighting spirit and push on fighting. As a bonus action, You recover 2d4 + your character level hit points. Once you use Recuperate in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Swiftcast
entries: You hasten the casting of a spell. You may cast a spell with a casting time of an action as a bonus action. Once you use swiftcast in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Lucid Dreaming
entries: When you cast a spell, you can cause a surge of potency in your magics. You double your proficiency bonus to your spell attack roll or spell save DC for that spell until the start of your next turn. Once you use lucid dreaming in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Arm's Length
entries: When you are targeted by a melee weapon attack, as a reaction you actively keep your attacker at arm's length. The attack against you has disadvantage and the attacking creature may not make attacks of opportunity against you until the end of your next turn. You may use Arm's Length a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. Use of Arm's Length is recovered when you complete a long rest.

entries.name: Peoloton
entries: As a bonus action, you inspire all allied creatures within 30ft. of you with a battle cry or war song. You and all allied creatures have their base movement increased by 10ft. until the start of your next turn. You may use Peloton a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. Use of Peloton is recovered when you complete a long rest.

entries.name: Cleric Stance
entries: When you cast a spell which recovers hit points you may change the healing into radiant damage instead. The spell deals bonus damage equal to your spell casting ability modifier and the healing must require a die roll to be affected by cleric stance. You may use cleric stance a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. Use of cleric stance is recovered when you complete a long rest.

entries.name: Surecast
entries: When you are hit by an attack, as a reaction you can choose to pass on any concentration check and saving throws against effects that forcibly move you until the start of your next turn. Once you use Surecast in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Provoke
entries: As a bonus action. you call out to a creature you can see within 30ft. of you and challenge them to focus on you. The creature has disadvantage on attacks made against creatures other than you until the start of your next turn. You may use provoke a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. Use of provoke is recovered when you complete a long rest.

entries.name: Rampart
entries: As a reaction, you can reinforce your defenses against an incoming onslaught. Damage you receive is reduced by your proficiency bonus until the start of your next turn. Once you use rampart in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a short rest.

name: Rolling Thunder
entries: You can lend your tumbling momentum to a cannonballing assault. When you move at least 10 feet while curled up on your turn, you can take the Attack action while in your defensive ball. The only attacks you make while in the ball are unarmed strikes that deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier on a hit. For every 5 additional feet you move before making an attack in this way, you gain a +1 bonus to the attack and damage rolls on the attack.

items: You gain proficiency with ropes and nets. Proficiency with ropes allows you to add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to craft, repair, or dismantle ropes and objects made of rope such as nets, traps, ladders, and bridges. In addition, you can add your proficiency bonus to ability checks made when interacting with rope, such as when attempting to remove bindings, climbing with ropes, or crossing unstable rope bridges. Finally, you add your proficiency bonus plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the DC of any ability checks made by a creature to free itself or another creature from bindings, traps, or nets you have made with rope.
You can make bindings or release any bindings you have made as a bonus action. In addition, you can use rope or a net to restrain a grappled creature as a bonus action.
Attacking at long range or being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on your attack rolls with nets.

name: Royal Authority
entries: You are a leader by nature and your voice and stature makes that clear to everyone. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Dexterity, Wisdom or Charisma score by 1, up to a maximum of 20.
Your proficiency bonus is double for any check you make with the Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) skill.

As an action, you can let your voice boon to confirm your superiority. Each creature of your choice within 30 ft. of you has to make a Charisma saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier). On a failed save, a creature becomes {@condition frightened} of you for 1 minute. If the {@condition frightened} target takes any damage, it can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success. You can't use this feature again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Royal Commission
entries: Your queen has taken inspiration from the outside world, and can motivate the drones of the hive to create substances and structures that were previously beyond their understanding. At the end of each long rest, choose one of the following spells: {@spell find familiar|PHB}, {@spell goodberry|PHB}, or {@spell web|PHB}. You can cast the chosen spell once, and regain the ability to do so the next time you choose it after finishing a long rest. When you cast each of the spells, they are subject to the following changes:

items: A familiar you create by casting the {@spell find familiar|PHB} spell in this way is made of the same materials as your body, and animated by a group of your drones in a facsimile of its chosen form. As an extension of yourself, its creature type is humanoid. The familiar drops to 0 hit points at the end of a long rest as the drones rejoin your body to recuperate.
A creature that willingly eats a berry you create when casting the {@spell goodberry|PHB} spell in this way regards you warmly for 10 minutes, and is charmed for the duration.

When you cast the {@spell web|PHB} spell in this way, you can expend two of your Hit Dice to command a group of drones forth from your body to assist with its creation. If you do so, the spell dos not require concentration for that casting.

name: Royalty Revealed
entries: Your kin belong to a bloodline of kings, but they have learnt to hide from their enemies in the twilight years of their kingdom. Should you choose to reveal your heritage, your noble bearing will cause your allies to cast away their doubts. You reveal yourself by shouting an ancestral battle-cry, or unsheathing a weapon of high lineage, or by showing a device or coat of arms.

items: As a bonus action, you can choose to reveal your lineage. When you do so, choose a number of friendly creatures (which can include yourself) within 30 feet of you who can see or hear you, up to twice your proficiency bonus. Until the end of your next turn, each creature gains advantage on attack rolls and Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) checks, and is immune to being {@condition frightened}. It also gains temporary hit points equal to your choice of your Strength or Charisma modifier (minimum 1). These temporary hit points last until they are depleted or the creature finishes a short or long rest. Once you use this virtue, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Ruffian
entries: You have turned kicking people when they're down into an art form. You gain the following benefits:

items: {@b Ability Score Increase.} Increase your Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution by 1, to a maximum of 20.

{@b Painful Critical.} When you score a critical hit with a melee weapon attack against a creature, it must make a Constitution saving throw or become {@condition blinded} or dazed† until the start of your next turn. This does not affect undead, constructs, or other creatures that can feel no pain.
Gain the {@b Dirty Strike} special ability (below)

entries.name: Dirty Strike
entries: {@italic Active Ability (Special)}

When you make a melee weapon attack, you can follow up with a dirty trick (a knee to the gut, handful of sand to eyes, etc.). The creature must make a Constitution saving throw. On failure, they become your choice of {@condition blinded} or dazed{@sup †} (your choice) for 1 minute. The target can repeat its saving throw at the end of each of their turns. A creature can spend their action treating their condition to automatically pass the saving throw. Once you use this against a target once, they are ready for subsequent attempts and automatically pass saving throws against it.
Once you use this feature to successfully blind or daze a creature, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

entries.name: {@sup †}Dazed Condition
entries: A dazed creature can only do one of the following: move, take its action, or take a bonus action. It cannot take reactions.

name: Run and Gun
entries: On any turn in which you use your action to {@action Dash}, you can make a ranged weapon attack as a bonus action.

name: Rune Expert
entries: You can select a single Runic Mark from the Inventor Runesmith subclass. You learn and can mark this rune as per the Runic Mark feature of the Inventor class.

name: Rune Knowledge
entries: You are wise in the lore of two {@filter runes|optionalfeatures|feature type=Rune} of your choice. You always have access to the benefit that a rune provides. In addition, you can invoke one rune power of each rune you have learned, provided you meet any other requirements such as a minimum level.
You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do, you gain the benefit and powers of two additional {@filter runes|optionalfeatures|feature type=Rune} of your choice.

name: Rune Mastery
entries: You have mastered the special powers of one rune. Choose one {@filter rune|optionalfeatures|feature type=Rune} that you have already learned through {@feat Rune Knowledge|KPDM}. You can invoke one of its mastery powers, provided you meet any other requirements such as a minimum level.
You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do, you learn the mastery powers of a different rune from your repertoire.

name: Rune-Craft
entries: You can now read and write runic inscriptions. You can use the runes to convey secret messages to other creatures who know them, or whom you previously instructed in their meaning.

At the end of a short or long rest, you can spend a craft slot and choose a magical item in the Company's possession. Make an Intelligence ({@skill Old Lore|TLotRR}) check. The DC is 10 for a Marvellous Artefact, 15 for a Wondrous Item, or 20 for a Famous Weapon or Armour. If you succeed, you learn all there is to be discovered about the item's qualities, and whether it is cursed or not.

In addition, during a Fellowship Phase, you can spend a craft slot to inscribe runes of power on a non-magical item of your choice, or on two items when you reach 5th level. You must be proficient with the tools related to the substance of which the item you choose is made ({@item smith's tools|PHB} for metal, {@item woodcarver's tools|PHB} for wood, etc.). While a creature holds or wears the item, it gains a +1 bonus to saving throws. If the item is a shield or a weapon, you may attribute it a bane instead (see {@book Chapter 7|TLotRR|6|Famous Weapons and Armour}). Choose a creature type among Evil Men, Orcs, Spiders, Trolls, Undead, or Wolves. If the item has one or more rewards, their effects are doubled against bane creatures (for example, a Keen weapon scores a critical hit on a roll of 18–20 against bane creatures). The runes can only be inscribed once on each item, and you cannot regain a craft slot expended in this way until the next Fellowship Phase, when you can cancel the runes inscribed with that slot and regain the slot, if you wish.

name: Runescarring
entries: You have learned an ancient technique which involves burning down spell scrolls and preparing the ashes into a poultice. The magical ashes are applied to a needle or blade used to tattoo or scar a creature, imbuing them with the ability to cast spells. To do so, you must successfully cast a spell from a spell scroll. Instead of the spell taking effect, you spend the next hour reducing the scroll to ashes and preparing the mixture. You must then spend one hour per spell level applying it to the creature. This process can be considered light activity during a long rest, and you can stop and start as many times as needed to complete it.
Once the tattoo is complete, the bearer can cast the spell once using Constitution as their spellcasting modifier, after which the magic fades.

A complete scar or tattoo that has not been activated can be detected as magical through the detect magic spell and similar means, giving off an aura based on the spell's school of magic. In addition, it can be removed with the dispel magic spell and similar effects

name: Runesmith Adept

otherSummary.entry: Runic Lore feature

entries: Through your contemplations of runes and their influence on weapons and armor, you know how to inscribe them harmonically, granting you the following benefits:

items: You can inscribe two runes onto an object if the object is a weapon or armor.

You add a {@filter rune of your choice|optionalfeatures|feature type=R} to your runic lexicon that translates to Armor or Weapon. If the rune has a prerequisite of any kind, you must meet the prerequisite to add it.

name: Runesmithing Adept

prerequisite.other: Artisan of the Runesmith's Guild (if using the guild system)

entries: You have excelled in your study of runesmithing and are regarded as a prodigy by your peers, gaining the following benefits:

items: Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make with {@item runesmith's tools|TCAH}

Over the course of a short rest, you can attempt to remove a runestone affixed to a piece of equipment without destroying it. At the end of the short rest, make a check with your {@item runesmith's tools|TCAH}, where the DC is equal to the DC to create the runestone. On a success, the runestone is recovered.

name: S.S. St. Vincent: Archon
entries: You are a shining beacon of law and order, bringing justice and peace to those of the Frontier. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: First Aid
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Medicine|XPHB} skill. You also learn the {@spell Spare the Dying|XPHB} cantrip and can cast it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: White Angel's Vengeance
entries: When an enemy you can see within 60 feet of you deals damage that causes you or an ally you can see within 60 feet to become {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests} until the end of your next turn. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Faction Feats
entries: Veteran adventurers are likely to make enemies across the 'Verse, but if they're lucky, they might forge some alliances too. The greatest of these alliances are likely to be with factions, which provide work, services, and connections to spacers everywhere. Factions in Dark Matter are detailed in Chapter 1: The 'Verse.

Of course, such allies don't come free. Factions generally also require work and commitment from their members, which might come in the form of small tasks, important favors for higher ranking members, or even regular obligations for the organization. For their efforts, adventurers gain specific and useful skills from their factions, as represented by Faction feats.

entries.name: Gaining a Faction Feat
entries: The GM can award you a Faction feat for joining a faction or completing a quest for one. If allegiance to a faction is important to your backstory, the GM can also replace the feat granted by your background with an appropriate Faction feat.

name: Sadistic Reward
entries: Your mind and body are fortified by harming others. You gain the following benefits:

items: The first time you deal damage to a hostile creature on your turn, you gain a +1 bonus to your attack and damage rolls until the end of your next turn.
Whenever you roll a 1 on a Wisdom ability check or Wisdom saving throw, you can reroll the die. You must use the new result, even if it is a 1.

You may make Wisdom skill checks you are proficient in as a bonus action instead of as an action (for example, you may attempt to stabilize a creature with {@skill medicine}, calm a beast with {@skill animal handling}, understand a foe better with {@skill insight}, spot something with {@skill perception} or track someone with {@skill survival}).

name: Sangromantic Initiate
entries: You have become adept enough with weaving blood magic to mitigate some of the harm of Sangromancy. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Blood Magic
entries: Choose a {@filter Sangromancy spell|spells|subschool=sangromancy} from any spell list of a level for which you have spell slots. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast the spell using any spell slot you have.

entries.name: Sanguine Potency
entries: You have a pool of two d12s that you can expend instead of {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} when you cast {@filter Sangromancy spells|spells|subschool=sangromancy}. Your pool regains all expended dice when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Sapper
entries: You have practiced extensively with a variety of explosives, gaining the following benefits:

items: You can add half your proficiency bonus to the planted explosives DC.

name: Savage Attacker (Alternate)
entries: Your savage battle instincts let you exploit even the smallest weakness. You gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Piercing Critical
entries: Whenever you score a critical hit with a melee weapon attack you roll the weapon's damage die three times instead of twice.

entries.name: Savage Strikes
entries: Once per turn when you hit with a melee weapon attack, you can roll all the damage dice that are part of your attack twice, and use the higher total.

name: Savage Attacker
entries: Whenever you hit a target with a Weapon and roll the max number on one of your weapon's damage dice, roll an additional die of that type and add it to the damage. The new die counts as one of your weapon's damage dice. This cannot happen more than a number of times equal to the ability modifier used to make the attack on a single attack.

name: Savage Attacker
entries: You excel at delivering death to your enemies as swiftly as possible. You gain the following benefits:

items: When you roll damage for a melee weapon attack, you can reroll the weapon's damage dice and use either total.

When you miss with a melee weapon attack, you can use your reaction to reroll the attack roll and to take the second result. Once you use this ability, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Savage Attacker
entries: Gain the first two available Tiers of the Savage Attacker feat:
{@b The Tiers of the Savage Attacker Feat:}

name: Savage Attacker
entries: Once per turn when you roll damage for a melee weapon attack, you can reroll the weapon's damage dice and use either total.

name: Savage Creature
entries: You follow your base instincts and impulses, giving you a bestial, feral demeanour. You gain the following benefits:

items: While you aren't holding anything in your hands your base walking speed increases by 10 feet.
You have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) and Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks made to track another creature.
You can use your action to consume the flesh and blood of a dead organic creature within 5 feet of you, regaining hit points equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).

name: Savage Howl
entries: Your rages are accompanied by feral howls that inflame the blood of your allies and drive them forward; an echo of ancient hunting packs. Each turn while you are raging, if you hit with at least one attack, you may nominate one ally within 30 feet of you. That ally receives a {@damage 1d6} bonus to its next damage roll. You may nominate the same or a different ally each round, but damage bonuses do not stack.

name: Savage Training
entries: You can draw upon the anger within your soul to perform Savage Exploits. You gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Savage Exploits Known
entries: You learn two {@filter 1st-degree Savage Exploits|optionalfeatures|feature type=ll:1se} from those available to the {@loader Alternate Barbarian|class/LaserLlama; Alternate Barbarian.json}. If required, their Exploit save DC equals 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice).

entries.name: Retraining Exploits
entries: Whenever you gain a level, you can replace one of the Savage Exploits you learned through this Feat with another 1st-degree Savage Exploit of your choice.

entries.name: Exploit Dice
entries: You gain two {@dice d4} Exploit Dice to fuel these Exploits, which are expended when you use them. You regain expended Exploit Dice when you finish a short or long rest.
If you already have Exploit Dice when you gain this Feat, you instead gain a single Exploit Die equal to your others.

name: Savagery
entries: When you make your first melee weapon attack roll on your turn, you can decide to attack savagely. Doing so allows you to add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to your melee weapon damage rolls but lowers your AC by 2 until the start of your next turn.

name: Savagery*
entries: The chieftons smile upon you, true-blood. Bring Apothis' hell upon our enemies! You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain an additional Critical Damage Dice.
You gain the Relentless Endurance racial ability of the Half-Orcs.

name: Scale and Fang: Scaleguard
entries: As one of Scale & Fang's illustrious bodyguards, your duty is to protect your charge, no matter the cost. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Block
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can choose one ally you can see. Until the start of your next turn, the ally's AC equals your AC if it is lower than that while the ally is within 5 feet of you. This effect ends early if you or the ally have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Quick Shield
entries: You can don or doff a {@item Shield|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Faction Feats
entries: Veteran adventurers are likely to make enemies across the 'Verse, but if they're lucky, they might forge some alliances too. The greatest of these alliances are likely to be with factions, which provide work, services, and connections to spacers everywhere. Factions in Dark Matter are detailed in Chapter 1: The 'Verse.

Of course, such allies don't come free. Factions generally also require work and commitment from their members, which might come in the form of small tasks, important favors for higher ranking members, or even regular obligations for the organization. For their efforts, adventurers gain specific and useful skills from their factions, as represented by Faction feats.

entries.name: Gaining a Faction Feat
entries: The GM can award you a Faction feat for joining a faction or completing a quest for one. If allegiance to a faction is important to your backstory, the GM can also replace the feat granted by your background with an appropriate Faction feat.

name: Scaleborn
entries: Whether as a blessing granted to you at birth or some dormant part of your heritage, you have the magic of dragon's blood within you. You gain the following benefits:

items: You learn two cantrips from the {@filter Sorcerer spell list|spells|level=0|class=Sorcerer}. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.
Choose one damage type: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison. You gain resistance to the chosen damage type.

name: Scaleguard
entries: As one of Scale & Fang's illustrious bodyguards, the duty to protect your charge, no matter the cost, has been burned into the scales of your armor. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Intimidation} skill and with shields.

While using a shield, if you are within 5 feet of a friendly creature and you both must make a saving throw against an effect that would deal damage, you can use your reaction to give that creature advantage on its saving throw. If you do so, you automatically fail your saving throw against that effect. If the creature would take half damage from succeeding on that saving throw, they take no damage instead.

name: Scamp Social Tricks
entries: Your words have a special power, and you've honed that power to an edge. You learn the {@spell friends} and {@spell message} spells and can cast them at-will. You also learn {@spell charm person} and {@spell enthrall}, each of which you can cast once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast those two spells in this way when you finish a long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for all four spells. When cast in this way, they only require verbal components and can't affect {@condition deafened} creatures.

name: Scamper
entries: If you are hidden, you can move up to 10 feet in the open without revealing yourself if you end the movement in a position where you're not clearly visible.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Scamper
entries: If you are hidden, you can move up to 10 feet in the open without revealing yourself if you end the movement in a position where you're not clearly visible.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Scatter Weapon Master
entries: Through many hours spent using these destructive weapons, whether on the training grounds or setting hag huts ablaze, you have gained immense experience with scatter weapons and gain the following benefits:

items: Critical hits double the damage dealt by the Scatter property on a failed save.
When making an attack with a weapon with the Scatter property, you may choose any number of targets to gain advantage on saving throws caused by your attack.
You ignore the Loading quality of Scatter weapons with which you are proficient.

name: Scattershot Master
entries: You have mastered getting the most effect out of firearms with the {@itemProperty HoE:Sc|HoE|scatter} property. You get the following benefits:

items: You gain a +1 to attack rolls with these weapons
Your scattershot damage can target any creature of your choosing within the scatter range of your target.
You can reroll 1s and 2s to your scatter damage.
You can load all of the ammo for shell loading firearms with the {@itemProperty HoE:Sc|HoE|scatter} property using a bonus action.

name: Scavenger
entries: You become stronger, gaining the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in one of the following skills: Investigation, Perception, or Survival.

For the purposes of scrapping, you are considered to be proficient in any toolset needed to scrap an item. If you are already proficient in that toolset, you are considered to have expertise with the toolset only for the purposes of scrapping items with it.
When scrapping items, add an additional 10% to the value you're able to recover in useable scrap.

name: Scholar of Lore
entries: You have spent time learning everything there is to know about a specific area of study. You gain the following benefits:

items: You master a {@filter Scholarly Pursuit|optionalfeatures|feature type=ll:sp} of your choice from those available to the {@loader Savant|class/LaserLlama; Savant.json}. If the Pursuit requires an Intellect Die, you use a {@dice d4} unless your Intellect Die is higher.

name: Scholar of Lore
entries: You have spent time learning everything there is to know about a specific area of study. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in one of the following skills: Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, or Religion.

Choose one skill from the list above. Once per day when you make a check with that skill, you can treat a roll of 9 or lower on the {@dice d20} as a 10. You can use this feature after you roll, but before you know if you succeed or fail.

name: Scion of Bakuryō

prerequisite.other: {@feat Gift of Bakuryō|WrathOfTheKaiju} and {@feat Fragment of Bakuryō|WrathOfTheKaiju} Feats

entries: You are a vassal of the koi dragon Bakuryō—her divine power incarnate. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have a swimming speed equal to your walking speed.
You gain 3 Rampage Points.

You learn the {@spell water wyrm|WrathOfTheKaiju} spell and can expend 3 Rampage Points to cast it without material components, using Constitution as your spellcasting ability. If you have the Spellcasting or Pact Magic class features, you can use that feature's spellcasting ability instead, and you can cast the spell with any spell slots you have of 3rd level or higher. When you cast the spell using this feat, it does not require concentration and lasts for the duration, or until you use this benefit again.

name: Scion of Iminada

prerequisite.other: {@feat Gift of Iminada|WrathOfTheKaiju} and {@feat Fragment of Iminada|WrathOfTheKaiju} Feats

entries: You are a vassal of the bakekujira Iminada—its undead fury incarnate. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have a swimming speed equal to your walking speed.
You gain 3 Rampage Points.

As an action, you can expend 3 Rampage Points to conjure a haunting, magical song that reverberates out from your body in a 15-foot radius. Each creature of your choice within that area that can hear you must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be wrecked with necrotic energy, taking {@damage 8d6} necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

name: Scion of Magatsuchi

prerequisite.other: {@feat Gift of Magatsuchi|WrathOfTheKaiju} and {@feat Fragment of Magatsuchi|WrathOfTheKaiju} Feats

entries: You are a vassal of the Plant kaiju Magatsuchi—its primal power incarnate. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain 3 Rampage Points.

As a bonus action, you can expend 3 Rampage Points to channel your magic and power through vibrations in the earth. For the next minute, you gain tremorsense out to 30 feet, and you can make melee attack rolls and cast spells with the range of touch targeting creatures you can see using this tremorsense, regardless of your reach.

name: Scion of Nomi

prerequisite.other: {@feat Gift of Nomi|WrathOfTheKaiju} and {@feat Fragment of Nomi|WrathOfTheKaiju} Feats

entries: You are a vassal of the kabuto kaiju Nomi—its bestial fury incarnate. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain 3 Rampage Points.

At the start of your turn, you can expend 1 Rampage Point to sprout spectral, insectoid wings. Until the end of your turn, you gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed, and you can hover. This speed isn't reduced by dragging a creature you're grappling. If you are airborne and unsupported at the end of your turn, you fall.

name: Scion of Raiko

prerequisite.other: {@feat Gift of Raiko|WrathOfTheKaiju} and {@feat Fragment of Raiko|WrathOfTheKaiju} Feats

entries: You are a vassal of the Elemental kaiju Raiko—its tempestuous wrath incarnate. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have resistance to lightning damage.
You gain 3 Rampage Points.

As a bonus action, you can expend 2 Rampage Points to magically transform you and all objects you are wearing and carrying transform into a bolt of pure, crackling energy. You move in a straight line, passing through creatures and objects, and reform in an unoccupied space up to 60 feet away. Each creature you move through in this way must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 1d8} lightning damage.

name: Scourge Master

otherSummary.entry: Proficiency with {@item whip|PHB} or {@item tetherhooks|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting}

entries: Your skill with whips and tetherhooks allows you to manipulate items at a distance.

items: When you hit a creature with an attack using a {@item tetherhooks|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting} or {@item whip|PHB}, you can use a bonus action to attempt to disarm the creature of a shield, or of one item it is holding. Make a Strength or Dexterity check (your choice) contested by the target's Strength check. If you succeed, the item is dropped on the ground midway between you and the creature.
You can use your {@item whip|PHB} or {@item tetherhooks|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting} to grab items weighing less than 1 lb within the reach of your weapon, pulling them back to your person.

name: Screening
entries: When you have cover from a creature's ranged attacks, you treat half cover as if it were three-quarters cover, even if your position is otherwise revealed.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Screening
entries: When you have cover from a creature's ranged attacks, you treat half cover as if it were three-quarters cover, even if your position is otherwise revealed.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Scribe
entries: Your extensive study and mastery of penmanship allows you to spot forgeries and create more economically sized scrolls. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with calligrapher's tools. If you are already proficient with them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.
When comparing 2 examples of writing side by side you are able to tell if they are from the same person and have advantage on any investigation checks to spot forged handwriting.

Your economical penmanship has allowed you to develop a special filing system for scrolls that only you can make sense of. You may treat one of your belt slots as a special container in which you can keep a number of scrolls you have crafted equal to your proficiency modifier, but it takes anyone else 1 minute to retrieve one of these complexly stored and sorted scrolls.

name: Script Carver
entries: You have learned how to expertly scribe two {@filter hieroglyphs|optionalfeatures|feature type=Hieroglyph} of your choice, and you gain the benefit associated with each one. In addition, you can invoke one power of each hieroglyph you have learned, provided you meet any other requirements, such as a minimum level.

items: You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do, you gain the benefit and powers of two additional Hieroglyphs of your choice.

name: Script Sage
entries: Through dedicated study, you have mastered one hieroglyph of your choice. Choose one {@filter hieroglyph|optionalfeatures|feature type=Hieroglyph} that you have already learned through {@feat Script Carver|KPDM}. You can invoke one of its mastery powers, provided you meet any other requirements, such as a minimum level.
You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do, you learn the mastery powers of a different hieroglyph from your repertoire.

name: Sculpt Spells
entries: You can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocation spells. When you cast an evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 + the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

name: Sea and Sky Shape
entries: You gain the ability to transform into beasts that have a swimming speed or flying speed.

name: Sea Legs
entries: Your time spent aboard boats has earned you the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in {@filter vehicles (water)|items|type=Vehicle (water)}
You have advantage on saving throws and ability checks made to avoid being knocked {@condition prone}.
Climbing doesn't cost you extra movement.

name: Sea Legs
entries: Your time spent aboard boats has earned you the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in {@filter vehicles (water)|items|type=Vehicle (water)}
You have advantage on saving throws and ability checks made to avoid being knocked {@condition prone}.
Climbing doesn't cost you extra movement.

name: Sea Legs

prerequisite.other: Achievement of rank of First Mate on a sailing vessel.

entries: You have advantage on ability checks and saving throws to resist being knocked {@condition prone}.

name: Sea Wolf
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Tactical Boarder
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength ({@skill Athletics}) and Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) checks made to board vehicles.

entries.name: Reaver's Ferocity
entries: When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} against a creature with a melee attack, you can make another melee attack against the same creature or an adjacent creature as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

name: Search for the Dragon
entries: You've managed to unlock the sorcerous might within your lineage through the draconic rite of passage. This ritual is mostly done by kobolds, but any draconic race can take it.

items: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

You learn one 1st level and one 2nd level spell of your choice from the sorcerer spell list. You can cast each spell at their lowest level without expending a spell slot. Once you cast either of these spells in this way, you can't cast that spell in this way again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast these spells using spell slots you have of the appropriate level. The spells' spellcasting ability is the ability increased by this feat.

name: Seasonal Determinism
entries: The state of the world at the moment of your birth left an indelible imprint on your body. Choose one of the seasons within which you were born; you gain the associated benefits:

items.name: Spring.
items.entry: Your Dexterity score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20. In addition, your speed increases by 5 feet, and you can use a bonus action to prepare yourself to move in a dextrous flourish. When you do, the next attack roll made against you before the start of your next turn has disadvantage.

items.name: Summer.
items.entry: Your Charisma score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20. In addition, you can use a bonus action to give yourself advantage on the next attack roll or ability check you make before the start of your next turn. You can use this bonus action a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

items.name: Autumn.
items.entry: Your Wisdom score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20. In addition, you have darkvision out to 30 feet, and you can take the Hide action as a bonus action while in dim light or darkness. If you already have darkvision, its range increases by 30 feet.

items.name: Winter.
items.entry: Your Constitution score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20. In addition, when you create a magical vial of water with your Water Magic trait, you can choose the following option as an effect: The water freezes and crackles with evocation magic.
