When a creature holding the vial takes the Attack action, it can use one attack to hurl the vial towards a target within 20 feet of it. The creature makes a ranged attack against the target, treating the vial as an improvised weapon. On a hit, the vial shatters, and the target takes {@damage 1d8} cold damage. If the target is a creature, its speed is also reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn. The cruel evocation magic you imbue in the vial increases in potency as you level up. The cold damage dealt by the vial increases by 1d8 when you reach 5th level ({@damage 2d8}), 11th level ({@damage 3d8}), and 17th level ({@damage 4d8}).

items: You can use a bonus action to drink one healing potion/elixir instead of an action. If you do so, you gain the maximum healing of the potion. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your highest class level per long rest.
Damage inflicted with the chosen weapons increases by 2.
Once per round, when holding one of those weapons and getting hit by a melee attack, you can use your reaction to make an attack against your attacker.

name: Second Wind
entries: You learn to channel the adrenaline rush from combat to protect yourself from harm. On your turn, you can spend one Hit Die to heal yourself as a bonus action. Roll the die, add your Constitution modifier, and regain a number of hit points equal to the total (minimum of 1).

name: Secret

otherSummary.entry: You can only take this feat during character creation

entries: When you gain this feat, choose one falsehood about yourself that you practice until you can recite it perfectly. This falsehood can be a single lie or an entire false history. You never need to make a {@skill Deception} check for this falsehood.

name: Secrets from Beyond
entries: You have detailed knowledge of extraplanar creatures. When you make a check to recall information about an aberration, celestial, elemental, fey, or fiend, in addition to what you would normally learn, you can also determine the creature's skills and abilities, common attacks, and if the creature is considered especially dangerous to a party of your level, though you don't necessarily learn the specifics of the creature's statistics.
In addition, studying an opened portal for one minute lets you identify if it leads to another plane of existence and what that plane is, if you know it.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Secrets from Beyond
entries: You have detailed knowledge of extraplanar creatures. When you make a check to recall information about an aberration, celestial, elemental, fey, or fiend, in addition to what you would normally learn, you can also determine the creature's skills and abilities, common attacks, and if the creature is considered especially dangerous to a party of your level, though you don't necessarily learn the specifics of the creature's statistics.
In addition, studying an opened portal for one minute lets you identify if it leads to another plane of existence and what that plane is, if you know it.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Seeker
entries: Every time you successfully find a hidden creature using the {@action Search} action, you have advantage on your attacks against them until the end of your next turn.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Seeker
entries: Every time you successfully find a hidden creature using the {@action Search} action, you have advantage on your attacks against them until the end of your next turn.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Seething Swarm
entries: Your drones have been drilled to defend the hivebody with vigorous ferocity. You gain the following benefits:

items: Whenever you use your Incensed Host feature, the mass of swarming drones grants you a bonus to your AC equal to half of your Constitution modifier (rounded up).

When you have no uses of your Incensed Host feature remaining, you can expend two of your Hit Dice to use the feature again. When used in this way, the swarm of drones lasts until the end of your next turn.

name: Self-Control
entries: You manage your Beast better than many. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Reining the Beast
entries: When you would be affected by the {@classFeature The Beast|Kindred|BoundByBlood|1||Hunger} of your Beast feature, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to immediately end the effect.
You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Selfless Martyr
entries: Your faith helps you preserve through anything, taking the suffering of others onto yourself and offering relief to those that need it most. You gain the following benefits:

items: As an action, you can touch a creature that is {@condition blinded}, {@condition charmed}, {@condition deafened}, {@condition frightened}, {@condition paralyzed}, {@condition petrified} {@condition poisoned}, {@condition stunned} or suffering from one or more levels of {@condition exhaustion}, and immediately end that condition on the target creature, but suffer that condition yourself (as it affected the target creature) yourself. When relieving {@condition exhaustion} this way, you take only 1 level at a time. If that condition has a save against its ongoing effect, you can immediately make a save against the effect to end it as part of taking the condition onto yourself. You can do this a number of times equal to your Proficiency bonus, and regain all uses when you complete a long rest.

Additionally, you can use the above feature on a creature that is {@condition unconscious} due to having zero hit points, when you do so, you can expend a hit die taking damage equal to the roll and granting the target creature hit points equal to the damage taken.

entries: Each time you take on the suffering of another creature with this feat, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Proficiency bonus.

name: Sense Enchantment
entries: When you observe or interact with a creature for 1 minute or more or you spend an action to closely examine it by touch and smell, you can determine if its mood or behavior is being influenced by a spell or other magical effect.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Sense Enchantment
entries: When you observe or interact with a creature for 1 minute or more or you spend an action to closely examine it by touch and smell, you can determine if its mood or behavior is being influenced by a spell or other magical effect.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Sense Movement
entries: When you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, the creature's speed becomes 0 for the rest of the turn.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Sense Movement
entries: When you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, the creature's speed becomes 0 for the rest of the turn.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Sentinel
entries: You excel at protecting your allies in combat by drawing fire to yourself. You gain the following benefits

items: As a bonus action, you can enter a protective stance until the start of your next turn. For the duration, you can force any attack targeted at an ally within your reach to target you instead, even if you would normally be outside of its range or reach.
Allies within your melee reach have advantage on checks and saves made to avoid or escape being {@condition grappled} or {@action shove|phb}.
You have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition charmed} or {@condition frightened}.

name: Sentinel
entries: Creatures provoke opportunity attacks from you even if they take the {@action Disengage} action before leaving your reach.

In addition, when a creature within 5 feet of you makes an attack against a target other than you (and that target doesn't have this ability), you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against the attacking creature.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Sentinel
entries: Creatures provoke opportunity attacks from you even if they take the {@action Disengage} action before leaving your reach.

In addition, when a creature within 5 feet of you makes an attack against a target other than you (and that target doesn't have this ability), you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against the attacking creature.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Sentinel
entries: You gain the following benefit and the first two available Tiers of the Sentinel Feat:
{@b The Tiers of the Sentinel Feat:}

name: Sentinel
entries: You have mastered techniques to take advantage of every drop in any enemy's guard, gaining the following benefits:

items: When you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, the creature's speed becomes 0 for the rest of the turn.
Creatures provoke opportunity attacks from you even if they take the {@action Disengage} action before leaving your reach.

When a creature within 5 feet of you makes an attack against a target other than you (and that target doesn't have this feat), you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against the attacking creature {@color (This does not count as an attack of opportunity!)|e40707}.

name: Sentinel Raven
entries: Your familiar can take the form of a sentinel raven. While the raven is perched on your shoulder, you gain darkvision with a range of 30 feet and have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks. While perched on your shoulder, the raven can't be targeted by any attack or other harmful effect; only you can cast spells on it; it can't take damage; and it is incapacitated.
If the raven is slain by a creature, you gain advantage on all attack rolls against the killer for the next 24 hours.
The raven doesn't require sleep. While it is within 100 feet of you, it can awaken you from sleep as a bonus action.

name: Sepulcher Knight: Deputy
entries: You've been inducted into a Knight's Precinct as a deputy lawbringer or a knight-in-training. This appointment confers a badge and gun, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Badge
entries: You can display your badge on your turn (no action required). Creatures that see it will regard you as they do the Sepulcher Knights as a whole: lawabiding citizens will often be {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} and criminals will often be {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile}.

entries.name: Cuffs
entries: You can use {@item Manacles|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Gun
entries: You have an assigned service weapon, a {@item Repeater|DarkMatter24}. You have proficiency with this weapon and can use its Mastery property even if you don't have the Weapon Mastery feature, and it doesn't count against the number of weapons you can use.

entries.name: Faction Feats
entries: Veteran adventurers are likely to make enemies across the 'Verse, but if they're lucky, they might forge some alliances too. The greatest of these alliances are likely to be with factions, which provide work, services, and connections to spacers everywhere. Factions in Dark Matter are detailed in Chapter 1: The 'Verse.

Of course, such allies don't come free. Factions generally also require work and commitment from their members, which might come in the form of small tasks, important favors for higher ranking members, or even regular obligations for the organization. For their efforts, adventurers gain specific and useful skills from their factions, as represented by Faction feats.

entries.name: Gaining a Faction Feat
entries: The GM can award you a Faction feat for joining a faction or completing a quest for one. If allegiance to a faction is important to your backstory, the GM can also replace the feat granted by your background with an appropriate Faction feat.

name: Serenity of the Night
entries: Your faith grants you a deep wisdom and serenity, you feel a special connection to your faith, in particular the moonlight. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain {@sense darkvision} of 60 feet. If you already have {@sense darkvision}, darkness withing that range is softly illuminated to your gaze as if bathed in moonlight, allowing you to see in dim light as bright light.

You learn the spell {@spell guidance}. You can cast this spell in a special way as a bonus action without verbal or somatic components a number of times equal to your Proficiency bonus. You regain all uses of it when you complete a long rest.

As an action, you can offer a prayer of guidance and protection, shrouding you a nimbus of moonlight until the end of your next turn. For the duration you shed bright light for 10 feet and dim light for another 20 feet. For that duration, creatures within the radius of light cannot gain advantage on attacks against you, and you and allied creatures within the bright light are under the effect of {@spell protection from evil and good}. Once you do use this action, you cannot do so again until you complete a long rest.

name: Serpent Form
entries: You have unlocked more of your serpentfolk heritage. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can use an action to polymorph into a Medium snake or back into your true form. Your statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment you are wearing or carrying isn't transformed. If you die, you stay in your current form

While in snake form, you gain a bite attack as a natural weapon, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with it, you deal piercing damage equal to {@dice 1d4} + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike. When you hit with a bite attack, you can choose to deal {@dice 2d6} additional poison damage to the target. Once you deal this poison damage, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

name: Serpentine
entries: Thanks to your gorgon heritage you have developed a strong kinship with serpents, granting you the following benefits:

items: You learn the {@spell find familiar} spell and can cast it as a ritual. A familiar summoned this way is always a {@creature giant poisonous snake} or a {@creature constrictor snake} (your choice).
You learn the {@spell speak with animals} spell (snakes only) and can cast it at will, without expending a spell slot.
You learn the {@spell animal friendship} spell (snakes only) and can cast it at will, without expending a spell slot.

entries: Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

name: Serpentine Heritage
entries: You further embrace your serpentine heritage. You can take this feat twice, and its benefits stack.

items: Increase your Dexterity, Constitution, or Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

The damage dice of your constrict attack and Crushing Coils trait (if you have it) increase by one step (1d6 to 1d8 etc. to a maximum of 1d12). The DC of your Venom trait (if you have it) increases by 1. The range of your poison spray cantrip (if you know it) increases by 30 feet.
You gain Infravision (page 34) out to a range of 60 feet. If you already have Infravision, then its range is increased by 60 feet instead.
The first time you take this feat you become immune to the poisoned condition, and the second time you take this feat you become immune to poison damage.

entries: When you take this feat you gain a trait of one of the other lamia subraces of your choice, but you must choose a lamia subrace whose trait you don't have yet. You gain the following trait based on your choice:

entries.caption: Lamia Subraces
rows: You gain the Crushing Coils trait
You gain the Innate Spellcasting trait.

name: Sexy Tattoo

prerequisite.other: Tattoo, may NOT have {@feat Grotesque Tattoo|INK}

entries: Your tattoos are particularly alluring, adding to your attractiveness.
{@b Benefit}:

items: Increase your Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20
You gain proficiency in the Persuasion skill. If you are already proficient in the skill, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it
Gain the abilty to effectively generate an effect akin to {@spell Friends}, or if you can cast {@spell friends} already its duration increases to up to 10 minutes when you cast it.

entries: {@b Note}: A character cannot have the Sexy Tattoo feat if they have the {@feat Grotesque Tattoo|INK} feat. A drawback is that these tattoos make people take you less seriously, incurring disadvantage -2 to Intimidate checks. These modifiers only apply when the tattoos are clearly visible.

name: Shadow Dancer
entries: You learn an ancient fighting style of your people, attacking your enemies from all angles with a flurry of spiked chains. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with the {@item spiked chain|SCOE} if you don't already have it.
A spike chain has the finesse property when you wield it.
When you gain this feat, a small rift opens from the Shadowfell, laying a single {@item spiked chain|SCOE} at your feet.

name: Shadow Mage
entries: You have practiced manipulating areas of dim light and darkness with your spells, granting you the following benefits:

items: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
When you cast a spell that targets an area, you can extinguish any non-magical light sources within that area.
As an action, you can wreathe your space in magical darkness until the end of your next turn.

name: Shadow Paw Rogue
entries: You are a difficult foe to pin down. If you hit in combat with a Sneak Attack, you may choose to move up to ten feet as a free action. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.

name: Shadow Step
entries: You gain the ability to step from one shadow into another. When you take the Hide action in dim light or darkness, you can teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is also in dim light or darkness. You can select this feat a second time after 14th level. When you do so, the range you can teleport to increases to 120 feet.

name: Shadow Strike
entries: You gain the ability to pass between shadows in the blink of an eye. When you take the Attack action, you can teleport up to 10 feet before each attack to an unoccupied space you can see that is in dim light or darkness.

If you have the {@feat Action Surge|Adventurer} feat, you can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is in dim light or darkness when you use your {@feat Action Surge|Adventurer}. You can teleport before or after the additional action.

name: Shadow-Touched
entries: You gain the following benefit and the first two available Tiers of the Shadow-Touched Feat:
{@b The Tiers of the Shadow-Touched Feat:}

name: Shadow's Gift of Stone
entries: You have learned to channel arcane power through your gaze. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Innate Magic
entries: When you reach a character level specified in the Shadow's Gift of Stone Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. You can cast each of these spells once without expending a spell slot, and you must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can cast them in this way again. You can also cast these spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
Your spellcasting ability for these spells is the same as the spellcasting ability you chose for your Petrifying Gaze trait.

name: Shadow's Metamagic
entries: You've learned the forbidden secrets of {@deity the Shadow|Eberron|ERLW}, allowing you to alter how your spells function:

items: You learn two {@filter Metamagic|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=MM} options of your choice from the Forbidden Metamagic list. You can use only one {@classFeature Metamagic|Sorcerer|PHB|3} option on a spell when you cast it, unless the option says otherwise. Whenever you reach a level that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can replace one of these {@classFeature Metamagic|Sorcerer|PHB|3} options with another one from the Forbidden Metamagic list.

You gain 2 {@classFeature sorcery points|Sorcerer|PHB|2} to spend on {@classFeature Metamagic|Sorcerer|PHB|3} (these points are added to any {@classFeature sorcery points|Sorcerer|PHB|2} you have from another source but can be used only on {@classFeature Metamagic|Sorcerer|PHB|3}). You regain all spent {@classFeature sorcery points|Sorcerer|PHB|2} when you finish a long rest.

name: Shadowmage
entries: The yokai magic that flows through your veins lets you draw on a wider pool of magic than is typical to most hanataka, granting you the following benefits:

items: You learn two cantrips of your choice from the druid or sorcerer spell list. You can cast these cantrips without any spell components while in dim light or darkness. Your spellcasting ability for these spells is the ability score you increased with this feat.

name: Shadowsteel Adept
entries: You have learned to tap into the dangerous but powerful art of Shadowsteel casting. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Curse Caster
entries: You always have {@filter Shadowsteel curses|spells|subschool=shadowsteel curse} prepared, and you can cast them with any spell slots you have.

entries.name: Shadowsteel's Bite
entries: While holding your {@item Shadowsteel Focus|GrimHollowPG24}, you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your spells.

entries.name: Shadowsteel Weapon
entries: If your {@item Shadowsteel Focus|GrimHollowPG24} is also a weapon, that weapon has a +1 bonus to weapon attack rolls and damage rolls.

name: Shadowsteel Master
entries: Your mastery over Shadowsteel grows stronger. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Necrotic Harmony
entries: While holding your {@item Shadowsteel Focus|GrimHollowPG24}, when you cast a spell that targets one or more creatures and requires an attack roll or saving throw, you can choose one target you hit or who failed the saving throw to also take {@damage 1d4} Necrotic damage for each spell slot level expended to cast the spell.

entries.name: Necrotic Weapon
entries: If your {@item Shadowsteel Focus|GrimHollowPG24} is also a weapon, that weapon has a +2 bonus to weapon attack rolls and damage rolls. Additionally, once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with a weapon attack roll using your {@item Shadowsteel Focus|GrimHollowPG24}, you can cause the target to take an extra {@damage 2d8} Necrotic damage.

name: Shake it Off
entries: Once per long rest you may take advantage on any saving throw to end a condition currently affecting you. The condition can be {@condition blinded}, {@condition deafened}, {@condition paralyzed}, or {@condition poisoned}.

name: Shapeshifter
entries: You can use your Biomimicry trait over the course of 1 minute to perfectly alter your appearance. You decide what you look like, including your height, weight, facial features, sound of your voice, hair length, coloration, and other distinguishing characteristics. You can make yourself appear as a member of another species, though none of your statistics change. You can't appear as a creature of a different size, and your basic shape stays the same.

name: Shapeshifter
entries: You learn to attune yourself to the natural world, allowing you to change your form into that of a beast. When you gain this feat, choose {@filter a beast that has a challenge rating of 1/4 or lower that doesn't have a flying or swimming speed|bestiary|Challenge Rating=[&0;&1/4]|type=beast|miscellaneous=!reprinted;!swarm|speed type=!fly;!swim}. If you have the {@classFeature Wild Shape|Druid|PHB|2} feature, you may choose a new beast each time you transform using this feat.

You can use your action to magically transform into that creature for 1 hour. Otherwise, your transformation follows the criteria and limitations of the druid's {@classFeature Wild Shape|Druid|PHB|2} feature.
You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a short or logn rest.

name: Shard Swarm
entries: You have meditated upon your nature as a fragment of a greater crystal and discovered how to relocate your mind in space, causing your physical body to follow and leaving a fragment of yourself behind to burst apart.

You learn the {@spell misty step} spell and can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a short or long rest. Constitution is your spellcasting ability for this spell. When you cast it in this way, the spell's range is doubled, and you can also choose to leave a cloud of crystal dust in a 15-foot diameter sphere centered on the space you teleported from which lasts until the end of your next turn. The cloud is difficult terrain and heavily obscured for other creatures.

name: Shared Agony

prerequisite.other: {@feat Spellbook|Adventurer} (School of Enchantment) or {@feat Acolyte: Eldritch|Adventurer}, 10th Level

entries: Your alien knowledge gives you the ability to touch the minds of other creatures. You can communicate telepathically with any creature you can see within 30 feet of you. You don't need to share a language with the creature for it to understand your telepathic utterances, but the creature must be able to understand at least one language.

Additionally, your thoughts can't be read by telepathy or other means unless you allow it. You also have resistance to psychic damage, and whenever a creature deals psychic damage to you, that creature takes the same amount of damage that you do.

name: Sharpshooter (Alternate)
entries: You have trained extensively with ranged weapons to become a master marksman. You gain the benefits listed below:

entries.name: Expert Marksman
entries: You gain the Archery Fighting Style. If you already know this Fighting Style, you gain a +1 bonus to ranged weapon attacks, and your ranged weapon attacks can completely ignore Half and Three-Quarter's cover.

entries.name: Sniper
entries: Attacking a target within a ranged weapon's long range does not impose disadvantage on your roll.

entries.name: Steady Aim
entries: As a bonus action, you focus to give yourself advantage on the next ranged attack that you make on your current turn.

name: Sharpshooter
entries: You gain the following benefits:

items.name: Shrapnel
items.entry: When you make an attack with a ranged weapon against a creature that is behind cover and hit, deal extra damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

items.name: Firing in Melee
items.entry: Being within reach of an enemy doesn't impose Disadvantage on your ranged Attack Rolls with Weapons.

items.name: Long Shots
items.entry: Attacking at Long Range doesn't impose Disadvantage on your ranged Attack Rolls with Weapons.

name: Sharpshooter
entries: You have mastered ranged weapons and can make shots that others find impossible. You gain the following benefits:

items: You ignore half and three-quarters cover on any ranged attack roll that has advantage.
You have advantage on ranged attack rolls against creatures that are grappled. If a creature doesn't willingly move on their turn, you also gain this advantage until they move again.
Whenever you have disadvantage on a ranged weapon attack roll, you can reroll one of the dice once.
On your turn, when you score a critical hit with a ranged weapon or reduce a creature to 0 hit points with one, you can make one ranged weapon attack as a bonus action.

name: Sharpshooter
entries: You're a master of ranged warfare and can pull off shots that others call impossible:

items: The normal and long range of ranged and thrown weapons is doubled for you.
Your ranged weapon attacks ignore half cover, and three-quarters cover is considered half cover for you.
Once on each of your turns when you make a ranged weapon attack, you can add your proficiency bonus to the damage roll.

entries: {@note {@b Design Note:} This optional feat replaces {@feat Sharpshooter|PHB|the feat with a similar name}, balancing player options introduced in Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt.}

name: Sharpshooter
entries: Attacking at long range doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged weapon attacks.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Sharpshooter
entries: Attacking at long range doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged weapon attacks.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Sharpshooter
entries: You gain the following benefit and the first two available Tiers of the Sharpshooter Feat:
{@b The Tiers of the Sharpshooter Feat:}

name: Sharpshooter
entries: You have mastered ranged weapons and can make shots that others find impossible. You gain the following benefits:

items: Attacking at long range doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged weapon attack rolls.
Your ranged weapon attacks ignore half cover and three-quarters cover.
Before you make an attack with a ranged weapon that you are proficient with, you can choose to take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, you add +10 to the attack's damage.

When you hit with a one-handed melee weapon and your other hand is holding a shield, you can forgo half of your damage and get a bonus to AC equal to your Strength modifier until the start of your next turn.
At the end of your turn, if you haven't moved during that turn, an adjacent ally gets a +2 bonus to their AC as long as they are within 5 feet of you.

foundryEffects.name: Shield Artist Adjacent Ally AC Bonus

name: Shield Bash
entries: If you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can use a bonus action to try to {@action shove} a creature within 5 feet of you with your shield.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Shield Bash
entries: You can use a bonus action to try to {@action shove} a creature within 5 feet of you with your shield.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Shield Basher

otherSummary.entry: Proficiency with Shields

entries: The best offense is a good defense, especially one that can inflict blunt-force trauma. You specialize in the use of shields as a weapon, granting you the following benefits:

items: When you make a melee attack with a shield, you can treat it as a simple melee weapon rather than an improvised weapon. Melee weapon attacks you make with shields deal {@dice 1d6} + your Strength modifier bludgeoning damage on a hit.
If you take the Attack action on your turn, you can make an attack with a shield as a bonus action.

when you move 15 feet or more in a straight line you can take an action to charge an enemy with your shield. Make a melee weapon attack roll, dealing 1d4 bludgeoning damage and knocking them prone on a hit.

name: Shield Master
entries: You use shields not just for protection but also for offense. You gain the following benefits while you are wielding a {@item shield|phb}:

items: As a bonus action on your turn, you can attempt to shove acreature within 5 feet of you with your shield.
If you aren't {@condition incapacitated}, you can add your shield's AC bonus to your Dexterity saving throws.

If you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you can use your reaction to interpose your shield between yourself and the source of the effect. You instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

name: Shield Master
entries: If you aren't {@condition incapacitated}, you can add your shield's AC bonus to any Dexterity saving throw you make against a spell or other harmful effect that targets only you.

In addition, if you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you can use your reaction to take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, interposing your shield between yourself and the source of the effect.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Shield Master
entries: If you aren't {@condition incapacitated}, you can add your shield's AC bonus to any Dexterity saving throw you make against a spell or other harmful effect that targets only you.

In addition, if you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you can use your reaction to take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, interposing your shield between yourself and the source of the effect.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Shield Master
entries: You gain the following benefit and the first two available Tiers of the Shield Master Feat:
{@b The Tiers of the Shield Master Feat:}

name: Shield Master
entries: You use shields not just for protection but also for offense. You gain the following benefits while you are wielding a {@item shield|phb}:

items: If you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can use a bonus action to try to {@action shove} a creature within 5 feet of you with your shield.
If you aren't {@condition incapacitated}, you can add your shield's AC bonus to any Dexterity saving throw you make against a spell or other harmful effect that targets only you.

If you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you can use your reaction to take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, interposing your shield between yourself and the source of the effect.

name: Shield of the Sisters*
entries: In the grace of Anu, you are protected by the elements that serve you. Drawing on your ancestry, you can create and aura around you to shield you from attackers. You gain the Following Benefits:

items: As a Bonus Action, you can create a 5ft aura around you with the element of your choice from Fire, Lightning, Cold, or Force, which will last for up to a minute or until you dispel it as a free action. Whenever a hostile enters the aura, they take 1d4 + your CON modifier of your selected damage type, and must make a CON save with a DC based on your CON modifier or be unable to attack you until the beginning of their next turn. You can activate this aura only once per day.

name: Shield Wall
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Shield Ally
entries: When a creature you can see hits an ally adjacent to you with an attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to grant your ally your {@item Shield|XPHB}'s {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} bonus against the triggering attack.

entries.name: Shoulder to Shoulder
entries: When you and an ally are both wielding a {@item Shield|XPHB} and are adjacent to each other, you both gain a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}.

name: Shieldbreaker
entries: Your attack rolls with a {@item morningstar|PHB} or {@item flail|PHB} gain a +2 bonus against any target using a shield.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Shieldbreaker
entries: Your attack rolls with a {@item morningstar|PHB} or {@item flail|PHB} gain a +2 bonus against any target using a shield.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Shifting Combatant
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Domino Strike
entries: When you hit a creature with a weapon and activate the Push mastery property to push that creature into a space occupied by a Large or smaller creature, you can force the creatures to collide. Each creature makes a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier of the score increased by this feat and your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}), taking {@damage 1d10} Bludgeoning damage on a failed save.

entries.name: Fearless Leap
entries: When you make a {@variantrule Long Jump|XPHB}, moving at least 10 feet immediately before the jump, and land in a space within 5 feet of two or more enemies, attack rolls made against you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} until the start of your next turn.

name: Shining Star
entries: Your intuition always leads you safely back home. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Wisdom score by 1, upm to a maximum of 20.
Traveling at a fast pace doesn't impose the normal -5 penalty on your passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) score.

You can create a guiding light that leads you to your destination. If you concentrate on a location you have been to on the same plane of existence, you can create a floating globe of light that leads you along the most direct physical path to the specified location. The light can't lead you to a destination on another plane of existence, a destination that moves, or a destination you haven't personally been at. You have to concentrate on the light as if it were a spell and it vanishes after 1 day or if you loose concentration. You can't use this feature again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Shock Trooper
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: First Strike
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} and don't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the roll, you can draw a weapon and make an attack using it.

entries.name: Rapid Advance
entries: During the first round of each combat, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is doubled.

name: Shock Trooper
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: First Strike
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} and don't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the roll, you can draw a weapon and make an attack using it.

entries.name: Rapid Advance
entries: During the first round of each combat, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is doubled.

name: Shock Trooper
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: First Strike
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} and don't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the roll, you can draw a weapon and make an attack using it.

entries.name: Rapid Advance
entries: During the first round of each combat, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is doubled.

name: Shove About
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with melee weapon that deals bludgeoning damage, you may use a bonus action to attempt to {@action shove} a creature.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Shove About
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with melee weapon that deals bludgeoning damage, you may use a bonus action to attempt to {@action shove} a creature.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Showdown Veteran*
entries: You have won many showdowns, keeping your calm in high pressure situations lets you better observe and predict your enemy's movements.

items: When you make a ranged attack with a gun against targets who have disadvantage on Dexterity checks or Dexterity Saving Throws, add your Wisdom modifier to the attack roll.

You have learned to use your gun in acrobatic maneuvers. You can add your proficiency bonus for Acrobatics checks made while carrying a gun. If you are already proficient in Acrobatics, you can instead add double your proficiency bonus.

You can attempt to intercept an opponent's ranged weapon attack with one of your own. When a creature that you can see makes a ranged weapon attack against another creature that you can see, you can use your reaction to make a ranged attack with your gun against the opponent's projectile. The projectile's AC is equal to the opponent's attack roll plus 5. On a hit, the opponent's attack misses. ({@color Boulders hurled by giants or siege engines, and similar projectiles, are unaffected|e40707})

name: Showman
entries: Presentation is at least as important as being effective, if not more so. After all, there is little reason to do something unless is looks impressive. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Performance} skill. If you are already proficient in the skill, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.

If there is a non-combative audience watching you fight, once per turn, you can gain a bonus to an ability check or attack roll equal to the number of people in the audience, up to a maximum of your Charisma modifier. You can use this ability three times, and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Showman
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Expert Performer
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Performance|XPHB} skill. If you already have proficiency in it, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it.

entries.name: Taunt
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to mock a creature within 15 feet of yourself. If the target can hear you (though it need not understand you), it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next attack roll it makes against a creature other than you before the end of its next turn. You can use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Showman
entries: Though many siegeball players are dedicated athletes, placing all their attention on the game at hand, some relish in appeasing the crowd, curring their favor and performing stunts. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You gain proficiency in the Performance skill. If you are already proficient in the skill, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.

If there is a non-combative audience watching you fight, once per turn, you can gain a bonus to an ability check or attack roll equal to the number of people in the audience, up to a maximum of your Charisma modifier. You can use this ability three times, and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Showman
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Expert Performer
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Performance|XPHB} skill. If you already have proficiency in it, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it.

entries.name: Taunt
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to mock a creature within 15 feet of yourself. If the target can hear you (though it need not understand you), it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next attack roll it makes against a creature other than you before the end of its next turn. You can use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Showman
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Expert Performer
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Performance|XPHB} skill. If you already have proficiency in it, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it.

entries.name: Taunt
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to mock a creature within 15 feet of yourself. If the target can hear you (though it need not understand you), it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next attack roll it makes against a creature other than you before the end of its next turn. You can use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Showman
entries: Presentation is at least as important as being effective, if not more so. After all, there is little reason to do something unless it looks impressive. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Performance} skill. If you are already proficient in the skill, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it

If there is a non-combative audience watching you fight, once per turn, you can gain a bonus to an ability check or attack roll equal to the number of people in the audience, up to a maximum of your Charisma modifier. You can use this ability three times, regaining all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Showstopper

prerequisite.other: {@feat Specialty Acts|TalentTrees} or {@feat Stage-Fighting|TalentTrees} or {@feat Leadership|TalentTrees}

entries: Your mastery of performance elicits deep emotional responses from those around you. As an action, you can begin a performance, which lasts for up to one minute and which requires your action each turn to maintain. Each creature of your choice that can see or hear you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your Performance bonus) at the beginning of each of its turns or be enraptured by you until the end of the performance or until it takes damage. While under the influence of the performance, the creature is overcome with emotion and is incapacitated, can't speak, and has disadvantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks made to perceive any creature other than you. Once you use this ability, you can't do so again until you complete a long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Showstopper

prerequisite.other: {@feat Specialty Acts|TalentTreesMod} or {@feat Stage-Fighting|TalentTreesMod} or {@feat Leadership|TalentTreesMod}

entries: Your mastery of performance elicits deep emotional responses from those around you. As an action, you can begin a performance, which lasts for up to one minute and which requires your action each turn to maintain. Each creature of your choice that can see or hear you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your Performance bonus) at the beginning of each of its turns or be enraptured by you until the end of the performance or until it takes damage. While under the influence of the performance, the creature is overcome with emotion and is incapacitated, can't speak, and has disadvantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks made to perceive any creature other than you. Once you use this ability, you can't do so again until you complete a long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Siberys Mark of Death
entries: You possess a Siberys Dragonmark, the largest and most powerful expression of a dragonmark. This may have evolved from an existing Dragonmark, or you may have manifested it spontaneously. The Siberys Dragonmark of Death provides the following benefits:

items: When you make a Charisma ability check to interact with a dragon or another dragonmarked creature, you can roll one Intuition die and add the number rolled to the ability check. With these interactions, the minimum Intuition die you can roll is a {@dice d6}. For example, if you already have a dragonmark, your Intuition die is a {@dice d8}.

You know the {@spell revivify}, {@spell speak with dead}, and {@spell spirit guardians} spells and can cast these spells once with your mark. You can't cast these spells again until you finish a long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

name: Siberys Mark of Detection
entries: The Siberys Dragonmark of Detection provides the following benefits:

items: You gain the ability to sense and pinpoint hidden objects in your vicinity.  As an action, you can open your awareness for the next minute to magically detect the location of hidden creatures, objects, secret doors, or traps within 30 feet of you that aren't behind total cover and aren't protected from divination magic. When you do, you can't use this feature again until you finish a short or long rest.

When you reach 15th level, you can cast {@spell foresight} once without expending a spell slot using your Siberys mark. When you cast it in this way, its duration is an hour and its range is self. You regain the ability to cast it in this way after you finish a long rest. Intelligence is the spellcasting ability for this spell.

name: Siberys Mark of Finding
entries: The Siberys Dragonmark of Finding provides the following benefits:

items: As an action, you can imprint a creature in your mind as your quarry whenever you succeed on a Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check to track it. The target is imprinted in your mind until it dies or you use this feature again. While you are tracking only that creature, you can follow its trail exactly, and if presented with a choice of paths along the way, you automatically determine which is the most recent route and when the creature traveled it, accurate within one week's time. You don't learn information about the route, the means needed to traverse the path, or whether it is on the same plane of existence, if you don't already know.

name: Siberys Mark of Handling
entries: The Siberys Dragonmark of Handling provides the following benefits:

items: When you make a Wisdom or Charisma ability check to interact with a beast, you can roll one Intuition die and add the number rolled to the ability check. With these interactions, the minimum Intuition die you can roll is a {@dice d6}.

You can cast the {@spell enhance ability} spell on a beast once with your Siberys mark. When you do, its casting time is 10 minutes (as if casting a ritual spell), the beast gains the benefit of all of the spell's properties, and its duration is 24 hours. You can't cast it again this way until you finish a long rest. If you use your mark in this way on the same beast for 30 days, the effect becomes permanent. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

name: Siberys Mark of Healing
entries: The Siberys Dragonmark of Healing provides the following benefits:

items: When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell, you can roll one Intuition die and add the number rolled to the total.

You learn the {@spell greater restoration} and {@spell mass cure wounds} spells and can cast these spells once without expending a spell slot using your Siberys mark. You regain the ability to cast these two spells in this way when you finish a long rest. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for them.

name: Siberys Mark of Hospitality
entries: The Siberys Dragonmark of Hospitality provides the following benefits:

items: You are always under the effects of a {@spell detect poison and disease} spell while you are conscious.

When you, and friendly creatures within 30 feet of you, would normally roll one or more Hit Die to restore hit points during a short rest, you can roll one Intuition die and add the number rolled to the total number of hit points a creature regains at the end of the rest.

You learn the {@spell heroes' feast} spell and can cast it once without expending a spell slot using your Siberys mark. This requires the expenditure of 1,000 gp worth of dragonshards. You regain the ability to cast this spell in this way when you finish a long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it.

name: Siberys Mark of Making
entries: The Siberys Dragonmark of Making provides the following benefits:

items: When you make a Charisma ability check to interact with a dragon or another dragonmarked creature, you can roll one Intuition die and add the number rolled to the ability check. With these interactions, the minimum Intuition die you can roll is a {@dice d6}.

You gain the ability to spend 10 minutes (as if casting a ritual spell), to enchant a nonmagical weapon or suit of armor. For the next 24 hours or until you finish a long rest, it becomes a magic item, granting a +1 bonus to AC if it's armor or a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls if it's a weapon. You can't use your mark in this way again until you finish a long rest. If you enchant the same armor or weapon for 30 days, the effect becomes permanent.

name: Siberys Mark of Passage
entries: The Siberys Dragonmark of Passage provides the following benefits:

items: When you make an ability check to operate or maintain a {@filter land vehicle|vehicles|terrain=land}, you can roll one Intuition die and add the number rolled to the ability check. With these interactions, the minimum Intuition die you can roll is a {@dice d6}.

You learn the {@spell teleportation circle} spell and can cast it once without expending a spell slot using your Siberys mark. When you cast it in this way, you don't need to provide the spell's material components and its duration becomes 1 minute. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a long rest.

name: Siberys Mark of Scribing
entries: The Siberys Dragonmark of Scribing provides the following benefits:

items: When you make a Charisma ability check to interact with a dragon or another dragonmarked creature, you can roll one Intuition Die and add the number rolled to the ability check. With these interactions, the minimum Intuition die you can roll is a {@dice d6}.

You can cast the {@spell magic mouth} spell at-will, without expending a spell slot. When you reach 15th level, you learn the {@spell Rary's telepathic bond} spell, if you don't already know it, and can cast it once without expending a spell slot. When you do, you can choose to connect to a {@spell magic mouth} you have created, instead of one of the creatures the spell allows. While this spell is active, you can spend 1 minute to change its message and the circumstance that will trigger the spell to deliver your message. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a long rest.

name: Siberys Mark of Sentinel
entries: The Siberys Dragonmark of Sentinel provides the following benefits:

items: When you roll initiative, you can cast {@spell warding bond} on one willing creature. When you cast it in this way, its duration is equal to a number of rounds equal to your Strength modifier.

When you reach 15th level, you can cast the {@spell sequester} spell once using your Siberys mark and its duration lasts a number of minutes equal to your Strength modifier. You regain the ability cast it in this way when you finish a long rest. Strength is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

name: Siberys Mark of Shadow
entries: The Siberys Dragonmark of Shadow provides the following benefits:

items: You learn the {@spell mislead} spell if you don't already know it, and can cast it once using your Siberys mark without expending a spell slot. When you reach 15th level, you learn the {@spell programmed illusion} spell and can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast these two spells in this way when you finish a long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

name: Siberys Mark of Storm
entries: The Siberys Dragonmark of Storm provides the following benefits:

items: You learn the {@spell planar binding} spell and can cast it once without expending a spell slot. When you cast it with your Siberys mark in this way, its casting time becomes 10 minutes (as if casting a ritual spell), and it targets only elementals. When you reach 15th level, you learn the {@spell control weather} spell and can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability cast these two spells in this way when you finish a long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

name: Siberys Mark of Warding
entries: The Siberys Dragonmark of Warding provides the following benefits:

items: You learn the {@spell alarm} spell if you don't already know it, and can cast it once without expending a spell slot. When you reach 15th level, you learn the {@spell demiplane} spell and can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast these two spells in this way when you finish a long rest. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

When you cast the {@spell alarm} spell with your Siberys mark, or when you use a 2nd-level spell slot or above, you can also choose to arm it with the {@spell glyph of warding} spell, in addition to its normal effects. Both spells end when the {@spell alarm} spell is triggered or ends.

Your Scoridra siblings have started to understand each other's personalities and skillsets in the field. Sibling Cooperation negates Sibling Rivalry's negative effects of having the following skill check after using Sibling Rivalry to always having Disadvantage.

name: Side Gig
entries: The character gains proficiency in 2 skills of their choice, or double the proficiency modifier of a single skill they are proficient in. The character can also spend time, at least 1 hour for 4 out of 7 days a week, performing a side job that will earn them {@dice 2d6} gp per week, added every 7 days.

name: Sidearm Master
entries: You have mastered the art of wielding a sidearm with delicate precision. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls made with these weapons.
When you take the attack action with a sidearm can use a bonus action to make an attack roll at a creature within 10 feet of you.
When you roll initiative and are not surprised, you can use your reaction to draw a sidearm and attack a creature within its normal range.

name: Siege Expert
entries: You have spent significant time operating siege equipment, earning you the following benefits:

items: You add your proficiency bonus to attack and damage rolls using siege weapons.
If a siege weapon would require an action to aim, you can use a bonus action instead.
During a short rest, provided you have access to {@item carpenter's tools|phb} or similar equipment, you can restore {@dice 1d10} hit points to a siege weapon.

name: Signature Technique

otherSummary.entry: At least one Martial Exploit Known

entries: You have practiced a single technique to the point of mastery. Choose a {@filter 1st-degree Exploits|optionalfeatures|feature type=ll:1me} you know from those available to the {@loader Alternate Fighter|class/LaserLlama; Alternate Fighter.json} that does not restore hit points.
In combat, you can use this Exploit once per round without expending an Exploit Die, rolling a {@dice d4} for the Exploit Die. You regain this feature at the start of each of your turns.

name: Silver Pyromancer

prerequisite.other: must be able to use an arcane spellcasting focus and worship the Silver Flame.

entries: Your faith in the Silver Flame empowers and augments your arcane spellcasting. You gain the following benefits:

items: You learn the {@spell sacred flame} or {@spell light} cantrip. Once you make this choice it cannot be changed. You cast this cantrip using the same spellcasting ability that you use for other spells you cast using an arcane spellcasting focus.
You have advantage on Constitution saving throws that you make to maintain your concentration on a spell when you take damage.
Whenever you use an arcane spellcasting focus to cast a spell that deals fire damage, you can choose for the spell's damage to be radiant damage instead.

name: Silver Soul

prerequisite.other: Requires the blessing of Argynvost, a Breath Weapon and a superiority die

entries: Part of Argynvost's spirit now resides within you, making it possible to for you to use an extent of his power for a short period of time. You learn the following Battlemaster maneuvers:

items: {@optfeature Diamond Dust|COMOptFeat}. When you take the Dragonborn Breath Weapon action, you can expend one superiority die to increse its range and damage. The range of the Breath Weapon is doubled and every damage dice turns into the superiority die used. Example: if your Breath Weapon normally deals {@dice 4d6} damage, has 15 ft. cone range and the expended superiority die is a d10, when you use this maneuver, the Breath Weapon would instead deal {@dice 4d10} damage and have 30 ft. cone range.

{@optfeature Spectral Wings|COMOptFeat}. When you fall from any height, you can expend your superiority die and use your reaction to protect yourself from any fall damage. When you do so, your falling rate becomes 60 ft per round until you land. The first time you hit a creature with an attack before landing, you can add your superiority die to the damage.

entries.name: Credits
entries: Art and item designed by {@link Zordnael for 'Curse Of Strahd'|https://github.com/Zordnael/Zordnael-Homebrew}. Please credit if you repost elsewhere.

When you do so, your falling rate becomes 60 ft per round until you land. The first time you hit a creature with an attack before landing, you can add your superiority die to the damage.

name: Silver Tongue

prerequisite.other: {@feat Enduring Encouragement|TalentTrees} or {@feat Captivating|TalentTrees} or {@feat Leading by Example|TalentTrees}

entries: Your influence leads others to follow your directions without even stopping to consider why. As an action, you can suggest a reasonable course of activity (limited to a sentence or two) to subtly influence a creature within 30 feet of you that can hear and understand you. It must make a Wisdom saving throw against a DC of 8 + your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus or behave as if a {@spell suggestion} spell has been cast on it. This suggestion is not magical, and lasts for a number of hours equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1 hour). Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you complete a long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Silver-Tongued
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Argumentative
entries: You can use your choice of Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma for Persuasion checks.

entries.name: Diplomatic
entries: When you take the {@action Influence|XPHB} action, you can treat a {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} creature as {@variantrule Indifferent [Attitude]|XPHB|Indifferent}, and an {@variantrule Indifferent [Attitude]|XPHB|Indifferent} creature as {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly}.

entries.name: Polyglot
entries: You learn three languages of your choice.

name: Silver-Tongued
entries: You develop your conversational skill to better deceive others. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Deception} skill. If you are already proficient in the skill, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.

When you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can replace one attack with an attempt to deceive one humanoid you can see within 30 feet of you that can see and hear you. Make a Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check contested by the target's Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check. If your check succeeds, your movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks from the target and your attack rolls against it have advantage; both benefits last until the end of your next turn or until you use this ability on a different target. If your check fails, the target can't be deceived by you in this way for 1 hour.

name: Simian
entries: You hail from a world that followed a slightly different evolutionary path than High Terra; your people all resemble monkeys or apes. Despite your more primitive appearance and your prominent tail, you are just as intelligent as other humans—you just like bananas a little more. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a climbing speed equal to half your movement speed.
You can hold and manipulate objects and weapons with your hands, feet, and tail, but you can't make attack rolls with weapons held by your tail.

name: Simian
entries: You hail from a world that followed a slightly different evolutionary path to High Terra; your people all resemble monkeys or apes. Despite your furry appearance and prominent tail, you are just as intelligent as other humans—you just like bananas a little more. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Climbing Speed
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Prehensile Tail
entries: You can hold and manipulate objects and weapons with your hands, feet, and tail, but you can't make attacks with weapons held by your tail.

entries.name: Soft Landing
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when you fall to reduce any damage you take from the fall by an amount equal to five times your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

name: Sin of Envy

prerequisite.other: You can't have another Sin or Grace Feat

entries: You embody the essence of Envy, carrying within you the spiteful desire to drag those above you down to your level. This manifestation grants you the power to strip away advantages, suppress extraordinary abilities, and reduce even the mightiest foes to something ordinary.
You gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Devil Inside
entries: You gain the Fiend Creature Type in addition to your other Creature Types.

entries.name: Demonic Lore
entries: The Seven Demon Princes have witnessed countless ages and remember the history of the world. You have Advantage on History checks.

entries.name: Manifestation of Envy
entries: You are skilled at concealing your resentment behind false admiration and carefully chosen words. You have Advantage on Deception checks.

entries.name: Avatar of Leviathan
entries: Your body carries the bitter cold of envy, a presence that chills even those who stand above you. You have Resistance to Cold damage.

entries.name: Drag Them Down
entries: You focus your envy upon a single creature, seeking to strip away everything that makes it superior.

As an Action, choose one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The creature becomes the target of your Envious Mark. This effect requires Concentration, as if you were concentrating on a spell, and lasts for up to 1 minute.
While you maintain Concentration on Envious Mark, the target is subject to the effects granted by your current level.
If your Concentration ends, Envious Mark ends immediately, and all effects caused by Envious Mark end.

entries.name: Level 1
entries: Your envy begins by stripping away the foundations that allow others to endure. While a creature is affected by your Envious Mark, its AC is reduced by an amount equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Whenever the target regains Hit Points, it regains only half the normal amount. Any Regeneration the target possesses is reduced by half.

entries.name: Level 3
entries: Your envy strips away what others have given the target. All temporary Hit Points the target currently has are removed, and the target can't gain Temporary Hit Points while affected by your Envious Mark.
The target can't regain Hit Points or benefit from Regeneration.

entries.name: Level 5
entries: Your envy begins to tear away the strengths that make the target formidable. The target takes a penalty to its Attack Rolls equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
The target's Speed is halved.
The target loses Darkvision.

entries.name: Level 7
entries: You refuse to allow the target any advantage that places it above you. Advantage on Attack Rolls, Ability Checks, and Saving Throws is negated, causing those rolls to be made normally.
The target loses all Resistance.
The target loses Blindsight.

entries.name: Level 9
entries: You begin stripping away the gifts that make the target exceptional. Each of the target's Ability Scores is reduced by an amount equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
The effects of the target's Magic Items are suppressed while it remains affected by your Envious Mark.
The target loses Tremorsense.

entries.name: Level 11
entries: Your accumulated power no longer requires uninterrupted rest to return. You regain the use of Drag Them Down when you finish a Short or Long Rest.
Additionally, at the end of each of your turns, if you have no uses of your Drag Them Down remaining and you did at least one of the following during that turn, roll 1d6:

items: Made an Attack Roll against an enemy.
Forced an enemy to make a Saving Throw.
Took damage from an enemy since the end of your previous turn.

entries: On a roll of 6, you regain one use of your Drag Them Down.

entries.name: Level 13
entries: You strip away the traits that make the target something greater than ordinary. The target loses all Immunities to damage and Conditions.
The target loses its ability to Fly, Swim, or Climb unless those movement modes are provided by its normal walking speed.
The target loses all Passive Traits.
The target loses Truesight.
All of the target's Senses are reduced to normal sight.

entries.name: Level 15
entries: There is nothing left for your envy to take, so you begin dragging the target itself into decline.
At the end of each of the target's turns, it gains 1 level of Exhaustion.
The target can't speak or communicate telepathically while affected by your Envious Mark.

entries.name: Level 17
entries: At the height of your envy, nothing about the target is allowed to remain beyond your reach. The target loses all Traits.
The target can't use Mythic Actions, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Regional Effects, or Multiattack.
The effects of the target's passive and activated Features are suppressed while it remains affected by your Envious Mark.

entries.name: Level 19
entries: Your envy becomes absolute. Your Envious Mark cannot be countered, interrupted, dispelled, or otherwise prevented by any spell, feature, ability, or other effect.

name: Sin of Gluttony

prerequisite.other: You can't have another Sin or Grace Feat

entries: You embody the essence of Gluttony, carrying within you an insatiable hunger that consumes not only flesh, but the very essence of those you devour.
You gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Devil Inside
entries: You gain the Fiend Creature Type in addition to your other Creature Types.

entries.name: Demonic Lore
entries: The Seven Demon Princes have witnessed countless ages and remember the history of the world. You have Advantage on History checks.

entries.name: Manifestation of Gluttony
entries: Your insatiable hunger allows you to endure what would overwhelm others. You have Advantage on Survival checks.

entries.name: Avatar of Beelzebub
entries: Your body has become resistant to the corrosive nature of your endless hunger. You have Resistance to Acid damage.

entries.name: Feed The Void
entries: You can consume the remains of a creature that has been reduced to 0 Hit Points or has died within the last 24 hours.
When you Devour a creature, you gain Devour Points equal to its Challenge Rating. If it has no Challenge Rating, you instead gain Devour Points equal to its Level.

You can gain Devour Points from a specific creature stat block only once. Once you have gained Devour Points from a creature using a particular stat block, consuming another creature that uses the same stat block provides no additional Devour Points.
Your accumulated Devour Points can be spent to permanently enhance your body and abilities. Unless otherwise stated, spent Devour Points are lost.
You unlock additional ways to spend your Devour Points as you gain levels in this feat. You can only use the options unlocked at your current level or lower.

entries.name: Level 1
entries: You have Advantage on Saving Throws against Disease.
1 Devour Point → Regain Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

entries.name: Level 3
entries: You have Advantage on Saving Throws against the Poisoned condition.
2 Devour Points → Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

entries.name: Level 5
entries: You have Resistance to Poison damage.
3 Devour Points → Increase your Hit Point Maximum by 1, up to a maximum of your Level × 10.

entries.name: Level 7
entries: You are Immune to Disease.
5 Devour Points → Increase your AC by 1. This bonus is Natural Armor and can increase your AC by up to your Proficiency Bonus + your Primary Ability Modifier.

entries.name: Level 9
entries: You have Advantage on Death Saving Throws.
10 Devour Points → Increase one Ability Score by 1. There is no maximum total increase, but each Ability Score can be increased by no more than your Proficiency Bonus × 2.

entries.name: Level 11
entries: Your accumulated power no longer requires uninterrupted rest to return. You regain the use of Feed The Void when you finish a Short or Long Rest.
Additionally, at the end of each of your turns, if you have no uses of your Feed The Void remaining and you did at least one of the following during that turn, roll 1d6:

items: Made an Attack Roll against an enemy.
Forced an enemy to make a Saving Throw.
Took damage from an enemy since the end of your previous turn.

entries: On a roll of 6, you regain one use of your Feed The Void.

entries.name: Level 13
entries: You are Immune to Poison damage and the Poisoned condition.
15 Devour Points → Gain one Damage Resistance.

entries.name: Level 15
entries: You automatically succeed on all Death Saving Throws.
25 Devour Points → Gain one Condition Immunity.

entries.name: Level 17
entries: Your hunger has become limitless. Whenever you Devour a creature, you gain Devour Points equal to twice its Challenge Rating. If it has no Challenge Rating, you instead gain Devour Points equal to twice its Level.
100 Devour Points → Gain one Damage Immunity.

entries.name: Level 19
entries: Your Sin Feat cannot be countered, interrupted, or otherwise prevented by any spell, feature, ability, or other effect.

name: Sin of Greed

prerequisite.other: You can't have another Sin or Grace Feat

entries: You embody the essence of Greed, carrying within you the boundless avarice and insatiable hunger of Mammon. This manifestation grants you supernatural resilience, a covetous presence, and the power to claim that which you desire as your own.
You gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Devil Inside
entries: You gain the Fiend Creature Type in addition to your other Creature Types.

entries.name: Demonic Lore
entries: The Seven Demon Princes have witnessed countless ages and remember the history of the world. You have Advantage on History checks.

entries.name: Manifestation of Greed
entries: You embody insatiable desire and avarice, driven to possess anything of value. You have Advantage on Sleight of Hand checks.

entries.name: Avatar of Mammon
entries: Your desire to possess and control manifests as an unyielding force. You have Resistance to Force damage.

entries.name: Now Is Mine
entries: When a creature you can see casts a spell, you can use your Reaction to prepare that spell. You retain the prepared spell until you finish a Long Rest.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Level 3
entries: The creature that cast the triggering spell must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the spell has no effect, and the creature regains the Spell Slot expended to cast it.

entries.name: Level 5
entries: The target automatically fails the saving throw, and the creature doesn't regain the Spell Slot expended to cast it.

entries.name: Level 7
entries: The triggering effect no longer needs to be a spell. You can steal any spell or feature of a creature you can see, causing the spell or feature to have no effect. The creature doesn't regain any resource expended to use the stolen spell or feature.

After you steal a spell or feature, you gain the benefits of the stolen spell or feature. If the stolen effect is a spell or an activated feature, you can use it once without expending any resources. You retain the stolen spell or feature until you steal another spell or feature, and it doesn't disappear when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Level 9
entries: The number of spells or features you can steal and retain at the same time increases by an amount equal to your proficiency bonus. You can replace any spell or feature you currently retain whenever you steal a new spell or feature.

entries.name: Level 11
entries: You regain the use of Now Is Mine when you finish a Short or Long Rest.
Additionally, at the end of each of your turns, if you have no uses of your Now Is Mine remaining and you did at least one of the following during that turn, roll 1d6:

items: Made an Attack Roll against an enemy.
Forced an enemy to make a Saving Throw.
Took damage from an enemy since the end of your previous turn.

entries: On a roll of 6, you regain one use of your Now Is Mine.

entries.name: Level 13
entries: After you steal a spell or feature, the creature that cast the spell or used the feature can't use that spell or feature again until it finishes a Long Rest.

entries.name: Level 15
entries: You can target the corpse of a creature or the soul of a creature if its soul still exists to steal one spell or feature that creature possessed. You gain the benefits of the stolen spell or feature as though you had stolen it using Now Is Mine.

entries.name: Level 17
entries: There is no limit to the number of spells or activated features you can retain at the same time.

entries.name: Level 19
entries: Your Sin Feat cannot be countered, interrupted, or otherwise prevented by any spell, feature, ability, or other effect.

name: Sin of Lust

prerequisite.other: You can't have another Sin or Grace Feat

entries: You embody the essence of Lust, carrying within you the irresistible temptation and overwhelming desire of Asmodeus. This manifestation grants you supernatural resilience, an enchanting presence, and the power to awaken absolute devotion in the hearts of others.
You gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Devil Inside
entries: You gain the Fiend Creature Type in addition to your other Creature Types.

entries.name: Demonic Lore
entries: The Seven Demon Princes have witnessed countless ages and remember the history of the world. You have Advantage on History checks.

entries.name: Manifestation of Lust
entries: You embody irresistible beauty and desire, causing others to become drawn toward you. You have Advantage on Persuasion checks.

entries.name: Avatar of Asmodeus
entries: Your voice carries the irresistible temptation of Asmodeus, and your body has adapted to withstand the power of sound itself. You have Resistance to Thunder damage.

entries.name: Look At Me
entries: As an Action, choose one creature you can see within range.
The creature must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC or have the Charmed condition for 1 hour.
While affected, the creature regards you as a trusted companion, speaks to you in a friendly manner and am happy to accommodate your small requests.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Level 3
entries: The duration increases to 8 hours.
The creature regards you as one of its closest companions and deeply trusts you. It willingly accepts requests that don't directly harm itself or violate its core beliefs.

entries.name: Level 5
entries: The duration increases to 1 day.
The creature considers you one of the most important people in its life and refuses to knowingly harm you.
It willingly accepts requests that cause it personal inconvenience or minor losses.

entries.name: Level 7
