entries: The duration increases to 7 days.
The creature becomes devoted to you. It willingly places itself in danger to protect you and accepts requests involving reasonable personal risk.
If another creature threatens you, it instinctively attempts to defend you before considering its own safety.

entries.name: Level 9
entries: The duration increases to 1 month.
The creature's affection becomes obsession.
It can no longer willingly act against your interests and accepts requests that provide no benefit to itself or require great personal sacrifice.

entries.name: Level 11
entries: The duration increases to 1 year.
You regain the use of Look At Me when you finish a Short or Long Rest.
Additionally, at the end of each of your turns, if you have no uses of your Look At Me remaining and you did at least one of the following during that turn, roll 1d6:

items: Made an Attack Roll against an enemy.
Forced an enemy to make a Saving Throw.
Took damage from an enemy since the end of your previous turn.

entries: On a roll of 6, you regain one use of your Look At Me.

entries.name: Level 13
entries: The duration increases to 10 years.
You become the most important person in the creature's life.
It is willing to risk its life, betray allies, abandon loyalties, reject its beliefs, and sacrifice treasured possessions if doing so benefits you.

Additionally, if the creature is immune to being Charmed or immune to magical effects that influence the mind, it must still make the Charisma saving throw against Look At Me normally. On a failed save, this feature ignores that immunity.

entries.name: Level 15
entries: The duration increases to 100 years.
The creature's devotion becomes absolute.
It willingly sacrifices its life, soul, memories, or anything else it possesses if you command it to do so.
Additionally, A creature targeted by Look At Me automatically fails saving throws against this feature.

entries.name: Level 17
entries: The duration becomes permanent.
Look At Me no longer charms or magically compels its target.
Instead, it permanently rewrites the creature's desires, emotions, and loyalties.
The creature genuinely believes that its devotion toward you is its own free will, and this effect isn't considered being Charmed, magically compelled, or under mind control.

entries.name: Level 19
entries: Your Sin Feat cannot be countered, interrupted, or otherwise prevented by any spell, feature, ability, or other effect.

name: Sin of Pride

prerequisite.other: You can't have another Sin or Grace Feat

entries: You embody the essence of Pride, carrying within you the power and arrogance of Lucifer. This manifestation grants you supernatural resilience, an imposing presence, and the ability to reject any outcome that would place you beneath another.
You gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Devil Inside
entries: You gain the Fiend Creature Type in addition to your other Creature Types.

entries.name: Demonic Lore
entries: The Seven Demon Princes have witnessed countless ages and remember the history of the world. You have Advantage on History checks.

entries.name: Manifestation of Pride
entries: You embody superiority and perfection. You have Advantage on Intimidation checks.

entries.name: Avatar of Lucifer
entries: Your mind is unyielding, and your ego refuses to be broken. You have Resistance to Psychic damage.

entries.name: That's Your Flaw
entries: When you take damage, are hit by an attack, or fail a saving throw, you can take a Reaction to reject that outcome. You can use this feature to protect yourself from damage or an attack. You take half damage that triggered this feature.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Level 3
entries: You take no damage and suffer no other effects from the attack or damage that triggered this feature.

entries.name: Level 5
entries: You can now use That's Your Flaw when you fail a saving throw. You instead succeed on that saving throw, suffering no effects that would occur as a result of failing it.

entries.name: Level 7
entries: When you use That's Your Flaw to negate an attack or the effects of a failed saving throw, you can cause the effect to be reflected back upon its source.

If you reflect an attack, the attack is resolved against its original attacker, using the same attack roll and comparing it against the attacker's AC. The attacker can still make any saving throw normally allowed by the attack.
If you reflect the effects of a failed saving throw, the creature that caused the saving throw must instead suffer the effects of that failed save.

entries.name: Level 9
entries: When you reflect an attack using That's Your Flaw, you can choose one of the following effects:

items: The reflected attack automatically hits and becomes a Critical Hit.
The target automatically fails any saving throw caused by the reflected attack.

entries.name: Level 11
entries: You regain the use of That's Your Flaw when you finish a Short or Long Rest.
Additionally, at the end of each of your turns, if you have no uses of your That's Your Flaw remaining and you did at least one of the following during that turn, roll 1d6:

items: Made an Attack Roll against an enemy.
Forced an enemy to make a Saving Throw.
Took damage from an enemy since the end of your previous turn.

entries: On a roll of 6, you regain one use of your That's Your Flaw.

entries.name: Level 13
entries: After you use That's Your Flaw, you gain the benefits of a Short Rest, except that That's Your Flaw can't be recharged this way. You also gain resistance to all damage until the end of your next turn.
Additionally, The reflected attack deals the maximum damage instead of rolling its damage dice.

entries.name: Level 15
entries: When you die, you can use That's Your Flaw to reject your death. You return to life with Hit Points equal to half your Hit Point maximum, and you suffer no negative effects from dying. The creature that caused your death takes Psychic damage equal to the total damage you took during the current turn.
You can use That's Your Flaw even if you are unconscious or otherwise unable to take actions or reactions.

entries.name: Level 17
entries: After you use That's Your Flaw, you gain the benefits of a Long Rest, except that That's Your Flaw can't be recharged this way. Until the end of your next turn, you are Immune to all damage and Conditions, and nothing can cause you to die.
Additionally, all creatures within 120 feet of you become Frightened for 1 minute, ignoring Immunity to the Frightened condition.

entries.name: Level 19
entries: Your Sin Feat cannot be countered, interrupted, or otherwise prevented by any spell, feature, ability, or other effect.

name: Sin of Sloth

prerequisite.other: You can't have another Sin or Grace Feat

entries: You embody the essence of Sloth, carrying within you the endless stagnation and lethargy of Belphegor. This manifestation grants you supernatural resilience, an oppressive stillness, and the power to accumulate destructive force by refusing to act.
You gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Devil Inside
entries: You gain the Fiend Creature Type in addition to your other Creature Types.

entries.name: Demonic Lore
entries: The Seven Demon Princes have witnessed countless ages and remember the history of the world. You have Advantage on History checks.

entries.name: Manifestation of Sloth
entries: You embody stillness and unnatural patience, allowing you to endure while others exhaust themselves. You have Advantage on Stealth checks.

entries.name: Avatar of Belphegor
entries: Your body remains unnaturally still even as destructive energy gathers within you. You have Resistance to Lightning damage.

entries.name: Far Too Late
entries: As a Bonus Action, you begin accumulating destructive energy within yourself. The first time you use this feature, you gain one Inertia Die.
At the start of each of your turns, the current Inertia Die remains until you use a Bonus Action to increase it. You can use a Bonus Action on subsequent turns to gain the next Inertia Die.
Whenever you use a Bonus Action to increase your Inertia Die, you gain the additional benefits granted by your current level until the start of your next turn.

You can release the accumulated energy whenever you deal damage to a creature with an attack or other effect. When you do so, you add all accumulated dice to the damage dealt. The damage dealt by the accumulated dice is the same damage type as the damage that triggered the release.
You can release the accumulated energy even if you have not reached the maximum number of Inertia Dice.
Once you release the accumulated energy, you can't use Far Too Late again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Level 3
entries: As the power within you begins to settle, your body becomes harder to disturb. Whenever you use a Bonus Action to increase your Inertia Die, your AC increases by an amount equal to your Proficiency Bonus until the start of your next turn.
Your Inertia Die becomes a d6 starting on your second turn.

entries.name: Level 5
entries: The longer you remain still, the more your body absorbs the force that would otherwise break it. Whenever you use a Bonus Action to increase your Inertia Die, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your primary ability modifier.
Your Inertia Die becomes a d8 starting on your third turn.

entries.name: Level 7
entries: Your stillness begins to reject the violence of the world itself. Whenever you use a Bonus Action to increase your Inertia Die, you have Advantage on Saving Throws until the start of your next turn, and the first Attack Roll made against you before then has Disadvantage.
Your Inertia Die becomes a d10 starting on your fourth turn.

entries.name: Level 9
entries: The force you refuse to release begins sustaining your body, turning patience into unnatural recovery. Whenever you use a Bonus Action to increase your Inertia Die, you regain Hit Points equal to one roll of your current Inertia Die plus your Constitution modifier. This does not expend the Inertia Die.
Your Inertia Die becomes a d12 starting on your fifth turn.

entries.name: Level 11
entries: Your accumulated power no longer requires uninterrupted rest to return. You regain the use of Far Too Late when you finish a Short or Long Rest.
Additionally, at the end of each of your turns, if you have no uses of your Far Too Late remaining and you did at least one of the following during that turn, roll 1d6:

items: Made an Attack Roll against an enemy.
Forced an enemy to make a Saving Throw.
Took damage from an enemy since the end of your previous turn.

entries: On a roll of 6, you regain one use of your Far Too Late.

entries.name: Level 13
entries: Your stillness reaches an unnatural perfection, causing both body and mind to resist the world around you. Whenever you use a Bonus Action to increase your Inertia Die, you gain Resistance to all damage and Immunity to all Conditions until the start of your next turn.
You can continue accumulating energy beyond the sixth Inertia Die.

entries.name: Level 15
entries: The force you have accumulated becomes too great to vanish with your death. If you die while Far Too Late is active, the energy within you erupts violently.
Each creature within 30 feet of you must make a Dexterity Saving Throw, taking 66d6 Force damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
After this eruption occurs, Far Too Late ends.

entries.name: Level 17
entries: At the height of your power, even restraint becomes terrifying. The longer you refuse to act, the more catastrophic the force you accumulate becomes. Starting on your sixth turn, your Inertia Die becomes a d100.
After the sixth Inertia Die, each additional Inertia Die is a d100.
You can continue accumulating energy without being limited by the normal maximum number of Inertia Dice.

entries.name: Level 19
entries: Your Sin Feat cannot be countered, interrupted, or otherwise prevented by any spell, feature, ability, or other effect.

name: Sin of Wrath

prerequisite.other: You can't have another Sin or Grace Feat

entries: You embody the essence of Wrath, carrying within you the boundless fury of Satan. This manifestation grants you overwhelming physical power, relentless speed, and the ability to unleash your anger without limit.
You gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Devil Inside
entries: You gain the Fiend Creature Type in addition to your other Creature Types.

entries.name: Demonic Lore
entries: The Seven Demon Princes have witnessed countless ages and remember the history of the world. You have Advantage on History checks.

entries.name: Manifestation of Wrath
entries: Your fury manifests through overwhelming physical force. You have Advantage on Athletics checks.

entries.name: Avatar of Satan
entries: Your rage burns with an infernal fire that cannot be extinguished. You have Resistance to Fire damage.

entries.name: Burn It All
entries: As a Bonus Action, you unleash your Wrath, entering Wrath Form for 1 minute.
While in Wrath Form, whenever a creature hits you with an attack, you can use your Reaction to make an Attack or cast a spell that requires an Attack Roll against that creature.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Level 3
entries: While in Wrath Form, you are Immune to the Frightened and Charmed conditions, and your Speed is doubled.

entries.name: Level 5
entries: While in Wrath Form, you have Advantage on Attack Rolls, and your Attack Rolls score a Critical Hit on a roll of 6

entries.name: Level 7
entries: Your attacks ignore Resistance. If a creature is Immune to the damage dealt by your attack, it instead takes damage as though it had Resistance.

entries.name: Level 9
entries: While in Wrath Form, you gain one additional Action on each of your turns, and your Attack Rolls score a Critical Hit on a roll of 13

entries.name: Level 11
entries: You regain the use of Burn It All when you finish a Long Rest.
Additionally, at the end of each of your turns, if you have no uses of your Burn It All remaining and you did at least one of the following during that turn, roll 1d6:

items: Made an Attack Roll against an enemy.
Forced an enemy to make a Saving Throw.
Took damage from an enemy since the end of your previous turn.

entries: On a roll of 6, you regain one use of your Burn It All.

entries.name: Level 13
entries: Your attacks ignore Immunity.
Your attacks made as a reaction to being hit are always Critical Hits

entries.name: Level 15
entries: Your attacks made as a reaction to being hit no longer require a Reaction.
Whenever one of these attacks deals damage, you regain Hit Points equal to half the damage dealt.

entries.name: Level 17
entries: While in Wrath Form, nothing can end or suppress your Wrath Form before its duration expires.
Your attacks made as a reaction to being hit deal twice the normal damage of a Critical Hit.

entries.name: Level 19
entries: Your Sin Feat cannot be countered, interrupted, or otherwise prevented by any spell, feature, ability, or other effect.

name: Singer
entries: You are professionally trained or gifted as a vocalist, granting you the following benefits:

items: You are proficient with your voice, which you can use to make tools checks as a musical instrument.

name: Six-Gun Ace
entries: You have perfected the art of shooting with your revolver or hand cannon. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls with these weapons.
You cannot be disarmed while wielding a revolver or hand cannon in one hand and your other hand is free.

When you make an attack with your revolver or hand cannon and are not holding anything in your other hand, you can use your bonus action to make two additional attacks against creatures within its normal range. You do not add your ability score modifier to the damage of these attacks.

items.name: Proficiency
items.entry: You gain proficiency in one skill of your choice.

items.name: Expertise
items.entry: Gain expertise in a skill offered by the class that granted you this feat. If you were proficient in that skill, gain proficiency in a skill of your choice.

name: Skilled
entries: You gain proficiency in any combination of three {@book skills|phb|7|skills} or {@filter tools|items|type=tools;artisan's tools;instrument;gaming set;vehicle (land);vehicle (water)|source=yastah} of your choice.

name: Skirmisher
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Mobility
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet.

entries.name: Strike and Fade
entries: Once on each of your turns, you can deal extra damage equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to a creature you hit with an attack that deals Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, as long as you have moved 15 feet prior to making the attack.

name: Skulker (Alternate)
entries: You are an expert at slinking through shadows and staying hidden when you need to. You gain the benefits below:

entries.name: Skuler's Sight
entries: Dim light does not impose disadvantage on your ability checks that rely on your sense of sight.

entries.name: Silent Steps
entries: When you are lightly obscured, you can take the {@action Hide} action as a bonus action on your turn.

entries.name: Silent Shots
entries: If you are hidden from a creature and miss with a ranged attack, you do not reveal your position.

name: Skulker
entries: When you are hidden from a creature and miss it with a ranged weapon attack, making the attack doesn't reveal your position.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Skulker
entries: When you are hidden from a creature and miss it with a ranged weapon attack, making the attack doesn't reveal your position.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Skulker
entries: You gain the following benefit and the first two available Tiers of the Skulker Feat:
{@b The Tiers of the Skulker Feat:}

name: Skulker
entries: You are expert at slinking through shadows. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can try to hide when you are lightly obscured from the creature from which you are hiding.
When you are hidden from a creature and miss it with a ranged weapon attack, making the attack doesn't reveal your position.
Dim light doesn't impose disadvantage on your Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks relying on sight.

name: Sky Bridge
entries: Your arcane panels no longer disappear at the end of your turn, allowing you to stay aloft between turns. Other creatures can also walk across your arcane panels.
As a bonus action, you can remove sections of your arcane panels. Any creature or object on the removed panels fall if nothing else is holding them aloft.

name: Sky Warden
entries: You are trained for both scouting the skies and aerial combat. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in the Perception skill if you don't already have it. You add double your proficiency bonus to Perception checks that rely on sight.
Once per turn, if you are flying and dive at least 30 feet straight toward a target and then hit it with a melee weapon attack, the attack deals an extra {@dice 1d6} damage to the target.

name: Sky Warden
entries: You are trained for both scouting the skies and aerial combat. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Perception} skill if you don't already have it. You add double your proficiency bonus to {@skill Perception} checks that rely on sight.
Once per turn, if you are flying and dive at least 30 feet straight toward a target and then hit it with a melee weapon attack, the attack deals an extra {@damage 1d6} damage to the target.

name: Sky-Splitting Comet

entries.name: Repeatable:
entries: No
The deceptive deadliness of the meteor hammer reaches its full potential in your hands. You gain the following benefits:

items: You may use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier for attack and damage rolls with a meteor hammer.
If you have the {@classFeature Martial Arts|Monk|PHB|1} feature, a meteor hammer is a monk weapon for you.
When you use a meteor hammer, its damage die changes from a d8 to a d12.
When you make a melee attack with a meteor hammer on your turn, you can use your reaction to increase your reach by 20 feet (to 30 feet total) until the start of your next turn.

name: Skybound Imitation*
entries: The skies bless you, whether you know it or not. You gain the following benefits:

items: The time of day no longer slows you down. When the celestial body in the sky is not the one you were born under, your speed will be its base 30.

Once per day, you can create Sunlight or Moonlight respectively. This racial Spell makes you glow with 10 ft of bright light, requires concentration to keep active, and lasts for 1 minute. When you create your respective light during the time of day in which you'd normally gain no benefits, you do gain those benefits while the spell is active. Only your own spell can give you this effect.

name: Skyterror
entries: The weight of your body is a terrifying weapon in its own right, and you've learned to master it by brutally diving onto your enemies. You gain the following benefits:

items: On your turn, when you score a critical hit with a natural weapon or reduce a creature to 0 hit points with one, you can use your bonus action to launch yourself up to 15 feet into the air without provoking opportunity attacks.
Your Glide & Fly Speed is doubled when moving directly toward the ground.

If you move at least 30 feet directly toward a target on a turn, you can choose to take a -5 penalty to any attack roll made with a natural weapon. If the attack hits, you add +10 to the attack's damage.

name: Slasher
entries: Once per turn when you hit a creature with an attack that deals slashing damage, you can reduce the speed of the target by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Slasher
entries: You gain the following benefit and the first two available Tiers of the Slasher Feat:
{@b The Tiers of the Slasher Feat:}

name: Slashing Claws, Silent Paws
entries: When making a Sneak Attack, if any of the Sneak Attack dice roll their maximum face value, you may {@action Hide} as a free action.

name: Sledgehammer Fists
entries: Your hands and forearms increase in size, your metal and stone construction forming them into heavier, bulkier gauntlet-like forms. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your Iron Fists racial trait now allows you to deal bludgeoning damage equal to {@dice 1d8} + your Strength modifier when you hit with an unarmed strike.

If both of your hands are free and you hit with an unarmed strike on your turn, as bonus action you may clasp your hands together and deliver a hammer blow as an unarmed strike. If the hammer blow hits, it deals bludgeoning damage equal to {@dice 1d12} + your Strength modifier.

name: Sleeping Poison
entries: Sleeping Poison

items: Increase your Dexterity or Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
Over a short or long rest, you can conjure a fey poison, which you can apply one weapon or up to 10 pieces of ammunition with the Use an Object action.
You can only have one such conjured poison at any time. Once applied, this poison lasts for 1 hour.

Immediately after a creature takes damage from a weapon or piece of ammunition coated in this poison, if that creature has remaining hit points less than or equal to 5 + your total character level, the creature falls unconscious.
Creatures immune to the poisoned condition ignore this effect.
A creature unconscious in this way remains so for up to 1 hour, or until an adjacent creature uses an action to rouse them.

name: Sleepwalker
entries: As a creature born of dreams, your body remains agile while you sleep. You do not automatically fall {@condition prone} while {@condition unconscious}, and while unconscious you can move and take the {@action Dash}, {@action Disengage}, and {@action Dodge} actions normally.

name: Sling Master
entries: The range of slings increases to 60/150 feet in your hands.

Finally, once per turn you may try to load two stones into a sling when you attack with it. If you do, when you take the attack action on your turn to attack with a sling, you may make one additional attack with disadvantage against the same target as part of the action.

name: Slinger
entries: You are with trained with a sling as a weapon of war.

items: When using lead or other dense, uniform {@item sling bullet|phb|bullets} rather than rough stones as ammunition, your range with {@item sling|phb|slings} increases to 60/240.
If you wield a weapon or shield in your other hand while using a sling, you may still load it as if you had a free hand.
You may use your bonus action to make a ranged attack with your sling.

name: Slinger
entries: You are an expert with the sling, capable of striking your foes with deadly precision. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to damage rolls made with a sling.
When you use a sling, its damage die increases from a d4 to a d6. (This benefit has no effect if another feature has already improved the weapon's die.)
Your weapon attacks with a sling score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.
When you score a critical hit using a sling, the target can't take reactions until the end of your next turn.

name: Slinger
entries: Once per turn, when you make a ranged attack with a {@item sling|PHB}, you can target two creatures that you can see that are within 5 feet of each other. You must have ammunition for each of them.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Slinger
entries: Once per turn, when you make a ranged attack with a {@item sling|PHB}, you can target two creatures that you can see that are within 5 feet of each other. You must have ammunition for each of them.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Slippery
entries: You have advantage on saving throws made to avoid or resist traps and you have resistance to the damage dealt by traps. Whenever you succeed on a Dexterity saving throw, you can use your reaction to move up to half your movement.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Slippery
entries: You have advantage on saving throws made to avoid or resist traps and you have resistance to the damage dealt by traps. Whenever you succeed on a Dexterity saving throw, you can use your reaction to move up to half your movement.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Slither
entries: You are considered to be lightly obscured while you are {@condition prone}.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Slither
entries: You are considered to be lightly obscured while you are {@condition prone}.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Small but Mighty
entries: You overcome the limits of your small frame. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your strength score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You count as if you were one size larger for the purpose of determining your carrying capacity.
You count as if you were one size larger for the purpose of making attacks.

name: Small Folk
entries: Hobbits are a little people, but their resourcefulness far exceeds their stature. You have learnt how to exploit your small size to your advantage in a fight.

items: Medium or larger creatures cannot gain advantage on attack rolls against you while you are not {@condition incapacitated}.
You don't provoke {@action opportunity attack||opportunity attacks} from Medium or larger creatures.

name: Smite
entries: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can expend one spell slot to deal radiant damage to the target, in addition to the attack's normal damage. The extra damage is 2d8 for a 1st-level spell slot, plus 1d8 for each spell level higher than 1st, to a maximum of 6d8 (5th-level spell slot). If you have the {@feat Greater Favored Enemy|Adventurer} feat, the damage increases by 1d8 if the target is the type of your Greater Favored Enemy.

otherSummary.entry: proficiency with {@item smith's tools|phb}

items: After the end of a long rest, you can temper a melee weapon to increase its damage by 1. Each individual weapon can be modified once.

Additionally, choose an amount of armor equal to your proficiency, you temper armor to have temporary protection. Each armor tempered gives to the wearer temporary hit points according to its type: Light: equal to the highest class level of the wearer. Medium: two times the highest class level of the wearer. Heavy: three times the highest class level of wearer. Each armor can be tempered once.

name: Smooth Talker
entries: You are accustomed to using words to get out of difficult situations and know just the right thing to say in most circumstances. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on Wisdom (Insight) and Charisma (Persuasion) checks with individuals you have never met before.
If you are in combat with a creature and are able to speak a language that creature understands, you may use your action to try to convince the creature to hold their attack.

The creature must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier). On a failed saving throw the target does not attack you or your allies until the start of your next turn, or until another creature makes an attack against it

name: Smuggler
entries: Daring pilots can profit handsomely from small shipments of questionable legality basically anywhere in the 'verse. Having learned the ins and outs of smuggling, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Piloting|DarkMatter} skill. If you are already proficient in the skill, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.
You have advantage on ability checks you make to pilot a ship undetected, conceal cargo, and to deceive others about the contents of your cargo.

When things go awry, you shoot first. When you roll initiative and you aren't surprised, you can use your reaction to draw and make a ranged weapon attack with a one-handed blaster against a target within the weapon's range.

name: Snake in the Grass
entries: You have honed the innate abilities of your kin, able to assume the form of any snake you have seen. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can cast the {@spell suggestion} spell, requiring no spell slot or components, and you must finish a long rest before you can cast it this way again. Your spellcasting ability for the spell is the ability increased by this feat. If you have spell slots of 2nd level or higher, you can cast this spell with them.

YOu can use your action to magically transform into a {@creature Giant Poisonous Snake|MM}. The transformation follows the criteria and limitations of the druid's {@classFeature Wild Shape|Druid|PHB|2} feature, though it only lasts for up to 1 hour. When you transform, you may choose the appearance of the snake, though not so much that its size changes. Once you use this ability, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

name: Snake Tongue
entries: Snakes are renowned for their unparalleled sense of taste. Your tongue has become a sensitive sensory organ that you can use to perceive the world around you. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain {@sense blindsight} out to a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can see anything that isn't behind total cover, even when blinded or if you are in darkness. You can see {@condition invisible} creatures in that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you.
You can communicate with serpentine beasts and monstrosities, as if you share a language.
You have advantage on all Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks you make using your taste.

name: Snapback
entries: As an action, you can use a {@item whip|PHB} to pull objects weighing 5 lbs or less which are within your reach towards you. If you have a free hand, you catch the object, otherwise it lands at your feet.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Snapback
entries: As an action, you can use a {@item whip|PHB} to pull objects weighing 5 lbs or less which are within your reach towards you. If you have a free hand, you catch the object, otherwise it lands at your feet.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Snarecrafting Adept

items: You are skilled in devising simple traps. You gain proficiency with {@item tinker's tools|PHB}, and you learn to craft two snares of your choice from the {@filter Basic Snares list|optionalfeatures|source=tmr|feature type=mr:bs} (see the {@class Martial Ranger|TMR|Trapper|Trapper|TMR} archetype from the {@homebrew martial} ranger class). If you have the {@subclassFeature Snarecrafter|Martial Ranger|TMR|Trapper|TMR|3|TMR} feature, you learn two additional {@filter Basic Snares|optionalfeatures|source=tmr|feature type=mr:bs}; if you have the {@subclassFeature Advanced Snarecrafter|Martial Ranger|TMR|Trapper|TMR|11|TMR} feature, you can learn one {@filter Advanced Snare|optionalfeatures|source=tmr|feature type=mr:as} instead.

entries: A snare is built within a single 5-foot square. Once constructed, it can't be moved without destroying or triggering the snare.
Crafting a snare takes one minute and requires you to be holding {@item tinker's tools|PHB} in both hands. You can have a number of snares crafted equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded up.
Your snare DC equals {@b 8 + your proficiency bonus + the ability modifier of the score increased by this feat}. All saving throws and checks triggered by snares use your snare DC.
You can choose whether the snare is visible or hidden; if you choose hidden, a creature must succeed on a {@skill Perception} or {@skill Investigation} check against your snare DC to find it.

name: Sneak Attack
entries: You learn how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll. The attack must use Dexterity.

You don't need advantage on the attack roll if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn't incapacitated, and you don't have disadvantage on the attack roll. You can select this feat multiple times, increasing the extra damage by 1d6 each time."

name: Sneak Attack
entries: You gain the {@classFeature Sneak Attack|Treasure Hunter|TLotRR|1|TLotRR} feature. The extra damage is {@dice 1d6}.

You know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra {@dice 1d6} damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll. The attack must use a {@itemProperty F||finesse} or a ranged weapon.
You don't need advantage on the attack roll if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn't {@condition incapacitated}, and you don't have disadvantage on the attack roll.

name: Snow Dog
entries: You love the snow! You are naturally adapted to cold climates, as described in {@book chapter 5 of the Dungeon Master's Guide.|DMG|5|Weather}

name: Snowrunner
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Ice Walking
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws and ability checks to maintain your balance on slippery surfaces and on snow.

entries.name: Winter's Edge
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks in snowy or icy terrain.

name: Socialite
entries: The character becomes especially proficient at navigating in high society. When wearing the appropriate style of dress (either merchant or noble dress) the character can gain advantage on a {@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Deception} roll (as high society individuals are more likely to hang on their every word) when interacting with a noble or celebrity a number of times equal to their proficiency modifier; all uses are regained at the end of a long rest. In addition, they can request meetings with such individuals or their presence at high-society events.

name: Song-Craft
entries: You have been trained in the art of singing, according to the tradition of the wandering minstrels. Your musical lore runs deeper than most, as you partake of the knowledge of the mighty singers of old. As an action, you can spend a craft slot and make a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) check, contested by the Intelligence ({@skill Riddle|TLotRR}) check of each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you that can hear you. A creature can choose to fail its ability check if it wishes. For each target against which you win the contest, choose one of the following options:

items: You can suppress any effect causing the target to be {@condition charmed} or {@condition frightened} until the end of your next turn. This effect ends if the target can no longer hear you.

You can make the target indifferent about creatures of your choice that it is hostile towards until the end of your next turn. The target also has disadvantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks made to perceive any creature other than you for the same duration. This effect ends if the target can no longer hear you, it is harmed, or if it witnesses any of its friends being harmed.

Until the end of your next turn, whenever the target makes an attack roll or a saving throw, the target must roll a {@dice d4} and either add the number rolled to the attack roll or saving throw (if the target is friendly to you), or subtract it (if the target is hostile). This effect ends if the target can no longer hear you.

entries: When you reach 5th level, you can use a bonus action on each of your turns to extend the duration of each of these effects on all targets until the end of your next turn, up to 1 minute.

name: Sonon Mastery
entries: You have proven your ability to the gatekeepers of {@i sonon}. You have been entrusted with a secret {@i sonon} word that would destroy anyone not strong enough to utter it. Knowledge of this word has enhanced one of your skills. Increase the skill of your choice according to the table below by 1, to a maximum of 20, to represent this enhancement.

entries.name: Sonon Ability
entries: You gain one of the following abilities, corresponding to the {@i sonon} word you learned. The starting size of the Sonon die used by these abilities is a d6.

items.name: Rī Strike
entries: Once on each of your turns when you hit with an attack roll, you can roll your Sonon die after you make the damage roll and add it to the total damage.

items.name: Shu Incantation
entries: Whenever you make a spellattack, you can roll your Sonon die and add the number rolled to the attack roll. You can choose to do so before or after rolling the d20, but before you know whether the attack hit.

items.name: Kan Technique
entries: Whenever you make a skill check for a skill you are proficient in, you can roll your Sonon die and add the number rolled to the check. You can choose to do so before or after rolling the d20, but before you know whether the check succeeded.

items.name: Ken Blessing
entries: Whenever you or an ally within 30 feet makes a saving throw, you can use your reaction to roll your Sonon die and add the number rolled to the saving throw. You can choose to do so before or after rolling the d20, but before you know whether the saving throw succeeded.

entries.name: Changing the Die's Size
entries: When you roll your Sonon die, it decreases by one die size after the roll. This represents you burning through your Sonon energy. For example, if the die is a d6, it becomes a d4. The minimum die size is a d4.

If you roll a 1 on your Sonon die, you are overwhelmed by the force of the Sonon flowing through you, and you take psychic damage equal to the maximum roll of the Sonon die. The die then shrinks to a d4.

Whenever you finish a long rest, your Sonon die resets to its starting size. When you reach certain levels, the starting size of your Sonon die increases: at 5th level (d8), 11th level (d10), and 17th level (d12). If you take the Sonon Mastery feat more than one time, you don't get more than one die.

entries.name: Sonon Replenishment
entries: As a bonus action, you can calm your mind for a moment and restore your Sonon die to its starting size. You then can't use Sonon Replenishment again until you finish a long rest

name: Sorcerous Blood
entries: Gain the first two available Tiers of the Sorcerous Blood feat:
{@b The Tiers of the Sorcerous Blood Feat:}

name: Sorcerous Spark
entries: While you may not be a true Sorcerer, within you dwells a small spark of arcane power. You gain the benefits below:

items: You learn two Cantrips and a single 1st-level spell of your choice from the {@loader Alternate Sorcerer|class/LaserLlama; Alternate Sorcerer.json} spell list. Charisma is your spellcasting modifier for all three spells, unless you already have a spellcasting modifier, then you use it.

You gain two Sorcery Points which you can expend to cast any spells that you know, as if you were a Sorcerer. If you already have Sorcery Points, these are added to your pool of Sorcery Points. You regain your Sorcery Points from this feature each time you finish a long rest.

name: Sorcerous Vigor
entries: When your magical reserves are low, you can call on your lifeforce to fuel your magic.

items: When you start your turn and have no {@classFeature sorcery points|Sorcerer||2} remaining, you can use a reaction to spend one Hit Die. Roll the die and add your Constitution modifier to it. You regain expended sorcery points equal to up to half the total (minimum of 1). You can never have more sorcery points than the maximum for your level. Hit Dice spent using this feat can't be used to regain hit points during a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|short rest}. You regain spent Hit Dice as normal.

name: Soul of the Raven
entries: You gain the ability to merge with your raven spirit. As a bonus action when your raven is perched on your shoulder, your body merges with your raven's form. While merged, you become Tiny, you replace your speed with the raven's, and you can use your action only to Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Help, Hide, or Search. During this time, you gain the benefits of your raven being perched on your shoulder. As an action, you and the raven return to normal.
Additionally, you gain advantage on death saving throws, immunity to the {@condition frightened} condition, and resistance to necrotic damage while the raven is perched on your shoulder.

name: Soul Projection
entries: You learn the {@spell find familiar} spell and can cast it as ritual. When casting the spell this way, your familiar is a {@creature specter|MM}, with it being considered an undead, instead of a celestial, fey, or fiend. It doesn't have it's Sunlight Sensitivity trait.

name: Soul Twin

otherSummary.entry: You can only take this feat during character creation

entries: You were born as a pair of soul twins, identical twins that share a single soul and act as an extension of one another. These twins function as a single character with two bodies, which you control.

entries.name: Actions
entries: Your twins share a single action, bonus action, and reaction between them, each of which can be taken only once by one of the twins on your turn. If you take the {@action Dash}, {@action Disengage}, {@action Dodge}, {@action Help}, {@action Hide}, {@action Ready}, or {@action Search} actions, both twins perform the action and gain its benefits.

entries.name: Attacks
entries: If you take the {@action Attack} action to attack with one twin, the other twin can attack as a bonus action. You don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative. If you're able to make multiple attacks, you can divide these attacks between the twins.

entries.name: Hit Points
entries: Soul twins have separate hit points, which are divided between them. At 1st level, each twin has the hit points of a character of the same class. At higher levels, each soul twin's hit point maximum increases by your Constitution modifier + half a roll of the class's Hit Die (rounded up). If you use the average value instead of rolling the Hit Die, each twin gains 2 for a d6 class, 3 for a d8 class, 3 for a d10 class, 4 for a d12 class.
When you spend Hit Dice following a short rest, you must spend the dice separately on each twin.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries: A pair of soul twins can only concentrate on one spell at a time. However, only one of the twins needs to concentrate on a spell to maintain it. When you cast a spell which requires concentration, you choose which twin is concentrating on it.
When casting a spell, either twin can provide the spell components, and the spell can originate from the twin of your choice.

entries.name: Magical Effects
entries: If a spell or magical ability affects one soul twin, it affects them both, unless that spell or ability affects hit points, or if the two twins are further than 100 feet apart. In either case, it affects each twin separately.

entries.name: Conditions
entries: A condition, such as being {@condition poisoned} or {@condition grappled}, affects only one twin, even if imposed by a spell.

entries.name: Death
entries: When a soul twin is reduced to 0 hit points and begins to make death saving throws, the other twin becomes {@condition incapacitated} and its speed is halved. If a soul twin dies, the other twin quickly begins to deteriorate, and perishes 24 hours later if their partner doesn't return to life.

entries.name: Empathic Link
entries: As long as both twins are on the same plane, they can empathetically sense the other's emotional state. Each twin knows when the other takes damage.

entries.name: Soul Twins
entries: The Soul Twins feat is an advanced option that shouldn't be taken by new players or those that routinely control other creatures, such as captains and necromancers. If it is unclear how a spell or effect would affect the soul twins, the GM adjudicates the outcome. A good rule of thumb is that if it heals, harms, or grabs a twin, it affects only one; if it charms, curses, enchants, or protects a twin, it affects both.

name: Spawn oF Juiblex
entries: Your faint relation to Juiblex becomes apparent, as your fiendish traits manifest.

items: The first time on a turn you hit with a pseudopod attack, it deals {@dice 2d6} acid damage instead of {@dice 1d6}.

A creature that start its turn grappled by you must succeed a Constitution saving throw or be poisoned until the end of your next turn. The DC is equal to 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus. You can suppress this effect at will.
You gain a climbing speed equal to half of your walking speed and can use it to climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings without needing to make an ability check.
You learn the {@spell Acid Splash|PHB} cantrip. Constitution is your spellcasting ability to cast the spell.

name: Speak of the Devil
entries: When you hear a creature within 30 feet of you say your name, you can use your reaction to teleport to an available space within 5 feet of the creature. You can do this a number of times equal to your charisma modifier. You regain all expended uses of this feature after completing a long rest.

name: Speak of the Devil
entries: When you hear a creature within 30 feet of you say your name, you can use your reaction to teleport to an available space within 5 feet of the creature. You can do this a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier. You regain all expanded uses of this feature after completing a long rest.

name: Spear Expert
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Deflecting Haft
entries: You can use a {@item Spear|XPHB} to deflect incoming attacks. While holding a {@item Spear|XPHB}, you gain a +1 bonus to your AC.

entries.name: Expert Thrower
entries: The range of any {@item Spear|XPHB} you throw is 30/90.

entries.name: Spear Ready
entries: If you take the {@action Ready} action to attack with the {@item Spear|XPHB}, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the triggered attack.

name: Spear Specialist
entries: You have trained to become a deadly warrior with pole weapons, capable of making lunging attacks and long-distance throws. You gain the following benefits:

items: When you use a {@item javelin|phb}, {@item spear|phb}, or {@item trident|phb}, its damage die changes from a {@dice d6} to a {@dice d8}, and from a {@dice d8} to a {@dice d10} when wielded with two hands, if possible (this feature has no effect if another feature has already improved the weapon's die).
As a bonus action, you can extend the reac of your javelin, spear, or trident by 5 feet.
You can make a ranged attack with a javelin, spear, or trident up to its long range without disadvantage, even underwater.

name: Spear Specialist
entries: You have trained to become a deadly warrior with pole weapons, capable of making lunging attacks and long-distance throws. You gain the following benefits:

items: When you use a {@item javelin|phb}, {@item spear|phb}, or {@item trident|phb}, its damage die changes from a {@dice d6} to a {@dice d8}, and from a {@dice d8} to a {@dice d10} when wielded with two hands, if possible (this feature has no effect if another feature has already improved the weapon's die).
As a bonus action, you can extend the reac of your javelin, spear, or trident by 5 feet.
You can make a ranged attack with a javelin, spear, or trident up to its long range without disadvantage, even underwater.
You swap out one skill proficiency you had for expertise in two skills that you already are proficient with.

name: Specialized Weapon Arts

prerequisite.other: A feat or fighting style which specializes in a weapon

entries: Your mastery over a weapon class or fighting style grants you further benefits to your Weapon Arts. You may use any Weapon Art twice per turn when wielding a weapon you specialize in.

name: Specialty Acts
entries: Performers can specialize in a variety of different kinds of acts, utilizing many different skills while plying their entertainment trade. Choose two skills from the list below.

items: Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics})
Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling})
Strength ({@skill Athletics})
Charisma ({@skill Deception})
Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand})

entries: You can substitute your bonus to {@skill Performance} for the original bonus when making a check with either of the chosen skills.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Specialty Acts
entries: Performers can specialize in a variety of different kinds of acts, utilizing many different skills while plying their entertainment trade. Choose two skills from the list below.

items: Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics})
Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling})
Strength ({@skill Athletics})
Charisma ({@skill Deception})
Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand})

entries: You can substitute your bonus to {@skill Performance} for the original bonus when making a check with either of the chosen skills.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

items: You gain a bonus to your initiative equal to your proficiency bonus.
Choose a creature type (Aberration, Beast, Celestial, Construct, Dragon, Elemental, Fey, Fiend, Giant, Monstrosity, Ooze, Plant, Undead).
As long as you're not {@condition incapacitated}, you know when one or more creatures of the chosen type are within 60 feet of you.
You have advantage on Wisdom checks to perceive (Perception) and track (Survival) creatures of the chosen type.
You have advantage on attacks against creatures of the chosen type that you can see.

name: Spectral Visage

prerequisite.other: {@feat Spellbook|Adventurer} (School of Illusion or Necromancy)  or {@feat Acolyte: Grave|Adventurer} or {@feat Acolyte: Trickery|Adventurer}, 6th Level

entries: You gain the ability to adopt a humanoid's persona. When a humanoid dies within 30 feet of you, you can magically capture its shadow using your reaction. You retain this shadow until you use it or you finish a long rest.

As an action, you can transform the shadow into a disguise that appears on you, granting you the humanoid's appearance while they were healthy and alive. This disguise lasts for 1 hour or until you end it as a bonus action. While you're in the disguise, you gain access to all information that the humanoid would freely share with a casual acquaintance such as general details on its background and personal life. The information is enough that you can pass yourself off as the person by drawing on its memories. Another creature can see through this disguise by succeeding on a Wisdom (Insight) check contested by your Charisma (Deception) check. You gain a +5 bonus to your check.
Once you capture a shadow with this feature, you can't capture another one with it until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Speech of the Ancient Beasts
entries: You have a special connection with the natural world. Great beasts regard you as their kin, and you possess the ability to speak the languages of the most powerful and mystic of their kind. You gain the following benefits:

items: Beasts of Large size or larger have a friendly disposition toward you unless you have attacked them.
You have advantage on Charisma checks made against beasts that are of Large size or larger.

You can speak and understand {@language Giant Eagle|MM}, {@language Giant Elk|MM}, and {@language Giant Owl|MM}. You can otherwise be understood by any beast of Large size or larger, whether or not they speak a language. Beasts with Intelligence scores of 4 or lower may only be able to understand simple concepts.

name: Speech of the Lotus
entries: You have spent your waking hours in the comfort of nature, learning the calm, soothing ways of nature's prose. You gain the following benefits:

items: You learn to speak, read, and write Sylvan and two additional languages of your choice.

When you reach 5th level, you can cast the {@spell speak with plants} spell, without expending a spell slot, and you must finish a long rest before you can cast it this way again. You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

name: Speech-Craft
entries: You are a student of {@language Sindarin|TLotRR} and {@language Quenya|TLotRR}, the Ancient Tongue, and have advantage on Charisma checks when interacting with Elves.

In addition, as an action you can spend a craft slot and choose a creature other than an Elf, or a Wizard, or a similarly powerful creature, within 30 feet of you who can hear you. Then, choose one of the following options:

items: Make a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check contested by the target's Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check. A target has advantage on this check if it is Large or larger or if it cannot understand you. If you win the contest, the target is {@condition frightened} of you for 1 minute. The {@condition frightened} target can make a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check against your passive Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) score at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. When you reach 5th level, you can target one additional creature, or two additional creatures at 9th level.

Make a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) or Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check contested by the target's Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check. A target has advantage on this check if it is immune to being {@condition charmed} or if it cannot understand you. If you win the contest, you can speak a one-word command that the target must follow on its next turn, if it can and if the command is not directly harmful to it. Once the target has executed the command, it ends its turn. Some typical commands include {@i "Fall!"} (the target falls {@condition prone}), {@i "Flee!"} (the target moves away from you), and {@i "Halt!"} (the target doesn't move and takes no actions), and the effect may be considered a Misdeed depending on the circumstances. When you reach 5th level, you can target one additional creature, or two additional creatures at 9th level.

name: Speedy
entries: You gain the following benefit and the first two available Tiers of the Speedy Feat:
{@b The Tiers of the Speedy Feat:}

name: Speedy Metabolism
entries: Your body's needs have taught you the value of speed over flavor.

items: You may eat an entire meal in a full round, and may drink a potion as a bonus or free object interaction (if already in hand).
You gain proficiency in {@item cooking Utensils} or expertise if you are already proficient.
You may use an additional food item a day.
You require an additional meal each day. (4 meals)

When a non-abjuration spell that targets you and only you is cast, you can use your reaction to make an {@skill Arcana} check. If the {@skill Arcana} check is higher than 10 + the spell's level, you choose to negate either the damage or the rest of the spell's effects. If the {@skill Arcana} check is higher than 14 + the spell level, you negate both. If the {@skill Arcana} check is higher than 20 + the spell's level, you deflect the spell back to the caster.

name: Spell Mastery (1st-Level)
entries: You gain mastery over a basic spell and can cast it with no effort. When you take this feat, choose one 1st-level spell from your {@feat spellbook|Adventurer}. You can cast this spells at its lowest level without expending a spell slot when you have it prepared. If you want to cast the spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal.

name: Spell Mastery (2nd-Level)
entries: You gain mastery over a powerful spell and can cast it with no effort. When you take this feat, choose one 2nd-level spell from your {@feat spellbook|Adventurer}. You can cast this spells at its lowest level without expending a spell slot when you have it prepared. If you want to cast the spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal.

name: Spell Scrivener

otherSummary.entry: proficiency with a {@item calligrapher's supplies|PHB}

entries: Using {@item calligrapher's supplies|PHB|calligrapher's tools}, you can select one spell you know and spend the corresponding amount of gold and time from the table below to craft one {@item Spell Scroll} of that spell:

This gold and time expenditure does not need to happen consecutively. If this spell requires a material component that is consumed in casting, you must expend it in this process. At the end of the process, you must expend a spell slot of a level equal to the spell you are scribing the Spell Scroll for.

name: Spell Slinger Initiate

otherSummary.entry: Spellcasting, Pact Magic, or Velocity Spellcasting feature

entries: You learn two cantrips of your choice from the {@filter marksman spell list|spells|class=marksman (DXM)}.

Your spellcasting ability for these spells is Intelligence. If the spell is also on the spell list of a class that you have the Spellcasting or Pact Magic feature from, you can use that class's spellcasting ability instead.
In addition, you can cast any spell you know from the marksman spell list as if you had the {@classFeature Spell Slinger|Marksman|DXMarksman|5|DXMarksman|} feature from the marksman class.

name: Spell Sniper (Expanded)

prerequisite.other: The ability to cast at least one spell

entries: You have learned techniques to enhance your attacks with certain kinds of spells, gaining the following benefits:

items: When you cast a spell that requires you to make an attack roll, the spell's range is doubled.
Your ranged spell attacks ignore half cover and three-quarters cover.

You learn one cantrip that requires an attack roll. Choose the cantrip from the Bard, Cleric, Druid, Sorcerer, Warlock, Witcher, or Wizard spell list. Your spellcasting ability for this cantrip depends on the spell list you choose from: Charisma for Bard, Sorcerer, or Warlock; Wisdom for Cleric or Druid; or Intelligence for Witcher or Wizard.

name: Spell Sniper
entries: You gain the following benefits.

items.name: Shrapnel
items.entry: When you hit a creature that is behind cover with a spell attack, deal extra damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

items.name: Casting in Melee
items.entry: Being within reach of an enemy doesn't impose Disadvantage on your Attack Rolls with Spells.

items.name: Increased Range
items.entry: When you cast a Spell that has a range of at least 10 feet and that requires you to make an Attack Roll, you can increase the Spell's range by 60 feet.

name: Spell Sniper
entries: When you cast a spell that requires you to make an attack roll, the spell's range is doubled. Your ranged spell attacks ignore half cover and treat three-quarters cover as half cover.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Spell Sniper
entries: When you cast a spell that requires you to make an attack roll, the spell's range is doubled. Your ranged spell attacks ignore half cover and treat three-quarters cover as half cover.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Spell Sniper
entries: You have learned techniques to enhance your attacks with certain kinds of spells, gaining the following benefits:

items: When you cast a spell that requires you to make an attack roll, the spell's range is doubled.
Your ranged spell attacks ignore half cover and three-quarters cover.

You learn one cantrip that requires an attack roll. Choose the cantrip from the {@filter bard|spells|level=0|class=bard|spell attack=m;r;o|source=yastah}, {@filter cleric|spells|level=0|class=cleric|spell attack=m;r;o|source=yastah}, {@filter druid|spells|level=0|class=druid|spell attack=m;r;o|source=yastah}, {@filter sorcerer|spells|level=0|class=sorcerer|spell attack=m;r;o|source=yastah}, {@filter warlock|spells|level=0|class=warlock|spell attack=m;r;o|source=yastah}, or {@filter wizard|spells|level=0|class=wizard|spell attack=m;r;o|source=yastah} spell list. Your spellcasting ability for this cantrip depends on the spell list you chose from: Charisma for bard, sorcerer, or warlock; Wisdom for cleric or druid; or Intelligence for wizard.

name: Spell Thief

prerequisite.other: {@spell dispel magic} spell or {@spell counterspell} spell, 17th Level

entries: When you cast {@spell counterspell} or {@spell dispel magic} and successfully negate the spell, you can force the caster to make a saving throw with its spellcasting ability modifier. The DC equals your spell save DC used to cast {@spell counterspell} or {@spell dispel magic}. On a failed save, you steal the knowledge of the spell if it is at least 1st level and of a level you can cast. For the next 8 hours, you know the stolen spell and can cast it using your spell slots. If you use this ability again to steal another spell, you lose the ability to cast the stolen spell. The original caster can't cast the stolen spell while you know the stolen spell.

name: Spell Versatility
entries: The breadth of your aptitude for magic expands, allowing you greater flexibility. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma by 1, to a maximum of 20.

The number of spells you can prepare increases by 2. If you don't prepare spells, you instead learn two spells of your choice from the spell list mentioned in your Spellcasting or Pact Magic feature, which don't count against the number of spells you know. The spells must be of a level you can normally learn.

When you complete a short rest, you can choose one of the spells you have prepared and replace it with a different spell from the same list. Alternatively, when you complete a long rest, you can choose one of the spells you know and replace it with another spell from the same list. A spell you learn or prepare in this way must be of a level you can normally learn or prepare.

name: Spellblade
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Blade Cantrips
entries: You learn two of the following cantrips of your choice: {@spell Arc Blade|ValdaPlayerPack2}, {@spell Burning Blade|ValdaPlayerPack2}, {@spell Frigid Blade|ValdaPlayerPack2}, or {@spell True Strike|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells (choose when you select this feat). Whenever you gain a new level, you can change your cantrip selection.

entries.name: Arcane Strike
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can replace one of the attacks with casting {@spell Arc Blade|ValdaPlayerPack2}, {@spell Burning Blade|ValdaPlayerPack2}, {@spell Frigid Blade|ValdaPlayerPack2}, or {@spell True Strike|XPHB}.

entries.name: Channeled Attack
entries: When you make an attack using Strength or Dexterity with a weapon with which you have proficiency, you can gain a bonus to the attack roll equal to your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier (minimum of +1). Choose the ability each time you use this benefit. You can gain this bonus a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Blade Cantrips
entries: You learn two of the following cantrips of your choice: {@spell Arc Blade|ValdaSpire24}, {@spell Burning Blade|ValdaSpire24}, {@spell Frigid Blade|ValdaSpire24}, or {@spell True Strike|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells (choose when you select this feat). Whenever you gain a new level, you can change your cantrip selection.

entries.name: Arcane Strike
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can replace one of the attacks with casting {@spell Arc Blade|ValdaSpire24}, {@spell Burning Blade|ValdaSpire24}, {@spell Frigid Blade|ValdaSpire24}, or {@spell True Strike|XPHB}.

entries.name: Channeled Attack
entries: When you make an attack using Strength or Dexterity with a weapon with which you have proficiency, you can gain a bonus to the attack roll equal to your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier (minimum of +1). Choose the ability each time you use this benefit. You can gain this bonus a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Spellblade
entries: You've learned to meld your strikes with sparks of arcane magic, gaining the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with one {@filter martial melee weapon|items|type=melee weapon;martial weapon|category=} of your choice.
When you deal bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage with a melee weapon, you can change the damage to your choice of acid, cold, fire, or lightning damage.

You learn two cantrips of your choice from among the following: {@spell arc blade|VSS}, {@spell burning blade|VSS}, {@spell caustic blade|VSS}, and {@spell frigid blade|VSS}. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells.
You can cast the {@spell shield} spell once without using a spell slot. Once you cast this spell using this feat, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

name: Spellbook
entries: Select a school of magic from the following list: Abjuration, Conjuration, Divination, Enchantment, Evocation, Illusion, Necromancy, and Transmutation. You gain a spellbook containing three 1st-level spells from your chosen school. You gain the ability to use your spellbook as your spellcasting focus. Cantrips cannot be recorded in a spellbook. If you have a spellbook from another feat such as {@feat Ritual Caster}, you can use the same book for both feats.

entries.name: Preparing Spells
entries: You prepare the list of spells that are available for you to cast. To do so, choose a number of spells from your spellbook equal to your spellcasting modifier + your proficiency bonus (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of spells requires time spent studying your spellbook and memorizing the incantations and gestures you must make to cast the spell: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list.

entries.name: Copying a Spell into the Book
entries: When you find a spell of 1st level or higher, you can add it to your spellbook if it is of a level you can cast and if you can spare the time to decipher and copy it.

For each level of the spell, the process takes 2 hours and costs 50 gp. The cost represents material components you expend as you experiment with the spell to master it, as well as the fine inks you need to record it. Once you have spent this time and money, you can prepare the spell just like your other spells.

A spell scroll can be copied just as spells in spellbooks can be copied. When you copy a spell from a spell scroll, you must succeed on an Intelligence (Arcana) check with a DC equal to 10 + the spell's level. If the check succeeds, the spell is successfully copied. Whether the check succeeds or fails, the spell scroll is destroyed.

entries.name: Replacing the Book
entries: You can copy a spell from your own spellbook into another bookâ€"for example, if you want to make a backup copy of your spellbook. This is just like copying a new spell into your spellbook, but faster and easier, since you understand your own notation and already know how to cast the spell. You need spend only 1 hour and 10 gp for each level of the copied spell. If you lose your spellbook, you can use the same procedure to transcribe the spells that you have prepared into a new spellbook. Filling out the remainder of your spellbook requires you to find new spells to do so, as normal. For this reason, it may be wise to keep a backup spellbook in a safe place.
You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do so, you must choose a different school of magic.

name: Spellcasting Affinity*
entries: You have become adept at casting particular spells, so they take on additional effects. When you gain this feat, choose one of the following damage types: acid, cold, fire, force, lightning, necrotic, poison, radiant, or thunder. You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do so, you must choose a different damage type.
When you damage a target with the chosen damage type using a spell of 1st level or higher, an additional effect applies:

rows: The target takes a -2 penalty to its AC until the start of your next turn.
The target's speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.
The target is set ablaze and takes 1d6 fire damage per turn until put out.
The target is pushed back up to 5 feet.
The target can't take reactions until the start of its next turn.
The target can't regain hit points until the end of your next turn.
The target is poisoned until the start of your next turn.
The target is blinded until the start of your next turn.
The target is deafened until the start of your next turn.

name: Spellcasting Style

prerequisite.other: The ability to cast a cantrip

entries: You adopt a particular style of spellcasting as your specialty. Choose a spellcasting style from the list below. You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do so, you must select a different spellcasting style.

entries.name: Destructive
entries: You can add your spellcasting modifier to the damage you deal with any cantrip that involves a ranged or melee spell attack.

entries.name: Elementalist
entries: Choose a damage type. Whenever you cast a cantrip, you can choose whether to cast it with its original damage type or with your chosen damage type. You can select this style multiple times. Each time you do so, you must choose a different damage type.

entries.name: Repelling
entries: When you hit a creature with booming blade, green-flame blade, or a cantrip that involves a melee or ranged spell attack, you can push the creature up to 10 feet away from you in a straight line.

entries.name: Prepared
entries: When you take take the Ready action to cast a cantrip that involves a saving throw, you can impose disadvantage on the saving throw against a target by casting the cantrip immediately after their turn ends.

entries.name: Dualcast
entries: When you cast a cantrip that does not deal damage, you can cast the cantrip twice in the same action. If the cantrip requires concentration, both effects are treated as part of the same spell. If you lose concentration of the spell, both effects end.

name: Spelldriver
entries: Through intense focus, training, and dedication, you've harnessed the techniques of rapid spellcasting. You are no longer limited to only one non-cantrip spell per turn. However, should you cast two or more spells in a single turn, only one of them can be of 3rd level or higher.

name: Spelldriver
entries: Through intense focus, training, and dedication, you've harnessed the techniques of rapid spellcasting.

When you use your bonus action to cast a spell of 1st level or higher, you can also use your action to cast another spell of 1st level or higher. However, if you cast two or more spells in a single turn, only one of them can be 3rd level or higher.

entries.name: Rules Tip: Casting Multiple Spells
entries: Normally, when you cast a spell as a bonus action, you can't use your action to also cast a spell that turn unless that spell is a cantrip—{@note see {@book PHB p202|PHB|10|Bonus Action}.} The Spelldriver feat removes that restriction, but the focus necessary to channel multiple spells in the same round still limits the overall power of those spells.

items.name: Somatic Components
items.entry: You can perform the Somatic Components of a spell with a hand that is holding a shield.

items.name: Protect Concentration
items.entry: If you receive a bonus to your AC from your shield or cover against an effect and that effect causes you to make a saving throw to maintain concentration, add those AC bonuses to the saving throw.

items: When you cast a spell using a spell slot on your turn, you can choose to take a penalty to the spell attack roll equal to your proficiency bonus. If the attack hits, it deals additional damage equal to two times your proficiency bonus. You can affect up to 2 spell attack rolls per turn. This limit increases to 3 at level 11.
Reducing a creature to 0 hit points with Spellslinger allows you to cast a cantrip as a bonus action.

name: Spellsneak
entries: When you fulfill the criteria for {@feat Sneak Attack|Adventurer} with a ranged or melee spell attack, excluding the ranged or finesse weapon requirement, you can expend 1 sorcery point to apply your Sneak Attack damage to the attack.

name: Spellsword
entries: You can perform the somatic components of a spell with a hand that isn't empty. It cannot be a hand that is holding a material component that is being used in a spell. Your weapon's base damage has +1 while you have a hand that isn't holding a weapon or a shield.

name: Spellsword Adept
entries: You have trained to combine your minor magics with close-range weapon attacks. You gain the benefits listed below:

entries.name: Bonus Cantrips
entries: You learn two {@filter Cantrips|spells|level=0|class=magus (llmag)} from the {@loader Magus|class/LaserLlama; Magus.json} spell list. One must deal damage. Choose either Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as their spellcasting ability. If you can learn Cantrips from your class, you can instead choose to learn two additional Cantrips from your class spell list.

entries.name: Spellstrike
entries: Once on your turn, when you make a melee weapon attack, you can imbue the magic of one Cantrip you know into your strike. On hit, your weapon attack deals the damage type of the Cantrip, and any of the Cantrip's effects, other than damage, are applied to your target on hit.

activation.condition: Once on your turn, when you make a melee weapon attack

name: Spellweaver
entries: Further delving into your aberrant heritage, you have grown in your mastery of their alien magic. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Charisma score by 1, up to a maximum of 20.
You can use your legs to perform ths somatic components of a spell. If you are {@condition restrained} you are unable to use this feature
You learn 1 Cantrip from the Warlock spell list. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell.
You know the {@spell web} spell and Charisma is your spellcasting modifier for it. Once you cast this spell through this feature, you need to finish a long rest before you can do so again.

name: Spiderfriend Magic
entries: Your spells can't harm your vermin allies. You gain the following benefits:

items: When you cast a spell with an Area of Effect, you can choose any number of spiders, rats, snakes, bats, or other vermin within that area to be unaffected by the spell.
If an ally casts a spell that would negatively effect any of your allied spiders, rats, snakes, bats, or other vermin, you can use your reaction to prevent them from being affected by that spell.
When you cast a ranged spell, you can increase its range by 30 feet if a friendly vermin creature that is not a familiar is within 30 feet of you.

name: Spiked Plating
entries: Your aggression is manifested in sharp metal blades and spikes that grow from your plating, granting you the following benefits.

items: Whenever you deal damage with an unarmed strike, you may deal slashing or piercing damage (your choice) instead of bludgeoning damage.
Whenever you succeed on a grab or shove attempt, you deal your unarmed strike damage to the target.
Creatures grappled by you and creatures you are grappled by take your unarmed strike damage automatically at the start of their turn.

name: Spilt Arrow
entries: You have learned to modify your bow to shoot at two targets at once. When you are about to make a ranged weapon attack with a shortbow or longbow, you can choose to fire two arrows at once at two different targets that are within 30 feet of each other. When you do so, make an attack roll with disadvantage against each target.

name: Spirit Bonded
entries: You have formed a friendship with a spirit who wishes to act as your familiar.

You learn the {@spell find familiar} spell and can cast it without components or a spell slot. When you cast it in this way, your familiar ignores the restriction that prevents it from attacking. After you cast the spell with this feat, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

When you select this feat, choose one of the following familiar forms: {@creature bancho-gama|RyokoGuideToYokaiRealms}, {@creature betobeto-kun|RyokoGuideToYokaiRealms}, {@creature kawawappa|RyokoGuideToYokaiRealms}, {@creature ko-inari|RyokoGuideToYokaiRealms}, or {@creature senryoka|RyokoGuideToYokaiRealms}. You can summon your familiar in the chosen form or one of those listed in the spell's description.
