You gain proficiency with the History skill. If you already are proficient with this skill when you gain this feat, your proficiency bonus is doubled when making an ability check that uses this proficiency.
As a bonus action on your turn, choose a creature that shares a language with you within 30 feet. The next attack made by that creature has advantage.

name: Tactician
entries: You have studied history and learned to apply its lessons to battle. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

You gain proficiency with the History skill. If you already are proficient with this skill when you gain this feat, your proficiency bonus is doubled when making an ability check that uses this proficiency.

As a bonus action on your turn, choose a creature that shares a language with you and can see or hear you within 30 feet. The next attack made by that creature before the end of its next turn has advantage.

name: Tail Master
entries: You've trained your tail coordination to the point where you can use it like a third hand. You may use your tail to perform actions you would normally need a free hand for. Your tail can wield {@filter simple weapons with the light property|items|source=|type=simple weapon|property=light|category=}, but no other types of weapons and no shields. When you take an {@action attack} action while wielding a weapon with your tail, you may make an additional {@action Two-Weapon Fighting|PHB|off-hand attack}, allowing you a maximum of two off-hand attacks.

name: Tail Rejuvination
entries: Due to the magic stored inside your tails you may regain some spent spell slots. Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you may spend 1 minute to regain spell slots with a combined level that equal to or less than half your tail amount (rounded up).

name: Tailor
entries: You have become a master of sewing, weaving, and clothing design, and have developed an eye for how to make the most of any outfit. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with weaver's tools. If you are already proficient with them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.

As an action, you can assess someone's social status and lifestyle based on their clothing and accessories. Additionally, if you spend 1 minute examining a piece garment or piece of fabric, you can accurately estimate its value and, at the discretion of the DM, you gain one further piece of information about it: its age, cultural origins, or some other snippet of potentially useful information.
As a reaction, when a willing creature within 5 feet of you makes a Charisma check, you can "adjust their tie" to grant advantage on the check. You can use this feature once per short or long rest.

name: Takes One to Know One
entries: As a mimic, you have an unsurpassed insight into creatures disguised as objects . You gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on all Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks to notice a creature disguised as an object, including other mimics, constructs holding still to appear as normal statues, and so on.

If you notice that a creature has disguised as an object before it reveals itself, you have advantage on your first attack against that creature, and that creature has disadvantage on their first attack against you.

name: Talentan Warrior
entries: You have trained extensively with the traditional halfling weapons of the Talenta Plains. You gain the following benefits:

items: You may use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier for attack and damage rolls you make with a sharrash or tangat.
When you use a sharrash or tangat, its damage die changes from a {@dice d8} to {@dice 1d10}.

When you throw a Talenta boomerang, its range becomes 60/100 ft. and it always returns to you at the end of your turn, whether you hit or miss. Furthermore, you automatically succeed on catching a Talenta boomerang that returns to you.

name: Talented Linguist

prerequisite.other: Replaces the {@feat Linguist|PHB} feat found in the Player's Handbook if using the alternative language proficiency rules in Chapter 4

entries: You have studied languages extensively, gaining the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on Intelligence (Language) checks.
Choose up to three languages you know. Your proficiency level in each of the chosen languages increases by one.
When you spend your downtime Training to increase your level of language proficiency, you halve the number of workweeks required to achieve the next level of proficiency in the trained language.

name: Tanarukk Blood
entries: Through fell magic or an ancestor, you are touched by the corruptive power of Baphomet. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have resistance to fire and poison damage.

You gain a bite attack as a natural weapon, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with it, you deal piercing damage equal to {@dice 1d6} + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

name: Tattoo Mastery
entries: You have mastered a small number of spell tattoos, and can prepare these spells without referencing your caudex at all.
{@b Benefit}:

items: Increase your Intelligent score by 1, to a maximum of 20
Add a number of spells permanently to your prepared spells list equal to your proficiency bonus, tattooing them upon your skin
You gain proficiency in the Arcana skill. If you are already proficient in the skill, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.

name: Tauran
entries: Your large nose, strong jaw, and wide head do much to reveal your distantly bovine nature, but the prominent bull-horns atop your head reveal to all that you are half-minotaur. Taurans tower over most people and can solve mazes with ease, but typically possess only a shadow of their minotaur parent's might. You have the following racial traits:

entries.name: Horns
entries: You have horns that you can use to make unarmed strikes. When you hit with them, the strike deals {@damage 1d6} + your Strength modifier piercing damage, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike

entries.name: Labyrinthine Recall
entries: You always know which direction is north, and you have advantage on any Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check you make to navigate or track.

entries.name: Rush
entries: On any turn in which you only move in a straight line, your speed increases by 10 feet.

name: Tavern Brawler
entries: Renouned as a fierce unarmed fighter, you are never without a weapon. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your unarmed strikes use a {@dice d4} for damage.
When you make at least one unarmed strike as part of the the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can make one unarmed strike as a bonus action.
When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike or an improvised weapon on your turn, you can use a bonus action to attempt to {@action grapple} the target.

entries: {@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Tavern Brawler
entries: Renowned as a fierce unarmed fighter, you are never without a weapon. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your unarmed strikes use a {@dice d4} for damage.
When you make at least one unarmed strike as part of the the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can make one unarmed strike as a bonus action.
When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike or an improvised weapon on your turn, you can use a bonus action to attempt to {@action grapple} the target.

entries: {@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Tavern Brawler
entries: Gain the first two available Tiers of the Tavern Brawler feat:
{@b The Tiers of the Tavern Brawler Feat:}

name: Tavern Brawler
entries: Accustomed to rough-and-tumble fighting using whatever weapons happen to be at hand, you gain the following benefits:

items: You are proficient with improvised weapons.
Your unarmed strike uses a {@damage d4} for damage.
When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike or an improvised weapon on your turn, you can use a bonus action to attempt to grapple the target.

name: Team Coordination
entries: An entire team of all-star champions can easily lose a siegeball game against a well-coordinated team of rookies. You know that careful passes and clever tactics always count more than raw might, and as such, you gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Wisdom score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

You can effortlessly pass the siegeball to your teammates. When you make a melee weapon attack against a siegeball, you can choose to make it a pass. The ball must be directed to collide with one of your allies. You then automatically hit the ball, requiring no attack roll, and the ball does not deal damage to your ally when it collides with them.

When you roll initiative, you can switch your place in initiative order with one willing ally that has also rolled initiative. Additionally, that ally has advantage on the first attack roll it makes its first round of combat.

name: Team Player
entries: A number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1), the character can grant advantage on any save roll to a willing creature that they can see as a reaction. You regain all uses at the end of a long rest.

items: You can take the {@action Help} Action as a bonus action and the range becomes 30 feet. If the assisted character fails, you can spend your reaction to move up to half your speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

name: Teamwork
entries: You excel at lending your allies a helping hand. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Strength, Constitution or Intelligence score by 1, up to a maximum of 20.
When a creature within 5 feet of you has to make a saving throw, you can use your reaction to grant them the benefits of the {@action help} action on that roll.
When you use the {@action help} action to aid a creature with an ability check or attack role, they can add a {@dice d4} to the roll.

name: Tech Savant
entries: Thanks to extensive work and understanding of electronic devices, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with the {@item engineering kit|MH} or the {@item mechanic tools|MH} (your choice).
You have advantage on Intelligence checks made to diagnose and {@action Repairing a Device|MH|repair electronic or mechanical devices}.

name: Technical
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Cantrip Device
entries: You build a device that allows you to cast cantrip of your choice from the Wizard spell list that doesn't deal damage (choose when you build this device). When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can build a new device and choose a different cantrip for it, causing the old one to become inactive.
Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the cantrip you cast with this device (choose the ability when you select the feat).

entries.name: Mind Over Matter
entries: Choose one skill. When you make an ability check using that skill, you can use your Intelligence modifier instead of the normal ability score for that skill. When you gain a level, you replace the skill you chose with a different one.

name: Technopath
entries: You know the {@spell Technomancy|DarkMatter24} cantrip. When you reach character level 3, you learn the {@spell Technical Difficulties|DarkMatter24} spell, and when you reach character level 5, you learn the {@spell Circuit Breaker|DarkMatter24} spell. You always have these spells prepared. You can cast each of these spells once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast the spell in that way again when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast either spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells when you cast them with this feat (choose the ability when you select this feat).

name: Telekinetic
entries: You gain the following benefit and the first two available Tiers of the Telekinetic Feat:
{@b The Tiers of the Telekinetic Feat:}

name: Telekinetic Expert
entries: As a bonus action, you can try to telekinetically shove one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. When you do so, the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your chosen psionic modifier) or be moved 5 feet toward you or away from you. A creature can willingly fail this save.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Telekinetic Mastery
entries: You've studied with the master unicorn mages and have enhanced your deftness with telekinesis, including your ability with the unicorn's {@spell horn hand|mlpplaneshift} cantrip.  Gain the following benefits:

items: The max weight limit of {@spell horn hand|mlpplaneshift} increases to 30 lbs.

You can split the aura from {@spell horn hand|mlpplaneshift} to manipulate 2 objects at once, up to the max weight limit. You can use this to wield two weapons at once for Two Weapon Fighting and when used this way Two Weapon Fighting does not use your bonus action; in addition you can use this to wield versatile or two handed weapons, but not heavy weapons, in both auras.

As long as you are proficient in a weapon or set of tools, when used with {@spell horn hand|mlpplaneshift} you may use your spellcasting ability in place of your Strength or Dexterity. This does not apply to skill checks.
The range of {@spell mage hand} is increased to 60 feet.
The spell {@spell levitate} can move creatures up to 30 in altitude per turn.
While using the spell {@spell telekinesis}, you're considered proficient in the ability checks it calls for.

name: Telekinetic Novice
entries: You learn the {@spell mage hand} cantrip. You can cast it without verbal or somatic components, and you can make the spectral hand {@condition invisible}. If you already know this spell, its range increases by 30 feet when you cast it. Its spellcasting ability is the chosen psionic ability score.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Telepathic Expert
entries: You can cast the {@spell detect thoughts} spell, requiring no spell slot or components, and you must finish a long rest before you can cast it this way again. Your spellcasting ability for the spell is your chosen psionic ability score. If you have spell slots of 2nd level or higher, you can cast this spell with them.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Telepathic Novice
entries: You can speak telepathically to any creature you can see within 60 feet of you. Your telepathic utterances are in a language you know, and the creature understands you only if it knows that language. Your communication doesn't give the creature the ability to respond to you telepathically.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Tellu and Scale's Master Cut

prerequisite.other: You must have beaten a master at Master Tellu and Scale's Sword School

entries: Having trained with the masters of the valley sword school, you have learned the usefulness of quickly changing between different fighting techniques in the midst of battle. You gain the following benefits:

items.name: One Handed
entries: While wielding a {@itemProperty V||versatile} weapon in one hand, your quick movements and agile defense allow you to regain ground even when your enemy advances. Once before the start of your next turn when you're missed by a melee attack from a creature within your reach, the attacker takes damage from your weapon equal to twice your proficiency bonus.

items.name: Two Handed
entries: When wielding a {@itemProperty V||versatile} weapon in two hands, your powerful stance allows you to catch your target off guard. Whenever an enemy within your reach makes a melee weapon attack against you and misses, you can use your reaction to attempt to knock the attacker off balance. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 + your Strength modifier + your proficiency bonus) or be knocked {@condition prone}.

name: Tempered Shards*
entries: Being in this new realm has caused you to become inventive as to how you keep yourself from cracking under the strain. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with Glassblower's tools. If you are already proficient, you gain Expertise.

Once per day, as an Action, you can repair yourself with your Glassblower's tools. Gain your Cha mod + 1d6 + your level in HP. You gain an extra d6 at 5th, 11th, 17th, 21st, 25th, 31st, and 37th levels.

name: Tenacious
entries: You gain two special bonus Hit Dice, which are {@dice d6}s. You always regain both of these dice at the end of a long rest in addition to the normal number of hit dice you would regain. Your maximum hit points are not affected.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Tenacious
entries: You gain two special bonus Hit Dice, which are {@dice d6}s. You always regain both of these dice at the end of a long rest in addition to the normal number of hit dice you would regain. Your maximum hit points are not affected.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Tengu Training
entries: The tutelage of a hanataka tengu, or countless hours of careful study of hanataka treatise on combat, has granted you the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with one Finesse weapon of your choice.

As a reaction when a creature misses you with a melee attack while you are holding a Finesse weapon, you can make one weapon attack with that weapon against the creature. You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Terminal Velocity
entries: Your flying speed and ferocity with your stinger are unparalleled. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Strength, Dexterity or Charisma score by 1, up to a maximum of 20.
Your flying speed increases to 20 feet, or 40 feet if you are 5th level or above.

Immediately after you use the {@action Dash} action on your turn while flying and move at least 20 feet, you can make one melee attack with your stinger as a bonus action. When you make an attack in this way, you can add your Proficiency bonus to the damage dealt.

name: Terrain Savvy
entries: You make the best out of any battlefield, and take any moment you can to catch your breath in the middle of a skirmish.

items: Half cover counts as three-quarters cover for you.

When you gain cover from a hostile creature, you can spend a number of Hit Dice up to your Wisdom modifier to heal yourself. Roll the dice, add your Constitution modifier to the result, and regain a number of hit points equal to the total (minimum of 1). You must finish a short or long rest before you can heal yourself in this way again.

name: Terran Heritage
entries: You manifest more of the magical power of your heritage. You gain the following benefits:

items: You learn the {@spell detect magic} spell and can cast it at will, without expending a spell slot.
You gain natural armor. While you aren't wearing armor, you can calculate your AC as 13 + your Dexterity modifier. You can use a {@item shield|PHB} and still gain this benefit.

name: Terrasoul
entries: You have discovered the obstinate magics of elemental earth inside yourself, granting you the following benefits:

items: You have {@sense tremorsense|MM} with a range of 30 feet. Within that range, you can detect and pinpoint the origin of vibrations, provided you and the source of the vibrations are in contact with the same ground or substance. Your {@sense tremorsense|MM} can't be used to detect flying or incorporeal creatures.

Once you reach 5th level, you can cast the {@spell erupting earth|XGE} spell, requiring no spell slot or components, and you must finish a long rest before you can cast it this way again. You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Constitution is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

name: Terrifying Presence
entries: The area in a 10 foot radius around you is considered difficult terrain for creatures of your choice, creatures immune to being {@condition frightened} are not affected by this feature.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Terrifying Presence
entries: The area in a 10 foot radius around you is considered difficult terrain for creatures of your choice, creatures immune to being {@condition frightened} are not affected by this feature.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Tessen Master
entries: You have learned to manipulate the tessen in new ways, using its pointed spokes as weapons and tossing it at your foes from a distance. You gain the following benefits:

items: For you, a {@item tessen|RyokoGuideToYokaiRealms} has the Adaptable (Piercing) and Thrown (range 20/60) properties.

While wielding a {@item tessen|RyokoGuideToYokaiRealms}, you gain an extra reaction that you can take once during each round. This reaction can only be used to attempt to deflect a projectile with the tessen's Special: Fan Shield property, and you can't use it on the same turn that you take your normal reaction.

name: Thayan Circle Caster

otherSummary.entry: or ritual caster class feature, and must have received a unique arcane blessing from Szass Tam

entries: You have been blessed by Szass Tam himself and have become a conduit for enhanced arcane power. You may participate in {@variantrule Circle Magic|TLotRW|Thayan circle casting}.

name: The 7th Lotus - Enlightened
entries: In addition to the 6 Lotus States listed above, there exists a 7th, final Lotus, which a Chakara is said to only experience when they are ready to take the final steps beyond the material plane. This enlightened state, referred to as the Crown Lotus, comes to Chakara Only in their final moments, before they leave this world forever. When you are reduced to 0 hit points and killed outright or after failing your final death saving throw, your binding seals dissolve and enter your final Lotus and gain the following benefits. This Lotus State lasts for a Number of rounds Equal to your proficiency bonus, during which you continue to act as if you were alive. When the Final Lotus ends, you immediately die and cannot be resurrected by any means short of a Wish spell.

entries.name: Enlightened
entries: You Immediately gain the benefits of a long rest, and your hit points return to their maximum value. You have resistant to all damage types, and gain the benefits of all 6 Lotus states listed above

name: The Art of Smoking
entries: You have mastered the art of smoking pipe-weed, and you always carry your {@item pipe|TLotRR} with you, as well as a bag of tobacco, for using it grants you patience and clarity of mind.

items: Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make with {@item pipe|TLotRR|pipes}.
You can use your {@item pipe|TLotRR} to gain inspiration a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, instead of once, before you need to finish a long rest.

name: The Cabal: Soul Broker
entries: You have passed the legal and ritualistic exams necessary to become a bonded soul broker for the Cabal, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Soul Dividends
entries: You are rewarded for sending souls to the afterlife. When you kill an enemy, you gain 1 Soul Credit for each point of its {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB} (rounded down, to a minimum of 0). You can exchange 10 Soul Credits for 100 CR.

entries.name: Moral Relativism
entries: When you make an {@action Influence|XPHB} check against a {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} creature, you can give yourself {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the roll instead of {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Faction Feats
entries: Veteran adventurers are likely to make enemies across the 'Verse, but if they're lucky, they might forge some alliances too. The greatest of these alliances are likely to be with factions, which provide work, services, and connections to spacers everywhere. Factions in Dark Matter are detailed in Chapter 1: The 'Verse.

Of course, such allies don't come free. Factions generally also require work and commitment from their members, which might come in the form of small tasks, important favors for higher ranking members, or even regular obligations for the organization. For their efforts, adventurers gain specific and useful skills from their factions, as represented by Faction feats.

entries.name: Gaining a Faction Feat
entries: The GM can award you a Faction feat for joining a faction or completing a quest for one. If allegiance to a faction is important to your backstory, the GM can also replace the feat granted by your background with an appropriate Faction feat.

name: The Coalition: Recruit
entries: To join the Coalition, you have undergone a rigorous training regime or accomplished a feat representative of it, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Basic Training
entries: You gain one of the following benefits of your choice: proficiency in the {@skill Athletics|XPHB} skill, proficiency with Martial Weapons, training with Light Armor, or training with {@item Shield|XPHB|Shields}. If you have all of these benefits already, you gain Weapon Mastery with the {@item Repeater|DarkMatter24} or {@item Standard Carbine|DarkMatter24}, and it doesn't count against the number of weapons you can use with Weapon Mastery.

entries.name: Dive for Cover
entries: When you make a Dexterity saving throw against an effect with an area of effect, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to move up to 15 feet without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}, potentially leaving the effect's area. Once you take this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Faction Feats

The greatest of these alliances are likely to be with factions, which provide work, services, and connections to spacers everywhere. Factions in Dark Matter are detailed in Chapter 1: The 'Verse.

Of course, such allies don't come free. Factions generally also require work and commitment from their members, which might come in the form of small tasks, important favors for higher ranking members, or even regular obligations for the organization. For their efforts, adventurers gain specific and useful skills from their factions, as represented by Faction feats.

entries.name: Gaining a Faction Feat
entries: The GM can award you a Faction feat for joining a faction or completing a quest for one. If allegiance to a faction is important to your backstory, the GM can also replace the feat granted by your background with an appropriate Faction feat.

name: The Eyes Have it
entries: You are just the cutest. You have advantage on any Charisma based ability checks. Unfortunately this ability cannot be used against hostile creatures

name: The Firm: Contractor
entries: As a licensed Contractor, you know that while the pen is mightier than the sword, the {@item dagger|XPHB} is stronger still. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Backstabber
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with a Simple weapon that deals {@damage 1d4} damage, you deal {@damage 2d4} damage instead.

entries.name: Expertise
entries: You gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in one of your skill proficiencies of your choice.

entries.name: Faction Feats

The greatest of these alliances are likely to be with factions, which provide work, services, and connections to spacers everywhere. Factions in Dark Matter are detailed in Chapter 1: The 'Verse.

Of course, such allies don't come free. Factions generally also require work and commitment from their members, which might come in the form of small tasks, important favors for higher ranking members, or even regular obligations for the organization. For their efforts, adventurers gain specific and useful skills from their factions, as represented by Faction feats.

entries.name: Gaining a Faction Feat
entries: The GM can award you a Faction feat for joining a faction or completing a quest for one. If allegiance to a faction is important to your backstory, the GM can also replace the feat granted by your background with an appropriate Faction feat.

items: You are proficient in all {@filter firearms|items|type=firearm}.
You can conceal handguns with advantage on your Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check.
You have advantage on initiative checks when wielding a firearm.

name: The Kiss
entries: Your bite is intoxicating to your prey.

entries.name: Pleasurable Feeding
entries: When you feed, you can choose to roll d4s instead of d6s for your Feed Dice. When you do so, you regain 1 Blood Point on a roll of a 4 on the {@dice d4}, and the creature is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you. The {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition lasts until the end of your next turn.

name: The Language of Birds
entries: Stories told in the North say how Dalemen can become so wise as to comprehend the speech of birds, and so by understanding their song be forewarned of impending threats, or be able to spot a weakness in their enemies' defences.

items: You can comprehend and verbally communicate with birds, and you can obtain a magical success on any Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) and Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) check related to birds.

When you are outside and you make an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw, you can do so with advantage. You can use this virtue a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: The Mother of Invention
entries: Increase your Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
A burst of insight and a little application, and you've learned a new {@filter infusion|spell|Feature Type=AS:G;AS:O;AS:I;AS:P;AS:T;AS:W;AS:F}.

name: The Pack is Many, the Pack is One
entries: As an action, you can distribute healing equal to three times your Monk level among any number of creatures within 30 feet. You must finish a long rest before you can use this ability again.

name: The Past Never Forgets
entries: You can choose to gain two traits from the Race chosen in the Size, Speed, Past Life and Languages traits.
For instance, if you chose to be a Fallen Changeling, you can pick the Shapechanger and Changeling Instincts traits.

name: The Raven's Ear
entries: You have the hearing and mimicry capabilities of the raven, an extension of the corvian talent for memory and observation. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) and Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on hearing.

You can mimic sounds you have heard, including voices. A creature that hears the sounds you make can tell they are imitations with a successful Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check opposed by your Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check.

name: The Soul of the Pack
entries: When you perform a Mark the Ground Ritual, you may create a Pack Bond for yourself or any number of allied creatures up to your Druid level. For one hour, any Pack Bonded creature may, as an action, roll one of its hit dice and receive that much psychic damage. It may then heal an ally who is Pack Bonded and within 60 feet for an equal amount.

name: The Tower: Agent
entries: As a fully-inducted Tower Agent, you are familiar with the organization's cryptic ciphers and are trained in their clandestine, magical arts. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Mark of Induction
entries: You bear a tattoo which is visible only to other Tower Agents, used to mark your membership.

entries.name: Mage Cypher
entries: You can cast {@spell Illusory Script|XPHB} without a spell slot or Material components. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

entries.name: Subtle Spell
entries: When you cast a spell, you can cast it without any Verbal, Somatic, or Material components, except Material components that are consumed by the spell or that have a cost specified in the spell. You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Faction Feats
entries: Veteran adventurers are likely to make enemies across the 'Verse, but if they're lucky, they might forge some alliances too. The greatest of these alliances are likely to be with factions, which provide work, services, and connections to spacers everywhere. Factions in Dark Matter are detailed in Chapter 1: The 'Verse.

Of course, such allies don't come free. Factions generally also require work and commitment from their members, which might come in the form of small tasks, important favors for higher ranking members, or even regular obligations for the organization. For their efforts, adventurers gain specific and useful skills from their factions, as represented by Faction feats.

entries.name: Gaining a Faction Feat
entries: The GM can award you a Faction feat for joining a faction or completing a quest for one. If allegiance to a faction is important to your backstory, the GM can also replace the feat granted by your background with an appropriate Faction feat.

name: The Wisdom of Playfulness
entries: You can channel the positive attitude of dogs and their delight at the world. Once per long rest, as an action you can choose to receive the benefit of one of the below effects. Spend one Ki point per additional creature within 30 feet you wish it to affect.

items.name: Laughing at danger
entries: For one Hour, you have resistance to a specified damage type.

items.name: The folly of fear
entries: For one hour, you are immune to fear effects.

items.name: Irrepressible joy
entries: For one hour, you have advantage on all Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma saving throws.

name: Theatrics
entries: When you take the {@action Help} action to aid an ally by distracting an enemy, you can also choose to distract any number of additional creatures within 5 feet of the target, giving the chosen ally advantage on attack rolls against each of the affected creatures.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Theatrics
entries: When you take the {@action Help} action to aid an ally by distracting an enemy, you can also choose to distract any number of additional creatures within 5 feet of the target, giving the chosen ally advantage on attack rolls against each of the affected creatures.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Theologian
entries: Your extensive study of religion rewards you with the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Religion} skill. If you are already proficient in the skill, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.

You learn the {@spell thaumaturgy} and {@spell detect evil and good} spells. You can cast {@spell detect evil and good} once without expending a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.
When you spend one or more hours of uninterrupted talking with a single creature, you bestow them the following:
Temporary HP equal to your highest class level + your charisma modifier.
Advantage against {@condition frightened|fear} effects until the next day
Advantage on all attacks on the first round of each combat, until the next day.
Advantage on their first death saving throw, until the next day.
Advantage on the first initiative check, until the next day.

name: Thermalsight Upgrade
entries: You upgrade your optics to make better use of your thermal vision, gaining the following benefits:

items: The range of your {@sense thermalsight|DarkMatter} extends to 60 feet.
Your {@sense thermalsight|DarkMatter} penetrates one foot of any material.
You see {@condition invisible} creatures within range of your {@sense thermalsight|DarkMatter} as if they were visible. This doesn't apply to creatures that are in the Ethereal Plane.

name: Thick Coat
entries: Your thick and glossy fur is a natural defence. You have an armour class of 12 + your Dexterity modifier when not wearing armour.

name: Thick-Shelled
entries: You are covered in a tough, chitinous exoskeleton that is more durable than that of other skathári. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your AC when you aren't wearing armor equals 13 + your Dexterity modifier.
As a reaction when you would be hit by a ranged spell attack, you can roll a {@dice d4}. On a roll of 4, the attack bounces harmlessly off your shell.

name: Thief of Focus
entries: When a creature within 5 feet of you casts a spell with material components or an arcane focus which is held in its hand, you can use your reaction to attempt to disturb the components or focus to disrupt the casting of the spell. Make a Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check contested by the target's spell save DC. You have disadvantage if the target can see you. On a success, you disturb the components or the focus in the creature's hand and it fails to cast the spell this turn. This does not expend the affected creature's spell slot. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Thief of Focus
entries: When a creature within 5 feet of you casts a spell with material components or an arcane focus which is held in its hand, you can use your reaction to attempt to disturb the components or focus to disrupt the casting of the spell. Make a Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check contested by the target's spell save DC. You have disadvantage if the target can see you. On a success, you disturb the components or the focus in the creature's hand and it fails to cast the spell this turn. This does not expend the affected creature's spell slot. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Thief of Order
entries: When you roll initiative at the beginning of combat, if you are not surprised, you can use your reaction to don or doff a shield or take the {@action Use an Object} Action.
In addition, whenever you could make an attack of opportunity against a creature, you can choose to instead take the {@action Use an Object} action.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Thief of Order
entries: When you roll initiative at the beginning of combat, if you are not surprised, you can use your reaction to don or doff a shield or take the {@action Use an Object} Action.
In addition, whenever you could make an attack of opportunity against a creature, you can choose to instead take the {@action Use an Object} action.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Thief of Propriety
entries: As long as you are hidden from a creature no more than one size larger than you, you can {@note as an action} try to steal an object that it is holding or wearing loosely on its person. You must make a Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check contested by the target's Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}). If you succeed, the creature releases the object and you can choose to either take it in your empty hand or force the creature to drop it.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Thief of Propriety
entries: When you attempt to steal an object that a creature is wearing loosely on its person, you can do so without being noticed by the creature if your ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check beat the target's Passive ({@skill Perception}) by 5 or more. The item must be visible to its former owner at the end of your turn or else it will still be seen.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Thin-Blooded

otherSummary.entry: Can Be Chosen in Place of Any Origin Feat

entries: You have a portion of a vampire's blood flowing in your veins. You are a thin-blood, often destined for a place among the clanless. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Able to Feed
entries: You feed on the blood of other creatures. This is most often accomplished through your sharp fangs. As an action, you can feed on another creature within 5 feet of yourself if the target is willing, {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you, or has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, {@condition Restrained|XPHB}, {@condition Stunned|XPHB}, or {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition. You can feed only once per turn.

You have {@dice 2d6} Feed Dice. When you feed, roll up to your maximum Feed Dice plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1). The creature takes Necrotic damage equal to the roll's total. This damage only reduces the creature's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum by an amount equal to the roll's total. If you roll a 6 on a {@dice d6} on a Feed Die, you can regain 1 expended Blood Point. If a creature's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is reduced to 0, you can regain 1 expended Blood Point.

entries.name: Feeding from the Willing
entries: If you feed on a willing creature or a creature {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you, it can spend 1 {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die}. It rolls the {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die} and reduces its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum by the amount rolled, and you can regain 1 expended Blood Point. Feeding in this way doesn't end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Hit Die Deficit
entries: If a creature has no remaining {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, the creature takes Necrotic damage equal to a roll of your Feed Dice plus your Constitution modifier, and the creature's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the roll's total.

entries.name: Maximum Successful Feedings
entries: A creature can provide a number of Blood Points based on its size. A Small creature provides 1 Blood Point, a Medium provides 3, a Large provides 5, a Huge provides 7, and a Gargantuan provides 10. A creature regains all lost Blood Points when it finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Creature Susceptible to Feed
entries: You can feed on any creature with blood or other life-giving fluid. Work with your GM to determine the types of creatures you can feed on.

entries.name: Kindred, but Not Kindred
entries: You ignore the Kindred class prerequisite for choosing {@filter Kindred feats|feats|category=kf}. You can't gain levels in the Kindred class.

entries.name: Kindred Vitae
entries: You have a number of Blood Points equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} minus one.

entries.name: Supernatural Spellcasting
entries: Charisma is your spellcasting ability for spells from your Kindred feats. Your spells require no Verbal or Somatic components, and they require no Material components unless they are consumed by the spell or have a cost specified in it. Taking damage can't break your {@status Concentration|XPHB} for spells cast using this feature.

name: Thoughtsinger
entries: You have honed your telepathic abilities, allowing you to link to and guide your companions as a united group. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Wisdom or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

When using your Mind Link trait, you can maintain links to up to 6 creatures at a time. When you establish a link, you decide whether the linked creature can telepathically communicate only with you, or if they can telepathically communicate with all of the creatures you are linked to at once. Likewise, you can communicate with one specific creature, or you can communicate with all creatures you're currently linked to.
If you can speak telepathically to an ally using your Mind Link trait, you can use the {@action Help} action to aid them in attacking a creature, even if you are more than 5 feet away from them.

name: Thoughtsinger
entries: You have honed your telepathic abilities, allowing you to link to and guide your companions as a united group. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Superior Telepathy
entries: The telepathy granted by your Mind Link trait has a range of 120 feet or 10 times your level, whichever is higher.

entries.name: Thoughtsong
entries: When you use your Mind Link trait to grant a creature the ability to speak to you telepathically, you form a mental connection with that individual. When you communicate telepathically, you may choose to send the message to all creatures you currently have a mental connection to. You may also allow those creatures to speak telepathically with one another. These effects last for as long as the Mind Link remains in effect.

entries.name: Telepathic Aid
entries: If you can speak telepathically to an ally using your Mind Link trait, you can take the {@action Help|XPHB} action to aid them in attacking a creature, even if you are more than 5 feet away from them.

name: Three is Company
entries: The Wise say that it is sometimes best to trust to friendship than to great wisdom. This is particularly true for Hobbits, as everyone knows that it is hardly possible to separate them from their friends. You have given your trust to your fellow Company members, and a true friendship has grown from the bond unifying you.

items: Increase the Fellowship rating of your Company by 1.

Whenever you or a companion you can see spend a Fellowship point, choose a number of companions (which can include yourself) who can see or hear you, up to your proficiency bonus. Each of those companions gains inspiration.

name: Thrower
entries: You have practiced throwing–you can launch things further and with more accuracy than most.

entries.name: Strong arm
entries: The standard distance you can throw without penalty is calculated by [1 + your strength modifier] multiplied by 10 ft. Your long range is three times this. {@i (Minimum of 20 ft. standard, 60 ft. longrange)}

entries.name: Accuracy
entries: If you only make one {@i attack action} this round you can add +5 onto your {@i proficiency roll} when throwing anything.

entries.name: Blade first
entries: You can throw any melee weapon you are proficient with as a one-shot {@i ranged attack} using the same base proficiency bonus as your melee strike. The damage inflicted remains the same.

entries.name: Ricochet
entries: You can try to bounce any object thrown off of one surface to hit your target without any penalty to your {@i proficiency roll} . {@i (To bounce, the thrown object cannot be bladed, pointy or breakable.)}

name: Thrown Arms Master
entries: You've honed your ability to lob weaponry into the fray, including weapons not meant for ranged combat. You gain the following benefits:

items: Simple and martial melee weapons without the thrown property can be treated as if they have the thrown property. One-handed weapons have a range of 20/60, while two-handed weapons have a range of 15/30.
Weapons that naturally have the thrown property increase their range by +20/+40.
When you miss with a thrown weapon attack using a {@i light} weapon, the weapon immediately boomerangs back into your grasp.

name: Thrown Arms Master
entries: You've honed your ability to lob weaponry into the fray, including weapons not meant for ranged combat. You gain the following benefits:

items: Simple and martial melee weapons without the thrown property have the {@itemProperty T|PHB|thrown} property for you. One-handed weapons have a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet, while two-handed weapons have a normal range of 15 feet and a long range of 30 feet.
Weapons that already have the {@itemProperty T|PHB|thrown} property increase their short range by 20 feet and their long range by 40 feet for you.

When you miss with a thrown weapon attack using a light weapon, the weapon returns to your grasp like a boomerang at the end of your turn, unless something prevents it from returning. You can catch and stow as many weapons as you threw in this way.

name: Thrown Weapon Fighting
entries: Add 30 ft to the close range of your thrown weapons (60 instead if it's also a ranged weapon). The long range becomes twice your close range (4 times instead if its also a ranged weapon).

name: Thrown Weapon Master
entries: You have mastered projectile weapons, and have learned to use them to pressure and harry your foes. You gain the following benefits:

items: The short and long range of your thrown weapons are doubled.
You can draw a thrown weapon as part of making an attack with it.

If you take the Attack action on your turn, you can replace a ranged attack with a thrown weapon that you are proficient with (excluding nets) with two ranged attacks at disadvantage. To do so, you must have a different thrown weapon in your other hand or a free hand to draw a different thrown weapon, and you must not have disadvantage on the initial attack.
When you hit a creature with a ranged attack using a thrown weapon, it can't take reactions until the start of its next turn.

name: Thrown Weapon Master
entries: You excel at thrown weapons and gain the following benefits:

items: When you take the attack action to throw a weapon with the Thrown property, you may immediately use a bonus action to make two more attacks with a Thrown weapon. These must also be thrown attacks. You may use this ability a number of times equal to your dexterity or strength modifier per short rest.
If you throw a weapon as part of an attack, you may immediately draw another one handed weapon as part of that attack.

name: Thrown Weapon Master
entries: You excel at thrown weapons. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Multithrow
entries: After you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action to make a ranged attack roll using a Simple weapon that has {@itemProperty T|XPHB|Thrown}, you can make two additional ranged attacks using Simple weapons that have {@itemProperty T|XPHB|Thrown} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Quick Hands
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can retrieve and stow or wield all Simple weapons with {@itemProperty T|XPHB|Thrown} that are within 5 feet of you. You need a free hand to perform this maneuver.

entries.name: Returning
entries: Simple weapons with {@itemProperty T|XPHB|Thrown} that you are proficient with also have the {@itemMastery Returning|GrimHollowPG24} mastery property.

name: Thrown Weapon Master
entries: You are an expert at the techniques of throwing weapons. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to damage rolls you make with thrown weapons.
Attacking at long range doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged weapon attack rolls with thrown weapons.
When you hit a creature with a ranged weapon attack with a thrown weapon, you have advantage on your next melee weapon attack against that creature before the end of your next turn.
You can use two-weapon fighting even when the one-handed melee weapons you are wielding aren't light, if at least one of them has the thrown property.

name: Thrown Weapons Master
entries: You have mastered the art of throwing weapons. You gain the following benefits:

items: The normal and long range of thrown weapons is doubled for you.

You draw an additional thrown weapon beyond that which is considered free (as per chapter 9, Combat, Player's Handbook). You can do this before each weapon attack you make if you have the free hand to do so.
Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls.

When you take the Attack action and make only ranged weapon attacks with thrown light weapons on your turn, you can use a bonus action to make two ranged weapon attacks with thrown light weapons. These two ranged attacks cannot target the same creature.

name: Thrown Weapons Master
entries: You have mastered the art of throwing weapons. You gain the following benefits:

items: The normal and long range of thrown weapons is doubled for you.
You can draw a weapon that has the thrown property as part of the attack you make with the weapon.
Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls.

When you take the {@action Attack} action and make only ranged weapon attacks with thrown light weapons on your turn, you can use a bonus action to make two ranged weapon attacks with thrown light weapons. These two ranged attacks cannot target the same creature.

name: Thunder Guide
entries: You have traveled the length and breadth of the Thunder Sea, learning from cultures indigenous to disparate regions, from the jungles of Xen'drik to the Seren Isles. Pick three of any of the following abilities, to represent the tricks and knacks you've picked up from your travels. You must have adventured in the region under which the ability is listed in order to select it.

items.name: Rescue Artist
entries: You are skilled at saving others from harrowing situations. If a creature begins to fall within your line of sight, you may use your reaction to move up to your speed and automatically catch them. Additionally, when you take the Help action to aid another creature in escaping from a grapple, they automatically succeed on their escape attempt. Finally, you may carry a Medium or smaller creature in addition to your normal carrying capacity without becoming encumbered for up to 1 minute. After a minute of doing so, you must finish a short or long rest before you can carry a creature this way again.

items.name: Lionized in the Press
entries: The Korranberg Chronicle, the Breland Ledger, the Aundarian Scroll, and other chronicle sheets recount your adventures across the Thunder Sea in thrilling detail. You have advantage on Charisma checks when interacting with members of the press, nobility, and Dragonmarked Houses. Once per month, you may give a lecture at a notable institution, such as Morgrave University or the Library of Korranberg, and earn gold pieces equal to 10 times the result of a Charisma (Performance) check.

items.name: Eye of the Chamber
entries: Learning patience and planning from draconic agents of the Chamber, you apply those traits in combat. As an Action during combat, you may study a creature hostile to you and begin concentrating (as though concentrating on a spell). For up to 1 minute, or until your concentration ends, you have advantage on all attacks against the opponent. Once you have observed an opponent this way, you may not do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

items.name: Aereni Crystallomancy
entries: You may cast the {@spell false life} spell. When you do, it requires an additional material component of an Irian-infused Eberron dragonshard found only on the Isle of Aerenal worth at least 200 gp, and it is cast as though from a 3rd level spell slot. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for this spell. Once you cast this spell, you must finish a long rest to do so again.

items.name: Friend of Aereni
entries: Your presence is always welcome in the Aereni port of Pylas Talaear. You always have free accommodations in the city, and the governor, Syraen Melidith, will subsidize half the cost of any House Lyrandar airship or galleon trip you make to or from Pylas Talaear. Additionally, you may purchase mundane goods at half-cost while in the city.

items.name: Honorary Tairnadal
entries: The Valenar elves welcome you as one of their own, and one of their majestic mounts has even formed an unbreakable bond with you. You learn the {@spell find steed} spell, but you may only summon a Valenar Riding Horse with it (even if you are not a Valenar elf). Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for this spell. Once you cast this spell, you must finish a long rest to do so again. (See page 14 of The Korranberg Chronicle: Threat Dispatch for the Valenar Riding Horse's statistics.)

items.name: Dragonsong
entries: Once, distantly, you heard the rocky barrier coast of Argonnessen come alive with the song of dragons. You may call on the memory of the tragic glory of dragonsong as a Reaction to gain advantage on all saving throws against becoming {@condition charmed} for as long as you concentrate (as though concentrating on a spell) for up to 1 minute. Once you call upon this memory, you may not do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

items.name: Seren Hide
entries: Conditioning yourself with techniques learned alongside Seren barbarians, you have inured yourself to physical harm. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage you take from non-magical weapons is reduced by 1, and when not wearing armor you have an AC of 12 + your Dexterity modifier.

items.name: Vicious Barbarism
entries: You've learned to fight like the vicious barbarians of the Seren Isles. As a bonus action, you may enter a reckless frenzy for 1 minute. During this frenzy, you deal 2 additional damage with all melee weapon attacks, but all attack rolls against you are made with advantage. You may end your reckless frenzy early by taking another bonus action to do so. It also ends early if you are knocked unconscious. When your reckless frenzy ends, you may not enter another reckless frenzy until you finish a long rest.

items.name: Blessed of Shargon
entries: You have earned the blessing of Shargon, preventing the need for you and any crew or passengers of the ship you are traveling on from making sacrifices or offerings to the sahuagin of the Thunder Sea. Because of this boon, any captain will welcome you and your party aboard their vessels at no cost, including Lyrandar wind galleons. Furthermore, the sahuagin escort you and your vessel on journeys across Shargon's Teeth, eliminating the possibility of being attacked by creatures of challenge rating 9 or less.

items.name: Breath of Shargon
entries: You can hold your breath for a number of minutes equal to your Constitution score.

items.name: Malenti Pearl Trick
entries: You may cast the {@spell charm person} spell. When you do, it requires an additional material component of a pearl worth at least 100 gp. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell. Once you cast this spell, you must finish a long rest to do so again.

items.name: Ally of Rushemé
entries: You have communed with the Guardians of Rushemé and have been granted the mystical ability to call on the strength of giantkind. You gain the ability to cast {@spell enlarge/reduce}, but only on yourself and only using the enlarge option. Strength is your spellcasting ability for this spell. Once you cast this spell, you may not do so again until you finish a long rest.

items.name: Ghost in Xen'drik
entries: In any jungle environment, you have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) and Wisdom (Survival) checks. Additionally, you are considered a native to Xen'drik for the purposes of navigation and the Traveler's Curse.

items.name: Pandin Temn
entries: You have trained at the side of Vulkoori drow to be a scourge of giants. Against the attacks of giants, you have a +1 bonus to AC if you are wearing no or light armor, and all of your attacks deal 2 additional damage against giants.

items.name: Xen'drik Boomerang Expert
entries: You are proficient with Xen'drik boomerangs and you double their short and long ranges when throwing them. Additionally, Xen'drik boomerangs always return to you at the end of your turn when you throw them, whether they hit or miss, and you automatically succeed on catching them.

items: {@b Ability Score Bonus.} Increase your Strength or Constitution ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
{@b Stable Footing.} You gain advantage from being knocked down by ground shaking or heaving.
You gain the {@b Quaking Smash} special attack (below).

entries.name: Quaking Smash
entries: {@italic Active Ability (Attack, Supernatural)}

As an attack as part of the attack action, you slam the ground causing an eruption of thunder to erupt outward in a 15 foot cone. Creatures in the area must make a Constitution save. On failure they take 2d6 thunder damage and are knocked prone. On success, they take half as much damage and aren't knocked prone. The number of d6 damage dealt increase when your proficiency bonus increases.
If you are Large or Larger when you take this action, the size of the cone caused by the effect doubles and the d6 damage dice become d8 damage dice.
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

name: Tidesoul
entries: You have unlocked the unfathomable magics of elemental water inside yourself, granting you the following benefits:

items: You can move into a hostile creature's space regardless of its size, and you can move through a space as narrow as 1 foot wide without squeezing.

Once you reach 5th level, you can cast the {@spell tidal wave|XGE}, requiring no spell slot or components, and you must finish a long rest before you can cast it this way again. You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Constitution is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

name: Tincture Master
entries: You have attained a mastery of distilling herbs into {@variantrule tinctures|HHbH}, halving the time and cost it takes for you to create one.

name: Tine Capture
entries: You do not need a free hand to perform a grapple while you are wielding a {@item trident|PHB}, {@item war pick|PHB}, or {@item sickle|PHB}.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Tine Capture
entries: You do not need a free hand to perform a grapple while you are wielding a {@item trident|PHB}, {@item war pick|PHB}, or {@item sickle|PHB}.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Tinker
entries: You have a knack for repairing and modifying mundane objects. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with {@item tinker's tools|phb}. If you are already proficient with them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.
Repairing an item takes half as much time and only requires half as many raw materials.

Using materials that you forage, store among your other possessions, or harvest from disassembled items, you can create mundane items that could be useful throughout your adventures. As part of a short or long rest, you can use these materials and your tinker's tools to create one or more nonmagical items. The combined value of these items must be worth 4 gp or less. If these items would require the significant use of other tools to make, such as a metal weapon or a disguise, they are too complex for you to create with this feature. Items created using this feature cease to function and return to their base components in an amount of time equal to the duration of the rest they were made during.

name: Tinker
entries: You are an expert with {@item Tinker's Tools|phb}.
Repairing an item takes half as much time and only requires half as many raw materials.

Using materials that you forage, store among your other possessions, or harvest from disassembled items, you can create mundane items that could be useful throughout your adventures. As part of a short or long rest, you can use these materials and your tinker's tools to create one or more nonmagical items. The combined value of these items must be worth 4 gp or less. If these items would require the significant use of other tools to make, such as a metal weapon or a disguise, they are too complex for you to create with this feature. Items created using this feature cease to function and return to their base components in an amount of time equal to the duration of the rest they were made during.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Tinkerer
entries: You have experimented with the craft most often practiced by artificers. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with tinkerer's tools. If you already have proficiency with them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.

You learn two artificer infusions of your choice from the Artificer class. If the infusion has a prerequisite of any kind, you can't choose that infusion. Whenever you gain a level, you can replace one of these infusions with another infusion from the artificer class that doesn't have a prerequisite. You count as being a 2nd-level artificer for the purposes of your infusions, unless you have more levels in the artificer class.

If you can already imbue objects with artificer infusions, you can infuse one additional item; otherwise, whenever you finish a {@quickref resting||2|0|long rest}{@sup {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB|'24}}, you can touch a nonmagical object and imbue it with one of your artificer infusions, turning it into a magic item. An infusion only works on certain types of objects, as specified in the infusion's description. If the item requires attunement, you can attune yourself to it the moment you infuse the item. If you decide to attune to the item later, you must do so using the normal process for attunement. Your infusion remains on the item indefinitely, but when you die, the infusion vanishes after a number of days equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum one). The infusion also vanishes if you imbue another item with one of your infusions or if you replace your knowledge of the infusion. If an infusion ends on an item that contains other things, like a bag of holding, its contents harmlessly appear in and around its space.

name: Tireless
entries: Your body has adapted to sleepless nights and grueling conditions, and you gain the following benefits:

items: You treat your levels of exhaustion as halved (rounded down), and suffer the effects accordingly.
When you are affected by the sleep spell, you are treated as having twice as many hit points for the purpose of resolving that spell.

name: Tiro Múltiplo
entries: O personagem é capaz de disparar várias flechas simultaneamente contra um alvo próximo.

{@b Beneficio:} Usando uma ação padrão, seu personagem é capaz de disparar duas flechas em um determinado oponente num raio de 30ft. Os dois disparos utilizam a mesma jogada de ataque (com Desvantagem) para determinar o sucesso e causam dano normalmente. A redução de dano e quaisquer outras resistências se aplicam separadamente para cada um dos disparos executados.

name: Tiro Rápido
entries: O personagem pode usar armas de ataque à distância com velocidade excepcional.
{@b Beneficio:} Seu personagem recebe um ataque adicional com uma arma de ataque a distância. Mas cada disparo (inclusive o adicional) é feito com Desvantagem.

name: Titan Grip
entries: When you would draw or stow a weapon you can instead add or remove the following effect from one of your hands: Weapons in this hand are treated as if they are being held by two hands. You cannot have this effect on both of your hands at the same time unless you take this fighting style again.

name: Titan Throw
entries: You can give a melee weapon the thrown property when you attack with it. Its range is 60/120 and you subtract 1 from its base damage if you throw it.

name: Titanic
entries: You awaken or learn a mystical ability drawing on the ancient power of the titans. You gain the following benefits:

items: {@b Ability Score Bonus.} Increase your Strength, Constitution, or Wisdom ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
{@b Mystic Language.} You learn giant. If you already know giant, you learn one additional language of your choice.
You gain the {@b Titanic Aspect} special transformation (below).

entries.name: Titanic Aspect
entries: {@italic Active Ability (Action, Supernatural)}
As an action, you come under the Enlarge effect of the enlarge/reduce spell.

In addition to the normal effect, your flesh takes on rough stone-like appearance, causing your unarmed strikes to deal an additional 1d4 damage and reducing all damage from bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage by your proficiency bonus, or your damage reduction is increased by 1 if you already have a stronger source of it.

The effect lasts 10 minutes. You can end this effect early as an action, returning to normal size. It ends early if you fall unconscious. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

name: Tomb Magic
entries: You possess an innate magical power tied to your unearthly animating force. You learn the {@spell infestation|xge} cantrip. You also learn the {@spell bestow curse} and {@spell wall of sand|xge} spells, and can cast only one of them once at its lowest possible spell level without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast a spell from this feature in this way when you finish a long rest. Choose Wisdom or Charisma as your spellcasting ability for all three spells.

items.name: Proficiency
items.entry: You gain proficiency in one tool of your choice.

items.name: Expertise
items.entry: Gain expertise in a tool offered by the class that granted you this feat. If you were proficient in that tool, gain proficiency in a tool of your choice.

items.name: Repeatable
items.entry: You can take this feat more than once.

items.name: Tools
items.entry: Gain proficiency in two tools that are not alliances.

items.name: Mechanical Focus
items.entry: You can use those tools as spell focuses.

items.name: Two Cantrips
items.entry: Learn two cantrips from a class of your choice. Your spellcasting ability for these cantrips is the spellcasting ability of that class. You can replace these cantrips whenever you gain a level.

items.name: Repeatable
items.entry: You can take this feat more than once.

items.name: Tools
items.entry: Gain proficiency in two tools.

items.name: Ease of Use
items.entry: You can make an ability check with one of these tools without holding it as long as it is on your person.

items.name: Masteries
items.entry: Gain 2 masteries. Whenever you gain a level you can swap one of these masteries with a different mastery.

items.name: Repeatable
items.entry: You can take this feat more than once.

name: Toraf and Bolder's Master Cut

prerequisite.other: You must have beaten a master at Master Toraf and Bolder's Sword School

entries: Having trained with the masters of the mountain sword school, you've learned how to pull off difficult weapon maneuvers which allow you to target specific parts of a creature's anatomy. You gain the following benefits:

items.name: Head Strike
entries: Before you make a melee attack with a weapon that you are proficient with, you can choose to take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, the target has disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn.

items.name: Torso Strike
entries: Before you make a melee attack with a weapon that you are proficient with, you can choose to take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, the target can't speak until the start of your next turn, after which it is immune to the effects of Torso Strike for the next minute.

items.name: Leg Strike
entries: Before you make a melee attack with a weapon that you are proficient with, you can choose to take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, the target's speed is reduced by 10 feet (to a minimum speed of 10 feet). This effect lasts until the start of your next turn.
You can only use one of these strikes per attack.

name: Tortle Protector
entries: You have mastered using your shell to better protect yourself and others. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your natural armor trait now provides a base AC of 18. As normal, your Dexterity modifier doesn't affect this number.

As a reaction when you are forced to make a Dexterity saving throw, choose any number of creatures within 5 feet of you. Each chosen creature is considered to have half-cover against any harmful attacks or effects while within 5 feet of you until the start of your next turn. Once you use this ability, you can't do so again until you've finished a short or long rest.

name: Total Mimicry
entries: Using a process similar to your normal object mimicry, only more complete, you can transform yourself fully into an object, rather than just a facsimile with the appearance of the object. As an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, you can become an object of your size or smaller made of vegetable matter or common minerals. The object you become can't rely on intricate artistry or complex moving parts, can't be used as a material component for a spell, and can't be made of precious materials such as gold or gemstone.

While in this form, others can use you as the intended item. However, you have no sensory organs and can't perceive the world around you other than to sense when others touch you. You can't take actions other than to use an {@variantrule Action|XPHB} to return to your normal form. You can condense yourself into an object with less volume than your normal form, but your mass remains the same, so if you become a particularly small object, your extremely high density might give you away.
Once you have used this ability, you must finish a short rest before you can do so again.

name: Totemic Spirit
entries: You have formed a connection with one of the minor Spirits bound to the material world. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain the benefits of one {@filter Totem Spirit|optionalfeatures|feature type=ll:tts} of your choice from those available to the {@loader Shaman|class/LaserLlama; Shaman.json} class. You must meet all prerequisites in order to learn that Totem Spirit.
Whenever you gain a level, you can replace your Totem Spirit with another Totem Spirit of your choice that you also meet all the prerequisites for.

name: Touch From The Beyond
entries: As a bonus action, you can touch a simple or martial weapon and infuse it your undeath abilities. For the next minute, the weapon deals an extra 1d4 necrotic damage when it hits. After you use this bonus action, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

name: Touch of Darkness
entries: There is darkness within you, and it has given you a gift. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Eyes of Night
entries: You can see normally in {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} and {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}—both magical and nonmagical—within 120 feet of yourself.

entries.name: Shadowplay
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks.

name: Touch of Sess'inek
entries: You embody the demonic bearing of a lizard king or queen. You gain the following benefits:

items: You learn to speak, read, and write Abyssal.
You are immune to being frightened.

name: Tough
entries: Your hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to twice your level when you gain this talent. Whenever you gain a level, your hit point maximum increases by 2 additional hit points.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Tough
entries: Your hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to twice your level when you gain this talent. Whenever you gain a level, your hit point maximum increases by 2 additional hit points.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Tough
entries: Your hit point maximum increases by an additional 2 hit points per level.

name: Tough as Old Tree-Roots
entries: They say that Hobbits are difficult to dismay or kill, and that they recover their health at a prodigious pace if allowed to enjoy some peace and quiet. You have discovered that you recover wonderfully from falls and bruises (at the cost of some considerable pain).

items: When you would roll one or more Hit Dice to regain hit points, you instead use the highest number possible for each die.

otherSummary.entry: Charisma score 8 or lower

items: Your natural way with words leaves everyone irritated. Creatures within 10 feet of you suffer a -3 penalty to attack rolls as long as their Intelligence is higher than 3 and they can understand you.

Your level of annoyance has become a taunting mechanism. Whenever an ally within 30 feet of you is targeted by a ranged attack or spell you can use your reaction to swap the targeting to yourself. If it's an AoE spell, you become the center. The attack must be able to see you and hear you and the attack/spell's limitations still apply.

name: Tracker
entries: You doggedly track your quarry over the most hostile landscapes. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in the Survival skill. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for Wisdom (Survival) checks made to track creatures, unless these checks are already benefiting from a feature, such as Expertise, that doubles your proficiency bonus.
While tracking other creatures, you learn their exact number, their sizes, and exactly how long ago they passed through the area.
You can ignore the effects of exhaustion while tracking other creatures for a number of hours equal to 1 + your Constitution modifier (a minimum of 1 hour).
The first time you target a creature you have been tracking within the last 24 hours with an attack, the attack scores a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

name: Tracker
entries: You've learned how to roam freely, as well as how to sleuth out the creature's that occupy it. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a climbing speed or a swimming speed equal to your walking speed (your choice).
You learn one cantrip of your choice from the {@filter druid spell list|spells|level=0|class=Druid}. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for this spell.
You gain proficiency with the {@skill Survival} skill.
You have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks to forage for food and fresh water.

name: Trade Expert
entries: The character gains advantage on any {@skill History} checks made to recall aspects of trading history or on any {@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Deception} check made to a trader or salesman a number of times per day equal to their Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1).

name: Tradeforged Customization
entries: Other people have to exercise to improve their bodies. You've fond that yours is just upgradable.

items: You can select an upgrade from the Warsmith upgrade lists, and apply it to yourself as if you were the mechplate. This upgrade cannot be a level restricted upgrade.

name: Trail Expert
entries: You've learned the complex truth that there are no living things that can't be tracked. Once you've caught the scent of a trail, your quarry is as good as found.

items: Your Wisdom score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.
