A {@condition frightened} creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of its turn, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Other creatures who can hear you suffer minor reactions to the void speech such as spontaneous nosebleeds, headaches, bits of hair falling out, and other unsettling effects. The first time you use this ability, you suffer no adverse effects. If you use it again before completing a short or long rest, you take {@dice 1d4} necrotic damage. Each additional time you use it before finishing a rest, the necrotic damage increases by {@dice 1d4}.

name: Void Scribe
entries: As an action, you can use a writing medium to inscribe a magical void glyph on an unattended object within reach. As long as the glyph remains intact, the object is vulnerable to necrotic damage and it takes {@dice 1d6} necrotic damage at the end of your turn.

For the glyph to remain intact, you must concentrate on it as if concentrating on a spell. In addition to the normal demands of concentration, you must also make a successful DC 10 Constitution saving throw at the start of your turn or the glyph crumbles away and ceases to function.

name: Volcanologist
entries: {@i 8th-Level Feat. Repeatable: No.}

entries.name: Heat Handler
entries: You gain resistance to fire damage.

entries.name: Assess Volcano
entries: If you can see a volcano, you may take 10 minutes to assess it. If you do, you are able to determine whether it is likely to erupt in either the next >100 years, 10 years, 1 year, 30 days, 7 days, or 24 hours. If the volcano is going to erupt in the next 7 days or less, you are able to determine the minimum safe distance from it.

name: Wand Expert
entries: You are adept with the use of {@item Wand|XPHB|Wands} as a swift {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Wand Mastery
entries: If you make a spell attack using a {@item Wand|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}, you gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the attack roll if the target hasn't taken a turn.

entries.name: Unshakeable Casting
entries: When you make a ranged spell attack roll while using a {@item Wand|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}, you do not have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the roll if you are within 5 feet of an enemy.

entries.name: Arcane Quickdraw
entries: Drawing or stowing a {@item Wand|XPHB} does not count against the number of object interactions you can take for free on your turn.

name: Wandslinger
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Arcane Aim
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls you make with spells.

entries.name: Mystic Force
entries: When you cast a cantrip that requires the target to make a saving throw, increase the DC of the saving throw by 1.

name: War Caster (Alternate)
entries: You have trained to make use of your spells in the chaos of pitched combat. You gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Hardened Focus
entries: Whenever you make a saving throw to maintain concentration on a spell, you can make the saving throw with your Spellcasting Ability instead of Constiutiton.

entries.name: Opportune Magic
entries: When you would make an opportunity attack, you can choose to cast a spell instead. It must have a casting time of one action and only target that creature.

entries.name: Warrior Mage
entries: You can perform the Somatic components of your spells while wielding a weapon or shield in your hand.

name: War Caster
entries: You gain the following benefits

items.name: Damage Reduction
items.entry: When you take damage from a weapon attack you can reduce the damage by an amount equal to the level of a spell you're concentrating on. If you do, you cannot do so again until the start of your next turn.

items.name: Opportunity Spell
items.entry: When a creature provokes an Opportunity Attack from you, you can use your Reaction to cast a Spell at the creature, rather than making an Opportunity Attack. The Spell must have a casting time of one Action and must target only that creature.

name: War Caster
entries: You gain the following benefit and the first two available Tiers of the War Caster Feat:
{@b The Tiers of the War Caster Feat:}

name: War Caster
entries: You have practiced casting spells in the midst of combat, learning techniques that grant you the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on Constitution saving throws that you make to maintain your concentration on a spell when you take damage.
You can perform the somatic components of spells even when you have weapons or a {@item shield|yastah} in one or both hands.

When a hostile creature's movement provokes an opportunity attack from you, you can use your reaction to cast a spell at the creature, rather than making an opportunity attack. The spell must have a casting time of 1 action and must target only that creature.

name: War Mage

prerequisite.other: {@feat Spell Sniper|TalentTrees}, {@feat Potent Spellcasting|TalentTrees}, or {@feat Martial Casting|TalentTrees}

entries: You have developed a magical affinity with weapons. You gain the following features.

items: By spending 10 minutes mystically attuning to a simple or martial weapon or a shield, you can use it as an {@item arcane focus|PHB}, {@item druidic focus|PHB}, or {@item holy symbol|PHB}. This does not count against the number of magic items to which you can attune.
You can add bonus damage to one damage roll of a cantrip you cast. This bonus is equal to the number of magic items to which you are currently attuned (maximum of +3).

When you deal acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, poison, radiant, or thunder damage with a spell while holding a weapon to which you are attuned, the next time you deal damage with that weapon before the end of your next turn, you deal an additional {@dice 1d4} damage of that type.

entries: {@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: War Mage

prerequisite.other: {@feat Spell Sniper|TalentTreesMod}, {@feat Potent Spellcasting|TalentTreesMod}, or {@feat Martial Casting|TalentTreesMod}

entries: You have developed a magical affinity with weapons. You gain the following features.

items: By spending 10 minutes mystically attuning to a simple or martial weapon or a shield, you can use it as an {@item arcane focus|PHB}, {@item druidic focus|PHB}, or {@item holy symbol|PHB}. This does not count against the number of magic items to which you can attune.
You can add bonus damage to one damage roll of a cantrip you cast. This bonus is equal to the number of magic items to which you are currently attuned (maximum of +3).

When you deal acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, poison, radiant, or thunder damage with a spell while holding a weapon to which you are attuned, the next time you deal damage with that weapon before the end of your next turn, you deal an additional {@dice 1d4} damage of that type.

entries: {@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: War Magic

prerequisite.other: {@feat Extra Attack|Adventurer}, The ability to cast a cantrip

entries: When you use your action to cast a cantrip, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

name: War Pick Expert
entries: You have mastered the use of a war pick, and are able to tear down the most formidable foes.

items: {@b Ability Score Increase.} Increase your Strength or Constitution ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
{@b Siege Pick.} Attacks you make with the war pick against objects deal double damage.

{@b Sunder.} When you hit a target that is wearing armor or benefiting from natural armor, you can use your bonus action to sunder the target, temporarily leaving them vulnerable. The next attack roll against that creature has advantage.

name: War Plating
entries: You've trained in wearing heavy armor into combat. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Strength score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You gain proficiency with heavy armor.
When you don a heavy armor, you can choose to forgo using its AC calculation. If you do, bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage that you take from nonmagical attacks is reduced by 3.
Wearing heavy armor no longer restricts the Flight or Stride features.

name: War Psion

feature: The ability to use at least one {@filter psionic discipline|optionalfeatures|feature type=PsiD}

entries: You have mastered utilizing psionics in the midst of combat, learning techniques that grant you the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on Constitution saving throws that you make to maintain your concentration on a psionic ability when you take damage.
You can perform the somatic components of psionic abilities even when you have weapons or a shield in one or both hands.

When a hostile creature's movement provokes an opportunity attack from you, you can use your reaction to use a psionic disciplines power or spell targeting the creature, rather than making an opportunity attack. The spell must have a casting time of 1 action and must target only that creature.

name: Warborn's Fury*
entries: Apothis and Merric dine on the devastation that you bring with your fury, and grant you the power to draw even more blood from your enemies in their names. You gain the Following Benefits:

items: Once per day you can enter an Orcish Rage as a Bonus Action. For the next 2 rounds, you are resistant to all Piercing, Slashing, or Bludgeoning damage from non-magical weapons. For every attack action in which you do not make at least 1 successful attack, your Rage extends for 1 round, but will immediately end if you do not attempt to do damage on your turn. During this Rage, you also do an additional 2 damage with your attacks, and can still cast spells. This Rage cannot stack with Barbarian Rage.
You no longer have penalties for sleeping in armor.

If you are proficient in medium armor, wearing it no longer counts towards your carry capacity. If you are proficient in heavy armor, wearing it now counts for half of its weight towards your carry capacity.
You ignore the Strength requirement of armor.
You do not suffer the negative effects of traveling at a Forced March.

name: Ward Mage
entries: You have learned how to bolster your shields, barriers, and walls of magic beyond their normal capabilities in order to better control a battlefield and protect yourself and your allies. You gain the following benefits:

items: When one of your spells or class features grants a protective ward with hit points to a creature (such as the Abjuration Wizard's ward, or the new {@spell barrier|TEB} spell) you grant that ward extra hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.

When a spell you cast creates a wall or barrier with no creature as a target (such as {@spell wall of stone} or the new {@spell screen of protection|TEB} spell) you increase the hit points of that object by an amount equal to twice your proficiency bonus, and you increase its AC by 2.
When a spell you cast grants a creature temporary hit points, you increase the temporary hit points by an amount equal to your proficiency bonus.

Any creature that has its AC increased from a spell you cast or that has a protective ward with hit points granted by a spell you cast also has an additional +1 bonus to AC. This bonus is not cumulative.

name: Ward of Faith
entries: Your dedication as an agent of divine power gives you authority over creatures of divine or profane origin. As an action, you can touch a willing creature in range, warding it against attack. Choose a type of creature: celestial, fey, fiend, or undead. The next time a creature of the chosen type would attack or target the creature with a harmful spell within the next 8 hours, it must make a Wisdom saving throw against a DC of 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom or Intelligence modifier (your choice), or lose the spell or attack. You can use this ability a number of times equal to 1 + your Intelligence or your Wisdom modifier, regaining all expended uses at the end of a long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Ward of Faith
entries: Your dedication as an agent of divine power gives you authority over creatures of divine or profane origin. As an action, you can touch a willing creature in range, warding it against attack. Choose a type of creature: celestial, fiend, or undead. The next time a creature of the chosen type would attack or target the creature with a harmful spell within the next 8 hours, it must make a Wisdom saving throw against a DC of 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom or Intelligence modifier (your choice), or lose the spell or attack. You can use this ability a number of times equal to 1 + your Intelligence or your Wisdom modifier, regaining all expended uses at the end of a long rest.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Warden Initiate
entries: You have learned some of the secrets and techniques of the Wardens of the Wood druidic order. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Warden's Proficiency.
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Animal Handling|XPHB} skill.

entries.name: Protect Ally
entries: When a creature you can see hits another creature within 5 feet of you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce the damage dealt to the target by {@dice 1d6} + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.
Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Warden Spells
entries: The secrets you've learned allow you to always have certain spells at the ready. When you have spell slots of a level specified in the Warden of the Wood Spells table, you thereafter have the spells listed for that level and lower prepared.

name: Warforged Colossus
entries: An unstoppable force on the field of battle, you gain the following benefits:

items: You can use your reaction to reduce the distance you are moved against your will by up to 10 feet.
When you move at least 30 feet in a straight line right before you make a melee weapon attack using Strength and you hit, you can add your Strength modifier to the damage twice, instead of once.

name: Warhammer Expert
entries: Your mastery over a warhammer ensures that your blows never fail to wear down the enemy, becoming an inexorable threat to any foe. You gain the following benefits:

items: {@b Ability Score Increase.} Increase your Strength or Constitution ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

{@b Battering Blows.} When you miss a melee weapon attack with the warhammer, the target takes half the weapon damage the attack would have dealt. This does not count as a hit for things that require you to hit the target (such as spells, Divine Smite, or similar features), but does include modifiers to the attack damage roll.

name: Warped
entries: You have been twisted by the insidious lights of the Void—irrevocably warped by its radiation. You gain the following changes:

items: Your face and body are unnerving to behold. You gain proficiency with {@skill Intimidation}.

In response to the ravages of the warp, many of your vital organs have shifted to new locations within your body. When you are targeted by an attack that is a critical hit, you can choose to take no additional damage from the critical hit, as if it were a normal hit instead. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

name: Warrior Mage
entries: You've trained to defend yourself even while casting spells, gaining the following benefits:

items: Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20
You gain proficiency with shields and your choice of a martial weapon that does not have the two-handed property, and you can use that weapon as a spellcasting focus for your spells.

name: Warzone Nomad
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Adrenaline Rush
entries: You can take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. When you do so, you gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Relentless Endurance
entries: When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} but not killed outright, you can drop to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead. Once you use this benefit, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Water Affinity
entries: You are granted a special affinity with water, allowing you to borrow and harness its power. You learn the {@spell water bullet|KT-CLL} and {@spell manipulate water|SpellsThatDontSuck} cantrips, and learn the {@spell become water|KT-CLL} spell. You can cast it innately without expending a spell slot once, regaining the ability to so when you complete a short or long rest. When you cast it this way, you cast it a level equal to your proficiency bonus.

name: Water Weaver
entries: You have mastered a special connection to water and can beckon it to your call. You gain the following benefits:

items: {@b Ability Score Bonus.} Increase your Strength, Dexterity, or Wisdom ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
{@b Water Walker.} You can walk on top of surfaces made of water as if they are solid ground.
You gain the {@b Water Whip} special attack (below).

entries.name: Water Whip
entries: {@italic Active Ability (Attack, Supernatural)}

When you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with creating and using a whip of water. You can slam this into a creature within 30 feet of you, forcing it to make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes a number of {@dice d8} damage equal to your proficiency bonus, and is knocked 10 feet in a direction of your choice (including straight up, if you so choose). On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage and isn't moved.
Once you use this ability, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

items: You gain proficiency with {@item navigator's tools|phb} and {@item cartographer's tools|phb}, if you are already proficient with either of them, you double your proficiency bonus for all ability checks you make with the tools you were already proficient with instead.
You always know the direction north and cannot become lost except by magical means.

You may spend one hour studying a map or {@item navigator's tools|phb} with a certain location in mind. After you do, you learn both the fastest and the safest way to reach the chosen location. You may do this only if you know where the chosen location is (at least on a map).

name: Ways of the Wild
entries: The Rangers of the North roam ceaselessly, hunting for wicked things and guarding all frontiers. For you the Wild has become as familiar as the road that leads home is familiar to Hobbits, and the land itself may reveal useful tidings.

items: During a journey, you can take on multiple roles without penalties.

You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Explore|TLotRR}, {@skill Hunting|TLotRR}, or {@skill Travel|TLotRR}. If you are already proficient in each of them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with one of them of your choice.

When you make a Wisdom check using a skill in which you are proficient, you can obtain a magical success. You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Weapon Adept
entries: You have spent many hours honing your skills with the deadly armaments of war. You gain the benefits listed below:

entries.name: Weapon Training
entries: You gain proficiency with all simple and martial weapons.

name: Weapon Arts
entries: Your proficiency with one or more weapons allows you utilize their unique features when you use them to attack. When you use the attack action, you may replace any attack with any Weapon Art assigned to that weapon. You may use multiple Weapon Arts per turn, but may not use the same one twice in one turn. You may use Weapon Arts a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses when you finish a short or long rest.

name: Weapon Bond
entries: You learn a ritual that creates a magical bond between yourself and one weapon. You perform the ritual over the course of 1 hour, which can be done during a short rest. The weapon must be within your reach throughout the ritual, at the conclusion of which you touch the weapon and forge the bond.

Once you have bonded a weapon to yourself, you have advantage on saving throws against being disarmed of that weapon unless you are incapacitated, and you can shunt it into an extradimensional space as an bonus action. If it is on the same plane of existence or in extradimensional space, you can summon that weapon as a bonus action on your turn, causing it to teleport instantly to your hand. You can only have one bonded weapon. If you attempt to create a new bond, it replaces the current one.
Your bonded weapon counts as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

name: Weapon Improvisation
entries: You have mastered making commonplace items into vicious tools of battle. You gain proficiency with improvised weapons. While the items remain sufficiently undamaged, your improvised weapons gain additional properties based on their weight as described in the Improvised Weapons Properties table below.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Weapon Improvisation
entries: You have mastered making commonplace items into vicious tools of battle. You gain proficiency with improvised weapons. While the items remain sufficiently undamaged, your improvised weapons gain additional properties based on their weight as described in the Improvised Weapons Properties table below.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

foundrySystem.chatFlavor: There is 3 improvised weapons you can import with Plutonium instead of this feature's damage rolls.

name: Weapon Initiate
entries: You learn the basics of martial combat:

items.name: Weapon Proficiency
items.entry: You gain proficiency in two weapons

items.name: Weapon Mastery
items.entry: Choose a class. Gain 2 Masteries from that class's mastery list. Whenever you gain a level you can swap one of these masteries with a different mastery from the same list.

items.name: Repeatable
items.entry: You can take this feat more than once.

name: Weapon Master (Alterante)
entries: You wield weapons with a deadly efficiency that is impressive even to most trained warriors. Choose a number of simple or martial weapons equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Whenever you make an attack with those weapons you gain a +1 bonus to both the attack and damage roll.
As your Proficiency Bonus increases, choose additional weapons to gain this benefit.

name: Weapon Master
entries: You have practiced extensively with a variety of weapons, gaining the following benefits:

items.name: Proficiency
items.entry: You gain proficiency in three weapons.

items.name: Weapon Mastery
items.entry: Choose a class. Gain 5 Masteries from that list. Whenever you take a long rest you canchange one of those masteries to a different mastery on the same list.

items.name: Repeatable
items.entry: You can take this feat more than once.

name: Weapon Master
entries: You have practiced extensively with a variety of weapons, gaining the following {@footnote benefits|Credit to Nine#5319 for making this feat.}:

items: Choose four simple or martial weapons. You gain proficiency with these weapons if you don't already have it, {@homebrew and you can treat any 1 you roll on their damage dice as a 2}.

name: Weapon Master
entries: You have practiced extensively with a variety of weapons, gaining the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with four weapons of your choice.

name: Weapon Specialist

prerequisite.other: Replaces the {@feat Weapon Master|PHB} feat found in the Player's Handbook

entries: You have practiced extensively to master a personal selection of weapons, gaining the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with four weapons of your choice. Each one must be a simple or a martial weapon. Attacks made with these weapons are never made at disadvantage due to the heavy property. When you make an attack with one of your chosen weapons, you can use the ability modifier of the score increased by this feat, instead of its usual modifier, for the attack and damage rolls.

When you make an attack using your Strength modifier with one of your chosen weapons, you can cause the attack to cleave or pierce through your target, dealing damage equal to your Strength modifier + your proficiency bonus to a different creature of your choice that you can see within 5 feet of it.

When you make an attack using your Dexterity modifier with one of your chosen weapons, you can prevent the attack from being affected by disadvantage. You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Weapon Thrower
entries: You excel at hurling objects, with a remarkably lack of concern for aerodynamics.

items: {@b Ability Score Increase.} Increase your Strength or Constitution by 1, to a maximum of 20.
{@b Reckless Aerodynamics.} All melee weapons gain the thrown 20/60 property for you, unless they already had the thrown property with a greater range.
Gain the {@b Thunderbolt Throw} special attack (below)

entries.name: Thunderbolt Throw
entries: {@italic Active Ability (Attack)}

When you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks to hurl a Small or smaller object (including weapons for creatures of Medium size) at a target. Make an attack treating the object as a simple melee weapon with the thrown 60/180 property unless it already has a longer thrown range. On hit, the creature takes {@damage 2d6} + your Strength modifier bludgeoning damage (replaced by the weapons damage type when throwing a weapon) and must make a Constitution saving throw or be knocked {@condition prone} and dazed{@sup †}. The number of d6 increases by one when your proficiency bonus increases (with the total number of d6 equaling your proficiency bonus).
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

entries.name: {@sup †}Dazed Condition
entries: A dazed creature can only do one of the following: move, take its action, or take a bonus action. It cannot take reactions.

name: Weapon Training
entries: You have either trained, formally or informally, under a master of arms or have otherwise come to earn mastery over nearly any weapon you come across. You gain proficiency with all simple and martial weapons. When you take this talent, if you already have proficiency with all simple and martial weapons, you can instead choose to progress again on this tree rather than gaining weapon proficiencies.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Weapon Training
entries: You have either trained, formally or informally, under a master of arms or have otherwise come to earn mastery over nearly any weapon you come across. You gain proficiency with all simple and martial weapons. When you take this talent, if you already have proficiency with all simple and martial weapons, you can instead choose to progress again on this tree rather than gaining weapon proficiencies.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Weapon-Craft
entries: Choose a type of weapon. You gain proficiency with this weapon if you don't already have it. When you attack with that type of weapon and the weapon is {@itemProperty F||finesse} or ranged, you can use your choice of your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier instead of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

In addition, when you hit a creature with the chosen weapon, you can spend a craft slot to roll a number of additional weapon damage dice on the damage roll. The number of additional weapon damage dice is equal to your proficiency bonus.

name: Weasel War Dancer
entries: Confounding opponents with your erratic movements, you gain the following benefits:

items: When you use the {@action Dash} action, all creatures that can see you have disadvantage on their attack rolls against you until the beginning of your next turn.
By reducing your speed by 10 feet, you gain advantage on an attack made after moving at least 5 feet.

name: Weather Magic
entries: You have trained and studied with the pegasi masters to learn how to harness the magic of the sky. You gain the following benefits:

items: You learn the cantrip {@spell cloudshape|mlpplaneshift} and can cast it at will, without expending a spell slot.

You learn the spells {@spell create or destroy water} and {@spell gust of wind}. You can cast them each once without using a spell slot or material components and cannot cast them again until you finish a short or long rest.
You learn the spell {@spell call lightning}. You can cast it once without using a spell slot and cannot cast it again until you finish a long rest.

entries: Use Charisma as the casting ability for these spells.

name: Weathered Tracker
entries: You gain advantage on checks to discern the species of the creature based on its tracks.

Additionally, you ignore the adverse effects of harsh weather. This can include not getting exhaustion due to being in very hot or very cold temperatures. You don't get disadvantage on {@skill Acrobatics} checks while on ice.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Weathered Tracker
entries: You gain advantage on checks to discern the species of the creature based on its tracks.

Additionally, you ignore the adverse effects of harsh weather. This can include not getting exhaustion due to being in very hot or very cold temperatures. You don't get disadvantage on {@skill Acrobatics} checks while on ice.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Weavebonder
entries: With a nuanced touch, you can manipulate even the smallest ebbs and flows of an item's magic.

items: When you make an Enchanting check with a skill with which you are proficient, you have advantage on the roll.
When you roll for a quirk's random element (such as damage type, skill, or creature type), you can roll the die twice and choose either result.
Each hour you spend enchanting an item counts as 3 hours towards the item's completion.

name: Weaver
entries: You are an expert with {@item Weaver's Tools|phb}.
You have advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) checks that require the use of a steady or completely stationary hand.
Creating an outfit or repairing a cloth object using weaver's tools only requires a short rest. During a long rest, you can perform five of these operations consecutively.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Weaver of Maledictions

prerequisite.other: The ability to cast at least one spell

entries: You have learned how to use effigy dolls when cursing your targets. These dolls take 8 hours to create and can only be used on the target that the effigy was created to resemble. Only you can benefit from dolls you have created. When you use an effigy doll you gain the following benefits:

items: The target of the curse has disadvantage on their initial saving throw.
The target of your curse does not know that you tried to curse them upon a successful save against being cursed.

name: Well of Inspiration
entries: You can give back more of the inspiring energy that nourishes you to your companions. You gain the following benefits:

items: The dice rolled whenever you use your When Inspiration Strikes or Thoughtful features become equal in size to your Hit Die.

When you have no uses of your When Inspiration Strikes or Thoughtful features remaining, you can expend two of your Hit Dice to use the feature again. Once you do so, you must complete a short or long rest before you can use the feature in this way again.

name: Well-Read
entries: You grew up with your nose buried in books. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Creature Lore
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you can recall lore about a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself; you know one {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}, {@spell Resistance|XPHB}, {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB}, or Trait of that creature. You decide when you use this ability.

entries.name: Font of Useful Knowledge
entries: When you roll a 1 on an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill History|XPHB}) check, you can reroll the die, and you must use the new roll.

entries.name: Rare Knowledge
entries: If you succeed on an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill History|XPHB}) check, you learn additional lore. The GM has final say on what you learn, if anything. The lore might consist of important details, amusing revelations, or even secret lore that has never been widely known. The more information you already know about the thing, the more precise and detailed the information you receive is. That information is accurate but might be couched in figurative language or poetry, as determined by the GM.

name: Well-Rested
entries: Your practiced napping leaves you invigorated when you are awake. You gain the following benefits:

items: Whenever you spend one or more hit dice during a short rest, you can regain an extra {@dice 1d6} hit points.
At the end of a long rest, you gain inspiration (described in chapter 4 of the Player's Handbook).

name: Well-Versed
entries: You know the sagas of your people and others and can use that knowledge to help you. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Lore Proficiency
entries: You gain proficiency in one musical instrument and one of the following skills: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion}.

entries.name: Useful Knowledge
entries: When you make an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion}) check, you can give yourself {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the roll. You can do this a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Weretouched Master
entries: The strength of your lycanthropic heritage increases, expanding your primal abilities. You gain the following benefits:

items: Choose a shifter subrace other than your own. You also gain the traits of that subrace, but not its ability score increase or shifting feature.
If you are conscious when your shifting feature ends, you regain a number of hit points equal to your Constitution modifier, up to your Hit Point Maximum.

name: Wetland Explorer
entries: Your deep knowledge of the dangerous creatures that inhabit the world aid you in both fighting and tracking them. You gain the following benefits:

items: Select two creature types of your choice. Whenever you roll initiative at the start of a combat that has one or more hostile creatures of the chosen type, you can add your proficiency bonus to the roll. If a creature has magically altered its form to appear as another creature type, you don't gain this benefit.
You gain a +5 bonus to Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) and Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks involving one or more of the chosen creature types.
You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls made against a target of the chosen creature type.

name: Wheelman
entries: You have become supernaturally familiar with vehicles of all shapes and sizes, gaining the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with all vehicles. While you are driving a non-sentient vehicle, add your proficiency bonus to that vehicle's ability checks and saving throws.

When you are driving a vehicle and your vehicle is hit with an attack, you can use your reaction to add your proficiency bonus to your vehicle's AC against that attack, potentially causing it to miss.
If a vehicle you are driving is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity save to take only half damage, it takes no damage if it succeeds and only half damage if it fails.
You can control a vehicle without having a free hand for the vehicle's controls.

name: Whip Aficionado
entries: An ex-slaver or lion-tamer, you have always had a love for whips. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can use the Help action as a bonus action provided you have made a melee attack with a whip this turn. Additionally, when you use the Help action to aid an ally in attacking a creature, the target of that attack can be within 30 feet of you, rather than within 5 feet of you, if the target can see or hear you.

If you hit a Large or smaller creature with a melee attack using a whip, you can choose to knock the creature prone, or pull the creature up to 10 feet closer to you. If you do so, roll a d8 and reduce any damage the creature would take from the attack by that amount (to a minimum of 0).
When you make a melee attack on your turn with a whip, your reach for it is 5 feet greater than normal.

name: Whip Aficionado
entries: You have always had a love for whips. You gain the following benefits when using one:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls you make with a whip.
As a bonus action on your turn, you can increase your reach with a whip by 5 feet for the rest of your turn.

Whenever you have disadvantage on a melee attack roll you make with the weapon, the target takes slashing damage equal to your Dexterity modifier (minimum of 0) if the attack misses but the higher of the two {@dice d20} rolls would have hit.
If you roll a critical hit on a melee attack roll with the weapon, as a reaction you can take the {@action Help} action to aid an ally's melee attack against that same target.

name: Whip Expert
entries: You master using a whip, gaining the following benefits:

items: {@b Ability Score Bonus.} Increase your Strength, Dexterity or Constitution ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

{@b Expert Handling.} Whips gain the Light property for you and you can use a whip to extend your reach for certain object interactions, such as opening and closing doors, picking up objects, or similar simple interactions.
{@b Whip Tricks.} You gain the Whip Tricks special attacks.

entries: Whip Tricks
You master the manipulation of a whip to allow a level of extreme control over its use.

When you make a weapon attack with a whip, you can replace the attack with a trick, forcing the enemy to make a Dexterity saving throw saving with a DC of 8 + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice) + your proficiency bonus. If the target fails its saving throw, you can perform any of the following tricks against it:

items: {@b Sudden Yank.} You wrap the whip around a Medium or smaller target, and yank them 5 feet towards you.

{@b Tangle Weapon.} You tangle one weapon the target is wielding, giving them disadvantage on attacks with that weapon until the start of your next turn, or until they miss an attack. You cannot make attacks with the whip used to make the attack until they free the weapon.
{@b Whip Trip.} You tangle a Large or smaller creature's feet, causing them to fall prone

name: Whip Master
entries: Whips you wield deal {@dice 1d6} instead of {@dice 1d4} slashing damage.

Whenever you jump while holding a whip, if there is something within range that you could use your whip to swing on (a tree branch, for example) you may do so as part of your movement to increase your jump distance by 10 feet.
Finally, as a bonus action you may use a whip to do the following things:

items: Activating a switch, pressing a button or pulling a lever within 10 feet of you.

Attempting to pull a small object or small or medium creature within 10 feet of you towards you. If it is an object, you pull it 5 feet towards you and may catch it in your hand if it is small enough. If it is a creature, it must succeed on a Strength ({@skill athletics}) or Dexterity ({@skill acrobatics}) check contested by you or be pulled 5 feet towards you.

Making a loud cracking sound. Each creature within 5 feet of you must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC: 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier, your choice) or be {@condition deafened} until the end of their next turn.

name: Whip Master
entries: You have extensive training with whip like weapons and have learned a handful of tricks useful in combat. You gain the following benefits:

items: Once per turn when you deal damage with a whip or weighted chain to a creature that is no more than one size larger than you, you can force that creature to make a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier). On a failure, you choose whether the creature drops one object of your choice that it's holding, falls prone, or has its movement speed reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn.
When you take the Attack action and attack with a one-handed weapon, you can use a bonus action to attack with a whip or weighted chain you are holding.

name: Whip Master
entries: You have extensive training with whip like weapons and have learned a handful of tricks useful in combat. You gain the following benefits:

items: Once per turn when you deal damage with a whip or weighted chain to a creature that is no more than one size larger than you, you can force that creature to make a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier). On a failure, you choose whether the creature drops one object of your choice that it's holding, falls {@condition prone}, or has its movement speed reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn.
When you take the {@action Attack} action and attack with a one-handed weapon, you can use a bonus action to attack with a whip or weighted chain you are holding.
When you use a whip, its damage die changes from d4 to d6.

When you hit a creature no more than one size larger than you with a whip on your turn, you can use a bonus action to pull the target up to 5 feet towards you. When you do this, you can immediately try to grapple it, try to shove it to knock it prone, or make a melee attack against it with a light weapon you are holding as if you were using two-weapon fighting.
As a bonus action on your turn, you can increase your reach with a whip by 5 feet until the start of your next turn.

name: Whip Mastery
entries: You have mastered the strange and difficult art of using a whip in combat. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to damage rolls made with a whip.
When you use a whip, its damage die increases from a d4 to a d6. (This benefit has no effect if another feature has already improved the weapon's die.)

Whenever you have advantage on a melee attack roll you make with a whip and hit, you can knock a weapon or another item from the target's grasp if the lower of the two d20 rolls would also hit the target.

name: Whip Wielder
entries: The {@item whip|PHB|whips} you wield gain the light property while you wield them.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Whip Wielder
entries: The {@item whip|PHB|whips} you wield gain the light property while you wield them.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Whirling Dervish
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with a melee attack you can move 5 feet without spending any movement. This movement may still trigger an attack of opportunity.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Whirling Dervish
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with a melee attack you can move 5 feet without spending any movement. This movement may still trigger an attack of opportunity.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

items: You can use your action to make a melee weapon attack against all hostile creatures within your weapon's reach. If you do so, you make a single attack roll and compare the result to each target's AC, and you make a single damage roll for all creatures you hit with the attack.

name: Wild Companion
entries: You have learned to bond with and train {@filter Beasts|bestiary|type=Beast|source=LLCompendiumOfBeasts} of the wild to adventure by your side. Choose one Beast with a CR equal to (or lower than) your level divided by 4. This Beast becomes a Wild Companion. It is Friendly to you and uses these rules:

entries.name: Stat Block
entries: Your Companion uses its normal stat block, but it learns to understand one language that you speak. You and your Companion can communicate simple ideas to each other using a series of clicks, whistles, and gestures. It gains all the normal benefits of both short and long rests.

entries.name: Combat
entries: In combat, your Companion acts on your turn. It can move and use its reaction on its own, but it will only take the Dodge action unless you use a bonus action to command it to take an action from its stat block or another action.
If you are Incapacitated, your Companion will defend itself to the best of its ability. Should you die, your Companion will do everything in its power to flee and return to its home.

entries.name: New Companion
entries: Should your Wild Companion die, or you release it from this bond, you can train a new Beast to be your Companion. To do so, you must spend 8 hours tracking, befriending, and bonding with a Beast within the CR limit as described above. A suitable Beast must be able to be found in your location within this 8-hour period.

You can only have one Wild Companion at a time. Should you seek out and bond a enw Wild Companion, any previous Wild Companions will leave you to return home. If you treat your Companion with hostility or recklessly risk its life, it will desert you and return home.

name: Wild Hunter
entries: You have significant experience studying, tracking, and hunting a particular kind of enemy. Choose a type of favored enemy: beasts, fey, humanoids, monstrosities, or undead. You have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks to track your favored enemies, as well as on Intelligence checks to recall information about them. Additionally, you gain a 1d4 bonus to damage rolls with weapon attacks against creatures of the chosen type.

name: Wild Lore
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Knowledge of the Land
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) checks.

entries.name: Provider
entries: You can use your knowledge of the land to find food and fresh water for yourself and up to 3 other people each day.

name: Wild Magic
entries: You learn to manipulate the forces of chance and chaos. Whenever you expend 1 or more sorcery points, roll a d20. If you roll a 1, you trigger a Wild Magic Surge, and roll on the Wild Magic Surge table to create a random magical effect. A Wild Magic Surge can only happen once per turn. If a Wild Magic Surge effect is a spell, it's too wild to be affected by Metamagic. If it normally requires concentration, it doesn't require concentration in this case; the spell lasts for its full duration. See page 104 of the Player Handbook for the Wild Magic Surge table.
Additionally, you can use an bonus action to spend 5 sorcery points to roll directly on the Wild Magic Surge table.
If you have the Action Surge feat, roll directly on the Wild Magic Surge table when you use it to take an additional action. The surge happens before the additional action is taken.

name: Wild Spirit Guides
entries: The spirits of wild animals guide you. Choose two of the following options:

items.name: Bear
entries: Your hitpoint maximum increases by 1 for each level you have, and increases by 1 each time you gain a level.

items.name: Dolphin
entries: You gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed and can hold your breath for double the amount of time.

items.name: Monkey
entries: You gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed and your jump distance increases by 10 feet.

items.name: Eagle
entries: You have advantage on {@skill Perception} checks that rely on sight.

items.name: Wolf
entries: Your movement speed increases by 5 feet and you have advantage on {@skill Perception} checks that rely on smell.

name: Wild Talent
entries: You harbor a wellspring of psionic energy within yourself. This energy is represented by your Psionic Energy dice, which are each a {@dice d6}. If you already have Psionic Energy dice, you gain one more; otherwise, you have a number of these dice equal to your proficiency bonus. You regain all your expended Psionic Energy dice when you finish a long rest. In addition, as a bonus action, you can regain one expended Psionic Energy die, but you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

items: {@b Psi-Boosted Ability.} When you make an ability check with your chosen psionic ability, you can roll your Psionic Talent die and add the number rolled to the check. You can choose to do so before or after rolling the {@dice d20}, but before you know whether the check succeeded or failed.

{@b Psi-Guided Strike.} Once on each of your turns when you hit with an attack roll that uses your chosen psionic ability, you can roll your Psionic Talent die after you make the damage roll and then replace one of the damage dice with the number rolled on the Psionic Talent die.

{@b Psi-Warded Body.} After you or another creature you can see within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw, you can use your reaction to roll your Psionic Talent die and add the number rolled to the saving throw, potentially causing it to succeed.

entries: {@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Wild Talent

entries.name: Repeatable:
entries: No
Your natural psionic talent awakens:

items: You learn the {@spell mage hand} and {@spell message} cantrips and the {@spell dissonant whispers} spell.
These spells require no spell components when cast via this feat.
Your mage hand is invisible.
Message is telepathic and requires no pointing.
You can cast dissonant whispers once per long rest without a slot, or with spell slots.

name: Wind Slash
entries: The wind conveys the will of your attacks, granting you the following benefits:

items: {@b Ability Score Bonus.} Increase your Strength, Dexterity or Wisdom ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

{@b Cloudbreaker.} You can cut dust, fog, or clouds. As an attack as part of the attack action, you can clear a 30 foot cone of dust, fog, or cloud. Depending on the source of the obscuring effect, the area may become obscured again after {@dice 1d4} rounds.
You gain the {@b Wind Slash} special attack (below).

entries.name: Wind Slash
entries: {@italic Active Ability (Attack, Supernatural)}

When you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with a special attack, launching a blades of wind at targets within 60 feet. You launch a number of blades equal to your proficiency modifier, but can increase the number of attacks made by giving up additional attacks you can make as part of the {@action Attack} action (launching one additional attack for each attack forgone). The blades are ranged weapon attacks using your Mystic Path modifier. Each blade deals {@damage 1d6} + your Mystic Path modifier slashing damage on damage on hit.
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

name: Wind Touched
entries: Your exposure to the Elemental Plane of Air has surrounded your magical presence with whirling winds, granting you the following benefits:

items: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You learn the wind scythe cantrip, which for you has a range of 120 feet. The spell's spellcasting ability is the ability increased by this feat.

You learn the gale strike and expeditious retreat spells. You can cast each of these spells without expending a spell slot. Once you cast either of these spells in this way, you can't cast that spell in this way again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast these spells using spell slots you have of the appropriate level. The spell's spellcasting ability is the ability increased by this feat.

name: Windsoul
entries: You have freed the liberating magics of elemental air inside yourself, granting you the following benefits:

items: You can cast the {@spell feather fall} spell on yourself at will, without expending a spell slot.

Once you reach 5th level, you can cast the {@spell fly} spell, requiring no spell slot or components, and you must finish a long rest before you can cast it this way again. You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Constitution is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

name: Windswept
entries: Carefree and constantly possessed of wanderlust, the extraordinarily pale windswept embody their connection to Elemental Air. Windswept humans are never likely to sleep in the same bed for two nights in a row; they are always moving, always exploring, and always following the wind. You are lighter than a normal human, capable of floating gently on the breeze, and have faint inborn power over the winds, which grant you the following racial traits:

entries.name: Lightning Resistance
entries: You have resistance to lightning damage.

entries.name: Zephyr Magic
entries: You know the {@spell message} cantrip. Starting at 3rd level, you can cast the {@spell feather fall} spell with this trait. Starting at 5th level, you can also cast the {@spell gust of wind} spell with this trait, without requiring a material component. Once you cast {@spell feather fall} or gust of wind with this trait, you can't cast that spell with it again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast either of those spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells when you cast them with this trait (choose when you select this race).

items.name: Windstep
items.entry: Once you can jump without a surface to push off of as long as you are held aloft or have a reduced fall speed. You regain this ability at the start of your next turn.

items.name: Feather Fall
items.entry: You know the Feather Fall spell and can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain this ability after a short rest.

items.name: Launch
items.entry: As a reaction to getting pushed or pulled you can double the distance that it pushes or pulls you.

items.name: Repeatable
items.entry: You can take this feat more than once.

name: Winged
entries: You sproute translucent wings. With your wings, you have a flying speed of 20 feet if you aren't wearing heavy armor.

name: Winged
entries: Winged humans, sometimes called Icarusians, are the offspring of aarakocra, harpies, or birdfolk. Depending on their parentage, these humans might possess feathers, talons, or beaks.

entries.name: Flight
entries: Because of your wings, you have a flying speed equal to your walking speed. You can't use this flying speed if you're wearing medium or heavy armor.

entries.name: Fly Speed
entries: You have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

name: Winter Initiate
entries: You have learned some of the secrets and techniques of the Children of Winter druidic order. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Life from Death
entries: Whenever you take Necrotic damage, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} after you take the damage.

entries.name: Summon Decay
entries: When you conjure a creature with a spell or magical ability, you can choose for that creature to be Undead instead of its usual creature type.

entries.name: Understand Disease
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks to research, diagnose, and treat disease.

entries.name: Children of Winter Spells
entries: The secrets you've learned allow you to always have certain spells at the ready. When you have spell slots of a level specified in the Children of Winter Spells table, you thereafter have the spells listed for that level and lower prepared.

name: Wisdom Breeds Caution
entries: Not getting into a dangerous situation is generally the wisest course, but if danger is unavoidable, you're prepared. You rely more on caution and forethought than you do on physical prowess. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a bonus to initiative rolls equal to the ability modifier for the ability score you increased with this feat.
You gain a +1 bonus to Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws.

name: Wise One
entries: You find ways to learn from every experience in life, always growing in wisdom. You gain the benefits on the table below that correspond to your current Wisdom modifier and lower.
Should your Wisdom modifier increase, the benefits that you gain from this Feat also increase with your modifier:

rows: You gain proficiency with one set of {@item artisan's tools|PHB} of your choice.
You can make Wisdom ({@skill Persuasion}) checks in place of Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) checks.
You gain proficiency in either {@skill Insight}, {@skill Medicine}, or {@skill Perception}.
When you make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check, you treat a d20 roll of 7 or lower as an 8.
You have advantage on saving throws to resist enchantment and illusion spells.

name: Witch Hunter
entries: You have honed and perfected your skills fighting against spellcasters. You gain the following benefits:

items: Whenever a hostile creature targets you with a spell, make a Wisdom saving throw against the spellcaster's spell save DC. On a success, the creature must choose a new target or lose the spell. This does not protect you from area effects, such as the explosion of a fireball.
Whenever you hit a spellcaster with a melee attack, the target's speed is reduced by 10 feet until the beginning of your next turn.
You have advantage on saving throws against being cursed.

name: Witch Hunter
entries: You have honed and perfected your skills fighting against spellcasters, possibly from your background hunting mages as part of the Arcanist Inquisition. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Dodge Spells
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to avoid a spell that is targeting only you and doesn't create an area of effect. Make a Wisdom saving throw against the spellcaster's spell save DC. On a successful save, the creature must choose a new target or the spell is canceled. A canceled spell dissipates with no effect, and any resources used to cast it are wasted.

entries.name: Keep Your Enemies Close
entries: When you hit a target that can cast spells with an attack roll using a Melee weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can reduce its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} by 15 feet until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Resist Curses
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against all Shadowsteel curses, and also against spells with a duration of more than 10 minutes.

name: Witch Hunter
entries: You have experience in the detection and elimination of warlocks, occultists, and creatures possessed by foul spirits.

items: You gain resistance to acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage (your choice when you gain this feat.)
You can instantly identify a creature that has cast a spell within the last 24 hours.

When you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can use a bonus action to disrupt its magic. This creature must make a Constitution saving throw or have disadvantage on spell attack rolls it makes until the beginning of your next turn. The DC equals 10 or half the damage dealt, whichever is higher.

name: Witch Hunter
entries: You have experience in the detection and elimination of warlocks, occultists, and creatures possessed by foul spirits.

items: You gain resistance to acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage (your choice when you gain this feat.)
You can instantly identify a creature that has cast a spell within the last 24 hours.

When you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can use a bonus action to disrupt its magic. This creature must make a Constitution saving throw or have disadvantage on spell attack rolls it makes until the beginning of your next turn. The DC equals 10 or half the damage dealt, whichever is higher.

name: Witchblood
entries: You have the blood of witches running through your veins, granting you the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in one of the following skills: {@skill Deception}, {@skill Intimidation}, or {@skill Persuasion}.
You gain one {@filter Eldritch Invocation|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=EI} on the warlock Invocation's list, provided you meet any prerequisites or requirements.
You can retake this feat only once again.

name: Witcher handbomb Adept
entries: You have studied the crafting of Witcher handbombs, gaining the following benefits:

items: You learn to prepare one Witcher handbomb of your choice, and gain one use of the Witcher Preparation feature for handbombs only.
The tier of the handbomb you craft is dependent on your highest class level.

entries: You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do so you must select a different handbomb to learn.

name: Witcher Potion Adept
entries: You have studied the brewing of Witcher potions, gaining the following benefits:

items: You have built up a resistance to the toxicity of Witcher potions and can consume them safely.
You learn to prepare one Witcher potion of your choice, and gain one use of the Witcher Preparation feature for potions only.
The tier of the potion you brew is dependent on your highest class level.

entries: You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do so you must select a different potion to learn.

name: Witcher spell Adept
entries: You have studied the arcana of Witcher spells, gaining the following benefits:

items: You learn a Witcher spell of your choice. You can select from the base {@i {@filter Witcher spells|spells|class=Witcher (WITCHERHLA)}} or the {@i {@subclassFeature alternative witcher spells|Witcher|WITCHERHLA|School of the Griffin|WITCHERHLA|6|}} lists, ignoring any prerequisites.

If the chosen spell is a 1st level spell, you can cast it once at 1st level without using a spell slot. You must finish a long rest before you can cast it in this way again, and you can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have.

name: Withdraw
entries: When you make an attack against a creature, you don't provoke opportunity attacks from that creature for the rest of the turn, whether you hit or miss.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

name: Withdraw
entries: When you make an attack against a creature, you don't provoke opportunity attacks from that creature for the rest of the turn, whether you hit or miss.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Wizard's Mark
entries: You have had your own arcane symbol tattooed or burned into your flesh.
{@b Benefit}: If you get your own personal arcane symbol impressed into your flesh, either via tattoo or brand...

items: You Advantage on Condentration Checks.
+1 Spell DC for spells of your Tradition (if you follow a school)
You gain proficiency in the Arcana skill. If you are already proficient in the skill, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.

name: Wood-Craft
entries: You are familiar with the difficulties encountered when crossing wild lands, and with the ways of overcoming them. You can make an Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) check in place of any Wisdom ({@skill Explore|TLotRR}) or Wisdom ({@skill Hunting|TLotRR}) check.

In addition, you can spend 1 hour and a craft slot to make an Intelligence ({@skill Nature}), Wisdom ({@skill Explore|TLotRR}), or Wisdom ({@skill Hunting|TLotRR}) check (your choice). The DC is determined by the terrain type the Company is currently traversing (as if a journey event was taking place there; see {@book Chapter 5|TLotRR|4|Event Resolution}). The check has disadvantage if it is autumn or winter. If you succeed, choose one of the following options:

items: Choose a number of creatures equal to your check result minus the terrain DC (minimum 1), which can include yourself. For 1 hour, each of those creatures has a +5 bonus to its Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks. When you reach 5th level, the bonus increases to +10. If you obtain a magical success, the creatures also leave behind no tracks or other traces of their passage for the duration.

Choose a number of creatures equal to your check result minus the terrain DC (minimum 1), which can include yourself. For 8 hours, each of those creatures has a +5 bonus to its passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) score. When you reach 5th level, the bonus increases to +10. If you obtain a magical success, the creatures also gain {@sense tremorsense|MM} out to a range of 60 feet for the duration.

You forage a number of pounds of food and gallons of water equal to your check result minus the terrain DC (minimum 1). The food lasts for 24 hours, or 48 hours when you reach 5th level. If you obtain a magical success, each pound of food foraged in this way also restores 1 hit point to the creature eating it during a short or long rest.

name: Woodcarver
entries: You excel at using wood to create intricate objects and designs. you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with {@item woodcarver's tools|phb}. If you are already proficient with them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.
The amount of time it takes you to scavenge wood from a tree or some other object is halved.
You can repair up to three wooden objects as part of a short rest, rather than one.

name: Woodcarver
entries: You are an expert with {@item Woodcarver's Tools|phb}.
The amount of time it takes you to scavenge wood from a tree or some other object is halved.
You can repair up to three wooden objects as part of a short rest, rather than one.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTreesMod}.}

name: Woodchuck
entries: No tree can stand against you and your axe! You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with woodcutter's supplies. If you are already proficient with them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.

You are accustomed to lugging around large pieces of timber and, as such, you count as one size larger for determining the number of inventory slots on your belt. You can also carry one additional large object on your belt using only one slot.
When you roll a natural 20 on a check to gather wood in downtime, you gain one extra success than you normally would.

name: Woodwise
entries: You have lived your entire life in the gnarled, wooded areas of the world. You are adept at finding your way through even the most treacherous terrain. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in either the {@skill Survival} or {@skill Nature} skill.
You ignore difficult terrain.
You cannot become lost in natural surroundings except by magical means.

name: Woodwise
entries: You are exceedingly dangerous when fighting in wooded areas, where you gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks in wooded areas.
If your speed is not zero, then it increases by 5 feet, even when moving through difficult terrain in wooded areas.

name: Worthless
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Worthless
entries: When you gain this Origin Feat, reduce your highest ability score (your choice if they are equal) until the sum of your six ability scores is equal to or lower than 72. Then, reduce each ability score by 1.

entries.name: From the Ashes
entries: When you reach character level 4, and again at character levels 8, 12, 16, and 19, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. You can't increase an ability score above 18 using this benefit.

items: Your Scoridra siblings have started to understand each other's physical movements and martial prowess in the heat of battle. Wrathful Cooperation negates Wrathful Sibling Rivalry's negative effect of having all attacks made on you until the start of your next turn to have Advantage to hit.

name: Wrestler
entries: You know how to utilise your body as a weapon, you gain the following benefits:

items: When you succeed on a Shove Attack you can push the creature a number of feet equal to 5 times your Strength Modifier.
You can move at full movement when you grapple a creature of same size or smaller than you.
When you attempt to grapple, you can make a special grapple instead where you take a -5 penalty to your check, but if you succeed the target is grappled and restrained.

name: Wrestler
entries: When you are {@condition grappled}, you can use your action to reverse the grapple. Make a {@action grapple} check against the creature. If you succeed, you are no longer considered {@condition grappled} and the creature that was grappling you becomes {@condition grappled} by you if it is your size or smaller.
Additionally, you have advantage on melee attacks you make against a creature you are grappling.
{@note This feat is meant to be used with the variant rule {@variantrule Talent Trees|TalentTrees}.}

otherSummary.entry: Divine Subclass

items: Once per day you can use Divine Smite at level 2 at no cost of spell slots (regardless whether you are Paladin or not).
As a bonus action, you gain hp equal to your {@skill Religion} bonus. (5 uses, recharge on long rest)

name: Zealous
entries: You've learned to channel divine energy to heal your allies or harm your enemies. You gain the following benefits:

items: As an action, you can touch a creature and restore a number of hit points to it equal to {@dice 1d4} + your proficiency bonus.
Whenever you make a successful melee weapon attack against a creature, you can choose to deal an additional {@dice d8} radiant damage to the target.

entries: You can use either of these abilities a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Zen Warrior
entries: Through deep meditation, you have learned to harness your inner power, channeling it to accomplish incredible acts of physical poise:

items: You learn one feature fueled by ki points, chosen from the options described in the Ki feature of either the monk class or the mystic class. Whenever you reach a level that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can replace the chosen feature with another one from the chosen class.

You gain 2 ki points to spend on your features (these points are added to any ki points you have from another source). You regain all spent ki points when you finish a short or long rest, at the end of which you draw all of your expended ki back into yourself. You must spend at least 30 minutes of the rest meditating to regain your ki points.
